articles.title: Surface-Engineered BiVO4 Photocatalyst Enables Selective Water Oxidation for Water Splitting via a Photocatalysis–Electrolysis Hybrid System
articles.abstract: Selective water oxidation in the presence of thermodynamically favored competing oxidation reactions remains a major challenge for photocatalytic systems. BiVO4 is one of the most efficient visible-light-responsive photocatalysts for water oxidation and exhibits high activity in Fe3+-mediated water-oxidation systems. However, although accumulated Fe2+ can introduce competing oxidation pathways under strongly acidic Fe3+/Fe2+ redox conditions, effective strategies for suppressing these processes and maintaining selective water oxidation remain largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate a surface-engineering strategy that overcomes this limitation in BiVO4. Systematic investigation revealed that the poor activity of BiVO4 under strongly acidic Fe3+/Fe2+ conditions arises not only from catalyst degradation but also from competition with Fe2+ oxidation reactions. Surface modification of BiVO4 with W species, originally intended to improve acid durability, not only suppressed catalyst dissolution but also mitigated Fe2+-related performance losses, resulting in a marked enhancement of photocatalytic water oxidation. The activity enhancement correlated with highly dispersed surface W species localized near the outermost region of BiVO4. Notably, the highest activity was obtained before or near the onset of detectable WO3 crystallization, suggesting that the surface state of W species in this temperature range is more closely associated with the enhanced activity than crystalline WO3 domains under strongly acidic Fe3+/Fe2+ conditions. The optimized photocatalyst maintained efficient water oxidation while suppressing Fe2+-related performance losses, achieving an apparent quantum yield of 63% under Fe3+-based conditions and approximately 30% even under strongly acidic and concentrated Fe(ClO4)3 conditions relevant to hybrid water splitting. The optimized photocatalyst maintained selective water oxidation even as Fe2+ accumulated to approximately 100 mM, enabling nearly quantitative Fe3+-to-Fe2+ conversion under strongly acidic conditions. When incorporated into a photocatalysis–electrolysis hybrid system, the enhanced photocatalytic activity was directly translated into approximately 1.5-fold higher water-splitting performance than that of the benchmark H-Fe-Cs-WO3 system. These findings demonstrate that selective water oxidation can be maintained even in the presence of thermodynamically favored competing oxidation reactions through appropriate photocatalyst surface engineering, providing a useful strategy for photocatalysts operating in redox-mediated reaction environments, including photocatalysis–electrolysis hybrid water-splitting systems.

articles.title: Unseen but Avoidable: How Impurities Bias Electrocatalysis from Interface to Interpretation
articles.abstract: Impurities exert profound effects on electrocatalytic measurements and interpretations. Trace levels of contaminants introduced through electrolytes, electrodes, gases, or cell materials routinely generate false activity signals, accelerate degradation, and alter product selectivity. This review categorizes impurity effects by functional impact, including misleading activity, compromised stability, and shifted selectivity, and offers strategies to recognize, isolate, and mitigate these influences. We argue that reliable and reproducible electrocatalytic data require an impurity-aware approach, integrating both experimental protocols and systems engineering. By intentional design, impurities can be transformed from hidden liabilities into controlled variables, ensuring that reported advances in electrocatalysis reflect intrinsic catalyst properties and translate into durable energy technologies.

articles.title: Structural Evolution of State-Dependent Kinetics during Potassium Storage in Layered CrSe2
articles.abstract: Layered CrSe2 reversibly accommodates approximately one potassium (K) per formula unit, but the structural origin of its rate-dependent capacity remains unresolved. Operando synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) reveals the sequential P-3m1-R3m-C2/m phase pathway during cycling at different current rates. The P-3m1/R3m transformation exhibits the lattice discontinuity and becomes incomplete when increasing the current rate, as directly observed by operando SXRD. Chemical K deintercalation and state-resolved impedance measurements provide complementary evidence for sluggish kinetics near the fully deintercalated regime. Restricting the upper cutoff voltage will sacrifice some capacity but will improve electrochemical cycling capacity retention. These findings identify a particularly rate-sensitive structural region and show how phase-resolved characterization can guide voltage-window selection for layered potassium-storage electrodes.

articles.title: Antiambipolar and Bidirectional Photoresponse in Ternary van der Waals Heterostructure Transistors
articles.abstract: Next-generation nanoelectronics require device architectures that integrate high density, multifunctionality, and low power consumption. Antiambipolar transistors (AATs) are promising candidates for multivalued logic and intelligent sensing, yet conventional two-dimensional (2D) AATs suffer from low peak-to-valley current ratios (PVRs) and unidirectional self-driven photoresponse. Here, we report a multifunctional AAT based on a MoS2/Ta2NiS5/MoTe2 double van der Waals heterostructure (vdWH). The device exhibits outstanding antiambipolar transport characteristics, achieving an ultrahigh PVR of 1 × 107 and a peak current of 1.2 μA, surpassing those of most previously reported 2D AATs. By introducing Ta2NiS5 as an intermediate layer, a back-to-back type-I band alignment is established, enabling efficient modulation and reversal of interfacial band bending under different bias conditions. Simultaneously, under 635 nm illumination, the device exhibits a gate-tunable bidirectional photocurrent response, with responsivities of +2.94 and −0.65 A/W at Vgs = +40 and −40 V, respectively. Furthermore, the device is demonstrated in ternary logic inverters, in-sensor image convolution processing, and multimodal information encoding. These results demonstrate the potential of van der Waals heterostructure-based antiambipolar transistors for integrated and reconfigurable optoelectronic systems.

articles.title: Biscoordinated Strontium–Phenolic Networks for Bidirectional Repair of Dentin Hypersensitivity
articles.abstract: Dentin hypersensitivity (DH) is a widespread dental disease characterized by transient and sharp pain affecting routine oral activities, with a reported prevalence that can exceed 70%. While remineralization offers a promising therapeutic strategy to address the anatomical basis of exposed dentinal tubules, achieving long-term efficacy remains challenging due to mechanical abrasion and cariogenic biofilms. Herein, strontium–phenolic network nanoparticles (Sr-EGCG NPs) are developed via a facile, one-pot aqueous process for DH treatment. Unlike conventional transition-metal-based metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), the assembly of Sr-based MPNs is found to be dependent on alkaline conditions, yielding a distinct biscoordinated structure. When applied to exposed dentin, Sr-EGCG NPs exhibit rapid and stable adhesion mediated by abundant galloyl groups, maintaining tubule occlusion ratios exceeding 91.8% after simulated oral challenges, especially surpassing commercial Duraphat in thermocycling (Duraphat: 2.0%), while simultaneously reducing live bacterial coverage by over 97.5% at day 3. Crucially, Sr-EGCG NPs enable bidirectional dentin repair: in situ remineralization (achieving complete mineralized occlusion by day 7 both in vitro and in vivo) and the induction of tertiary dentin formation via the CaSR-mediated MAPK signaling pathway. Overall, this work provides insights into the rational design of Sr-based MPNs and expands the framework for developing biomaterials targeting DH.

articles.title: Coordinating Photoacid Generators Enable Site-Defined Metal–Oxo Cluster Lithography
articles.abstract: Lithographic patterning, which employs the solubility switch of photoresists to convert optical signals into nanostructures on the substrate, constitutes the primary top-down approach for high-precision nanomanufacturing. However, the stochastic defects arising from inhomogeneous reaction sites in photoresists pose a formidable challenge to reconciling the precision of sub-10 nm lithography. In this study, we present a coordinating photoacid generator (cPAG)-driven lithography strategy that has achieved a performance breakthrough through precise spatial control of acid sites. The resulting zirconium-oxo cluster photoresists, operating via cPAG-triggered precoordination and cluster cross-linking, demonstrate a two-orders-of-magnitude decrease in UV exposure dose. Furthermore, electron beam lithography has been demonstrated to achieve a sub-10 nm line width, underscoring its suitability for high-resolution and high-sensitivity applications. This strategy is versatile across cPAGs with diverse structures and is also applicable to other metal oxide photoresist systems, including titanium-oxo and zinc-oxo clusters. This work introduces a cPAG design tailored for cluster-based photoresists and validates their ability to overcome the intrinsic trade-off in resolution, line edge roughness, and sensitivity, providing a framework for developing next-generation photoresists.

articles.title: Quantum Dot Colloidosomes as Triggerable Microlasers
articles.abstract: Quantum dot (QD) supraparticle lasers are promising platforms for microscale light sources and photonic labeling, yet their optical properties are set during assembly. Here, we introduce QD colloidosomes, liquid-core/solid-shell supraparticles that combine whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) optical feedback with stimulus-triggered structural collapse. Intact QD colloidosomes exhibit narrow, cavity-defined emission consistent with WGM-assisted lasing from 4.2 mJ/cm2, with line widths of 2.2–3.7 nm, demonstrating light confinement without a solid core. We identify shell continuity as a critical determinant for WGM feedback and lasing by exploring a morphological continuum of suprastructures comprising solid supraparticles, colloidosomes, and microporous hollow shells. Intact colloidosomes support narrow cavity modes, whereas porous shells remain broadband even at high pump fluence. We show that colloidosomes can be driven to rupture and release payload through well-defined pathways, including meniscus-driven capillary failure, uniform heating, and localized near-infrared activation, thereby configuring their optical response from cavity-defined lasing to broadband emission. These results establish QD colloidosomes as stimuli-responsive microlasers that couple optical-state switching and triggered release within a single self-assembled platform.

articles.title: Self-Dissociating Albumin Nanoclusters for Passive Lymph Node-Targeted Inverse Vaccination in a Rheumatoid Arthritis Model
articles.abstract: Engineering lymph node-targeted tolerogenic nanomaterials requires simultaneous antigen–drug coloading and efficient lymphatic transport. However, conventional biocompatible nanoparticles with static architectures often face a size-dependent trade-off: larger particles enable cargo coloading but drain inefficiently to lymph nodes, whereas smaller particles favor lymphatic transport but have limited cargo versatility. Here, a size-transformable, self-dissociating albumin nanocluster inverse vaccine is introduced to address this materials design trade-off. Citrullinated peptide antigens are conjugated to human serum albumin, and rapamycin (RAPA) is coloaded using ball-milling technology to generate 200–300 nm nanoclusters. After subcutaneous injection, the nanoclusters dissociate into sub-10 nm albumin-based units, enabling passive lymphatic transport and accumulation in draining lymph nodes while maintaining coordinated antigen–RAPA codelivery. In vitro mechanistic studies show that the nanoclusters induce a tolerogenic dendritic cell phenotype and promote antigen-specific immune regulation. In a collagen-induced arthritis mouse model, weekly administration attenuates synovial inflammation, humoral autoimmune responses, bone erosion, and cartilage degradation while expanding Foxp3+ regulatory T cells. These findings establish self-dissociation-mediated size transformation as a functional materials strategy for lymph node-targeted antigen-specific immune tolerance and tolerogenic nanomedicine.

articles.title: Unusual CD-ee Dependence in Self-Assembled Chiral Nanocomposites through Nanoparticle-Mediated Interactions
articles.abstract: Supramolecular self-assembly can produce a linear or a positive nonlinear CD versus enantiomeric excess (ee) relationship. Negative “racemate rules” behavior is rare. In this work, we report an unusual nonlinear CD-ee dependence in a coassembly system comprising chiral perylene diimide molecules and gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). In contrast to the linear majority-rules behavior observed for pure PDI molecules, the introduction of AuNPs induces a tendency toward heterochiral coaggregation, leading to a negative CD-ee correlation at low temperature (278 K) and a positive correlation at high temperature (318 K). Even both positive and negative CD-ee correlations can coexist and be tuned within a single self-assembling system. Combined molecular dynamics simulations and preassembly control experiments demonstrate that the nanoparticles reshape the chiral recognition pathway of PDI molecules through alkyl chain–chain van der Waals interactions, while the assembly temperature further modulates the majority-rules behavior. This work reveals a mechanism by which nanoparticles act as regulatory units in supramolecular chirality, offering a design strategy for programmable chiral materials.

articles.title: Vitamin E-Engineered Anti-Inflammatory Lipid Nanoparticles for Safer mRNA Delivery
articles.abstract: Great strides have been achieved in lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-mediated mRNA delivery. However, traditional LNPs can induce undesirable side effects such as inflammatory reactions. Oxidative stress damage arising from ionizable lipids within LNPs is regarded as a major underlying cause of these adverse effects. Herein, we propose incorporating endogenous vitamin E (VE) into the tail moiety of commercial ionizable lipids to improve biosafety. Proof-of-concept investigations using SM-102-derived W3 confirm that this endogenous antioxidant modification substantially mitigates the inflammatory toxicity of mRNA-loaded LNPs. Following intravenous administration, W3 LNPs markedly decrease the levels of multiple pro-inflammatory cytokines, demonstrating an improved safety profile compared to SM-102 LNPs. Further analysis reveals that W3 LNPs significantly reduce intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, alleviate oxidative stress damage, thereby inhibiting the activation of key inflammatory pathways such as NF-κB. Of note, the optimized formulation, sW3 LNPs enable efficient mRNA delivery to the spleen, with stronger antitumor efficacy and higher safety than SM-102 LNPs. In summary, W3 lipid confers minimal inflammatory adverse effects while preserving excellent delivery capability, which indicates that the VE-engineered LNPs possess great potential to serve as powerful and multifunctional platforms for next-generation mRNA therapeutics.

Anchoring LiZn Nanocrystals With Oligomer Binders for Enhanced Interfacial Stability in Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Lithium (Li) metal batteries have emerged as one of the most promising candidates for next‐generation energy storage systems due to the potentially high energy density. Nevertheless, repeated interfacial breakdown causes a short lifespan and poor safety. Inspired by the role of plant root systems in anchoring soil, an oligomer‐anchored LiZn nanocrystal composite interphase is constructed on the Li metal anode via a simple spray‐coating strategy, simultaneously enhancing the electrochemical stability and thermal safety of Li metal batteries. The LiZn alloy in the composite interphase restructures the interface energy distribution and reduces the local current density, thereby facilitating uniform lateral Li deposition. The oligomer serves as a binder to glue LiZn particles together and preserve the structural integrity of the interphase. A Li||LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 coin cell with the composite interphase exhibits a lifespan of 700 cycles at 1 C with a high cathode loading of 3.06 mAh cm−2. The 1.38 Ah Li||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 86% after 200 cycles. When the cycled pouch cells undergo forced thermal runaway, the composite interphase elevates the trigger temperature from 124°C to 191°C. This interphase design provides novel insights to enhance the service lifespan and thermal safety of high energy density batteries.

articles.title: Non‐Planar Chlorine‐Coordinated Activation of Triatomic Ruthenium Sites for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
articles.abstract: The intrinsic electronic structure of Ru-based catalysts exhibits strong adsorption of oxygen-containing intermediates, which runs counter to the adsorption requirements of the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), limiting their ability to achieve high activity. In this study, we employed a spatial confinement-pyrolysis strategy to develop a chlorine-doped triatomic Ru catalyst (Ru3ClNC), whose active center consists of a Ru3ON6Cl unit stabilized by both Ru─Ru bonds and Ru─N/O/Cl coordination bonds. Ru3ClNC delivers a high alkaline half-wave potential (E 1/2) of 0.90 V and an acidic E 1/2 of 0.79 V; the assembled zinc-air battery demonstrates excellent performance in terms of energy density and durability. In situ experiments and theoretical calculations have demonstrated the superiority of Ru3ON6Cl as the electrocatalytic ORR active site. The non-planar coordination effects and electronic effects of the Cl atom, in synergy with the triatomic site, disrupt the high symmetry, trigger charge redistribution, and significantly optimize the localized electron density at the active site. Importantly, the rearranged electronic structure breaks the linear scaling relationship in the d-band, enabling the catalyst to simultaneously optimize the rate-determining step of Ru3NC and OH* desorption, thereby enhancing reaction kinetics. This provides a new design concept for Ru-based catalysts to overcome the thermodynamic limitations and thereby improve the ORR activity.

articles.title: Rational Terminal‐Group Engineering of Guest Acceptors for 20.7% Efficient Organic Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Achieving higher efficiency in organic solar cells requires simultaneous control over energy-level alignment, acceptor aggregation, and active-layer crystallization. Herein, two guest acceptors, S-SMA and AS-SMA, were designed by stepwise replacing the fluorinated terminal group of L8-BO with a weaker electron-withdrawing 2-(3-ethyl-4-oxothiazolidin-2-ylidene)malononitrile (CN-Rh) unit. This terminal-group engineering upshifts the acceptor energy levels, enables cascade the lowest unoccupied molecular energy levels among D18, the guest acceptor, and L8-BO, and regulates blend morphology. In situ spectroscopic analysis reveals that both guest acceptors accelerate the liquid-to-solid transition during film formation and promote tighter molecular packing. Compared with symmetric S-SMA, asymmetric AS-SMA enables a more favorable morphology and device operation, as reflected by suitable domain sizes, suppressed trap-assisted recombination, and more balanced charge transport. Consequently, the ternary D18:L8-BO:AS-SMA device delivers the best overall photovoltaic performance, achieving a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.71% with an open-circuit voltage (V OC) of 0.930 V and a fill factor (FF) of 80.62%. These results demonstrate that asymmetric terminal-group engineering is an effective strategy for coordinating energy-level tuning, crystallization kinetics, and morphology optimization in high-performance ternary organic solar cells.

articles.title: Use of Biologics and Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors During Pregnancy in Patients with Systemic Autoimmune Diseases and Cancer
articles.abstract: Biologics and immune checkpoint inhibitors have transformed the treatment of autoimmune conditions and cancers. However, safety data regarding use during pregnancy are limited. Clinicians are left to weigh the potential benefits of treatment with frequently unknown risks to the pregnant patient and developing fetus. These therapies do not cross the placenta during the first trimester; thus, they are unlikely to cause teratogenicity. Use later in pregnancy has the potential to immunosuppress the neonate, which could lead to infection and inadequate vaccine response. These large molecules are minimally transferred into breastmilk and are mostly compatible with nursing.

articles.title: Differential Regulatory Activities of Potassium and Aldosterone in the Distal Nephron: A Resolution to the Aldosterone Paradox
articles.abstract: Aldosterone has long been viewed as a master regulator of fluid and electrolyte homeostasis, acting through the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) to stimulate electrogenic Na + transport via the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) in the distal nephron. This primary effect is thought to drive both K + secretion and Cl − reabsorption; however, the underlying mechanism has remained obscure and the dual regulation has generated an enigma often referred to as the aldosterone paradox. Here we propose a model for regulated K + secretion centered on local regulation of ENaC in the late distal convoluted tubule and early connecting tubule. In this segment, the MR is constitutively activated by glucocorticoids rather than by aldosterone, and yet ENaC activity and K + secretion through the renal outer medullary K + channel (ROMK) are not constitutive but, rather, are highly regulated. The model holds that the key regulatory step for K + secretion involves a cell-autonomous mechanism through which local interstitial [K + ] stimulates mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2)-dependent phosphorylation of the ENaC regulatory serum- and glucocorticoid-induced kinase 1 (SGK1); the K+-sensing kinase augments this phosphorylation by serving as a scaffold to enhance the physical interaction of mTORC2 with SGK1. Aldosterone acts further downstream to stimulate ENaC primarily in the late CNT and cortical collecting duct, in which ROMK apical expression is relatively low and Na + -Cl − reabsorption is favored. This revised paradigm resolves the aldosterone paradox and has important implications for hypertension, potassium disorders, and potentially medical therapies.

articles.title: What's Coming Up Next? The Physiology of Gastroparesis and GLP-1 Agonists
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is an incretin to regulate glycemia, activates peripheral and central neural pathways to control appetite, and inhibits upper gut transit to reduce food intake. Peptide and nonpeptide GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), as well as a combined GLP-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), agonist are approved for type 2 diabetes, weight reduction, and other indications. GLP-1RA therapy can be complicated by upper gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms, including nausea and vomiting. Delayed gastric emptying secondary to GLP-1RAs may be influenced by drug pharmacokinetics, associated neuropathy, and development of tachyphylaxis with repeated dosing. A theoretical risk of pulmonary aspiration from retained gastric contents is concerning for patients undergoing anesthesia before endoscopy or surgery. Managing upper GI complications of GLP-1RA therapy includes diet modifications, antiemetic medications, and treatments that stimulate gastric emptying. Newer agents in testing include nonpeptide GLP-1RAs and GLP-1RAs acting in concert with GIP, glucagon, or other receptor-mediated pathways.

Atomic-Scale Insights into Electron-Driven Ag Migration and Growth Across Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-8/Ag2SeO3 Interfaces: A Theoretical and Experimental Study
articles.abstract: The ZIF-8/Ag2SeO3 heterostructure was designed to combine the adsorption capacity and porous architecture of zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) with the multifunctional response of Ag2SeO3 (ASO), seeking synergistic interactions that could yield a material with enhanced, complementary functionalities. We report the synthesis and interfacial evolution of ZIF-8/ASO heterostructures and the in situ formation of metallic Ag nanoparticles (NPs) under electron irradiation. X-ray diffraction confirms the coexistence of cubic ZIF-8 (I43m) and monoclinic ASO (P21/c) phases, with a microstructure consisting of ZIF-8 NPs uniformly anchored on ASO microrods in intimate interfacial contact. Time-resolved electron microscopy directly captures the nucleation and growth of Ag NPs on the ZIF-8 surface during electron irradiation, as confirmed by HRTEM-SAED and elemental maps, indicating spatially confined cubic Ag NPs with exposed (111) and (200) planes. Photoluminescence measurements show pronounced emission quenching and spectral redistribution, indicating modified optoelectronic behavior following heterostructure formation. First-principles calculations identify the ZIF-8/ASO(010) interface as a favorable configuration, characterized by strong interfacial interaction and significant charge redistribution. These results are consistent with the experimentally observed localized formation of Ag NPs and suggest that interfacial electronic interactions contribute to Ag+ reduction. Overall, the ZIF-8/ASO heterostructure provides an electron-responsive platform for localized Ag NP formation and interfacial optoelectronic modulation, offering insights into electron-beam-induced processes in ZIF-8-based heterostructures.

articles.title: Descriptor Logic for Disorder in High-Entropy and Compositionally Complex Fluorite Oxides: A Critical Assessment
articles.abstract: No single scalar captures disorder in high-entropy and compositionally complex fluorites. This Perspective evaluates compositional and structural descriptors by physical meaning, reference frame, covariance, and transferability. Pairwise cation mismatch contains the same information as size variance, whereas host-referenced misfit adds a reference-dependent mean-radius offset. Analysis of twenty-four published compositions from three systematic datasets illustrates the limits of configurational entropy and size variance as independent descriptors of phase formation and transport. With equal Hf, Zr, and Ce fractions, changing the host reference reverses misfit rankings and alters the host-offset term up to 78-fold. In twelve dual-phase zirconates and mixed zirconate-hafnates, the nominal rA/rB ratio correlates with phase fraction but describes neither coexisting phase, whereas measured phase compositions give non-overlapping fluorite and pyrochlore values, distinguishing descriptor limitations from inappropriate evaluation frames. Structural observables are assessed by specificity, reproducibility, and relevance. Together, these criteria and the compositional analysis define a framework that distinguishes compositional inputs, multiplicity and crystal-chemical mismatch, from their structural realization. Its purpose is to test descriptor relevance and limits rather than predict untested compositions.

articles.title: Template-Guided Crystal Chemical Design of Eu2+-Activated La2Ca3[Si4N4O8] Oxonitridosilicate Phosphor
articles.abstract: Template-guided crystal-chemical design offers a route to oxonitridosilicates, but transfer of an oxide topology requires compatible cation coordination and charge balance. Here, we report the synthesis and structural characterization of the 6-ring host La2Ca3[Si4N4O8], designed by considering [SiN]+ for [AlO]+ substitution in the Ca3[Al2O6] template together with aliovalent La3+/Ca2+ substitution. The idealized structural description contains isolated rings of corner-sharing [SiN2O2] tetrahedra and partially occupied or vacant cation sites. The nominal substitution scheme, 3Ca2+ → 2La3+ + VCa, provides a charge-balanced crystal-chemical rationale for the cation deficiency. Theoretical calculations reveal that the aliovalent substitution induces cation vacancies accompanied by local charge redistribution and coordination rearrangement, which may alleviate the lattice strain arising from the cation-size mismatch. Eu2+ activation produces broadband orange emission centered near 600 nm, with a reported photoluminescence quantum yield of 29.3%. The phosphor was further applied to a white LED by combining it with multiple phosphors. This work illustrates how cation composition and occupancy can be considered alongside the topology in template-guided exploratory synthesis.

Leveraging AI-ECG Technology for Early Notification and Tracking of AF Development (LATENT): A Randomized Controlled Trial
articles.abstract: Electrocardiographic analysis aided by artificial intelligence (AI) may identify atrial electrical vulnerability during sinus rhythm. The objective of this study was to determine whether AI–enabled ECG (AI-ECG) is effective for detecting atrial fibrillation (AF), atrial flutter (AFl), or prespecified pre-AF atrial findings in a randomized trial. In this single-center, open-label trial, 14 665 adults 40 to 85 years of age without previous AF/AFl were randomized to an AI-ECG–guided strategy or usual care. Participants randomized to AI-ECG who were then identified by AI as having a high-risk sinus-rhythm ECG in the preceding year were offered Holter monitoring for ≤7 days. Each monitored high-risk intervention participant was paired with an age- and sex-matched control selected before control ECGs underwent AI analysis. Matched controls received identical monitoring to reduce ascertainment bias. Reporting cardiologists were blinded to AI results and randomized assignment. The primary outcome was a composite of newly detected AF, AFl, or pre-AF atrial findings within 90 days. Pre-AF atrial findings comprised frequent premature atrial complexes, short runs of premature atrial complexes, or nonsustained AF/AFl. Among 7337 intervention and 7328 control participants, 84 (1.1%) and 78 (1.1%), respectively, were classified as high risk. Of the 84 high-risk intervention participants, 48 (57.1%) underwent monitoring, as did 48 matched controls. The primary outcome occurred in 54 intervention participants (0.74%) versus 35 control participants (0.48%; odds ratio, 1.54 [95% CI, 1.01–2.37]; P =0.046). Hypothetical reclassification of 1 intervention event to a nonevent changed the primary analysis P value to 0.057. The intervention effect on detection of the primary composite outcome differed by baseline AI-ECG risk ( P interaction <0.001): 32.1% versus 2.6% among high-risk participants and 0.4% versus 0.5% among low-risk participants. AF/AFl detection (0.3% versus 0.2%) and antiarrhythmic therapy initiation at 180 days (2.3% versus 2.4%) did not differ significantly between the intervention and control groups. Participant-reported monitoring-related adverse events, including skin reactions and discomfort, occurred in 22.9% of monitored intervention participants versus 18.8% of matched controls. AI-ECG–guided monitoring resulted in a modest increase in the detection of new AF, AFl, or pre-AF atrial findings. However, these findings were fragile statistically and sensitive to reclassification of 1 event. LATENT (Leveraging AI-ECG Technology for Early Notification and Tracking of AF Development) demonstrates the clinical application of AI-ECG risk stratification to guide targeted rhythm surveillance, providing a foundation for larger trials evaluating its impact on patient outcomes. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT06847932.

articles.title: Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in Patients With Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease: ISCHEMIA-CKD EXTEND
articles.abstract: In the ISCHEMIA-CKD trial (International Study of Comparative Health Effectiveness With Medical and Invasive Approaches–Chronic Kidney Disease), at a median follow-up of 2.2 years, the primary composite outcome of death or nonfatal myocardial infarction was similar between an initial invasive strategy (INV) compared with an initial conservative strategy (CON) in patients with moderate or severe myocardial ischemia and advanced chronic kidney disease. However, the long-term outcomes comparing the 2 strategies are unknown. Participants in the ISCHEMIA-CKD trial were randomly assigned to either INV, involving coronary angiography and revascularization when feasible, added to guideline-directed medical therapy or to CON with guideline-directed medical therapy alone and invasive procedures reserved for failure of guideline-directed medical therapy. After the active intervention trial phase, long-term vital status follow-up was conducted through participant contact by participating sites and by health record and centralized death database searches. The primary outcome for the extended follow-up phase was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes were cause-specific mortality, including cardiovascular and noncardiovascular mortality. Among the 777 participants randomized (388 to INV and 389 to CON), over a median of 8 years of follow-up, vital status retention among survivors was 95%. There was a total of 429 deaths (55%). Cumulative all-cause mortality (57.4% versus 56.8%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.05 [95% CI, 0.87–1.28]) or cardiovascular mortality (40.3% versus 38.4%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.84–1.34]) at 8 years did not differ between INV and CON. The restricted mean survival time was 1941 days (1834–2047 days) for INV versus 1990 days (1885–2094 days) for CON, with an adjusted estimated difference of −99 days (−245 to 46). The posterior probability of at least a 1 percentage point lower or higher death with INV at the 8-year median follow-up was 28% and 52%, respectively. Similarly, the posterior probability of at least a 1 percentage point lower or higher cardiovascular mortality with INV was 23% and 56%, respectively. In patients with at least moderate ischemia and advanced chronic kidney disease, there was no significant long-term benefit of an initial INV at reducing the risk of all-cause or cardiovascular mortality compared with an initial conservative strategy. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT01985360

articles.title: Multimodality Cardiac Imaging Substudy of the DAPT-SHOCK-AMI Randomized Trial: Echocardiographic and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Assessment of Cangrelor versus Crushed Ticagrelor in Cardiogenic Shock Complicating Acute Myocardial Infarction
articles.abstract: Background: In acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), the myocardium sustains a dual injury: ischemia of the culprit territory and global hypoperfusion from low cardiac output. Whether platelet inhibition at reperfusion affects the microcirculation, the infarct, the noninfarcted myocardium, and ventricular function, and over what time course, has not been examined with serial imaging. The prespecified multimodality imaging substudy of the randomized DAPT-SHOCK-AMI trial (intravenous cangrelor versus crushed oral ticagrelor) addressed this question. Methods: Patients at prespecified imaging sites underwent serial echocardiography (208 enrolled; evaluable examinations in 175, 120, and 99 patients in the acute phase, at 1 month, and at 1 year) and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR; 93 enrolled; 73, 68, and 63); 81 patients (40 and 41) underwent both modalities. Blinded core laboratories analyzed all studies. The primary imaging endpoint was microvascular obstruction (MVO) on acute CMR, evaluable in 60 patients; secondary endpoints were infarct size, native T1 of the global, infarcted, and remote myocardium, left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e', and left atrial volume, and their changes. Comparisons between the cangrelor and crushed ticagrelor arms used covariate-adjusted logistic or linear regression; the substudy was not separately powered. Results: The odds of acute MVO were lower with cangrelor (adjusted odds ratio 0.27 [95% CI 0.08 to 0.98]; P=0.023). Infarct size did not differ between the arms. At 1 year, native T1 of the remote myocardium was lower with cangrelor (adjusted mean 1114 [95% CI 1057 to 1171] versus 1171 [1115 to 1228] ms; P=0.005). Over 1 year, LVEF increased more with cangrelor on echocardiography (37.9% versus 21.7% of the acute value; adjusted P=0.046) and CMR (15.8% versus 2.1%; P=0.027), with greater improvement in GLS, lower E/e', and less left atrial enlargement; no parameter differed between the arms at 1 month. Conclusions: In AMI-CS, serial multimodality imaging characterized microvascular, tissue-level, and functional injury over 1 year. Cangrelor was associated with less acute MVO, lower remote native T1, and more complete recovery of LV function than crushed ticagrelor, without a difference in infarct size; these hypothesis-generating findings suggest differences in the microcirculation and non-infarcted myocardial injury but do not establish a treatment mechanism.

articles.title: Statin–Ezetimibe Combination Therapy versus Statin Monotherapy in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: A Prespecified Secondary Analysis of the Randomized Ez-PAVE Trial
articles.abstract: In a target-directed low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C)–lowering strategy, the impact of the initial treatment regimen has not been investigated in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. We compared the efficacy and safety of initial statin–ezetimibe combination therapy versus statin monotherapy within intensive or conventional LDL-C–targeting strategies. In this prespecified second randomization of the randomized Ez-PAVE trial (Effects of Ezetimibe Combination Therapy for Patients With Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: Randomized Comparison of LDL Cholesterol Targeting <70 versus <55 mg/dL) conducted at 17 centers in South Korea, a total of 3048 patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were enrolled between January 2021 and July 2022. Following the first randomization to either an intensive (<55 mg/dL) or conventional (<70 mg/dL) LDL-C–targeting strategy, patients underwent subsequent randomization (initial statin–ezetimibe combination therapy [n=1525] versus statin monotherapy [n=1523]) and were followed up for 3 years. Lipid-lowering therapy was adjusted according to a predefined protocol to achieve LDL-C targets. The primary end point was a 3-year composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, any revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina. The mean±SD age was 64.4±9.0 years, and 638 patients (20.9%) were female. The incidence of the primary end point did not differ between statin–ezetimibe combination therapy (128 patients [8.5%]) and statin monotherapy (119 patients [7.9%]; hazard ratio, 1.07 [95% CI, 0.83–1.37]; P =0.596). Patients who received statin–ezetimibe combination therapy achieved lower median LDL-C levels during follow-up than those who received statin monotherapy in both the intensive-targeting (53 mg/dL [interquartile range, 45–62 mg/dL] versus 62 mg/dL [interquartile range, 53–74 mg/dL]) and conventional-targeting (63 mg/dL [interquartile range, 55–73 mg/dL] versus 70 mg/dL [interquartile range, 62–81 mg/dL]) strategies. During follow-up, ezetimibe was added to the treatment regimen of 241 patients (34.3%) and 177 patients (24.8%) who initially received statin monotherapy in the intensive- and conventional-targeting strategies, respectively. The treatment effect of intensive-targeting versus conventional-targeting strategies was consistent regardless of therapy regimens without significant heterogeneity ( P interaction =0.583). The safety end points were similar between the groups. Within a target-directed LDL-C–lowering strategy, cardiovascular efficacy and safety did not differ significantly, whether initiated as statin–ezetimibe combination therapy or as statin monotherapy, but combination therapy facilitated achievement of a lower LDL-C target. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT04626973.

articles.title: Genetic Structure of Harbour Seals Phoca vitulina vitulina Along the Coast of Norwegian Mainland: Implications for Management
articles.abstract: Alignment between biologically meaningful units and stock boundaries is one or the requirements for sustainable resource management. In Norway, harbour seals (Phoca vitulina vitulina) are managed at the county level and, when local populations are deemed sufficiently large to support harvesting, hunting is permitted under a quota corresponding to 5% of the counted individuals. An assessment of population structure along the entire Norwegian coastline based upon 16 microsatellites revealed significant overall differentiation (F ST = 0.036, p < 0.001) consistent with a pattern of Isolation by Distance, in agreement with the estimated effective migration surface (EEMS). Pairwise differentiation among sampling sites challenged the current stock outline. Specifically, (a) geographically large counties (e.g., Finnmark, Nordland) could warrant subdivision into smaller management units, whereas (b) no differentiation was detected across the four south-eastern counties (Agder, Vestfold, Telemark and Østfold). Positive and statistically significant spatial autocorrelation detected at distances of 0–300 km invoked larger genetical similarity than expected by chance and agreed with the fine-grained population structure revealed by former tagging studies. The absence of evidence for recent bottleneck events suggests that populations remain at mutation-drift equilibrium.

articles.title: Resolving the graphite compatibility boundary with an electrolyte-native anion 19F NMR descriptor
Soil Microbes Mediate Contrasting Effects of Plant Diversity on Biotic Resistance and Invasional Meltdown
articles.abstract: Biological invasions are intensifying worldwide as a major component of global change, with soil microbes increasingly recognized as key regulators of invasion outcomes. Yet how soil microbes interact with biodiversity to determine whether communities resist or facilitate invasion, particularly through their effects on plant growth and species interactions, remains unclear. Here, we conducted a two‐phase feedback experiment in which soils were conditioned across a diversity gradient of native or invasive plant communities. We characterized soil fungal communities and quantified microbial effects on plant growth and species interactions between phylogenetically paired native and invasive species. Biodiversity generated contrasting invasion outcomes depending on community origin, driven by distinct microbial pathways. In native‐conditioned soils, increasing diversity reduced invader dominance (biotic resistance), primarily mediated by microbial effects on interspecific competition that enhanced native competition strength while reducing that of invaders. In contrast, in invasive‐conditioned soils, increasing diversity facilitated invader dominance (invasional meltdown), primarily driven by enhanced invader growth and suppression of natives. These patterns were associated with shifts in key microbial groups. Putative pathogen richness increased with increasing plant diversity and was negatively associated with native growth, whereas AMF richness declined with increasing plant diversity in native communities but increased with increasing plant diversity in invasive communities, promoting invader growth and competition strength. By integrating biodiversity‐ecosystem functioning, biotic resistance, invasional meltdown, and competitive interactions within a plant–soil feedback framework, our study advances invasion ecology. It identifies soil microbes as central mediators that link biodiversity to ecosystem invasibility through distinct pathways affecting plant growth and species interactions.

Divergent associations of plant functional composition and species richness with above‐ and below‐ground multitrophic organization in a desert steppe
articles.abstract: In a desert‐steppe biodiversity experiment, legume biomass proportion was associated mainly with leaf‐trait reorganization, whereas species richness showed more consistent associations with nematode faunal indices and footprint metrics. Measured leaf traits differed in predictive importance between herbivore feeding guilds. Positive associations between piercing‐sucking insect abundance and selected nematode indicators suggested a potential connection between above‐ground and below‐ground communities. Abstract Plant functional composition and species richness may be associated with different aspects of above‐ and below‐ground communities. Distinguishing these relationships is important for understanding how biodiversity‐related patterns extend across trophic levels. However, their respective associations with plant traits, herbivore feeding guilds and below‐ground food webs remain unclear in resource‐limited desert steppes. We sampled 64 plots during the fourth growing season of a desert‐steppe biodiversity experiment. We examined associations of realized legume biomass proportion and plant species richness with community‐weighted plant traits, chewing and piercing‐sucking herbivores, and nematode faunal indices and footprint metrics derived from relative sequence composition. Analyses combined joint regressions, direct feeding‐guild comparisons, random‐forest analyses and theory‐informed piecewise structural equation modelling. Higher legume biomass proportion was associated with lower community‐weighted leaf mass per area and higher density‐normalized leaf punch strength and trichome density. Several plant traits showed relatively high predictive importance for chewing insects but consistently low importance for piercing‐sucking insects. However, the direct mixed‐effects comparison did not detect a significant difference between guild‐specific responses to legume biomass proportion. Plant species richness was positively associated with the nematode structure and enrichment indices and negatively associated with the composite footprint metric (MF), whereas legume biomass proportion showed no significant conditional associations with these measures. Piercing‐sucking insect abundance was positively correlated with the herbivore footprint metric after multiple‐testing correction and showed positive conditional associations with the nematode structure index and MF in the piecewise SEM. Synthesis. Legume biomass proportion was linked primarily to above‐ground leaf‐trait reorganization, whereas plant species richness showed more consistent associations with below‐ground nematode faunal organization. Piercing‐sucking insect abundance showed positive associations with the nematode structure index and the composite and herbivore footprint metrics, suggesting a potential cross‐realm connection involving this feeding guild. Together, these findings indicate that plant functional composition, species richness and consumer feeding guilds represent different but connected dimensions of multitrophic organization in resource‐limited grasslands.
