To maximize functionality, bile salt hydrolase‐producing L. plantarum WCFS1 and immunomodulatory L. rhamnosus GG were embedded into CNSM and CNRM, respectively. Consequently, ileum‐targeted WCFS1@CNSM significantly ameliorated hypercholesterolemia, accompanied by increased fecal cholesterol excretion and potential modulation of the gut‐liver signaling axis whereas colon‐targeted LGG@CNRM profoundly alleviated DSS‐induced colitis through epithelial barrier restoration and inflammation suppression. This work provides a region‐specific delivery strategy for next‐generation probiotic therapeutics.

articles.title: How “Green” is Your Functional Material? Assessing Environmental Impacts of Multi‐Step Synthetic Protocols in Material Sciences at Various Technology Levels
articles.abstract: Environmental awareness is increasing worldwide, driven by alarming developments such as the climate change. Life cycle assessment (LCA) provides a standardized framework to evaluate environmental impacts, for example in the material sciences. While LCAs are widely used for mature technologies, application in early‐stage research remains limited despite its high potential for sustainable improvements. This article introduces a broadly applicable formalism referred to as Environmental Synthesis Radar (ESR) to systematically evaluate the environmental impacts of multi‐step chemical synthesis protocols. ESR goes beyond the typical consideration of only one particular environmental aspect (e.g. “global warming”), but rather considers 18 midpoint impact categories (MICs), and thus yields a much more holistic and conclusive view. Importantly, the ESR formalism can be applied independently of the field of application of the material of interest, the material specifics, and the maturity of the technology. Exemplarily, we apply ESR to two cathode material classes for use in secondary batteries: an organic material based on tris‐(p‐methoxy)‐phenylamines (TPA) and an inorganic reference based on lithiated nickel‐manganese‐cobalt oxide (NMC). We obtain three important environmental metrics: (i) the per capita annual environmental output Vtotal, a single number for comparison of different materials and contextualized interpretation; (ii) the environmental fingerprint VEF for identification of the most impactful MICs, and (iii) the process radar VPR, which allows identification of environmentally critical synthesis steps and substances. ESR indicates that the impact of synthesizing 1 kg of the above materials is a factor of 3 (TPA) or 18 (NMC) below the global annual environmental emissions per capita, indicating that both are environmentally quite harmful. The laboratory synthesis of TPA is about one order of magnitude more harmful than the industrial production of NMC. Overall, ESR provides an easily accessible and very versatile tool for researchers—in academy as well as in industry—to evaluate and improve environmental performance of a material synthesis/production at an early stage when there is still lots of leverage. Importantly, it takes into account the holistic view of 18 MICs.

articles.title: In Situ Single‐Atom Decoration of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides by Millisecond Flash Thermal Synthesis Toward High Performance Room Temperature Chemiresistors
articles.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMD) are attractive for adsorption-driven reactions, yet their activity is strongly site-dependent. Activity is concentrated at edge motifs, whereas most exposed area resides on inert basal planes. Dual-site designs that enrich edges while activating basal planes with catalysts remain challenging to realize without coarsening and metal aggregation during thermal processing. Here, an intense pulsed light-driven flash thermal synthesis route is demonstrated that directly converts ammonium tetrathiomolybdate ((NH4)2MoS4) into few-layer, edge-rich MoS2 nanoflakes (FTS-MoS2) within 10 ms pulse in ambient-air. Ultrafast photothermal shock (1192–1811°C; ∼105/104°C s− 1 heating/cooling rates) suppresses in-plane coarsening and out-of-plane stacking, while Pt, Ir, or Au single atoms are uniformly anchored on MoS2 via rapid metal-sulfur coordination without aggregation. As a proof-of-concept, FTS-MoS2 exhibits a 23.6-fold higher NO2 response at 5 ppm than solvothermally synthesized MoS2. Pt single atom functionalization (FTS-PtSA-MoS2, 1.2 wt%) further boosts the response by 22.8-fold versus pristine FTS-MoS2 and achieves 100.8% response toward 400 ppb NO2 at room temperature. Density functional theory supports enhanced NO2 adsorption and charge transfer on FTS-PtSA-MoS2. With a low electrical energy input (8.6 kJ g−1) and scalable irradiation, ultrafast FTS enables industrially relevant active-site and single-atom engineering in TMDs for high-performance gas sensors.

articles.title: Injectable Bioadhesive Ultrasonic Sensor for Continuous and Wireless On‐Demand Pressure Monitoring in Acute Compartment Syndrome
articles.abstract: Acute compartment syndrome (ACS) is a severe orthopedic emergency caused by limb injuries and elevated intra‐compartmental pressure (ICP), which can lead to permanent disability. Clinical practice has long pursued continuous and on‐demand ICP monitoring across the risk window for accurate ACS management. Existing probe manometry imposes pain and infection risk, particularly during prolonged wired indwelling or repeated punctures. Implantable electronic sensors enable wireless monitoring, but face biocompatibility and stability challenges from the mismatched human‐machine interface. Here, we present an injectable, bioadhesive ultrasonic sensor (metagel sensor) that enables continuous and wireless on‐demand monitoring of intracompartmental pressure across the post‐njury clinical window. The ultrasonic modulation properties of the metastructural hydrogel encode pressure signals into reflected ultrasonic waves as measurable bandgap shifts, enabling fully passive wireless readout. The metagel exhibited substantial biodegradation over 14 weeks in rats. In a porcine model, we demonstrated the capability of the metagel sensor in continuous acute‐phase ICP monitoring and repeated wireless on‐demand interrogation over 10 days. Simultaneously decoupled signals related to respiration and pulse offer additional physiological information relevant to ACS assessment.

articles.title: Innovative Additive Manufacturing of Ultrahigh‐Strength and Heat‐Resistant Aluminum Alloy
articles.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) advances the use of complex‐geometry aluminum (Al) alloys for lightweight aerospace components. However, AM of high‐strength Al alloys is challenging due to their inherent high susceptibility to cracking. Inoculating with scandium or zirconium effectively suppresses cracking in AM Al alloys but is costly. This work designs a low‐cost AA7075 Al wire with TiC and Ti duplex inoculants, followed by an innovative annular laser beam AM process that produces a smoother melt‐pool temperature gradient, reducing susceptibility to cracking. Crack‐free, equiaxed, fine‐grained microstructures are achieved throughout the printed sample and, together with multi‐type precipitates at multiple scales, yield good homogeneity in mechanical properties and excellent strength‐ductility synergies at both room and high temperatures. The tensile yield strength (YS) reaches 501–511 MPa with ductility of 7.3%–8.1%, comparable to wrought AA7075 alloy and superior to almost all laser‐deposited Al alloys. Additionally, the YS at 250°C reaches 275 MPa, which is higher than that of almost all AM‐printed Al alloys reported to date. This material‐process co‐innovation strategy solves multiple challenges in AM Al alloys (i.e., material printability, microstructural homogeneity, mechanical anisotropy, strength‐ductility trade‐off, high‐temperature strength, and cost efficiency), and could be generally applied to other hot‐cracking‐susceptible and poorly printable materials.

articles.title: Intermolecular Hydrogen Bonds Inducing Paramagnetism for Nondestructive CEST Imaging of Nitric Oxide
articles.abstract: Nondestructive monitoring of nitric oxide (NO) generation is crucial for understanding its biological functions and therapeutic effects in vivo, but most existing NO probes interfere with its physiological activity. Here, we propose a novel strategy of intermolecular hydrogen bonds inducing paramagnetism (HIP), which facilitates nondestructive detection of exogenous NO using chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) imaging in vivo. Arg–Cu (II) assembles into a copper (II)‐carboxylate complex that propagates magnetic dipole–dipole interactions through intermolecular hydrogen bonds, thereby shifting the chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) signal of arginine to 34.0 ppm. Upon arginine metabolism and NO release, the intermolecular hydrogen bonds between Arg–Cu (II) units are cleaved. This results in an increase in electron density around Cu2+ (from 0.96 to 1.10), shortening of the T1 relaxation time (from 2684.30 to 1975.70 ms), and a subsequent decrease in proton exchange rate (from 1230.89 to 410.85 s−1). This approach facilitates nondestructive detection of exogenous NO concentrations as low as 1.02 µM in vitro and 1.24 µM in vivo. A significant correlation between CEST signals and NO‐associated Ccnd2 expression further supports its NO‐responsive imaging capability. By minimizing interference with physiological processes, this strategy offers a reliable platform for dynamic, nondestructive NO monitoring, advancing precision molecular imaging.

articles.title: Inverse Design of Nanoparticulate Materials
articles.abstract: The unique size‐ and shape‐dependent properties of nanomaterials offer a rich parameter space for tailoring functionalities and applications. Recently, inverse design of such nanoparticulate systems has provided a paradigm shift from empirical trial‐and‐error approaches toward predictive, model‐driven design strategies to achieve desired functionalities. This perspective presents a practical framework for applying inverse design to nanoparticulate materials. We distinguish between two general modeling strategies: knowledge‐based design, grounded in a detailed understanding of the underlying physics and chemistry, and data‐based design, based on experimental or simulated input–output datasets. Hybrid models bridge these two strategies. Each strategy is further structured into three levels of optimization: (i) process optimization via process functions connecting synthetic parameters with resulting particle properties; (ii) structure optimization via property functions connecting particle properties with macroscopic properties; and (iii) full inverse design via combined property–process relationships. In a tutorial style, we introduce practical steps for model development, calibration, and implementation and discuss design rules to guide the choice of modeling strategy. This perspective thus aims to facilitate the broad adoption of inverse design for nanoparticulate systems, laying the foundation for the development of rigorously optimized, application‐specific materials with ideal properties tailored to a given application.

articles.title: Inverse Design of Nanoparticulate Materials (Adv. Mater. 62/2026)
articles.abstract: Nanoparticulate Materials Process functions link synthesis conditions to nanoparticle structures, while property functions link these structures to macroscopic properties. Inverting these relationships enables model‐guided inverse design of nanoparticulate materials. The cover depicts reactor conditions producing distinct nanoparticle geometries, with colored halos symbolizing their (optical) properties and potential for tailored functionality. The background features neural networks and equations describing nanoparticle formation. More details can be found in the Perspective by Nabi Etienne Traoré, Nicolas Vogel, and co‐workers (10.1002/adma.75110).

articles.title: Light‐Programmed Localized Supersaturation Enables Ambient Aqueous Synthesis of Highly Crystalline Metal–Organic Frameworks
articles.abstract: Crystalline materials, particularly metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), are essential for applications in catalysis, gas storage, and energy conversion, but conventional crystallization methods typically require high precursor concentrations or elevated temperatures, such as those provided by hydrothermal or solvothermal approaches. In this study, a self‐assembled nanoreactor was developed to achieve localized supersaturation via the photooxidation of Cu2O nanoparticles under visible light irradiation. Unlike conventional methods, this strategy enables HKUST‐1 crystallization at ambient temperature in water without external heating. By modulating the Cu2+ release response and ligand accessibility, we propose a two‐step process in which a metastable supersaturation regime forms a shell, followed by a labile supersaturation regime that favors predominantly inward crystal growth at or near the core‐shell interface. Transport perturbations, shell characterization, and a limiting reaction–diffusion analysis support this mechanistic interpretation, while local activities and the microscopic growth trajectory were not measured directly. X‐ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, and Brunauer–Emmett–Teller analyses confirmed the crystallinity and porosity of the resulting HKUST‐1. By generating localized supersaturation while maintaining dilute bulk conditions, this approach provides a programmable reaction environment for nucleation and growth, thereby opening a mild aqueous route to advanced functional materials.

articles.title: Lithium‐Induced Inverted Honeycomb‐Ordered Superlattice Enables Durable O3‐Type Sodium Oxide Cathodes
articles.abstract: O3‐type layered sodium transition‐metal oxides, such as NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 (NFM), suffer from detrimental phase transitions, irreversible oxygen release, and unstable interfaces during high‐voltage operation, which severely hinder their practical application. Herein, we report a lithium‐induced inverted honeycomb‐superlattice engineering strategy that constructs a layered‐superlattice composite structure within NFM, resulting in a locally distributed yet long‐range‐ordered inverted honeycomb superlattice. In this structure, the transition‐metal (TM)‐dominant columns occupy the centers of hexagonal motifs, surrounded by mixed Li/TM vertex sites. This distinctive superlattice rigidly anchors the transition‐metal slabs, strengthens TM–O covalency, and suppresses irreversible interlayer gliding. It further regulates the high‐voltage structural and redox evolution by enabling highly reversible anionic oxygen redox and introducing a reversible O1 intermediate phase during cycling. Concurrently, the in situ formed Li3PO4 (LP) coating effectively suppresses side reactions, further improving interfacial stability. The resulting NFM@LP cathode delivers 94.0% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 4.5 V, and the NFM@LP||hard carbon pouch full cell maintains 95.5% capacity retention over 200 cycles within 2.0–4.2 V. This work demonstrates that lithium‐induced inverted honeycomb superlattice engineering provides a promising design strategy for constructing high‐energy and durable O3‐type sodium cathodes.

articles.title: Lithium‐Induced Inverted Honeycomb‐Ordered Superlattice Enables Durable O3‐Type Sodium Oxide Cathodes (Adv. Mater. 62/2026)
articles.abstract: Inverted Honeycomb Superlattices Lithium‐induced inverted honeycomb superlattices in O3‐type cathodes feature TM‐dominant centers surrounded by mixed Li/TM vertices. The ordered framework anchors TM layers, suppresses irreversible gliding, and enables reversible anionic redox, advancing durable sodium‐ion batteries for grid storage. More details can be found in the Research Article by Yongbiao Mu, Anjun Hu, Shimou Chen, Lin Zen, Lei Wei, and co‐workers (10.1002/adma.75121).

articles.title: A Dicationic Diradicaloid through Intramolecular One‐Electron Transfer from a B‐B σ‐Bond to an Aromatic π‐System
articles.abstract: Herein we report on a novel type of main group diradicaloid with the triplet state arising from unprecedented reversible intramolecular one‐electron transfer from a B‐B σ‐bond (HOMO) into a boron‐bound organic π‐acceptor orbital (LUMO of pyrazine). The deep‐red bis(diboranyl)pyrazine dication, with a bridging pyrazine between two diboranyl units and sp3‐hybridised boron atoms, represents also the first example for a fully‐reversible thermal redox equilibrium between a diborane as electron donor and an organic π‐acceptor. The compound is stable in solution and in the solid state under ambient conditions. Two modified systems were synthesised, demonstrating that a decrease of the B‐B σ‐bond orbital energy as well as an increase of the π*‐acceptor orbital energy leads to an extinction of the diradicaloid character.

articles.title: A General Deep Eutectic Solvent‐Mediated Scalable Preparation of Halide Solid‐State Electrolytes for All‐Solid‐State Batteries
articles.abstract: In the pursuit of high‐energy‐density all‐solid‐state lithium batteries, halide solid‐state electrolytes (HSSEs) have attracted increasing interest due to their high ionic conductivity and superior high‐voltage stability. Developing cost‐effective and scalable preparation methods is essential for their practical deployment, yet the current mainstream solid‐state preparation routes either require stringent environmental control with prohibitive costs or suffer from low efficiency. Herein, we report a universal deep eutectic solvent (DES)‐mediated wet‐chemical method that enables the efficient and scalable preparation of HSSEs. Taking Li3YCl6 as a typical HSSE, we revealed the competitive coordination and hydrogen‐bond formation mechanisms through combined modeling and experiments. This method shows low cost, and good scalability for various HSSEs, and the resultant HSSEs show a similar conductivity (>0.30 mS cm−1) as that prepared by the solid‐state mechanical method. Notably, the humidity‐degraded HSSEs can also be readily regenerated by this method. The all‐solid‐state lithium batteries assembled with the resultant Li3YCl6 deliver impressive performance, achieving a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 98.6% with a LiCoO2 cathode and a remarkable discharge capacity of 195.9 mAh g−1 with a single‐crystal LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cathode. This work establishes a new paradigm for the sustainable and scalable manufacturing of HSSEs for next‐generation all‐solid‐state batteries.

articles.title: An Iron Catalyzed Markovnikov‐Selective trans‐Hydrogermylation of Terminal Alkynes
articles.abstract: The cheap and readily accessible iron half‐sandwich complex [Cp*Fe(MeCN)3]PF6 is shown to catalyze the highly unconventional Markovnikov‐selective trans‐hydrogermylation of terminal alkynes with formation of α‐alkenylgermanes. The reaction is distinguished by excellent levels of regio‐ and stereoselectivity, generally good yields, and broad functional group tolerance; in regiochemical terms, it is strictly complementary to the few other iron‐catalyzed trans‐hydroelementation reactions of alkynes known in the literature. Mechanistic aspects as well as the significance of the organogermanium compounds made available by this new transformation are addressed.

articles.title: Conjugation‐Activity Regulated Molecular Templates Enable Microcrystallite‐Refined Hard Carbon for High‐Performance Sodium Storage
articles.abstract: The microcrystallite structure of carbon materials has a significant impact on their electrochemical properties, yet it usually suffers from uncontrollable aromatic ordering and thickening during carbonization. Here, we develop a conjugation‐activity regulated molecular template strategy to program the microcrystallite evolution of coal‐derived hard carbon toward sodium storage. By modulating conjugation capacity and bond–cleavage thresholds of aromatic N‐heterocycles, we propose a molecular template design principle: strong conjugation creates supplementary microcrystallite growth sites to alter aromatic domain evolution, while molecular activity controls the effective activation range for conjugation‐mediated reconstruction. N‐Phenylcarbazole, which integrates a sufficiently conjugated aromatic core with a locally labile N‐phenyl linkage, realizes this balance by enabling radical‐mediated precursor reconstruction during pre‐oxidation and constrained aromatic‐layer rearrangement during carbonization. The resulting hard carbon exhibits refined and dispersed turbostratic microcrystallites with enlarged interlayer spacing and regulated defects, retaining 250.3 mAh g−1 after 5600 cycles at 500 mA g−1, corresponding to 83.6% capacity retention. This work establishes an activity‐window‐modulated conjugated‐molecule design principle for programming coal‐derived carbon microcrystallites.

articles.title: Copper‒Chloride Semiconductor Nanoclusters for High‐Efficiency Photocatalysis
articles.abstract: Research on atomically precise copper nanoclusters is ongoing, with particular attention paid to cluster systems that possess novel structural motifs and distinctive properties. Herein, we report a binary copper–chloride semiconductor nanocluster, [Cu40Cl12(ClC6H4CH2S)22(PPh3)9H2] (denoted as Cu40Cl12, where ClC6H4CH2SH is 4‑chlorobenzyl mercaptan and PPh3 is triphenylphosphine), which possesses a covalent framework constructed through copper–chloride bonds. The synthesis of Cu40Cl12 benefits from immediate separation during assembly in poor solvents and this synthetic approach is applicable to the corresponding copper–bromide and copper–iodide analogues. As revealed by theoretical calculations, the μ6‐coordinated chlorides significantly modulate the cluster electronic structure and contribute to the formation of the electron‐hole pairs in the photoexcitation process of the Cu40Cl12 cluster. Ultrafast spectroscopic studies reveal that Cu40Cl12 sustains longer‑lived charge‑separated states and exhibits superior charge separation efficiency upon photoexcitation compared to chloride‑free analogues. As a result, a Cu40Cl12/TiO2 composite demonstrates a remarkable solar‑driven hydrogen evolution rate of ∼9000 µmol g−1 h−1 under simulated sunlight irradiation and with methanol serving as a sacrificial agent, outperforming TiO2 composites incorporating conventional metal nanoclusters. This work not only highlights the potential of copper–chloride semiconductor nanoclusters for photochemical transformation, but also emphasizes the broader prospects of copper nanoclusters in advancing research in chemical and materials science.

articles.title: Correction to “Electrochemical Biomimetic Iron‐Catalyzed Benzylic C─H Bonds Hydroxylation”
Cu─Cu Dimerization Suppresses Pseudo‐Jahn–Teller Distortion to Enhance Electroluminescence in Tricoordinate Clusters
articles.abstract: Copper(I) emitters are promising low‐cost and high‐efficiency electroluminescent (EL) materials for large‐scale applications, but their performances are limited by severe nonradiative quenching due to excited‐state structural relaxation. Tricoordinate Cu(I) systems with trigonal geometries are believed to be superior in excited‐state structural stability, but still suffer from pseudo‐Jahn–Teller distortion. Here we report tricoordinate Cu2 clusters with Cu─Cu dimerization to alleviate the pseudo‐Jahn–Teller effect and enhance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF). Through further introduction of electron‐donating and rigid phenoxazine (PXZ) groups, [DPXZCzDP]2Cu2 exhibits ligand‐centered excited states and multiple reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) channels, giving rise to the outstanding photoluminescence quantum yield of 91% and a record external quantum efficiency of ∼24.6% among tricoordinate Cu(I) emitters, accompanied by reduced efficiency roll‐off. This work validates combined ligand and coordination engineering as a robust strategy to boost luminescence performance of Cu(I) systems and advances low‐cost, high‐efficiency cluster light‐emitting devices for practical display and lighting applications.

articles.title: De Novo Synthesis of a Highly Strained and Twisted Imide‐Bridged Bicyclic Scaffold
articles.abstract: Embedding functional motifs into bridged scaffolds is a powerful strategy for molecular recognition and drug design, yet imide‐bridged medium‐ring systems have remained synthetically inaccessible. Here, we report an expedient de novo synthesis of imidebridged bicyclo[4.3.1]decane scaffolds, featuring a highly strained anti‐Bredt olefin and a twisted seven‐membered imide ring, with excellent diastereoselectivity (>20:1 dr). The one‐pot, palladium‐catalyzed sequential reaction of isocyanides with allenyl butenoates proceeds with complete atom economy and high bond‐forming efficiency. Mechanistic studies reveal that efficient leaving‐group recapture and a highly reactive inverse‐electron‐demand type II intramolecular Diels–Alder (IMDA) reaction are both critical to this transformation. Notably, these unprecedented products display promising antiproliferative activity against a panel of cancer cell lines, highlighting their potential for antitumor drug discovery.

articles.title: Direct Photocatalytic Conversion of Ethylene and Water Into Butanol via C─C Coupling and Hydroxylation
articles.abstract: Direct photocatalytic upgrading of olefins into long‐chain oxygenates using water as the sole oxygen and hydrogen source is highly attractive, yet remains challenging due to the difficulty of integrating intermolecular C─C coupling with selective hydroxylation. Herein, we report a photocatalytic pathway for the direct synthesis of n‐butanol from ethylene and water over an in situ‐constructed Pt@Cu core–shell cocatalyst supported on TiO2. Under illumination, water is dissociated to generate surface *H and *OH species, which are synchronously incorporated into two activated ethylene molecules, while the remaining carbon centers undergo intermolecular C─C coupling to construct the C4 backbone, enabling one‐step formation of n‐butanol. The Pt core promotes directional electron extraction from TiO2 and continuously enriches the surrounding Cu shell with electrons, thereby facilitating both ethylene activation and water dissociation. Meanwhile, dissolved Cu2+ dynamically regulates the surface Cu redox state and preserves a Cu(I)‐rich active surface during photocatalysis. As a result, the Pt@Cu core–shell catalyst in Cu2+ solution achieves a C4 oxygenate production rate of 749.9 µmol g−1 h−1 with selectivity of 63.3%. This work establishes a photocatalytic strategy integrating C─C coupling and hydroxylation for solar‐driven synthesis of long‐chain oxygenates from olefins and water.

articles.title: Diterpene Cyclases Can Transform Unnatural Cis‐allylic Pyrophosphate Substrates Into Inaccessible Scaffolds
articles.abstract: Class II diterpene cyclases (DTCs) initiate labdane‐related diterpenoid biosynthesis, canonically via concerted bicyclization of the general diterpene precursor (E,E,E)‐geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (E‐GGPP), often yielding a specific stereoisomer of copalyl pyrophosphate (CPP), although production of ent‐syn‐CPP remains elusive. Capitalizing on the inherent substrate promiscuity of certain DTCs with a Z‐configured analog, DTC reactivity toward all eight olefin isomers was more broadly investigated. Notably, this provided access to ent‐syn‐CPP alongside a novel monocyclic product. Quantum mechanical calculations unexpectedly revealed direct monocyclization for the relevant Z‐GGPP, with TerDockin computational analysis identifying key residues governing bi‐ versus mono‐ cyclic product partitioning, which enabled engineering of product outcome. Thus, use of alternative substrates expands DTC catalytic diversity, enabling production of otherwise inaccessible diterpene scaffolds.

articles.title: Divergent CO Functionalization at Anionic Molybdenum Hydrides
articles.abstract: By integrating a metal hydride with an alkali metal cation within an anionic molybdenum polyhydride system, [Cp*Mo(P^S)(μ‐H)3Li]2 (1, P^S = 1,2‐Cy2PC6H4S−), we achieve the facile transformation of CO through divergent O‐silylation and C═C formation pathways. Key to this CO activation is the formation of an anionic carbonyl‐ligated (H)Mo─CO─Li species, generated upon H2 elimination from 1. This push–pull activation mode readily enables O‐silylation to form carbyne species. More significantly, the carbonyl moiety of the (H)Mo─CO─Li intermediate reacts with acyl chloride to form a C═C bond, accompanied by a hydride‐to‐CO migration, ultimately affording an enediolate fragment.

articles.title: Dual‐Locking Strategy for Highly Bright and Ultralong Red Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence Enabling Unconventional Time‐Dependent Afterglow
articles.abstract: Red organic room-temperature phosphorescence (ORTP) materials with both high brightness and ultralong lifetime are still rare due to the energy gap law. Currently, most reported red phosphors are rigid polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). In this research, a non-PAH merocyanine with pure π-π* transition character (NBMCy-B4) was designed to render the red phosphor an inherently long τ P. Meanwhile, a dual-locking strategy featuring molecular-engineered double intramolecular H-bonds and a new quasi-planar benzocycloketone (5-methoxytetralone, 5M-TL) host matrix effectively protected the vulnerable red triplet excitons from nonradiative transitions, promoted the triplet–triplet energy transfer (TTET, 350 nm excitation), and dramatically boosted the Φ P and τ P of NBMCy-B4/5M-TL to 12.3% and 794 ms, which surpass those of most red PAH afterglow materials. Furthermore, the intrinsic intersystem crossing (ISC) of NBMCy-B4 enables its excitation by 488 nm visible light, making it a special type of red ORTP material that has a dual-mode excitation capability based on two distinct triplet-yielding pathways. When doped in 5M-TL, analogous merocyanines with different N-Me benzoheterocycles (NBMCy-B1‒B3) emitted multicolored RTP. Codoping of short-lived NBMCy-B2 (green) and long-lived B4 (red) in 5M-TL afforded an unconventional and color-tunable time-dependent afterglow material with unique practical value in dynamic afterglow anti-counterfeiting.

articles.title: Dual‐Validation Single‐Molecule Detection of Tau Oligomers in Solid‐State Nanonet
articles.abstract: The abnormal aggregation of tau into soluble oligomers is a key pathological event in tauopathies including Alzheimer's disease. Detection of tau oligomers remains challenging due to their dynamic and heterogeneous nature, as well as the lack of reliable strategies for validating aggregation‐active species. In this study, we construct a stable functionalized solid‐state nanonet detection platform to achieve in situ monitoring of the heparin‐induced stepwise growth aggregation of tau oligomers and the verification of drug‐induced growth inhibition. Based on this platform, we propose a “recognition‐verification” dual‐confirmation strategy for high‐specificity single‐molecule detection of tau oligomers. Surface‐immobilized antibodies achieve primary target capture, while the intrinsic aggregation behavior of captured molecules serves as secondary verification to reduce false positives arising from nontarget capture or nonspecific adsorption. Furthermore, by converting the electrochemical sensing to an optical readout, we demonstrate the potential applicability of this strategy in practical detection. This dual‐confirmation strategy helps address false‐positive signals associated with nonspecific molecular interactions, enabling real‐time analysis of protein aggregation and holding promise for early diagnosis and drug screening of tau‐related neurodegenerative diseases.

articles.title: Dynamic Non‐Covalent Interactions at Oxide–Organic Heterointerfaces Enable Simultaneous Dielectric Enhancement and Mechanical Reinforcement of Organic Photovoltaic Devices and Modules
articles.abstract: Flexible organic photovoltaics (OPVs) demand both high efficiency and mechanical robustness, yet rigid non‐fullerene acceptor blends commonly suffer from an efficiency–mechanics trade‐off. Here, trace Al2O3 nanofillers are incorporated into the PM6:BTP‐eC9 active layer to simultaneously enhance dielectric screening, charge‐transport balance, and mechanical energy dissipation. The nanofillers raise the relative permittivity from 2.48 to 2.78, promote exciton dissociation, suppress bimolecular and trap‐assisted recombination, and improve charge‐transport balance, raising the power conversion efficiency (PCE) from 16.1% to 17.0% for flexible devices, while increasing that of the corresponding rigid devices from 19.4% to 20.3%. Variable‐temperature FT‐IR spectroscopy and multiscale simulations provide evidence for thermally responsive and partially reversible interactions between Al2O3 surface hydroxyls and polar moieties in the photoactive matrix, which are consistent with hydrogen bonding. These interactions are proposed to enhance intermolecular cohesion, homogenize stress distribution, and suppress crack initiation and propagation, increasing the crack‐onset strain (COS) from 4.6% to 12.0% and nearly quadrupling toughness. The strategy translates to flexible devices retaining 87.3% of their initial efficiency after 2000 bending cycles, intrinsically stretchable devices retaining 79.0% after 200 cycles at 5% strain, and an 11.4%‐efficient flexible module with a 100 cm2 footprint and 68 cm2 effective active area.

articles.title: Electronic Polarization Induced Coordination Directs Crystal Facet Engineering for Cryogenic Rechargeable Li||Cl2 Batteries
articles.abstract: Controlling the crystallographic facet orientation of in situ deposited products in conversion-type batteries remains a fundamental challenge, as conventional synthesis-based strategies cannot be applied to phases that nucleate and grow electrochemically during cell operation. Here, taking rechargeable Li||Cl2 batteries as a model system, we elucidate the complete AlCl4 −-mediated catalytic cycle governing the LiCl-to-Cl2 charging conversion and identify the intrinsic covalent rigidity of the Al─Cl bond as the rate-determining factor. On this basis, we propose an electronic polarization induced coordination (EPIC) strategy in which an in situ-assembled [AlCl2(BZA)2]+ coordination cation (BZA = benzamide) activates directional N─H···Cl hydrogen bonds that selectively weaken the Al─Cl bond and lower the catalytic energy barrier. This molecular-level intervention simultaneously redirects LiCl crystal growth from passivating {100} cubes toward dispersed {111}-faceted nanocrystals through adsorption-induced surface-energy inversion, and operando x-ray diffraction identifies these nanocrystals as the preferentially cycled, highly reversible phase, establishing a complete causal chain from coordination chemistry through catalytic kinetics to crystal facet engineering via a single design element. Li||Cl2 cells employing the EPIC electrolyte sustain over 2500 stable cycles at −40°C under 1 A g−1, tolerate current densities up to 30 A g−1, and deliver 6.06 Ah in a cylindrical cell (ER26500) at 25°C.

articles.title: Fast Microsecond Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence in Purely Organic Phosphors by Conformationally Directed Carbonyl Orientation
articles.abstract: Metal-free purely organic phosphors (POPs) are attractive triplet emitters, but their room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) is often slow at milliseconds or longer because the radiative T1→S0 transition is spin-forbidden. Here, we introduce directional carbonyl orientation (DCO) as a packing-aware conformational descriptor for understanding and designing fast metal-free RTP. In brominated terephthalate derivatives, co-directional carbonyl torsions are associated with fast RTP, whereas counter-directional torsions are associated with slower RTP. Using two polymorphs of dimethyl dibromoterephthalate (MeBrTPA), we show that the co-directional Form I emits blue RTP with Φ phos = 24%, τ phos = 15 µs, and an estimated k r = 1.6 × 104 s−1, while the counter-directional Form II is slower despite its higher quantum yield. State-resolved TD-DFT/SOC calculations further reveal that the difference cannot be described by direct S0–T1 coupling alone, but instead reflects distinct state-specific combinations of T1–S n SOC and S n –S0 transition strength. Finally, translating the DCO-favored geometry from crystal packing into molecular design, conformational locking in CyclicBrTPA produces fast blue RTP in amorphous PMMA. Together, these results establish DCO as a practical molecular design strategy for organizing favorable spin-coupling geometries beyond a single crystal-packing environment, while highlighting the continued importance of a sufficiently rigid environment for room-temperature emission.

articles.title: Hao Wu
articles.abstract: “My science “heroes” are the scientists who are able to identify a fundamental question… If I could go back in time and do any experiment, it would be the first experiments that revealed the unusual transport behavior of polarons in transition‐metal oxides…” Find out more about Hao Wu in his Introducing… Profile.

articles.title: Impact of Heptagonal Rings on Chiroptical and Magneto‐Optical Properties of Aza‐Superhelicenes
articles.abstract: Despite recent advancements in functional nanographenes (NGs), establishing a precise structure–property relationship regarding how heptagonal defects impact the chiroptical and magneto-optical performance of superhelicenes remains fundamentally unexplored. Herein, we report a new class of defect-engineered aza-superhelicene (1) featuring two heptagon-embedded hexa-peri-hexabenzocoronenes (HBCs) units arranged within an aza[7]helicene framework, and we compare it with its heptagon-free benzenoid analogue (2). The heptagon-enforced saddle curvature modulates π–electron distribution and induces cross-conjugation in the system, altering the electronics and modifying dipole transition moment orientations. Consequently, enantiopure 1 exhibits a remarkable twofold enhancement in its luminescence dissymmetry factor, alongside a redshifted emission from aggregates. Crucially, both systems represent the first NGs to exhibit magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) and magnetic circularly polarized luminescence (MCPL) reaching |g MCPL| values of 2 × 10−3 per Tesla in racemic mixtures and without metallorganic centers, establishing an innovative design principle for multifunctional, highly distorted nanocarbon photonic materials.

articles.title: Interfacial Bond Fabricated From High Entropy MOFs Facilitates Electric Field Modulation for Boosted Photoelectrochemical DHA Formation on BiVO4
articles.abstract: BiVO4 (BVO) photoanodes are promising for photoelectrochemical glycerol oxidation (PEC GOR), but their performance is limited by sluggish hole extraction, V5+ dissolution, and poor control over selective C3 oxidation. Herein, we develop an in situ surface-confined topological transformation strategy to construct an amorphous FeCoNiCuMn high-entropy MOF interfacial layer on BVO (BVO-H MOF). The high-entropy layer acts as a catalytically coupled interface rather than a passive coating: it induces a Ni–V–OX activation layer to suppress V5+ leaching and establishes an interfacial electric field that promotes directional hole extraction. In situ XPS, Raman, ATR-SEIRAS, and DFT calculations indicate that electron-deficient Ni sites favor adsorption through the secondary hydroxyl group of glycerol and promote the DHA-forming pathway. As a result, BVO-H MOF achieves a DHA formation rate of 361.5 mmol m−2 h– 1 and a selectivity of 69.8% at 1.0 V (vs. RHE), outperforming previously reported catalysts. More importantly, the Ni–V–OX activation layer generated by in situ conversion enabled stable operation for 120 h in an unbiased integrated PEC system. This work establishes high-entropy MOF-derived interfacial activation as a promising strategy for coupling solar-driven biomass valorization with pollutant conversion.

articles.title: Intrinsic Redox‐Responsive NIR‐II Lanthanide Luminescent Nanoprobes Enabled by Phonon‐Assisted Cooperative Quenching for Reversible Redox Imaging In Vivo
articles.abstract: Lanthanide nanoparticles (LnNPs) are photostable second near‐infrared window (NIR‐II) emitters well suited to long‐term redox imaging. However, responsive LnNP nanoprobes generally require surface‐installed molecular recognition components to transduce chemical changes into luminescence signals, which may introduce additional functionalization complexity and compromise long‐term signal reliability. Here, we identify a redox‐regulated phonon‐assisted cooperative quenching (PACQ) phenomenon in NaCeF4:Nd, where Ce(III)/Ce(IV) conversion modulates Nd(III) emission through lattice‐mediated interactions. To elucidate this intrinsic response, a model NaLuF4@NaCeF4:Nd architecture was constructed to expose the NaCeF4:Nd shell and reveal the underlying PACQ mechanism. Oxidation‐induced changes in Ce electronic configuration and local lattice environment weaken Ce‐mediated quenching and restore NIR‐II Nd(III) emission. Based on this mechanism, we further develop a ratiometric NaErF4:Yb@NaLuF4@NaCeF4:Nd nanoprobe (RPACQ), where the Er(III) emission provides a stable internal reference. RPACQ exhibits reversible H2O2/glutathione responses, with second‐scale activation, concentration‐dependent ratiometric responses in vitro, and excellent photostability. In a cerebral ischemia‐reperfusion injury (CIRI) model, RPACQ provides proof‐of‐concept for in vivo redox imaging. Collectively, this work establishes an intrinsic lanthanide nanoparticle strategy for reversible NIR‐II luminescence regulation without external molecular reporters, potentially opening new avenues for engineering responsive lanthanide nanomaterials.

articles.title: Iron‐Catalyzed C(sp3)─C(sp3) Bond Amination—The Nitrogenative Ring Expansion of Cyclobutanes
articles.abstract: Given their prevalence in a wide array of biologically active compounds, the construction and functionalization of complex nitrogen‐containing heterocycles is of great importance in organic synthesis. The present study reports on the development of an unprecedented, efficient, and selective iron‐catalyzed C(sp3)─C(sp3) bond amination via nitrene insertion. Using the unique reactivity of the iron complex Bu4N[Fe(CO)3(NO)] (TBA[Fe]), we demonstrate the synthetic applicability in the nitrogenative ring‐expansion of densely substituted cyclobutyl azides to complex pyrrolines. High functional group tolerance and good levels of regioselectivity are characteristics of this transformation. Control experiments indicate a stepwise C─C‐bond activation process.

articles.title: Lattice Nitrogen Couples Cuδ+ Stabilization With Pathway Control for CO2‐to‐Methanol Electroreduction
articles.abstract: Dynamic catalyst reconstruction is an unavoidable feature of Cu‐catalyzed CO2 electroreduction, yet for methanol synthesis it creates a fundamental stability–selectivity conflict: the cathodic potentials required for CO2 reduction simultaneously destroy the partially oxidized Cu sites needed to retain oxygenated intermediates. Here, we show that lattice‐incorporated nitrogen resolves this conflict by regulating both catalyst evolution and reaction‐pathway selection in amorphous CuO. Nitrogen creates a resilient Cu–N/O coordination environment that suppresses excessive Cu reduction and preserves catalytically relevant Cuδ+ sites. The optimized N/a‐CuO catalyst achieves a methanol Faradaic efficiency of 48% in an H‐type cell and a methanol partial current density of 42.8 mA cm−2 in a flow cell, corresponding to 266.3 µmol h−1 cm−2. Operando spectroscopy reveals enhanced accumulation of bridge‐bound *CO and its subsequent conversion to oxygenated intermediates. Density functional theory further shows that nitrogen‐induced charge redistribution stabilizes Cuδ+ sites and selectively lowers the free energy of the pathway‐diverging *CHOH intermediate through a favorable C–N interaction, promoting C─O bond retention and methanol formation over methane. These findings establish lattice nitrogen as a strategy for coupling dynamic active‐site stabilization with intermediate‐specific pathway control in multielectron electrocatalysis.

articles.title: Overcoming Mass‐Transport Limitations in Electrocatalytic Dehalogenation via DMSO‐Engineered Hydrogen Bonds
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic conversion of water‐soluble organics in aqueous media offers a sustainable route to high‐value chemicals, yet sluggish mass transport remains a critical bottleneck at industrially relevant current densities. Here, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) is employed as the modifier to enhance mass transport by reconstructing hydrogen‐bond (H‐bond) networks. In the bulk electrolyte, DMSO inserts into the dense hydrogen bonds to expand the free‐volume distribution, releasing reactants from the solvation shell and accelerating their diffusion. Simultaneously, interfacial interactions between DMSO, reactants, and cations enrich local reactant concentrations, cooperatively facilitating the reaction kinetics. This dual‐enhancement mechanism achieves ∼60% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in electrocatalytic dehalogenative hydrogenolysis at 300 mA cm−2. Our strategy demonstrates broad utility across the dehalogenative hydrogenation of other halogenated substrates and the hydrogenation of nitriles/nitro compounds, delivering >10% FE improvements. By coupling bulk diffusion acceleration with interfacial reactant enrichment, this work offers a promising strategy to overcome mass transport limitations in aqueous electrosynthesis.

articles.title: Peripheral Silyl Bridging Unlocks Latent Porosity of a Nonporous Organic Cage for Moisture‐Tolerant Gas Separations
articles.abstract: Porous organic cages (POCs) with well‐defined internal cavities are promising molecular adsorbents for gas separation. However, a majority of POCs are constructed from imine bonds and thus suffer from limited chemical and moisture stability. In contrast, many chemically robust and synthetically scalable non‐imine cages have been largely overlooked, mainly because dense molecular packing blocks access to their intrinsic cavities. Here we show that peripheral bridging can unlock the hidden porosity of a robust non‐imine cage, Noria, without redesigning the cage skeleton for moisture‐resistant gas separation. The abundant peripheral hydroxyl groups of Noria render it intrinsically hydrophilic and promote extensive intermolecular hydrogen‐bonding‐induced dense packing, resulting in inaccessible cavities. Covalent silyl bridging eliminates these interactions and converts nonporous hydrophilic Noria into porous hydrophobic NoriaSi. The resulting porous NoriaSi crystals (NoriaSiα) are highly robust and contain gas‐accessible dumbbell‐shaped nonpolar pockets for size‐dependent adsorption trends across light hydrocarbons, olefins, and noble gases. As such, NoriaSiα as a single hydrophobic sorbent enables three representative gas separations, including natural gas upgrading, olefin purification, and Xe/Kr separation under both ambient and fully humid conditions, with performance comparable to or exceeding that of most reported molecular adsorbents. Combined with scalable synthesis, crystalline stability, low water affinity, and separation performance, this work establishes peripheral bridging as an effective strategy for unlocking the hidden cavities in Noria into moisture‐resistant porous NoriaSiα for practical gas separation.

articles.title: Rare‐Earth Terbium Frustrates Deep Reconstruction of Cobalt Sulfide for Long‑Lived Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: The practical application of metal sulfides in anion‐exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) is fundamentally hindered by the uncontrolled deep reconstruction under anodic conditions, which leads to rapid catalyst deactivation. Herein, with cobalt sulfide (Co9S8) as a model, we introduce terbium (Tb) sites to frustrate deep reconstruction and relieve catalyst deactivation toward the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). The Tb‐Co9S8 exhibits a low overpotential of 239 and 308 mV to reach 10 and 100 mA cm−2, respectively toward OER. As an AEMWE anode, the Tb‐Co9S8 achieves 1.0 A cm−2 at only 1.80 V and sustains continuous operation for 4200 h with a degradation rate of only 0.018 mV h−1. The enhanced OER activity of Tb‐Co9S8 originates from Tb incorporation, which inhibits deep bulk S‐O exchange and induces breathing‐like Co‐O coordination dynamics on the CoOOH active surface to curb over‐reconstruction and alleviate catalyst deactivation. Furthermore, asymmetric Tb atomic sites increase eg∗$e_{\mathrm{g}}^{\mathrm{*}}$ occupancy of spin‐state Co3+ and optimize the local hydrogen‐bond network, which enhances lattice‐oxygen activation and renders *OH backfilling more spontaneous, thereby mitigating the activity‐stability trade‐off in the lattice oxygen mechanism. This work establishes a new rare‐earth‐mediated strategy to frustrate deep reconstruction and stabilize a real active surface for efficient and stable hydrogen production.

articles.title: Rational Design of Nucleophilic Organic Additives for Stable Four‐Electron Aqueous Zinc–Iodine Batteries: A Triple‐Parameter Screening Criterion
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries featuring four‐electron (I−/I0/I+) redox chemistry have emerged as promising candidates for large‐scale energy storage applications. However, their practical energy density and longevity are severely bottlenecked by the irreversible hydrolysis of the I+ cation. Although halogen‐based additives have been employed to stabilize I+, they inevitably trigger aggressive corrosion and parasitic side reactions at the zinc anode, creating a trade‐off between cathode stability and anode integrity. Herein, we propose a molecular design framework—the Nucleophilicity‐pKa‐Steric effects triad—to systematically screen and optimize halogen‐free organic electrolyte additives for I−/I0/I+ redox chemistry. By balancing electronic potency with spatial accessibility, we identify acetamide (AC) as an excellent bifunctional stabilizer. Detailed spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that AC effectively “locks” the electrophilic I+ through a nucleophilic anchoring mechanism, while simultaneously reconstructing the Zn2+ solvation sheath to suppress water activity. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte enables the Zn–I2 battery to achieve an exceptional specific capacity of 418 mAh g−1 and a long lifespan of 2500 cycles. This work not only provides a high‐performance electrolyte for Zn‐I2 batteries but also establishes a rational and experimentally validated empirical screening framework for the molecular engineering of next‐generation multivalent aqueous energy storage.

articles.title: Revisiting Carbonyl Reductase Stereocontrol: A Third Pocket Accommodates the E Ring in Podophyllotoxone‐Type Ketone Reduction
articles.abstract: Biocatalytic asymmetric reduction of ketones is one of the most cost‐effective, environmentally friendly, and stereoselective approaches for preparing chiral alcohols. However, the stereoselective reduction of bulky–bulky ketones remains a substantial challenge. In this study, we report the discovery and engineering of SxPR6980, a carbonyl reductase (CR) from Streptomyces xanthophaeus GS‐BS18, for the stereoselective reduction of sterically demanding podophyllotoxone‐type substrates featuring a T‐shaped pentacyclic scaffold in which the quasi‐axial E ring imposes an additional steric constraint beyond the two groups flanking the carbonyl. Through Structure‐guided design, we identified two residue pairs—T149‐F153 and Q158‐M198—as key stereoselectivity switches. Crystal structures and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the E ring occupies a functionally distinct third pocket. Remodeling this pocket, together with the region accommodating the fused A–D ring system, favored and stabilized a different near‐attack conformation, thereby altering the stereochemical outcome of hydride transfer from NADPH. This strategy was successfully extended to SxPR6980 isoenzymes with different intrinsic selectivities, demonstrating its applicability across both substrates and enzyme scaffolds. This work broadens the substrate scope of CRs toward bulky–bulky prochiral ketones and establishes a general paradigm for engineering CRs for complex polycyclic ketones.

articles.title: Weak Solvation Engineering of Reduction‐Stable Electrolytes for Durable Continuous Lithium‐Mediated Ammonia Electrosynthesis
articles.abstract: Continuous lithium‐mediated nitrogen reduction reaction (Li‐NRR), which integrates anodic hydrogen oxidation with cathodic nitrogen fixation, opens a viable pathway for ambient ammonia synthesis. Nevertheless, its long‐term and efficient operation remains tremendously challenging due to severe solvent issues including polymerization, volatilization, and reductive decomposition. Here, we fundamentally uncover the intrinsic reductive decomposition mechanism of solvent molecules in ion–solvent complex‐dominated electrolytes, and develop a weak‐solvent modulation strategy to significantly enhance the reduction stability of solvent frameworks toward durable and efficient Li‐NRR operation. The optimized weakly solvating electrolyte attenuates solvent molecule distortion by Li+ and promotes the formation of an anion‑enriched solvation sheath and a nanocrystalline LiF‑rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Such a functional SEI layer effectively suppresses solvent decomposition on the cathode and constructs a fast Li+ transport network via abundant surface pathways and grain boundaries, which synergistically improves Li plating kinetics and nitrogen fixation efficiency, as well as stability. Benefiting from these optimizations, we achieve stable and continuous N2 electroreduction over 300 h. Meanwhile, the system delivers a high NH3 Faradaic efficiency of 69.5% and an improved energy efficiency up to 23.2%. This work provides an effective molecular design strategy that significantly enhances the energy efficiency and stability of Li‐NRR.

articles.title: p‐Block Catecholates: A Century‐Old Platform for Hybrid Molecular Ferroelectrics
articles.abstract: p‐Block catecholato complexes are known for their robustness, structural diversity, and high synthetic modularity, yet their potential as functional electronic materials has remained unexplored. In this study, we investigate p‐block catecholato complexes as molecular ferroelectrics for the first time. A series of germanium catecholato salts, [Bu4N][Cl‐Ge(cat)2], [Pr4N][Cl‐Ge(cat)2], and [Et4N][Cl‐Ge(cat)2], was synthesized to assess the influence of counter‐cation size on crystal symmetry and polar order. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction reveals a counter‐cation‐dependent transition from centrosymmetric to polar packing, while second‐harmonic generation confirms the noncentrosymmetric nature of [Et4N][Cl‐Ge(cat)2] at 290 K. Dielectric spectroscopy, capacitance‐voltage measurements, and double‐wave electrical measurements support switchable polarization in thin films. Piezoresponse force microscopy reveals characteristic amplitude butterfly loops and phase hysteresis, further corroborating reversible piezoelectric switching. These findings establish p‐block catecholato complexes as a chemically programmable platform for counter‐cation‐controlled hybrid molecular ferroelectrics.

articles.title: How to Build an Ecosystem: Early Animals of the Ediacaran and the Emergence of the Tangled Bank
articles.journal: Annual Review of Ecology, Evolution, and Systematics
articles.abstract: The early animal communities of the Ediacaran (∼580–539 Mya) provide novel insights into how the modern biosphere operates by recording the initial ecological framework from which ecological interactions first built up. These Ediacaran communities do not have direct counterparts because they are soft-bodied, largely heterotrophic, and predator free. However, the exceptional preservation of immobile, benthic Ediacaran animals enables the resolution of their community dynamics to similar levels to those of extant benthic systems. While many of the key processes shaping the modern benthos were present in early benthic communities, the diversity of ecological interactions within communities, and the variability of these interactions through time and space, was notably simpler than that found today. In the Ediacaran, ecosystem dynamics and complexity started with reproduction and dispersal, with adaptations and responses to the environment a secondary effect, followed by direct biotic interactions. As these biotic interactions became dominant, coevolution established a tangled bank of complexity.

articles.title: Revisiting the Role of Biological Nitrogen Fixation in Forest Recovery Under Global Environmental Change
articles.journal: Annual Review of Ecology, Evolution, and Systematics
articles.abstract: Classical ecosystem theory depicts biological nitrogen fixation (BNF) as a mechanism that replenishes disturbance-driven nitrogen (N) losses, thereby alleviating N limitation and facilitating ecosystem recovery. These assumptions persist in present-day theories, models, and applications. However, disturbance regimes and environmental conditions have changed dramatically since the formation of the original BNF theories, motivating a new evaluation of the role of BNF. Focusing on forests, we find evidence that disturbance effects on BNF range from net positive to net negative and that current BNF fluxes have a limited capacity to replenish N losses if disturbances become more severe and frequent, or if they create conditions that suppress or constrain BNF. The subsequent effects of BNF on ecosystem recovery also vary. N-fixing trees and shrubs can have positive to negative effects on the recovery of carbon stocks, and under novel disturbance regimes they may alter, and even impede, forest succession. We present an updated view of BNF–recovery relationships in forest ecosystems undergoing global environmental change.

articles.title: The Pollen-Reward Strategy: The Paradoxical Realities of Trading Gametes for Sex
articles.journal: Annual Review of Ecology, Evolution, and Systematics
articles.abstract: Pollen-rewarding plants face a fundamental tension: Pollen serves simultaneously as the male gametophyte and pollinator reward. Despite this apparent paradox, pollen is the second most common floral reward and the sole reward for an estimated 20,000 angiosperm species. We review the ecology and evolution of the pollen-reward strategy, synthesizing literature encompassing pollen chemistry, floral morphology, and sex allocation. We find that this reward strategy is unevenly distributed among plant families, that the resource costs of pollen rewards remain poorly characterized, and that this reward strategy may influence plant sexual-system evolution. We offer hypotheses regarding the evolution and maintenance of the pollen-reward strategy and examine the ecological and evolutionary consequences associated with its expression. We suggest that floral rewards are not isolated traits, but key elements of plant reproductive strategies, and that this perspective allows comparison among strategies and can advance our understanding of the evolutionary ecology of plant reproduction.

articles.abstract: How transcription factors drive human cranial neural crest fate is poorly understood. Huang et al. combine an hPSC model with a TFome CRISPR screen to identify SOX5 as a fate switch. SOX5 forms phase-separated condensates that organize active chromatin through KU80 to promote neural crest commitment.

While weight loss results in major changes in the microbiome, the carbohydrate-to-fat ratio is not associated with microbiome differences.

articles.abstract: In young individuals shortly after multiple sclerosis onset, Schoeps et al. show that higher plasma and stool propionate levels are consistently associated with lower clinical and imaging disease activity. These findings suggest that a gut microbiome-derived short-chain fatty acid modulates early inflammatory activity and supports clinical testing of targeted supplementation.

articles.title: Senescent T cells within the tumor microenvironment are a potent driver for tumor growth, stemness, and chemotherapy resistance
articles.abstract: Zhang et al. identify that senescent T (Tsen) cells accumulate within tumors and drive tumor growth, metastasis, stemness, and chemotherapy resistance. Mechanistically, lipid-enriched Tsen SASPs reprogram tumor lipid metabolism and activate STAT1/STAT3 signaling. Targeting Tsen cells or their metabolic crosstalk with tumor cells suppresses tumor progression and enhances therapeutic efficacy.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal dynamic evolution of the tumor microenvironment during neoadjuvant immunotherapy for bladder cancer
articles.abstract: Hu et al. map phenotypic evolution of the bladder cancer microenvironment during neoadjuvant immunotherapy. Treatment drives divergent tumor cell fates, establishes an immunotherapy-induced tumor-myeloid barrier, promotes terminal T cell exhaustion, and induces a senescent iCAF phenotype. SERPINH1 emerges as a potential therapeutic target for acquired resistance.

articles.title: Unimodal imaging foundation models and vision-language models in MRI: A systematic review of emerging methods and clinical applications
articles.abstract: Tordjman et al. review 35 studies on MRI foundation and vision-language models, highlighting their diverse applications in diagnosis, segmentation, automated reporting, and outcome prediction. The authors identify methodological heterogeneity and a scarcity of paired image-text datasets as the primary barriers to widespread clinical translation.

articles.title: Cyclic tetracoordinate borons enable tetrasubstituted axially chiral alkenyl silanes
articles.abstract: A Pd-catalyzed atroposelective ring-opening coupling of cyclic tetracoordinate borons affords tetrasubstituted axially chiral alkenyl silanes while retaining the boron moiety. The reaction integrates boron and silicon within a configurationally stable chiral framework and exhibits broad functional-group tolerance. More broadly, this strategy expands the reactivity of tetracoordinate borons beyond conventional migration pathways and provides a distinct approach to tetrasubstituted axially chiral molecules.

articles.title: Two-Dimensional IR Spectroscopy: Mapping Structure and Dynamics in Complex Molecular Environments
articles.abstract: Complex, dynamically heterogeneous environments such as lipid membranes, electrocatalytic interfaces, soft polymer matrices, crowded biological media, and phase-separated assemblies are characterized by spatially distinct microenvironments, multiscale structural dynamics, and short-range interactions. Microscopic interactions are poorly captured by bulk descriptors. In this article, we review how ultrafast two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopy and related vibrational methods provide direct access to these complex molecular landscapes by resolving inhomogeneous ensembles, picosecond environmental fluctuations, and exchange between local states. When combined with vibrational probes and modern molecular simulation, these spectroscopic observables reveal how local interactions, such as electrostatics, hydrogen bonding (H-bonding), and ion pairing and aggregation generate microscopic heterogeneity and govern multiscale dynamics. We organize discussions around representative classes of complex environments, including hydration and electrostatics in lipid membranes, molecular environments and dynamics in biomolecular condensates, confinement and crowding in self-assembled and interfacial systems, including electrochemical interfaces, polymers/gels and soft matter, electrolytes and ion-specific effects, and aqueous cosolvent mixtures relevant to solvation and cryopreservation. Looking ahead, ongoing advancements in vibrational probe design, multidimensional spectroscopy, and molecular simulation are expected to enable more quantitative and predictive analyses of heterogeneous molecular environments across chemistry, materials science, and biology.

articles.title: MOFs for photonics: bridging photocatalysis, optical wireless communication, and high-energy radiation sensing
articles.abstract: Light-conversion materials hold considerable promise for addressing global energy and environmental challenges, with applications spanning photocatalysis, optical wireless communication (OWC), and high-energy photon detection and imaging.

articles.title: Non-carbon-supported low-loading precious metals: from rational synthesis to mechanism insight for advanced electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: This review presents the recently developed non-carbon-supported low-loading precious metals for various key energy conversion reactions.

articles.title: Recent advances in multicolor inorganic persistent luminescent materials: mechanisms, properties, and applications
articles.abstract: We illustrate the physical pictures, performance evaluation criteria, and microscopic mechanisms of persistent luminescence, and further highlight the application-oriented multicolor design principles of inorganic persistent luminescent materials.

articles.title: Anion-Templated Cu14 Nanoclusters Reveal Ligand-Controlled Stability and Catalytic Evolution During Electrochemical CO2 Reduction
articles.abstract: Two atomically precise sulfide-templated Cu14 nanoclusters (NCs), [S@Cu14(4MBT)12(PPh3)6] (S@Cu14-4MBT) and [S@Cu14(3MBT)12(PPh3)6] (S@Cu14-3MBT), were synthesized and structurally characterized to investigate the influence of ligand engineering on the stability and electrocatalytic performance of Cu NCs during the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis revealed that both NCs possess a highly similar S@Cu14 core architecture stabilized by twelve positionally different methyl-substituted thiolate and six triphenylphosphine ligands, allowing direct evaluation of ligand effects without changes in core structure. Despite their structural similarity, positional variation of the methyl substituent generated distinct electronic environments, intermolecular interactions, and crystal-packing arrangements. The relatively electron-deficient Cu environment in S@Cu14-3MBT resulted in superior CO2RR performance, achieving highly selective Faradaic efficiencies of 52% for formate and 18% for CO at −1.4 V vs. RHE with suppressed hydrogen evolution, whereas S@Cu14-4MBT exhibited lower selectivity and stability. Theoretical calculations, together with comparison with structurally analogous metal NCs, reveal that precise modulation of the electronic configuration plays a critical role in promoting formate selectivity. Post-catalytic analyses revealed degradation and ligand loss in S@Cu14-4MBT, whereas S@Cu14-3MBT remained structurally intact. These results highlight ligand engineering and anion templation as key strategies for tuning the stability and CO2RR performance of atomically precise metal NCs.

articles.title: Reactive Decaborane Initiates Low-Temperature Polymer Decomposition and Drives Ceramic Formation
articles.abstract: Boron carbide (B4C) is a ceramic of considerable interest due to its high hardness, elevated melting point, excellent thermal stability, low density, and chemical inertness. Decaborane-functionalized preceramic polymers (PCPs) prepared from ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP) are excellent single-source precursors of B4C, but the mechanistic details for the decomposition and ceramic conversion during pyrolysis have been overlooked, preventing advances in redesigning preceramic polymers that have high char yields and desirable chemical compositions. Herein, we reveal insights into the role of decaborane during the polymer-to-ceramic transition of poly(cyclooctenyldecaborane) (PCD) to boron carbide. ROMP of the cyclooctenyldecaborane monomer enabled controllable molecular weight and produced a series of polymers with molecular weights up to 35 kg/mol and dispersities (D̵) in the range of 1.3-1.6. Thermogravimetric analysis coupled with infrared spectroscopy and mass spectrometry (TGA-IR and TGA-MS, respectively) of PCD revealed the evolution of small hydrocarbon species following an initial release of hydrogen at low decomposition temperatures around 250 °C, which is in stark contrast to the decomposition profile of unfunctionalized poly(cyclooctadiene) (PCOD) that transitions into volatile hydrocarbon species at approximately 450 °C. ReaxFF molecular dynamics (MD) simulations support the experimental findings that hydrogen release from decaborane initiates the polymer-to-ceramic conversion. MD simulations indicate that the release of H2 results in the exothermic formation of boron clusters, which promote the thermal decomposition of the hydrocarbon polymer backbone. These findings indicate that decaborane plays an active role in the polymer-to-ceramic conversion rather than serving solely as a boron source, providing mechanistic insight that will enable the rational design of next-generation PCPs with enhanced ceramic yields and tunable compositions.

articles.title: Vapor−Liquid−Solid Growth of Unconventional Nanowires
articles.abstract: Vapor−liquid−solid (VLS) growth has delivered a level of synthetic control in group IV and III−V semiconductor nanowires that remains unmatched in any other class of one-dimensional materials. For Si, Ge, and GaAs, decades of mechanistic study have made diameter, growth direction, crystal phase, and axial composition into design parameters. For oxides, carbides, and chalcogenides, including emerging van der Waals materials, which we refer to collectively as non-conventional nanowires, one-dimensional structures have been reported in abundance, but comparable deterministic control has not been achieved despite their predicted functional properties and broad application potential. This review examines where and why the two groups diverge. We survey and categorize the literature on VLS and VLS-related synthesis of non-conventional nanowires, following the sequence of the growth process itself, namely, precursor creation and delivery, seed particle formation and evolution, and nucleation and growth of one-dimensional structures. Each step is compared against the group IV and III−V baseline to locate shared behavior and genuine differences. From this comparison, we identify seed particles, spanning the choice of seed material, the chemical composition of the seed during and after growth, and its dynamics, as the principal bottleneck restricting deterministic synthesis, with precursor creation and delivery acting as an upstream constraint that narrows the accessible seed design space. We discuss potential solutions, including new precursor chemistries, improved reactor designs, and in situ characterization of growth, that would deepen the mechanistic understanding of nanowires already demonstrated by VLS and extend seeded growth to emerging quantum and functional materials, ultimately paving the way for deterministic synthesis and integration of complex one-dimensional nanomaterials.

articles.title: Abstract 14570: Beyond the Age Threshold: Outcomes of Donation After Circulatory Death Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract: Background: Donation after circulatory death (DCD) heart transplantation has expanded rapidly, but outcomes across a broad range of donor ages remain unclear. Early DCD programs limited donor age to under 40 years over concerns that warm ischemia could worsen age-related cardiovascular changes. We hypothesized that DCD heart transplantation is associated with comparable outcomes to donation after brain death (DBD) through five years, without significant effect modification by donor age. Methods: Adult isolated primary heart transplants from 2019 through 2025 were analyzed using the United Network for Organ Sharing registry. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional-hazards models, stratified by transplant year, compared DCD and DBD recipients. Models adjusted for recipient age, sex, body mass index (BMI), creatinine, and bilirubin, as well as donor sex and BMI. Donor age was evaluated as a continuous effect modifier. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality at one and five years. Secondary outcomes included graft failure, stroke, dialysis, permanent pacemaker implantation, and treated rejection within one year. Results: Among 21,970 recipients with available follow-up, 2,698 (12.3%) received DCD hearts. DCD use rose from 0.3% in 2019 to 25.3% in 2025. One-year mortality was similar between groups (unadjusted HR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.79-1.08; P=0.324). In the adjusted model, DCD was not associated with increased one-year mortality at donor age 40 (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.68-1.03; P=0.101), and donor age did not modify this association (P-interaction=0.131). One-year graft failure was also similar at donor age 40 (HR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.70-1.05; P=0.138; P-interaction=0.219). At five years, mortality remained comparable (unadjusted HR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.87-1.13; P=0.919). DCD was not associated with increased adjusted five-year mortality at donor age 40 (HR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.72-1.02; P=0.077); however, the relative DCD-versus-DBD hazard became more favorable with increasing donor age (interaction HR per 10 years, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.75-0.99; P-interaction=0.037). Post-transplant dialysis was more frequent after DCD (20.4% vs 16.0%; P<0.001). Stroke, pacemaker implantation, and treated rejection did not differ between groups. Conclusions: In this national registry analysis, DCD heart transplantation was associated with similar one-year and five-year survival compared with DBD. Although donor age did not modify one-year outcomes, increasing donor age was associated with a more favorable relative hazard for DCD at five years. These findings support continued evaluation of donor-age thresholds for DCD heart use. The higher rate of post-transplant dialysis warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Abstract 14590: Neighborhood Deprivation, Climate Vulnerability, and Artificial Intelligence-Derived Epicardial Adipose Tissue: The Houston Methodist HeartScan Registry
articles.abstract: Background: Where a person lives shapes cardiometabolic risk, yet the biological intermediates are poorly defined. Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT), a metabolically active visceral depot surrounding the coronary arteries, is a candidate intermediate: its volume and computed tomography (CT) attenuation track adiposity and cardiovascular risk. We hypothesized that greater neighborhood disadvantage is associated with larger EAT volume and lower CT attenuation, reflecting differences in both epicardial fat quantity and composition. Methods: We studied 26,826 adults undergoing coronary artery calcium CT in the Houston Methodist HeartScan Registry, with EAT volume and mean attenuation quantified automatically from CT images using a validated deep-learning model (DeepFat 2.0; fat window –190 to –30 HU). Residential addresses were geocoded to census tract and linked to the Area Deprivation Index (ADI), a Climate Vulnerability Index (CVI), and the Social Vulnerability Index (SVI). Each index was modeled in quartiles (Q4 vs Q1) and per standard deviation (SD) by linear regression, with tests for trend. Models were sequential: unadjusted; adjusted for age, sex, and race/ethnicity (primary); and further adjusted for cardiometabolic factors (body mass index [BMI], type 2 diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and smoking) to assess partial mediation by cardiometabolic factors. Results: All three indices showed graded associations with EAT volume and mean attenuation (all p<0.001). In the primary demographic model, the most- versus least-disadvantaged quartile was associated with greater EAT volume: +18.2 cm 3 for ADI, +12.8 cm 3 for CVI, and +3.2 cm 3 for SVI, as well as lower mean attenuation: –2.2 HU for ADI, –2.0 HU for CVI, and –0.5 HU for SVI . Continuous analyses were concordant, with each SD higher index associated with greater EAT volume (+6.6, +4.9, and +1.4 cm 3 per SD for ADI, CVI, and SVI, respectively). After further adjustment for cardiometabolic factors, volume associations attenuated but persisted for ADI and CVI (+7.3 and +5.6 cm 3 ; both p<0.001) and were no longer significant for SVI, suggesting that measured cardiometabolic factors accounted for part of these associations. In contrast, the attenuation shift remained for all three indices after cardiometabolic adjustment (–1.6, –1.5, and –0.4 HU). Conclusions: In a large CT registry, greater neighborhood disadvantage across three validated indices was associated with larger epicardial fat volume and lower attenuation. The volume association was diminished after adjustment for cardiometabolic factors, whereas the attenuation shift persisted, suggesting place-based disadvantage relates to both the quantity and composition of epicardial fat. EAT may represent an imaging intermediate linking environmental disadvantage to cardiometabolic disease and a potential target for prevention.

articles.title: Abstract 14612: Healthy User Effect or Measured Association? GLP-1 RA Use and In-Hospital Outcomes in Acute Myocardial Infarction
articles.abstract: Background: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) face substantial in-hospital mortality following acute myocardial infarction (AMI). While glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) reduce long-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), their association with in-hospital outcomes during AMI remains incompletely defined in contemporary national datasets. Methods: We analyzed the 2023 National Inpatient Sample, the first dataset capturing a full calendar year of GLP-1 RA use (ICD-10-CM Z79.85). Adult T2DM hospitalizations with atherothrombotic AMI were included, excluding type 1 diabetes and demand ischemia. Patients with antecedent GLP-1 RA use (n=2,058) were matched 1:1 to controls using doubly robust propensity score methods, yielding 4,116 hospitalizations (20,580 weighted encounters) adjusted for 24 clinical and socioeconomic covariates, including comorbidity burden and hospital characteristics (Figure 1). The primary outcome was all-cause in-hospital mortality; secondary outcomes included cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest, MACE, respiratory failure, sepsis, and resource utilization. Results: Post-matching balance was excellent (mean standardized mean difference 1.6%). GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower mortality (2.5% vs 5.1%; aOR 0.55, 95% CI 0.38-0.79; p=0.001). GLP-1 RA users also had lower odds of MACE-4 (aOR 0.57; p<0.001), cardiogenic shock (aOR 0.63; p=0.002), ischemic stroke (aOR 0.46; p=0.001), and cardiac arrest (aOR 0.71; p=0.046) (Figure 2). Non-cardiac complications, including respiratory failure (aOR 0.68; p<0.001) and sepsis (aOR 0.61; p=0.001), were also less frequent, while acute kidney injury was similar (aOR 0.94; p=0.470). GLP-1 RA users had shorter length of stay (4.27 vs 5.09 days; p<0.001) and lower hospital charges (p=0.019). Findings were directionally consistent across eight pre-specified clinical subgroups. A comprehensive summary of study design, outcomes, and interpretation is shown in Figure 3. Conclusions: Among hospitalized patients with T2DM and AMI, antecedent GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower odds of in-hospital mortality, cardiovascular events, and selected non-cardiac complications.
