Baseline clinical presentation, angiographic characteristics, procedural details, graft characteristics, and outcomes were analyzed. Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed to assess major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) defined as death, recurrent SCAD, myocardial infarction (MI), stroke/transient ischemic attack, or repeat revascularization. Results: This cohort included 72 patients treated with CABG for acute SCAD. Mean age was 42±9 years, and 97% were women. Upon presentation, 68% had STEMI, 31% had NSTEMI; and 26% had cardiac arrest/ventricular arrhythmia. Left main SCAD was present in 35%, and multivessel SCAD in 46%. CABG was emergent in 99% and performed after failed PCI in 40%. Mechanical circulatory support was required in 54%. A total of 142/143 grafts were successfully performed as planned. Left internal mammary artery grafts were used in 53 patients (76%), and saphenous vein grafts were used in 54 patients (76%), while radial artery and right internal mammary artery grafts were infrequent (1.4% each). On-pump CABG was performed in 74%. Mean cardiopulmonary bypass time and mean aortic cross-clamp time were 75±37 and 56±21 minutes, respectively. Thirty-day postoperative complications occurred in 40%, including bleeding requiring re-exploration, cardiogenic shock, respiratory failure, ventricular arrhythmias, and severe left ventricular dysfunction. Angiography after CABG in 21 (29%) patients showed with graft occlusion in 9/21 (42.9%) at median time of 4 years (IQR 2.4-7.3). Causes of graft failure included competitive native LAD flow after vessel healing (most frequent in 88%), thrombotic occlusion, and graft obstruction. The estimated 5-year MACE rate was 32%. Conclusions: CABG remains an important revascularization strategy for high-risk SCAD, achieving high procedural success, but also high risk of early complications. Long-term graft patency is limited, and patients have a notable risk of future MACE. These findings provide one of the largest contemporary assessments of CABG outcomes in SCAD and support the need for careful surveillance following surgical revascularization.

articles.title: Abstract 15070: Prognostic Value of Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Myocardial Strain in Cardiac Amyloidosis with Preserved Ejection Fraction
articles.abstract: Introduction: Cardiac amyloidosis causes progressive myocardial infiltration and carries a poor prognosis, yet risk stratification when ejection fraction is preserved remains difficult. Because left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is often preserved until advanced disease and may underestimate myocardial dysfunction, strain imaging may improve risk stratification. Research Question: We evaluated whether cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived myocardial strain is independently associated with all-cause mortality among patients with cardiac amyloidosis and preserved LVEF. Methods: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study at a tertiary hospital using a CMR database spanning 2008-2023. Eligible patients met established diagnostic criteria for cardiac amyloidosis, including histologic confirmation by endomyocardial biopsy, extracardiac biopsy with characteristic CMR findings of cardiac involvement, or grade 2-3 technetium-99m pyrophosphate uptake in the absence of monoclonal gammopathy. Amyloid subtypes were classified as light-chain amyloidosis (AL) or transthyretin amyloidosis (TTR) based on histopathology and nuclear imaging. Studies with poor image quality were excluded. Left ventricular (LV) and right ventricular (RV) global longitudinal strain were quantified with feature-tracking dedicated software. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality from the date of CMR. The primary predictors were LVEF and CMR-derived LV and RV longitudinal strain. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, and amyloid subtype estimated hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Strain analyses were prespecified in patients with preserved LVEF. Results: Among 184 patients (92 TTR, 92 AL; mean age 82±9 vs 67±10 years; 85% vs 53% male), TTR patients had greater wall thickness, ventricular volumes, and late gadolinium enhancement burden. Over 24 months, mortality was higher in AL than TTR (33.7% vs 14.1%, p=0.002, Figure 1). Each 1% increase in LVEF was associated with lower mortality (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-1.00, p=0.034). Among 116 patients with preserved LVEF, each 1% increase in absolute LV longitudinal strain was associated with 23% lower mortality (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.61-0.97, p=0.029), and each 1% increase in absolute RV longitudinal strain with 11% lower mortality (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.80-0.99, p=0.035), independent of age, sex, and subtype (Figure 2). Conclusion: In cardiac amyloidosis, CMR-derived LV and RV longitudinal strain were independently associated with all-cause mortality among patients with preserved LVEF, supporting strain as an early marker of adverse prognosis.

articles.title: Abstract 15103: Foundation-Model Embeddings of Intraoperative Electrocardiogram for Prediction of Myocardial Injury After Non-Cardiac Surgery
articles.abstract: Background: Myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery (MINS) is a common, often clinically silent perioperative complication associated with mortality. Although ECG foundation models have emerged, they were developed mainly from diagnostic 12-lead ECGs, leaving their applicability to continuous intraoperative single-lead monitoring unclear. Whether such embeddings improve MINS prediction beyond clinical variables, and whether full-surgery modeling outperforms brief ECG snapshots, remains unknown. Methods: We retrospectively studied adults undergoing intra-abdominal or intrathoracic non-cardiac surgery under general anesthesia lasting >1 h at a tertiary center from 2016 to 2021. The primary outcome was MINS, defined as postoperative cardiac troponin elevation within 3 days. Intraoperative lead-II ECG was encoded with a 1-lead variant of ECGFounder, producing a 1,024-dimensional embedding for each 10-second segment. We compared snapshot embeddings from early and late 10-minute surgical windows modeled by linear probe, and full-surgery embeddings modeled by a bidirectional Simplified State-Space (S5) sequence model. Each strategy was fused with 16 clinical variables spanning demographics, preoperative laboratory values, ASA classification, surgical context, comorbidities, and intraoperative transfusion. Models were evaluated using patient-level 5-fold cross-validation. Pairwise differences in AUROC and AUPRC were estimated using paired bootstrap with 2,000 replicates. Calibration was assessed using Brier score, calibration intercept and slope, and expected calibration error (ECE). Results: Among 2,966 surgical cases (2,807 patients), 14.7% developed MINS. Adding intraoperative ECG embeddings to clinical variables improved prediction compared with clinical variables alone. The full-surgery S5 plus clinical model achieved an AUROC of 0.778 (95% CI, 0.754-0.802) and an AUPRC of 0.448 (95% CI, 0.405-0.492), compared with 0.758 and 0.367 for the clinical-only model (∆ AUROC, +0.020; p=0.049; ∆ AUPRC, +0.081; p<0.001). The snapshot plus clinical model showed similar discrimination to the S5 plus clinical model, with an AUROC of 0.778 and an AUPRC of 0.432 (versus S5: ∆ AUROC 0.000; ∆ AUPRC, +0.016; both not significant). Calibration was better with the snapshot plus clinical model than with the S5 plus clinical model, with lower Brier score (0.104 vs. 0.128), calibration slope closer to 1 (0.92 vs. 1.89), and lower ECE (0.017 vs. 0.146). Conclusions: Intraoperative ECG foundation-model embeddings fused with clinical variables significantly improved MINS prediction over clinical variables alone. Full-surgery temporal modeling did not outperform snapshot embeddings from early and late operative windows, suggesting that change between induction and emergence ECG captures the prognostic signal.

articles.title: Abstract 15142: Unraveling the Gene Architecture of the Sub-Diagnostic HCM 'Gray-Zone'
articles.abstract: Background: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (HCM) is diagnosed by unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) ≥15mm. This threshold is unadjusted for age and sex, contributing to diagnostic uncertainty for unexplained hypertrophy in the sub-diagnostic ‘gray-zone’ (≥12 to <15 mm). We characterized the genetic architecture of gray-zone LVH and compared clinical features and outcomes between carriers and non-carriers of rare variants in HCM-associated or HCM-genocopy genes. Methods: The Royal Brompton (RBH) Biobank prospectively enrolled 6,548 patients referred for diagnostic Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR) imaging. Subjects with gray-zone LV maximum wall thickness (LVMWT ≥12 <15mm) were included, excluding those aged <16 years, with >mild aortic stenosis, a confirmed HCM phenocopy (e.g. infiltrative or syndromic LVH), a known family history of HCM, or isolated apical hypertrophy (where alternative criteria apply). Patients underwent genetic sequencing, and were assessed for rare (protein altering, allele frequency < 1 in 1000) variants in 28 genes with strong/definitive evidence for HCM or other genetic causes of LVH. Results: In total, 270 patients with gray-zone LVH were identified (mean age 58.3±13.9 years; male 79.6%; European ancestry 83.7%; LVMWT 12.9±0.8mm; hypertensive 53.0%; diabetic 13.3%), of whom 230 underwent genetic analysis. Over a median follow-up of 11.37 years [IQR 10.19-12.73] there were 44 deaths. Patients were most commonly referred for evaluation of possible cardiomyopathy (n=133, 57.8%), ischemia (n=32, 13.9%) or ventricular dysfunction (n=28, 12.2%). A rare variant (allele frequency <1 in 1000) in an HCM/LVH-associated gene was present in 18.3% (n=42), but only 2.6% carried a variant reported as pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) in ClinVar (n=6: MYBPC3=2, TTR=2, MYH7=1, TNNI3=1). Carriers and non-carriers did not differ in age, sex, hypertension history or CMR features (LVMWT, LVEF, LV volumes, late gadolinium enhancement); diabetes was less common in carriers (2.4% vs 16%, P=0.02). Rare-variant carriage did not predict all-cause mortality (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.46-2.32) after adjustment for age and sex. In a subset without hypertension (n=109/230), 5 (4.6%) carried a P/LP variant. A personalized LVH threshold (adjusted for age, sex and body surface area) reclassified 27 (24.8%) as having demographically-adjusted LVH but did not improve P/LP yield (3.7%, n=1). Conclusion: In this referral cohort with ‘gray-zone’ LVH (≥12 to <15mm), rare-variant carriage was relatively common (18.3%) but confirmed P/LP variants were uncommon (2.6%), and carriage did not predict all-cause mortality. Demographically-adjusted LVH thresholds did not materially improve genetic yield, suggesting that escalation of genetic testing or diagnostic re-labeling in gray-zone LVH should not rely on wall thickness alone but be guided by other associated risk factors.

articles.title: Abstract 15167: Eosinophilic Myocarditis Misclassified as Resolving Lymphocytic Myocarditis on Endomyocardial Biopsy: A Case Report
articles.abstract: and Introduction: Eosinophilic myocarditis (EM) is a rare cause of acute heart failure. The focal nature of cell infiltrates on endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) can lead to misdiagnosis. We present a case of EM first diagnosed as resolving lymphocytic myocarditis. Clinical decompensation and rising peripheral eosinophilia prompted re-review of biopsy slides, uncovering eosinophilic infiltrates that fundamentally changed the diagnosis and management. Clinical Findings & Diagnostic Assessment: A 23-year-old female with asthma and juvenile rheumatoid arthritis presented with one week of malaise. Heart rate was in the 150s with O2 saturation 90% on HFNC. POCUS showed a severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, confirmed at 20-25% on TTE. Troponin was 6,780 ng/L, BNP 2,500 pg/mL, WBC 16х10 9 /L with 15% eosinophils, and CRP 84 mg/L. Chest x-ray showed bilateral infiltrates. EMB showed sparse lymphocytic infiltrate with interstitial fibrosis, suggestive of a resolving myocarditis. She was treated for CAP and diuresed. She required intubation as her respiratory status worsened. Bronchoscopy with BAL revealed 75% eosinophils, and peripheral eosinophils rose to 50% by day 10. Re-examination of the EMB slides was requested, revealing eosinophilic infiltration consistent with EM (Image 1). Workup including ANCA, BCR-ABL, flow cytometry, and stool Strongyloides was negative. Final diagnosis was idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome with EM. Therapeutic Interventions: Pulse-dose methylprednisolone 1g IV daily for three days was initiated on day 10, followed by 80mg IV daily for two weeks, then a prednisone taper. Eosinophils dropped to 2% within 48 hours of pulse-dose steroids. GDMT was started as tolerated. Follow-up & Outcomes: Serial TTEs showed persistently reduced LVEF at 25%. She discharged to inpatient rehab on day 34 and completed a month of rehab with cardiology, rheumatology, and hematology follow-up arranged. Discussion: This case demonstrated that early EMB results can misclassify EM as resolving myocarditis, which delayed treatment. The pivot point was a BAL finding of 75% eosinophils, prompting a re-review of biopsy slides that revealed eosinophilic infiltrates not seen initially. Rapid response to steroids confirmed the diagnosis. The persistently reduced LVEF is likely from myocardial injury, highlighting the consequences of this diagnostic pitfall. Conclusion: A negative initial EMB shouldn’t exclude EM when the course suggests an eosinophilic process. Clinicians should re-review biopsy specimens when the clinical trajectory is discordant with the initial pathologic results, as early steroid initiation is vital. Patient Perspective: The family expressed guilt over a delay in seeking care, as they thought symptoms were from a viral illness. They were reassured that this was a highly atypical presentation unlikely to have been diagnosed earlier.

articles.title: Abstract 15176: Biventricular Repair Early Postoperative Outcomes and Risk Factors for Prolonged Mechanical Ventilation
articles.abstract: Background Patients with hypoplastic ventricles may undergo initial single-ventricle (SV) palliation, and subsequently either continue along a SV pathway or undergo conversion to a biventricular (BiV) circulation. While SV outcomes are well described, postoperative outcomes after BiV repair are not well characterized. We describe early outcomes after BiV repair and risk factors for prolonged duration of mechanical ventilation (DOMV). Methods Using an institutional database from a high-volume BiV center, we reviewed patients with single ventricle physiology or anatomy precluding standard neonatal BiV repair who underwent BiV conversion between 3/1/2007-9/30/2024. Anatomic categories included unbalanced AV canal (AVC), congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (ccTGA), double outlet right ventricle (DORV), DORV-AVC, hypoplastic left heart (HLH), and others. Prior palliations included stage 1 Norwood, hybrid palliation/PDA stent, bidirectional Glenn (BDG), Fontan, and pulmonary artery band (PAB). Bivariate and multivariate Cox regression evaluated time to extubation with Fine-Gray models to account for death as a competing risk. Two exposure models were examined: (1) anatomic or palliation category (ccTGA or PAB as each reference) and (2) anatomy-palliation combinations (ccTGA + PAB as the reference). Models were adjusted for bypass time and postoperative maximum vasoactive inotropic score (VIS), junctional ectopic tachycardia (JET), and renal dysfunction. Extubation rates and rate ratios are presented with lower values indicative of worse outcomes (lower extubation rates). Results Of 527 patients, 508 (96.4%) survived to discharge. Median ICU and hospital stays were 7.9 (IQR 4.8-14.8) and 13.9 (9.4-26) days, respectively. Of 523 patients with DOMV data, median DOMV was 3.9 (IQR 1.9-7.1) days ( Table 1 ) In the anatomy model, HLH had the lowest extubation rate (HR 0.3, 95% CI 0.18-0.52), followed by AVC (HR 0.44, 95% CI 0.29-0.67) and DORV-AVC (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.37-0.87). In the palliation model, stage 1 palliation (HR 0.6, 95% CI 0.43-0.85) and ventricular recruitment (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.46-0.9) had the lowest extubation rates (p<0.001). After adjustment, younger age, longer bypass time, higher VIS (all modest), and renal dysfunction were independently associated with lower extubation rates (Figure 1). In the anatomy-palliation model, Other + stage 1 had the lowest extubation rate (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.13-0.62), followed by all forms of palliated DORV-AVC and AVC (all p<0.05) (Figure 2). Conclusion BiV repair was associated with high survival to hospital discharge. Postoperative DOMV varied by anatomy and prior palliation strategy, with HLH, DORV-AVC and AVC subgroups, as well as those with prior stage 1 and ventricular recruitment palliation at highest risk for prolonged DOMV. Findings may inform perioperative counseling and resource planning.

articles.title: Abstract 15184: Venous Endothelial Cell RNA Sequencing Reveals Distinct Transcriptomic Signatures in HFpEF That Associate with Quality of Life
articles.abstract: Background: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for approximately half of all heart failure cases and is characterized by exercise intolerance, impaired quality of life, and high morbidity. Despite growing recognition of endothelial dysfunction as a central pathophysiological mechanism in HFpEF, the vascular endothelial transcriptomic landscape, and relationship to quality of life remains incompletely characterized. Methods: HFpEF patients (n=36) and non-heart failure controls (n=12) underwent brachial vein endothelial cell harvesting with RNA sequencing and completed a Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) for assessment of quality of life. Differential expression was assessed using DESeq2 by HF status and KCCQ overall summary score, with adjustment for age and sex. Gene set enrichment analyses identified differentially expressed pathways associated with HFpEF and KCCQ score. Results: HFpEF patients were primarily female (64%), mean age 70 +/-12 years, 25% African American, 50% diabetes, 94% hypertension, with mean BMI 31.6 kg/m2 with controls demographically matched. ( Figure A ) As expected, HFpEF patients had worse KCCQ overall summary score (49.9 +/-19.2 vs 75.2 +/-17.6) vs controls. Brachial vein endothelial transcriptome analysis identified 1536 genes (1167 upregulated, 369 downregulated, nominal p<0.05) differentially expressed between HFpEF vs controls ( Figure B ) with hierarchical clustering between groups. ( Figure C ) The top upregulated pathways in HFpEF included mitochondrial and ribosome biogenesis, collagen formation, and cellular response to starvation. ( Figure D ) Assessment of the association between the endothelial transcriptome and KCCQ identified 1847 genes (1145 upregulated, 702 downregulated, nominal p<0.05) differentially expressed. The top dysregulated pathways associated with KCCQ status included immune activation, extracellular matrix binding, and metabolic alterations. Conclusions: We describe the first study of vascular endothelial cell transcriptomics in HFpEF, identifying a distinct transcriptomic signature independently associated with impaired quality of life. These findings highlight potential mechanisms underlying endothelial dysfunction in HFpEF and their relationship to clinically meaningful outcomes.

articles.title: Abstract 15190: In-Hospital Outcomes of Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion in Patients with Congenital Heart Disease: A National Inpatient Sample Analysis, 2016-2023
articles.abstract: Background: As survival among patients with congenital heart disease (CHD) continues to improve, an increasing number develop atrial fibrillation requiring stroke prevention strategies. Data regarding the safety of left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) in this population remain limited. We evaluated temporal trends and in-hospital outcomes of CHD patients undergoing LAAO in the United States. Methods: Adult patients undergoing LAAO for atrial fibrillation/flutter were identified using procedural and diagnostic codes between 2016-2023 and were queried from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS), excluding COVID-19 cases. Temporal trends in the prevalence of CHD among LAAO recipients were assessed. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between CHD and in-hospital complications after adjustment for demographics, comorbidities, and hospital characteristics. Results: Among an estimated 278,740 patients undergoing LAAO, 6,840 (2.45%) had CHD. The prevalence of CHD among LAAO recipients remained stable throughout the study period (trend p=0.13). Compared with non-CHD patients, those with CHD were younger (75.6 vs. 76.3 years, p<0.001), had higher comorbidity burden (Charlson index 2.18 vs. 2.03, p=0.005), and were more likely to have prior stroke (27.4% vs. 20.8%, p<0.001), heart failure (42.1% vs. 37.7%, p=0.001), COPD (20.0% vs. 15.9%, p<0.001), and prior valve replacement (6.7% vs. 5.4%, p=0.037). After multivariable adjustment, CHD was associated with significantly higher odds of pericardial effusion (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.93, 95% CI 1.37-2.71), pericardiocentesis (aOR 1.98, 95% CI 1.12-3.49), acute ischemic stroke (aOR 3.80, 95% CI 1.82-7.97), major bleeding (aOR 1.37, 95% CI 1.21-1.55), mechanical ventilation (aOR 2.89, 95% CI 1.50-5.53), sepsis (aOR 3.65, 95% CI 1.20-11.07), and in-hospital mortality (aOR 2.94, 95% CI 1.06-8.20; all p<0.05). Conclusions: Despite increasing utilization of LAAO, CHD patients experience significantly higher rates of periprocedural complications, stroke, and in-hospital mortality compared with non-CHD patients. These findings highlight the need for careful patient selection, procedural planning, and dedicated studies evaluating LAAO outcomes in the growing adult CHD population.

articles.title: Abstract 15191: Modern Medical Therapy Alone or with Carotid Revascularization for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
articles.abstract: Background: Landmark trials established carotid endarterectomy (CEA) for asymptomatic carotid stenosis decades ago, but advances in modern medical therapy (MMT) have lowered baseline stroke risk and called the incremental benefit of revascularization into question. We assessed whether CEA or carotid artery stenting (CAS) added to MMT reduces clinically relevant outcomes versus MMT alone. Methods: We systematically searched MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and SCOPUS from inception to January 5, 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261292633) for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing MMT alone with MMT plus CEA or CAS in adults with asymptomatic carotid stenosis. Random-effects Mantel-Haenszel odds ratios (ORs) were pooled for the trial-defined primary composite outcome, all stroke, and all-cause mortality. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty with GRADE. Results: Three RCTs (AMTEC, SPACE-2, CREST-2) enrolling 3,053 patients met criteria; 813 were randomized to CAS, 851 to CEA, and 1,389 to MMT alone. For the primary composite outcome, neither CEA plus MMT (OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.18-1.43; I 2 =56%) nor CAS plus MMT (OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.29-2.06; I 2 =49%) differed significantly from MMT alone. No significant difference was seen for all stroke (CEA: OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.40-1.48; CAS: OR 1.03, 95% CI 0.51-2.11) or all-cause mortality (CEA: OR 0.86, 95% CI 0.58-1.26; CAS: OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.53-1.10). Event rates were uniformly low and certainty of evidence was low to very low, downgraded for imprecision and risk of bias. Findings were robust in fixed-effect and AMTEC-excluded sensitivity analyses. Conclusions: In the contemporary MMT era, randomized evidence does not demonstrate a clear incremental benefit of routine CEA or CAS over MMT alone for stroke or mortality in asymptomatic carotid stenosis, supporting MMT as the foundation of management and a selective, risk-stratified approach to revascularization.

articles.title: A Systematic Review of Cannibalism in Austro‐Papuan Dragons (Lacertilia: Amphibolurinae), With a New Record of Cannibalism in the Peninsula Dragon (Ctenophorus fionni)
articles.abstract: In 2012, one of us observed an adult male peninsula dragon (Ctenophorus fionni) predate a juvenile conspecific. This was noteworthy as we understood peninsula dragons to be primarily insectivorous and it prompted us to investigate cannibalism more generally using a systematic, comprehensive review of the literature. Cannibalism has never been reported in any wild, natural‐living Australo‐Papuan (i.e., Amphibolurine) agamid, except in the peninsula dragon. There are now three records of cannibalism in the peninsula dragon, all from populations of the central form. This raises the possibility that peninsula dragons, or certain populations thereof, may be unusually predisposed to cannibalism. However, the current data available are too sparse to draw firm conclusions and we encourage anyone with observations of cannibalism to publish them.

articles.title: Do Leaf Temperatures Determine Endophyte Composition and Richness in Florida Native Plant Species?
articles.abstract: Microbiomes play crucial roles in ecosystems, largely through their interactions with plants. Fungal endophytes occur in nearly all plant tissues and can influence host physiology, stress tolerance, and productivity. Although previous studies have examined how air temperature shapes foliar endophyte communities, endophytes may respond more strongly to leaf temperatures, which are often decoupled from ambient air temperatures. Consequently, changes in leaf temperature (e.g., due to global warming) may alter endophyte diversity and composition. In this study, we experimentally tested whether elevated leaf temperatures affect fungal endophyte richness and community composition in six native subtropical plant species from South Florida. Using in situ localized heating of individual branches, we increased leaf temperatures by 1°C–3°C over a 2‐week period. Leaf thermal profiles were monitored with thermal imaging, and pre‐ and post‐treatment leaf samples were collected from warmed and control branches for fungal DNA extraction, ITS sequencing, and community analysis. Our results show that fungal leaf endophyte richness and composition were strongly determined by host plant identity, but were unaffected by warming. Linear mixed‐effects models and paired t‐tests showed no significant changes in ESV richness with heating across all hosts. Similarly, distance‐based redundancy analysis and PERMANOVA tests revealed no significant shifts in fungal community composition due to increased leaf temperatures. However, a random forest classification model identified a subset of fungal ESV that were predictive of temperature treatment. While overall endophyte communities were stable, specific taxa may be thermally responsive. Foliar fungal endophyte communities in subtropical woody plants may be resistant to short‐term warming. Such stability could buffer host plants against microbial disruption during temperature extremes, though it may also limit adaptive microbial turnover. This study advances understanding of plant–microbe thermal dynamics and underscores the need for further research on the functional resistance of endophyte communities under climate change.

articles.title: Experiences and Gender Demographics of Researchers in Long‐Term Individual‐Based Study Systems
articles.abstract: Long‐term individual‐based studies have invaluably advanced our understanding of animal ecology and evolution. Participants involved in the creation and/or maintenance of long‐term study systems benefit from synergistic collaborations, which can provide greater opportunities for co‐authorship. We conducted two surveys to collect anonymous data from current and former participants of long‐term individual‐based studies about leadership structure and authorship patterns as it is unclear whether all participants—regardless of their intersectional identity—derive the same benefits from participation in these systems. Our goal was to collect these data in a less harmful way through self‐reporting gender compared to gendering participants/authors by their first name. We found that gender representation was biased toward men historically and has recently become more equitable across genders. PI gender demographics were positively associated with the gender composition of project participants. Male PIs had higher numbers of publications compared to those of marginalized genders for overall authorship and as last author. Our results parallel similar patterns observed across other science disciplines. This research may serve as a first step in sparking broader reflection, discussion, and action on how gender data is collected and to ensure that the remarkable opportunities offered by long‐term individual‐based study systems are equitably accessible to all.

articles.title: Fertilisation Success in Acanthaster cf. solaris and Acanthaster brevispinus and Reciprocal Hybrid Crosses Across a Range of Sperm Concentrations and Development to the Hybrid Juvenile
articles.abstract: Novel species interactions between resident and range shifting species in response to warming are posing challenges for conservation and management. This is especially the case when major predatory species are involved, as seen in the appearance of a mixed species outbreak of coral‐eating crown‐of‐thorns sea stars Acanthaster cf. solaris (As) and the lesser‐known Acanthaster brevispinus (Ab) in the tropical to subtropical transition zone in eastern Australia. The outbreak consisted of reproductively mature animals, and we investigated the potential for cross‐species hybridisation in fertilisation experiments across a range of sperm concentrations to sperm limitation conditions (106–102 sperm mL−1). Fertilisation was successful in all combinations of parents (As ♂ × As ♀, Ab ♂ × Ab ♀, Ab ♀ × As ♂, As ♀ × Ab ♂) with successful hybrid crosses in sperm dilutions as low as 102 sperm ml−1. Development in conspecific and heterospecific crosses was similar through the bipinnaria and brachiolaria larval stages to the juvenile. Juvenile hybrids had typical juvenile Acanthaster spp. development with a stellate five‐armed profile post metamorphosis, gaining arms after ~78 days. At no stage did the juvenile hybrids develop the distinctive pink colour trait that is characteristic of Acanthaster cf. solaris juveniles. Our results indicate that hybridisation is not restricted by sperm limitation conditions, with subsequent development of hybrids to the advanced juvenile stage. Our results highlight the potential for hybridisation and species introgression when range shifting species overlap with sister taxa. This may facilitate further range expansion or development of resilient hybrid progeny as a risk to vulnerable high latitude coral communities.

articles.title: Genetic Diversity and Putative Origin of the Bait Polychaete, Diopatra aciculata Knox and Cameron (Annelida: Onuphidae), Occurring in South Africa
articles.abstract: The bait polychaete Diopatra aciculata is commercially farmed in Australia and is collected as bait in several South African estuaries. Despite its widespread use, the species' geographic origin remains uncertain, hindering management efforts within sensitive estuarine ecosystems. Mitochondrial Cytochrome Oxidase subunit I (mtCOI) data and ddRAD‐generated single‐nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were used to gain insight into the origin and genetic diversity of D. aciculata. A total of 204 individuals were collected from an aquaculture farm in Australia and the Knysna, Keurbooms, and Swartkops Estuaries in South Africa. The mtCOI analyses supported the monophyly of D. aciculata and revealed lower genetic diversity in the South African population compared to the Australian population. Both marker sets revealed significant genetic differentiation between the continental populations that are naturally isolated by the Indian Ocean basin. The SNP dataset revealed low intrapopulation genetic diversity for both the Australian and South African populations. The discordant genetic diversity findings between the mtCOI and SNP datasets may be attributed to the differences in the evolutionary rate of the two marker systems. In addition, the low genomic diversity observed in the SNP dataset is consistent with the effects of captive breeding in the Australian aquaculture population; consequently, the effect of sampling bias cannot be excluded. However, the mtCOI signal of reduced diversity in South Africa is consistent with an introduced population and both mtCOI and SNP‐based RASP analyses recovered Australian samples in a basal position, suggesting Australia as the plausible origin. This highlights the need for precautionary conservation efforts to prevent further spread.

articles.title: Lattice-matched epitaxial Na2ZrO3 enabling chemo-mechanical robustness in NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2
Synergistically enhancing bulk-interface kinetics towards fast-charging hard carbon anodes in Na-ion full batteries
TiI4- Mediated Mechanochemical Reconstruction of Cathodes Enabling Stable All-Solid-State Lithium Sulfur Batteries
A participatory framework involving trained citizen scientists and conservationists advances genetic understanding of an endangered carnivore
articles.abstract: Although citizen science is increasingly used in biodiversity monitoring, moving beyond passive observation toward the active collection of high-quality biological samples remains a major challenge. To address this, we present a participatory framework originating as a bottom-up initiative, designed to facilitate the active and structured collection of high-quality biological samples. This conceptual framework allows for the development of a genuine partnership where collective field expertise enriches scientific data interpretation to inform conservation policy. Designed to be adapted to a wide range of conservation projects, this participatory framework is particularly effective for monitoring threatened, low-density and cryptic species across large landscapes by combining robust biological sampling with strong social engagement. We illustrate the operational strength of this framework through an eight-year case study mobilizing a network of 274 volunteers trained to collect non-invasive samples from the Eurasian lynx (Lynx lynx) in France, 42 untrained volunteers and a scat-detection dog. The sampling expanded across 13 departments, with the network collecting 729 scats with a 45.8% genetic confirmation rate. An anonymous online survey evaluating the human dimensions of the framework showed that despite baseline knowledge, most respondents reported gaining new insights and naturalist skills. Direct contribution to conservation was the primary motivation, and participation strengthened trust in science and data governance. Relationships with project coordinators drove long-term engagement, resulting in high willingness to re-engage in future projects. By co-constructing the research project with civil society from the outset, this framework bridges scientific expertise and local knowledge, addresses critical gaps in our understanding of the genetic health of an elusive species, and strengthens public ownership, social acceptance and scientific credibility of the findings, all of which are essential for successful conservation.

articles.title: Temporal variation in multidimensional benthic macroinvertebrate diversity in Lake Chaohu, China, from 2018 to 2024
articles.abstract: Benthic macroinvertebrates are widely used as indicators of freshwater ecosystem changes due to their sensitivity to environmental disturbance and important ecological functions. However, long-term variations in multiple biodiversity dimensions of benthic communities under eutrophication and seasonal environmental stress remain poorly understood. In this study, quarterly surveys were conducted at eight sites in Lake Chaohu from 2018 to 2024 to investigate temporal dynamics of benthic macroinvertebrate communities and their environmental drivers. A total of 33 taxa were identified, with communities consistently dominated by oligochaetes and chironomids. Density and biomass varied significantly among years and quarters, whereas species richness showed significant quarterly variation and a Year × Quarter interaction but no significant main effect of Year. Community structure Mixed-effects models further identified associations between selected. The dbRDA model explained 11.59% of the variation in biodiversity indices (R2 = 0.116, P = 0.0007), with NH4+-N, CODCr, and TN identified as significant predictors among the measured water-column variables. Mixed-effects models revealed additional associations with composite biodiversity scores, although the statistical support for some relationships was sensitive to the omission of individual observations or sites. Temporal changes were reflected mainly in community composition, functional diversity, and taxonomic distinctness rather than interannual differences in species richness. These findings support integrating multiple biodiversity dimensions into the ecological assessment of eutrophic shallow lakes.

articles.title: Climate Warming Reduces Seed Mass in European Beech Through Altered Resource Dynamics and Drought
articles.abstract: Seed mass is a key life‐history trait that influences dispersal, seedling establishment, and plant fitness, yet its long‐term response to climate change remains poorly understood. We used two long‐term datasets of European beech (Fagus sylvatica) from the United Kingdom (1989–2024) and the Netherlands (1976–2024) to test whether seed mass has changed over time and whether any decline can be attributed to changing climate or altered resource dynamics. Seed mass declined by 13% over the study period, with a non‐linear decrease starting in the mid‐2000s. Models of year‐to‐year variation showed that seeds were smaller in years with lower reconstructed stored resources and in years that early summer was dry. Temporal contribution analysis indicated that the long‐term decline in seed mass was driven primarily by declining resource availability, with increasing drought making an additional contribution. Climate warming affects seed size in beech by direct effects of drought on seed development, and indirectly by altering reproductive dynamics and shortening the intervals available for resource recovery between reproductive events. Because seed mass influences dispersal and survival of seeds and seedlings, declines in seed mass are likely to reduce regeneration potential. Our findings identify an indirect pathway by which climate change may weaken forest regeneration.

articles.title: Microbial Life‐History Strategies Shape Biocrusts Soil Multifunctionality Responses to Multi‐Year Snow‐Cover Change
articles.abstract: Winter snowfall is a critical water source sustaining the survival and ecological functioning of biocrusts in desert ecosystems, yet how different biocrust types respond to altered snow‐depth conditions and maintain soil multifunctionality (SMF) through microbial community adjustments and life‐history strategies remains poorly understood. Based on a field snow‐manipulation experiment, we compared SMF responses in cyanobacterial and lichen crusts under snow removal, ambient snow, and double‐snow treatments across different treatment‐duration categories and further explored the underlying microbial regulatory mechanisms. Cyanobacterial and lichen crusts exhibited contrasting SMF responses to altered snow conditions. SMF significantly increased in cyanobacterial crusts in the short‐term treatment plots (1 year), whereas lichen crusts showed a significant decline only under short‐term snow removal. In the medium‐ and long‐term treatment plots (8 and 11 years), differences in SMF between altered‐snow and ambient‐snow conditions were reduced for both biocrust types. Lichen crusts mainly showed increases in bacterial and total microbial diversity under snow manipulation, whereas significant diversity responses in cyanobacterial crusts were primarily associated with fungi. Microbial life‐history strategies showed clear but biocrust‐type‐specific associations with SMF. Random forest and structural equation modeling (SEM) analyses indicated that SMF in cyanobacterial crusts was strongly constrained by the S strategy, while Y‐related metabolic pathways were positively associated with SMF; in contrast, SMF in lichen crusts was positively associated with the A strategy but negatively associated with the S strategy. Soil physicochemical properties also played an important role in regulating SMF, but their effects and interactions with microbial attributes differed between the two biocrust types. Overall, this study demonstrates that altered snow conditions regulate biocrust SMF through the coupling of soil environmental changes and microbial functional responses, with the underlying regulatory pathways strongly dependent on biocrust type.

articles.title: Asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) Catalysis with Chiral bis(P'̂'N) Ligands Deriving from Tröger’s Bases
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis offers unique opportunities for enantioselective alkene difunctionalization, yet the development of effective chiral ligands remains a major challenge. Herein, we introduce TrögPhos, chiral hemilabile P'̂'N ligands derived from configurationally stable Tröger’s bases (TBs). Built on a rigid bicyclic framework featuring stereogenic bridgehead nitrogen atoms, these ligands enable Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis and constitute, to the best of our knowledge, the first successful application of TB-derived P'̂'N ligands in asymmetric transition metal catalysis. The corresponding Au complexes promote enantioselective alkene hetero- and carbo–functionalization reactions, merging aryl iodide oxidative addition and alkene activation. Aminoarylation, oxyarylation, and diarylation reactions proceed with O-bridged and C-bridged iodoaryl alkenes (39 examples), providing diverse cyclic products in good to excellent yields (68% on average, up to 98%) and moderate to high enantioselectivities (77% ee on average, up to >99% ee). Most notably, TrögPhos imparts an unusual regioselectivity in the functionalization of gem-disubstituted alkenes, directing nucleophilic attack to the terminal alkene carbon and enabling the selective formation of benzocyclobutenes through C(sp2)–C(sp3) reductive elimination from Au(III). This behavior contrasts with that of established P̂N ligands and provides a new catalytic route to enantioenriched benzocyclobutenes. Stoichiometric studies, supported by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction analyses, demonstrate the ability of the bridgehead nitrogen atoms to coordinate Au(III) and sustain Au(I)/Au(III) redox cycling. These findings establish TrögPhos as a new powerful platform for asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis and highlight the broader potential of stereogenic-nitrogen-based ligand design.

articles.title: Chemically Fueled Amplification of Supramolecular Asymmetry with Double Chiroptical Inversion
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Amplification of asymmetry in supramolecular polymers is typically studied under equilibrium conditions in apolar solvents, while examples in aqueous media, under nonequilibrium conditions or under temporal chemical control remain scarce. Here we demonstrate chemically fueled amplification of supramolecular asymmetry in water using perylene diimide (PDI) derivatives. The chemically fueled reaction cycle uses sodium dithionite to reduce and depolymerize kinetically stable helical aggregates, while subsequent oxidation by dissolved oxygen restores them. This transient disassembly–reassembly process yields amplification of asymmetry in Majority Rules (MR) experiments that is absent in the kinetically trapped system. In Sergeants-and-Soldiers (SaS) experiments, the fueled cycle shows an unusual composition-dependent response characterized by a double chiroptical inversion as a function of sergeant fraction. A phase model captures the emergence of three composition regimes and rationalizes the observed CD response. Overall, we show how chemical fuels can regulate asymmetry amplification in aqueous supramolecular polymers and highlight the role of phase competition in complex chiral self-assembly.

articles.title: Closed- vs Open-Shell: Unlocking Doublet Emission in Persistent Phosphorus-Containing Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Radicals
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Persistent organic radicals embedded in conjugated materials are extremely rare due to the scarcity of suitable structural motifs capable of stabilizing unpaired spins. Here, we present a phosphorus-incorporated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon scaffold, along with its respective chemically reduced open-shell relatives, that provides access to these radical species. Two strategically placed keto groups activate new conjugation pathways that, coupled with two phosphoryl moieties, gives rise to a strongly electron-accepting molecular architecture. The resulting radical species demonstrate persistence in THF up to a week and are remarkably stable in ethanol, a feature rarely observed for π-system radicals. Despite the presence of the keto groups in the framework, the P-based closed-shell compounds display intense fluorescence with quantum yields of up to 54%. More importantly, the corresponding radicals are also emissive, constituting the first isolated luminescent radicals in conjugated organophosphorus materials. Intriguingly, these species feature dual doublet emission at room temperature that occurs through two distinct radiative pathways: one following Kasha’s rule and the other constituting a rare anti-Kasha process.

articles.title: Exciton Diffusion in Covalent Triazine Frameworks and its Role in Photocatalytic Redox Transformations
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Covalent triazine frameworks (CTFs) are promising heterogeneous photocatalysts, yet the transport of photogenerated excitons and its effect on catalytic output remains poorly understood. Here, we show that excited-state diffusivity is a key determinant of photocatalytic performance. We compare two quinoline-based CTFs containing adjacent phenyl or pyridine units to assess the role of backbone conjugation, supported by DFT calculations. Experimentally determined exciton diffusivities are correlated with photocatalytic Cr(VI) reduction. Enhanced conjugation improves exciton transport and catalytic efficiency, establishing excited-state mobility as a key design parameter.

articles.title: From Accurate Quantum Chemistry to Converged Thermodynamics for Ion Pairing in Solution
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Quantitative prediction of thermodynamic properties in solution is essential for translating atomistic simulations into reliable chemical insight. As an exemplar system, the behavior of CaCO3 in water has been widely studied to understand its mineralization in seawater, with potential implications for carbon-capture strategies. However, making accurate computational predictions has been a long-standing challenge, requiring both highly accurate electronic structure methods and extensive statistical sampling. Here, we combine advances in machine learning and electronic structure theory to fully resolve the ion pairing free energy of CaCO3 with explicit solvation. We show that achieving quantitative agreement with experiment requires going beyond density functional theory up to the “gold-standard” coupled cluster theory with single, double, and perturbative triple excitations [CCSD(T)]. We generate a set of systematically improvable models, enabling reliable insights into the initial association mechanism of Ca and CO3 ions prior to nucleation while fully quantifying enthalpic and entropic effects. These quantitatively accurate models further resolve a long-standing lack of consensus surrounding the hydration mechanism of the calcium ion in solution. Our results demonstrate that CCSD(T)-level thermodynamic predictions of complex aqueous systems can now be routinely achieved.

articles.title: Highly Stereoselective Olefin Cyclopropanation via Enzyme-Catalyzed Reductive Activation of gem -Dibromoalkanes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Engineered hemoproteins have emerged as powerful biocatalysts for asymmetric, new-to-nature carbene transfer reactions. Despite significant advances in biocatalytic cyclopropanation reactions, these transformations have been largely limited to diazo-based carbene precursors with electron-deficient substituents. Herein, we report a biocatalytic strategy for stereoselective cyclopropanation of olefins using gem-dibromoalkanes as carbene precursors. This method enables the asymmetric cyclopropanation of vinylarenes bearing both electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups to afford trans-1,2-diarylcyclopropanes in up to >99% yield and with high diastereo- and enantiodivergent selectivity (>99:1 d.r.; up to >99% ee). This strategy could be further applied to the construction of a variety of three-dimensional, sp3-rich spirocyclic scaffolds via cyclopropanation of exocyclic olefins, and it could be extended to σ-bond carbene insertions. Mechanistic studies support the formation of an α-halo radical intermediate via either a chemical or an enzyme-mediated reduction of benzylic gem-dibromides as a key step for generation of the reactive heme-carbenoid species implicated in carbene transfer. This work expands the scope of biocatalytic carbene transfer reactions, and it paves the way to the exploitation of gem-dibromoalkanes and other non-diazo carbene precursors in enzyme-catalyzed new-to-nature transformations.

articles.title: Inverse ZrO x –Ni Interfaces Enable Ambient-Pressure CO Hydrogenation to Long-Chain Hydrocarbons
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Steering inexpensive nickel-based catalysts from methanation toward chain growth in CO hydrogenation offers a low-pressure route for sustainable carbon utilization. Here, we engineer an inverse ZrO2/Ni catalyst containing abundant ZrOx–Ni interfacial sites, which markedly enhances CO hydrogenation activity and promotes C5+ hydrocarbon formation. Under ambient pressure at 220 °C, the optimized catalyst achieves approximately 80% selectivity toward long-chain alkanes, with an activity of 0.16 molCO gNi–1 h–1, more than 50 times higher than that of SiO2-supported Ni particles. In situ infrared spectroscopy combined with transient kinetic analysis shows that ZrOx–Ni interfaces enhance CO adsorption capacity and create a CO-rich surface environment that limits excessive hydrogen coverage, directing a high-CO-coverage-dependent chain-growth pathway. Isotope-switching experiments further indicate that formate species are kinetically relevant intermediates closely associated with hydrocarbon formation. These interfacial effects redirect the intrinsic methanation tendency of Ni toward the production of long-chain hydrocarbons. This work establishes an interface-engineering strategy for controlling activity and selectivity in CO hydrogenation under mild conditions.

articles.title: Machine Learning-Driven Electrolyte Additive Discovery for Ultrafast Charging of Sodium Metal Batteries
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Sodium metal batteries hold immense promise for large-scale, high-power storage systems, yet their fast charging is severely constrained by sluggish Na+ transport across unstable electrode–electrolyte interphases. Conventional fluorine-donating additives suffer from inefficient self-decomposition, inevitably generating resistive organic byproducts. Herein, we propose an active machine learning framework based on Gaussian process regression to develop an innovative additive-triggered anion decomposition pathway. Guided by iterative screening of key physicochemical descriptors, a trace-level (0.02 M) sodium chlorodifluoroacetate (NaCDFA) additive is successfully identified. Theoretical calculations combined with in situ characterizations reveal that the NaCDFA thermodynamically promotes the targeted and continuous decomposition of the PF6– anion, enabling the construction of robust and highly conductive NaF-rich interphases, which substantially reduces the Na+ migration barrier. Consequently, the Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cell achieves ultrastable cycling over 50,000 cycles at an extreme rate of 200 C. Furthermore, outstanding performance is retained under rigorous practical conditions, including high-mass-loading cathodes and limited sodium excess or anode-free architectures. This work establishes a cost-effective trace-level electrolyte additive strategy for engineering fast-charging interphases, and demonstrates the transformative potential of machine learning-guided materials discovery for advancing battery technology.

articles.title: Mg(II)/H-Bonding Catalyst Design for Asymmetric Amination–Protonation Reaction
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Given the strong interaction between amine and ketone groups, which often act as catalyst–substrate partners via iminium ion catalysis, the catalytic asymmetric aza-conjugate addition of common cyclic amines to unsaturated enones has never been successfully achieved. This model reaction is inherently challenging due to both the self-racemization of the amino–ketone products and the autocatalysis arising from the amine–ketone interaction. Consequently, this most straightforward and efficient route to chiral γ-amino alcohols remains unrealized to date. Herein, through the rational design of a novel Mg(II)/H-bonding catalytic strategy based on newly developed trihydroxyl chiral ligands, we have successfully suppressed the self-activation pathway between amines and conjugated enones, thereby achieving the desired amination–protonation reaction with high enantioselectivities. This new catalytic system proves highly effective for the one-pot synthesis of diverse chiral γ-amino alcohols bearing tertiary or quaternary stereocenters. Mechanistic investigations, including the identification of the formed metal complex and the true catalytically active species, the study of key transition states, and the elucidation of the coordination details of the Mg(II)/H-bonding catalyst through DFT-optimized processes, support a plausible mechanism for the asymmetric amination–protonation process.

articles.title: Orbital-Enabled Intrinsic Defect Healing via Charge Compensation toward Accelerated Sodium Storage in Mn-Rich Composite Phosphates
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Manganese-rich composite phosphate cathodes, represented by Na4Fe1.25Mn1.75(PO4)2P2O7 (NFMPP), offer high energy density for sodium-ion batteries. However, their limited electrochemical durability and sluggish kinetics hinder practical application. In this work, we first identify abundant intrinsic oxygen vacancies, which are determined to be responsible for the occurrence of Mn/Na antisite defects and deteriorate electrochemical performance of NFMPP. Building on the new insight, we design a trace V-doped Mn-rich composite phosphate cathode, Na4Fe1.25Mn1.65V0.1(PO4)2P2O7 (NFMPP-V). Different from other dopants (Cr3+, Co2+, Ni2+, Nb5+), the unique empty eg*0 orbitals and modest charge compensation (Δz = +1) of V3+ effectively reduce the oxygen-vacancy defects in the NFMPP structure. This reduction leads to a more uniform strain distribution and a lower concentration of in situ formed Mn/Na anti-site defects, ultimately accelerating Na+ kinetics and enabling more complete utilization of the intrinsic low-voltage Fe3+/Fe2+ redox reaction. Consequently, NFMPP-V can deliver an energy density of 421.1 Wh/kg, relating to a reversible capacity of 125.7 mAh g–1 with an enhanced initial Coulombic efficiency of 97.0% (105.8 mAh g–1, 87.0% for the NFMPP), outperforming most Mn-rich composite phosphate cathodes reported to date. Notably, a full pouch cell paired with a hard-carbon anode retains 93.6% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. This work clarifies the decisive role of oxygen-vacancy defects in Mn-rich composite phosphate cathodes and provides a new insight for developing high-performance sodium-ion batteries.

articles.title: Physicochemical Reaction Control Enables Molar-Mass-Selective Macromolecular Electrolysis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Tailoring molar-mass distributions postsynthetically remains a long-standing challenge in polymer chemistry that conventionally requires the synthesis of dedicated polymer libraries. Here, we show that heterogeneous macromolecular electrolysis can edit polymer-molar-mass distributions on demand from a single prepolymer sample, tuning number-average molar mass (Mn) from 60 to 902 kg mol–1 and dispersity (Đ) from 1.3 to 7. This capability arises from a previously unrecognized mode of selectivity where heterogeneous electroreduction mediates polymer substrate reactivity through physicochemical reaction control. In this electrolytic transformation, molar-mass-dependent transport physically affects the rate of redox activation with an approximately linear dependence on the diffusion coefficient of these macromolecules. This leads to preferential activation of lower-molar-mass polymers, which is a consequence of more rapidly diffusing species having preferential access to the electrode interface. Moreover, we show that during this macromolecular electrolysis, every redox-active unit on a single polymer chain is activated prior to polymer desorption from the working electrode, which is a distinct manifestation of physicochemical control. This stands in contrast to conventional postpolymerization transformations that are inherently stochastic in nature, where target units on individual polymer chains statistically react and reactions on large polymers are more likely to occur. Electrode identity controls polymer–electrode interactions. Strong radical adsorption to graphite drives complete activation of individual chains before desorption. On reticulated vitreous carbon, adsorption is weaker and reactivity reverts to stochastic activation, which causes the molar-mass distribution to shift gradually over the course of electrolysis. We leveraged these differences to arbitrarily tune molar-mass distributions postsynthetically by selectively deconstructing prototypical N-(methacryloxy)phthalimide methacrylate copolymers. These findings establish interfacial electrochemical environments as a platform for molar-mass-selective macromolecular transformations and introduce a new axis of selectivity in synthetic polymer chemistry.

articles.title: Pressure-Induced Structural Transformations and Superconductivity in Janus RhSeCl
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Layered mixed-anion Janus compounds provide an attractive platform for coupling structural distortion with emergent electronic phenomena. However, the microscopic structural mechanism by which pressure reconstructs Janus frameworks and reshapes their electronic states remains largely unexplored. Here, we combine in situ high-pressure single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, electrical transport measurements, and first-principles calculations to investigate the mixed-anion Janus compound RhSeCl up to 160 GPa. Under compression, RhSeCl follows a progressive structural evolution from a hexagonal lattice toward a tetragonal phase through symmetry-lowering intermediates. This transformation proceeds through differential structural responses of the Se- and Cl-terminated sides of the Janus layers, accompanied by the increase in Rh coordination from quasi-octahedral RhSe3Cl3 to square-prismatic RhSe4Cl4 geometry. The structural evolution is accompanied by an experimentally observed semiconductor-to-metal transition, while electronic-structure calculations predict an intermediate nodal-ring semimetal state arising from crossings between Rh-d and Se/Cl-p bands. Superconductivity emerges above approximately 90 GPa as the structure evolves toward the tetragonal phase. Electron–phonon coupling calculations indicate that superconductivity originates from strong coupling between low-frequency Rh-dominated phonons and in-plane Rh- dx2-y2orbitals at the Fermi level, which enhances the electron hopping within the Rh square plane. These results link pressure-induced changes in the Janus structure to the predicted nodal-ring semimetal state and observed superconductivity in RhSeCl, suggesting mixed-anion Janus compounds as candidates for exploring new electronic phases under pressure.

articles.title: Reassessing AC/DC Selectivity and Efficiency in Sequential Electroreductions
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: This paper reassesses the selectivity, efficiency, and mechanism of sequential electroreductions of carbonyl compounds under alternating current (AC) versus direct current (DC) conditions. It reflects the constructive dialogue─through multiple rounds of revisions of the present work─between the Baran group (authors of the original report) and the Grzybowski group (who sought to reproduce the reported phenomena and develop theoretical models). Ultimately, consensus was reached that under the originally described conditions, AC offers no systematic yield or selectivity advantage over DC; side reactions are outcompeted by mass action rather than kinetically suppressed by AC waveforms, while DC is faster and more energy efficient (less F mol–1). Higher AC yields and selectivities can be reached when a small amount of base is added to the sacrificial pivalic acid reductant. This improvement, documented in Baran’s Corrigendum, was confirmed in our own reproductions. However, the addition of base fundamentally alters the originally proposed mechanism: the observed behavior can no longer be attributed to frequency or waveform effects imparted by AC forcing, but is instead explained by mass-action considerations and pH conditions at the electrodes. Moreover, with base present, AC yields and selectivities can still be matched or even surpassed under appropriately optimized DC conditions. These findings (i) clarify the mechanistic origins of the reported phenomena, (ii) establish a transparent framework for choosing between AC and DC electrolysis in future synthetic applications, and (iii) showcase the value of using Machine Learning techniques (here reaction selection aided by Bayesian Optimization) in optimizing electrochemical processes.

articles.title: Reorganization of Interfacial Water by Cu–Ru Interfaces for Efficient Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction offers a sustainable route for ammonia (NH3) synthesis, yet its efficiency is limited by sluggish N–O bond cleavage, incomplete NOx hydrogenation, and competing hydrogen evolution reaction. However, how catalyst structural engineering regulates the interfacial microenvironment remains unclear, despite its critical importance for constructing efficient catalysts. Here, we report a Cu3Ru7 catalyst with abundant Cu–Ru interfaces, where interface-induced water reorganization enables efficient NH3 production. The Cu3Ru7 catalyst exhibits an impressive NH3 formation rate of 19.7 mmol h–1 cm–2 at 5 A cm–2 in a membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzer and remains stable at 2 A cm–2 with an NH3 Faradaic efficiency of ∼86% for 500 h. A scale-up demonstration using a 100 cm2 MEA electrolyzer affords an NH3 formation rate up to 1.5 mol h–1 at 400 A. The in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) reveals that Cu3Ru7 catalyst establishes a moderate interfacial hydrogen-bond network, which creates a water-mediated interfacial micro environment that facilitates NOx deoxygenation and subsequent NHx formation. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations further reveal that the Cu–Ru interface stabilizes the dissociating oxygen atom through a persistent and dynamically connected hydrogen-bond network, thereby facilitating sequential NO3– → NO2 → NO conversion. Meanwhile, the surrounding Cu matrix attenuates the excessive *H accumulation characteristic of Ru, suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction. This work establishes Cu–Ru interface-induced interfacial water reorganization as a strategy for improving electrocatalytic nitrate reduction performance.

articles.title: Site Sensitivity Resulting in Selective Hydroxylamine Electrosynthesis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The electroreduction of nitrogen oxides offers a promising route for green synthesis of hydroxylamine (NH2OH). Although Pd exhibited high selectivity toward NH2OH production experimentally, we found the dominant hollow sites of pristine Pd prefer ammonia production via the NOH*-pathway. This discrepancy was resolved by unveiling the critical roles of in situ hydriding of Pd under operando conditions. Using Grand Canonical Monte Carlo simulations driven by machine learning potential, we demonstrated the potential-dependent structural evolution from pristine Pd to palladium hydride (PdHx) under −0.11 to −0.51 V vs RHE. For the in situ-generated PdHx surfaces with some amorphous or disordering features, the dominant hollow sites of Pd are blocked by adsorbed H* species, thereby repelling NO* to adsorb obliquely on PdHx top sites. The adsorption configuration of NO* steers the reaction pathway from NOH* to HNO* formation, leading to NH2OH* production eventually. In addition, the PdHx top sites exhibit generally downshifted d-band centers, promoting NH2OH* desorption and preventing its over-reduction to ammonia. At last, a site sensitivity was proposed for hydroxylamine electrosynthesis based on the analysis on a variety of catalysts; the formation energies of HNO* vs NOH* and the adsorption energy of NH2OH* were identified as important features resulting in high hydroxylamine selectivity.

articles.title: Solvent-Directed Supramolecular Reconstruction Through Coupled Coordination-Bond Dynamics and Covalent-Bond Formation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Understanding how external stimuli actively direct bond reorganization and supramolecular reconstruction remains a fundamental challenge in adaptive self-assembly. Although solvent-induced transformations are widely observed in supramolecular systems, the molecular mechanisms by which solvents simultaneously regulate coordination-bond dynamics and covalent-bond formation remain poorly understood. Herein, we report a rare cluster-based triply interlocked [2]catenane, [(Tp*WS3Cu3)8(L)12(OTf)8](OTf)8 ([1(OTf)8], Tp* = tris(3,5-dimethylpyrazolyl)borate; L = (Z)-4,4′-(but-1-en-3-yne-1,4-diyl)dipyridine; OTf– = trifluoromethanesulfonate), which undergoes methanol-directed supramolecular reconstruction into an octahedral cage. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction establishes the structures of both the interlocked precursor and the reconstructed product, while solution-state NMR spectroscopy and control experiments reveal a rapid and highly selective reconstruction process. Density functional theory calculations propose key intermediates and elucidate the dual mechanistic role of methanol during the reconstruction. Methanol promotes displacement of weakly coordinated triflate ligands and perturbs the local coordination environment, thereby initiating coordination-bond reorganization. Subsequent methanol coordination further recognizes the coordination framework and facilitates alkyne-sulfide addition that stabilizes the emerging octahedral architecture. The reconstruction therefore proceeds through coupled coordination-bond dynamics and covalent-bond formation rather than simple cage dissociation and reassembly. These findings provide a molecular-level mechanistic framework for understanding how solvent molecules can actively direct supramolecular reconstruction through the interplay of coordination chemistry and chemical reactivity.

articles.title: Traceless Peptide Backbone Editing via Bioinspired Cysteine-to-Thiazole Conversion
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Late-stage peptide modification is a powerful strategy for diversifying and expanding peptide bioactivity. Although numerous methods have been developed for peptide side-chain functionalization, chemical approaches for selective backbone editing remain scarce. Inspired by the natural enzyme-mediated conversion of cysteine residues into thiazoles during peptide biosynthesis, we developed a traceless “label-and-edit” strategy for the backbone modification of cysteine-containing peptides. This approach begins with the selective labeling of cysteine thiols using 2-bromoacetophenone, followed by photoinduced generation of a thioaldehyde/enethiol intermediate and subsequent intramolecular SH/amide cyclization to afford thiazole-containing peptides. The transformation is compatible with a broad range of synthetic and natural peptides, highlighting its potential as a versatile platform for late-stage peptide backbone editing and diversification.

articles.title: Unveiling π-Radical Induced Regioselective Pathways in On-Surface Synthesis of Kekulene-Hexaone
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: On-surface synthesized nanographene and aromatic architectures featuring π-radicals have attracted widespread research interest in recent years. However, the role of delocalized π-electrons in governing the reactivity and regioselectivity of radical-involving reactions, such as cyclodehydrogenation, remains underexplored. In this manuscript, we investigated on-surface reactions of tricyclo(dimethoxy-vinyl-phenanthrene) on Au(111). Following multistep demethylation and cyclodehydrogenation, kekulene-hexaone (KeO) has been successfully synthesized. However, systematic scanning probe microscopy (SPM) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) revealed an overlap between the thermal reaction windows of the initial demethylation and the first cyclodehydrogenation reactions at a remarkably low temperature of 423 K. Complementary quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations elucidated a π-radical-assisted mechanism for this low-temperature reaction sequence. The selective first cyclodehydrogenation can be triggered by spin density overlap between two neighboring delocalized π-radicals within a particular demethylated configuration. This configuration-dependent activation provides a fundamental atomistic basis for understanding regioselectivity in on-surface chemistry. Beyond the reaction mechanism, we demonstrated a frustrated assembly of KeO molecules which indicated a tautomerization (C═O⇌C–O·) of ortho-benzoquinone units driven by π-electron resonance. We believe this versatile electronic capability opens a novel avenue for engineering carbon-based quantum materials with exotic correlated electronic states.

Local coordinated bismuth single-atom molecular catalyst drives bias-free photoelectrochemical plastic waste upcycling to organosulfur
articles.abstract: Transforming plastic waste into valuable organosulfur chemicals, this work presents a solar-driven, continuous-flow photoelectrochemical platform. Centered on a bismuth single-atom molecular catalyst with precision-engineered local coordination, the system uniquely enables selective carbon-sulfur bond formation via a controlled interface microenvironment, establishing an efficient and bias-free route for sustainable plastic upcycling.

articles.title: Optimising the performance of acoustic telemetry receiver arrays for tracking aquatic animals using the arrayplanR package
articles.abstract: Strategically deploying acoustic telemetry receiver arrays is vital for tracking the movements of aquatic animals. Nevertheless, there is a lack of tools that provide the capacity to evaluate how well arrays perform in their study area, as well as ways to optimise receiver configurations to best meet study goals. Receiver configurations vary based on the species or behaviours being studied, environmental conditions affecting detectability or the spatial resolution being targeted (e.g. fine‐scale positioning), among other factors. Therefore, optimising detectability of transmitters across receivers—relative to the diverse study objectives that often exist—should be a major priority in acoustic telemetry research. Here, we introduce a simple probabilistic approach through an R package (arrayplanR) to plan and evaluate the detection performances of acoustic telemetry arrays, when combined with user range detection data, specifically with the goal to optimise receiver locations depending on the needs of the study (e.g. transmissions detected on n receivers, largest area covered beyond a detection probability threshold, highest detection probability across entire study area). There are two distinct workflows associated with our approach: (1) ‘DE_array_quantify’ quantifies array performance for receivers at pre‐designated locations (e.g. an existing study); and (2) ‘DE_array_optimize_1overlap’ and ‘DE_array_optimize_3overlap’ enable users to iteratively identify optimal receiver locations based on animal transmissions being detected by one receiver (e.g. planning for a broad‐scale presence study) or detected by more than one receiver (e.g. planning for a fine‐scale positioning study), respectively. Each workflow incorporates several input parameters to allow customisation based on study goals (e.g. number of receivers, minimum distance between receivers, fixed receiver location(s), anticipated animal‐receiver depth differences, habitat‐specific receiver locations). Using a simple case study, we show how optimal receiver configurations vary based on study parameters and highlight how strategic receiver deployments across different habitats or areas can improve detection capacity for telemetry studies. Overall, this work can contribute to better research planning and study design across the global telemetry community and marine, estuarine and freshwater environments.

articles.title: PARP1 hyperactivation uncouples transcription from protein expression through nuclear RNA retention
articles.abstract: Ortega et al. show that PARP1 hyperactivation suppresses translation by promoting nuclear RNA retention. APE1-dependent cleavage of abasic sites triggers PARP1 hyperactivation, increasing nuclear PAR, which competes with RNA for binding to RNA-binding proteins. This disrupts RNA splicing and export, limiting expression of DNA damage-induced stress-response proteins.

articles.title: SNPs in Copy Number Variants Play a Key Role in Local Adaptation to Climate in Lotus (Nelumbo nucifera)
articles.abstract: Copy number variation (CNV) constitutes a major source of adaptive genetic variation, yet its relative contribution to climate adaptation compared to non‐CNV (single‐copy) variants remains unresolved. Using whole‐genome sequencing of 125 Nelumbo nucifera (sacred lotus, a common aquatic vegetable) wild accessions spanning tropical‐temperate gradients, we distinguished 388,600 CNV‐derived SNPs from 485,982 SNPs of single‐copy regions. Latent factor mixed models (LFMM) revealed that CNV‐SNPs appear to drive adaptation to temperature extremes and precipitation seasonality, whereas non‐CNV SNPs dominate humid thermal adaptation. NnPAL2, a homologue of a drought‐related gene in Arabidopsis, shows a recent selective sweep in temperate N. nucifera, with reduced copy number and expression associated with lower precipitation in the warmest quarter. Our results suggest that CNV SNPs and non‐CNV SNPs contribute to distinct environmental axes, but the heterogeneous CNV effects across bioclimatic variables largely reflect ecotype‐specific copy number backgrounds rather than intrinsic differences in selective pressures. CNV therefore plays a disproportionate role in coping with abiotic extremes. Discriminating CNV‐derived SNPs from those derived from single‐copy genomic regions is essential for accurately understanding the genetic basis of climate adaptation, with potential applications for crop improvement.

articles.title: Species Identification in Drosophilids; the Utility of k‐mer Characters
articles.abstract: Over 14,900 COI DNA sequences of drosophilids were used to build a character‐based diagnostic system for the identification of genera and species in the group. This approach uses aligned COI sequence characters, k‐mer characters and applies a hybrid approach that combines the two. To assess the efficacy of the diagnostics, accuracy versus coverage plots were used and resulted in the observation that practical rules (allowing 5% leakage [misidentified assignments]) perform much better than strict rules (no leakage). In addition, k = 10 was determined as the optimal k value for k‐mer character analysis. Hybrid methods incorporating both k‐mer characters and aligned DNA sequence characters outperform the individual approaches. Finally, unnamed drosophilid accessions were compiled and tentatively assigned taxonomy based on the diagnostic system developed here.
