We found broad dose-dependent performance improvements of set shifting indexing cognitive flexibility, visual search indexing selective attention, antisaccade performance indexing inhibitory control, visuospatial maze learning, and temporal order serial object learning, while working memory span was non-systematically modulated. In addition, the M4 PAM reduced effort avoidance in an effort-based choice task documenting a pro-motivational effect. Task-composite performance scores showed pro-cognitive effects across multiple doses and an effective dose range for individual subjects in the absence of adverse dose-limiting cholinergic side effects. Together, the broad pro-cognitive and pro-motivational multi-task profile of M4 PAM modulation suggests that the M4 receptor is a master regulator of executive cognitive functioning, possibly acting on domain-general neural processes across the prefrontal-striatal circuits.

articles.title: Chemosensory receptor copy number evolution is not associated with host-plant specialization in butterflies
articles.abstract: Chemoreception plays an important role in how insects sense their environment and interact with other organisms. One important ecological role for chemosensory receptors is sensing chemical compounds to locate suitable host plants. Host-plant use is therefore expected to influence insect sensory system evolution as host-plant preferences changes and species become more generalized or specialized. Yet it remains unclear if species that are generalists require a larger chemosensory receptor repertoire. Here, we investigated the relationship between host-plant specialization and the evolution of olfactory receptor (OR) and gustatory receptor (GR) gene families across 87 butterfly species spanning six families. We annotated OR and GR repertoires and used phylogenetic comparative analyses to test whether receptor copy-number was associated with specialist versus generalist host-use strategies or with host-plant breadth. In addition, we reconstructed evolutionary transitions between generalist and specialist strategies and tested whether these transitions were associated with expansions or contractions in gene-family size. We found that OR and GR repertoire size did not differ between specialists and generalists, nor was it correlated with the number of host-plant families used by a species. We also did not find associations between gene family expansions or contractions and transitions between generalist and specialist strategies. Overall, we find that host-plant specialization is not associated with chemosensory receptor repertoire size across butterflies. We suggest that host-plant chemosensory adaptation may depend on other changes such as receptor tuning, expression differences, or changes in specific receptor lineages not captured by our analyses.

articles.title: Coarse-graining genome-scale metabolic models for dynamic, multi-scale simulations of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in gel environments
articles.abstract: Microbial communities are shaped by coupled interactions between microenvironment conditions and the intracellular adaptations that emerge in response external metabolic cues. For pathogenic microbes such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa , these interactions can rapidly generate heterogeneous sub-populations that exhibit adaptations for sustaining host infection and resisting antibiotic treatment. Technological strides in -omics data collection, combined with robust computational tools like genome-scale metabolic models (GEM) for predicting cellular metabolism, have yielded promising multi-scale depictions of microbial population development in simulated spatial environments. These multi-scale model simulations help establish and evaluate mechanistic contexts for how infection-enhancing behaviors might emerge in the population or be influenced by variable perturbations in the biological system. However, the number and rigorous tuning of parameters influencing the connections between intracellular-extracellular events pose barriers when shaping simulations to different in vitro systems of interest. In this work, we present a genome-scale, metabolism-informed continuum model (GEM-CM), a computational framework for coupling a reaction-diffusion model to a surrogate GEM representation that generates metabolic rate predictions informed by flux balance analysis outputs. A key feature of GEM-CM is its application of random forest regression, or ensembles, to coarse-grain the interface connecting the GEM and reaction-diffusion models down to a small set of input metabolites methodically chosen through the random forest’s evaluation of feature importance. To demonstrate GEM-CM’s utility, we evaluated simulation predictions against P. aeruginosa PA14 populations radially propagating in low weight percentage agar gels. In addition to biomass growth, we simulated PA14 populations producing the cytotoxic secondary metabolite pyocyanin (PCN). GEM-CM could capture PA14 growth dynamics in agar gels when ensembles were provided with three carbon source inputs describing the simulated growth media. Bacterial motility parameters and the random forest ensemble allowed GEM-CM simulations to accurately predict spatial biomass distributions for PA14 populations over time and probe their PCN production dynamics. Ensembles also demonstrated robust performance for single gene knockout conditions with GEM-CM simulation accurately capturing the partial or total biomass and PCN inhibition observed in transposon mutant screenings. When evaluating transposon mutant population development, the GEM-CM framework additionally suggested that metH may be a promising target to inhibit the spatial propagation of PA14. This work’s proof-of-concept applications illustrated GEM-CM utility as an early stage multi-scale modeling tool for interrogating in vitro metabolic behavior in microbial populations.

articles.title: Compositional computations in the primate frontal cortex
articles.abstract: A hallmark of intelligence is the ability to apply familiar operations to new inputs without relearning. How neural circuits carry a learned computation into states never visited during training remains unclear. Here we combined neural recordings, circuit modeling and human experiments to investigate compositional generalization. Monkeys learned to combine a start location with a displacement specified by the direction and duration of an optic-flow stimulus, then encountered novel combinations of these familiar inputs. Frontal population activity separated the computation into spatial and temporal components: start location and flow direction established the neural state, from which activity evolved along shared timing dynamics. Novel combinations elicited accurate responses when trajectories maintained this organization, whereas departures predicted systematic behavioral biases. Circuit models revealed a three-way alignment problem: input representations, recurrent dynamics and readout operations must jointly implement the required computation. Mismatches produced systematic biases that increased with distance from trained conditions. Humans exhibited similar biases when familiar sensory cues and spatial transformations were linked through an unfamiliar mapping. Together, these findings show how the coordination of reusable neural resources supports new computations, and how its disruption produces predictable failures of generalization.

articles.title: Concussion decreases brain signal variability
articles.abstract: Sports-related concussion represents a major public health concern, with millions of cases diagnosed annually. Despite significant methodological advances in functional brain imaging, a clinically meaningful neuroimaging biomarker of concussion has yet to be established. This may be due in part to a reliance on traditional measures. For example, approaches examining mean activation across trials reduce responses to a single measure of central tendency and therefore fail to capture important individual differences. In contrast, blood oxygenation level dependent (BOLD) variability offers a promising new approach to measuring brain function, Specifically, it captures individual differences in the temporal variability in the BOLD signal over time. Further, it is sensitive to neural, vascular, and neurovascular coupling changes that accompany concussion. We collected baseline (prior to injury) and post-concussion (within 48 hours of injury) neuroimaging data in 56 collegiate athletes. Within this longitudinal dataset, we investigated changes in BOLD variability across multiple spatial scales. In addition, we examined their relationships with self-reported symptoms and cognitive performance. As expected, symptoms increased following concussion while computerized cognitive performance declined. BOLD variability decreased from baseline to post-concussion, particularly in the somatomotor and language networks. Moreover, changes in BOLD variability were related to changes in symptom reporting and cognitive performance. Together, these findings advance our understanding of how concussion affects brain function and highlight BOLD signal variability as a promising biomarker to aid ongoing efforts to improve the diagnosis and treatment of sports-related concussion.

articles.title: Confidence: Its Measurement, Relation to Behavior, and Neural Representation
articles.abstract: Confidence (certainty/uncertainty about one's own decision) has attracted considerable attention in psychology, neuroscience, and artificial intelligence. Yet its relation to behavior remains unclear: Some treat confidence as a cause of behavior whereas others view it as a state controlled by environmental variables. The unobservable nature of confidence makes its measurement validation and analyses difficult. To tackle these issues, we developed a novel procedure combining a decision-making task, risk choices, and a post-task open-ended questionnaire. Point-gain/loss amounts for correct/incorrect decisions varied depending on choices between high-risk/high-return and low-risk/low-return. In the questionnaire, 90% of 16 participants reported feelings interpretable as certainty/uncertainty when making those risk choices despite no instruction about confidence, whereas 8% did so when the choices led to identical outcomes/returns. This suggests confidence is a state controlled by environmental contingencies rather than a cause of behavior. We also decoded changes in the state from electroencephalography and functional magnetic resonance imaging.

articles.title: Contrasting Range and Demographic Histories in two Palearctic Dragonfly Species (Odonata: Anisoptera)
articles.abstract: Climatic suitability is often used to infer historical range changes, yet whether suitable area predicts effective population size remains unexplored. We investigated this relationship in two Palearctic dragonflies with contrasting ecologies: Somatochlora arctica, a widespread peatland specialist, and S. meridionalis, a southern European species associated with shaded streams. We combined demographic reconstructions from individual reference genomes using the pairwise sequentially Markovian coalescent (PSMC), maximum entropy (MaxEnt) species distribution models projected across six paleoclimatic intervals spanning approximately 3.3 million years, and ancestral state reconstructions of peatland specialization. Predicted suitable area was consistently greater for S. arctica, reaching its greatest extent during the Last Glacial Maximum. However, its inferred effective population size was smaller than that of S. meridionalis for most of the last ~275,000 years. Ancestral reconstructions placed the most probable gain of peatland specialization in the S. arctica lineage (Clade I) during the late Miocene, with a median age of 9.4 million years, predating the modeled climatic intervals. These findings indicate a decoupling of climatic suitability and demographic history. Patchy breeding habitat, population structure, and the isolated Scottish origin of the sampled S. arctica may contribute to this mismatch. Combining genomic, ecological, and phylogenetic approaches provides complementary insights into historical biogeography and highlights the limitations of interpreting suitable climate as available breeding habitat or using individual genomes to characterize species-wide demographic histories. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: Decoding the molecular cues regulating the transition of Influenza virus polymerase from transcriptase to replicase.
articles.abstract: Influenza virus polymerase (FluPol) dynamically transitions between distinct conformational states to coordinate viral gene transcription and genome replication. While vRNP-associated monomeric FluPol supports transcription, ANP32-dependent asymmetric and ANP32-independent symmetric polymerase dimers mediate genome and antigenome (vRNA/cRNA) replication. How FluPol coordinates these distinct functional states to maintain the transcription-replication balance remains poorly understood. Here, we identify and characterize interdomain interactions within PB2 that govern the stability of the replication-competent conformation of FluPol. Specifically, a highly conserved salt bridge between PB2 Mid-E282 and NLS-K752 stabilizes the replicase conformation, while the charge state of residue 627 (E or K) dictates ANP32 engagement, together coordinating polymerase dimerization and replication activity. Strikingly, bat influenza A viruses H17N10 and H18N11 harbor unconventional serine substitutions at both positions, compromising polymerase dimerization, ANP32 interaction, and vRNA/cRNA replication. Remarkably, introducing these bat-signature substitutions (E282S/K627S) into human H1N1 polymerase results in phosphorylation at both positions in human cells. These findings suggest that phosphorylation can partially compensate for the loss of negative charge at these residues, revealing a phosphomimetic adaptation mechanism that modulates polymerase conformational dynamics and function. Collectively, our study reveals how a conserved interdomain interaction within PB2 regulates conformational transitions and transcription-replication balance of FluPol, which might have been driven by phosphomimetic adaptations during the course of a diverse range of influenza virus evolution.

articles.title: Deducing splicing events from transcript sets with splicelogic
articles.abstract: Long-read RNA sequencing captures a greater proportion of full-length transcripts, enabling more accurate isoform identification, discovery of novel isoforms, and more precise differential transcript usage analysis. However, comparing transcripts, whether between conditions or between sets such as novel and annotated isoforms, yields complex isoform changes that are hard to manipulate, summarize, and visualize. This is compounded by vertical integration of some tools, where downstream analysis depends on the specific output of a particular upstream tool. To address this gap, we have developed splicelogic, an R/Bioconductor package that makes transcript-set comparisons biologically interpretable by turning them into discrete splicing events, such as exon skipping, alternative splice sites, intron retention, and alternative transcription start and end sites. We designed splicelogic to integrate easily with existing RNA-seq workflows and tools. The splicelogic functions are modular, readable, and extensible, making it easy for users to adapt core logic to their own custom scientific questions or novel splicing definitions. By obtaining interpretable splicing events from transcript changes, splicelogic enables downstream analyses, including annotation of RNA-binding protein recognition sites, alongside summary statistics and visualization. The splicelogic package is publicly available and distributed through Bioconductor.

articles.title: Deprivation of dietary fiber promotes low-grade neuroinflammation and anxiety-like behavior in mice
articles.abstract: Background: Intestinal health is an important determinant of brain function in that an array of gut perturbants, especially those targeting microbiota, influence behavior. Fermentable dietary fiber nourishes gut microbiota and, consequently, promotes gut health. We hypothesized that depriving mice of fermentable dietary fiber would impact their brain and behavior. Methods: Male C57BL/6J mice were fed standard grain-based chow (GBC), a compositionally defined diet (CDD) which mimics macronutrient content of GBC but lacks fermentable fiber, or CDD supplemented with the fermentable fiber inulin (CDD+INU). Mice were subjected to behavioral testing 6-8 weeks later followed by analysis of the gut brain axis. Results: Relative to GBC-fed mice, CDD-fed mice exhibited low-grade gut inflammation and a reduction in open-field center exploration, signaling heightened anxiety-like behavior. CDD+INU fully reversed these abnormalities arguing they were a consequence of fiber deprivation. Analysis of the gut microbiome and serum metabolome showed that CDD+INU increased oxidative phosphorylation and immune suppressive metabolites. Flow cytometric and transcriptomic analyses of the brain revealed an array of pro-inflammatory alterations in myeloid cells, CD4+ T-cells, microglia and astrocytes in mice fed CDD but not CDD+INU. Most notably, microglia and astrocytes from mice fed CDD, but not CDD+INU, displayed reduced mitochondrial respiration and greater glycolytic activity. CDD, but not CDD+INU consumption also reduced the abundance of oligodendrocytes and neurons, and increased hippocampal pro-inflammatory gene expression. Conclusions: Deprivation of fermentable fiber results in coordinated changes in brain immune composition and glial metabolic state that is associated with increased anxiety-like behavior.

articles.title: Development of a Pan-Proteome Multi-Epitope Vaccine Candidate Against Nipah Virus Using Reverse Vaccinology and Immunoinformatics Approaches
articles.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a high-consequence zoonotic pathogen for which no licensed human vaccine is currently available. This study applied a consensus-guided pan-proteome immunoinformatics framework to design and prioritize a multi-epitope vaccine candidate using sequence information from all nine NiV proteins. A total of 901 NiV protein sequences were retrieved, of which 842 passed quality filtering and were processed through clustering, multiple-sequence alignment, and protein-specific consensus generation. Consensus-derived fragments were screened for cytotoxic T-lymphocyte, helper T-lymphocyte, and B-cell epitopes, followed by multi-criterion filtering based on antigenicity, allergenicity, toxicity, conservancy, class-specific immune-response properties, and human-proteome similarity. Ten epitope-selection strategies were combined with two adjuvant candidates and three construct architectures to generate 60 vaccine constructs. Shortlisted candidates were subsequently evaluated for physicochemical properties, HLA population coverage, structural characteristics, conformational B-cell epitopes, TLR3 docking, molecular dynamics, immune-response simulation, and expression-oriented optimization. VC033_V6_BD_L03 construct was prioritized as the lead candidate and showed combined predicted population coverage of 99.78% worldwide and 99.96% in South Asia. Docking against human TLR3 structure 1ZIW yielded a ClusPro score of -1624.8. During a 100-ns molecular-dynamics simulation, the complex underwent early conformational reorganization followed by lower late-phase structural variation and persistent interchain hydrogen bonding. MM/GBSA analysis yielded a mean interaction-energy estimate of -20.52, 15.42 kcal/mol. C-ImmSim predicted coordinated humoral and cellular responses, while codon optimization generated a 1,539-bp expression sequence compatible with virtual cloning into pET-28a(+). These analyses prioritize VC033_V6_BD_L03 as a consensus-derived, pan-proteome NiV multi-epitope vaccine candidate for experimental evaluation of expression, immunogenicity, safety, and protective efficacy.

articles.title: Developmental interactions between oscillatory and spontaneous neural activity support improvements in inhibitory control from adolescence into adulthood
articles.abstract: Adolescence is a critical period of development marked by improvements in cognitive control driven by maturation of executive brain systems. Neural mechanisms supporting inhibitory control (the ability to suppress a prepotent response in favor of generating a goal-directed response) mature into adulthood in parallel with refinements in frequency-specific neural oscillations and broadband spontaneous activity, supporting more accurate and reliable performance on response inhibition tasks, such as the antisaccade oculomotor task. Prior work has established that the maturation of neural circuitry contributes to age-related decreases in spontaneous activity, supporting higher-fidelity transmission of task-relevant activity, such as frequency-specific neural oscillations, which are crucial for antisaccade performance. Using longitudinal electroencephalography (EEG) data from 146 participants (72 F, ages 10-34, 253 total sessions) collected while participants performed an antisaccade task, we sought to understand the interplay between frontal oscillatory and spontaneous activity during cognitive processing and how it supports developmental improvements in inhibitory control. We found that spontaneous activity decreased developmentally during the preparation of an inhibitory response, and that this was associated with reduced trial-to-trial variability in response latency, indicating that reductions in spontaneous activity may increase the reliability of inhibitory control processing. Furthermore, performance-related decreases in broadband spontaneous activity were associated with the suppression of preparatory high-beta oscillations in an age-dependent manner, such that this relationship became more pronounced through development. Together, these results illustrate how developmental enhancements in the coordination of frequency-specific oscillations and spontaneous activity during inhibitory response preparation support developmental improvements in inhibitory control, providing a potential mechanism through which inhibitory control becomes more accurate and reliable from adolescence into adulthood.

articles.title: Disparities in avian genomic resources highlight gaps across the Global South
articles.abstract: Avian genomes have proliferated rapidly in recent years while expanding our knowledge of genomic evolution. However, evaluating bird sampling across the tree of life and across their distributions is necessary to assess their contributions to global bird diversity and diversification patterns. We evaluated all available avian genome assemblies across geography, taxonomy, conservation status, and time. The 1,712 species with at least one genome assembly represent only ~15% of recognized avian diversity. Although all orders were represented, 24 bird families (all restricted to the Global South) lacked any genome assembly, and only ~37% (N= 2,397) of recognized genera had genomic representation. Nearly 78% of the most evolutionarily distinct and globally endangered (EDGE) lineages lacked a genome. Genomic resources are concentrated in temperate regions of the Global North, whereas species-rich tropical regions in Africa, South America, and Southeast Asia remain severely underrepresented relative to their diversity. Even after accounting for conservation status, evolutionary distinctiveness, and ecology, Global South species had roughly fourfold lower odds of having a genome than Global North species. Notably, the post-2021 surge in genome sequencing has counter-intuitively widened this gap. Together, our results highlight persistent gaps in genomic resources across the Global South and the need to collectively address these global knowledge gaps via collaborative efforts.

articles.title: Distributed Network Sensing as an Escape Strategy
articles.abstract: The response of a swarm of ants or birds, living tissue of cells, or a robotic swarm, to spatial signals from the environment as a whole is a fundamental challenge for these decentralized systems. A promising alternative is embodied distributed sensing and decision-making, so that local environmental cues directly shape coordinated reconfiguration, growth, or movement without centralized control. Fluidic networks offer a physical basis for such systems, yet existing implementations are predesigned and limited in their ability to process spatial information across extended systems. Here, we investigate how fluid transport networks enable environmental sensing and adaptive response using the slime mould Physarum polycephalum. By exposing Physarum vein networks to dynamic pH environments, we show that the organism's ability to respond to aversive stimuli is governed by its spatial extent and network connectivity. Above a certain size, organisms with network morphology reliably detect and escape harmful conditions by network reconfiguration, whereas disconnected or spatially confined organisms fail to respond. In environments with competing stimuli, network morphologies enable integration of spatial information and repositioning into favorable regions. We identify local contractions as a physical mechanism that drives fluid redistribution and converts local stimulation into system-level responses. Finally, we generate different morphologies using fluidic and electrochemical control, demonstrating large-scale adaptation to complex environments. These results establish distributed fluidic networks as a framework for integrated sensing and actuation, providing design principles for autonomous soft robotic systems in dynamic environments.

articles.title: Elevated precontractile calcium set point is sustained by limited PMCA1 export in dystrophic muscle
articles.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is caused by loss of dystrophin and marked by elevated muscle calcium, usually attributed to contraction-induced membrane damage. Whether calcium rises before muscle can contract, and what sustains it, is unresolved. In Caenorhabditis elegans embryos and patient-derived human myoblasts, dystrophic muscle carries an elevated resting calcium set point before contraction is possible. Embryonic calcium is elevated 400 minutes after fertilization, before movement is detectable or the neuromuscular junction forms. Silencing the plasma membrane calcium pump gene mca-1 raises calcium in wild-type but not dystrophic animals, whereas silencing its paralogue raises it in both: the limitation is specific to that export route. Dystrophic human myoblasts have less pump; pump inhibition or silencing increases calcium preferentially in healthy cells, and raising pump expression lowers calcium most in dystrophic cells. Constrained calcium export is an early, continuing determinant of the dystrophic set point.

articles.title: Energetic and functional development of soil food webs along secondary succession
articles.abstract: 1. As ecosystems develop, aboveground biomass and belowground organic matter accumulate, while energy turnover declines. This trend is largely supported by vegetation studies, but remains unexplored for soil food webs that channel the majority of energy in terrestrial ecosystems. 2. Here, we tested whether successional theory applies to soil food webs across size-based compartments, ranging from microfauna (nematodes) to macrofauna (soil arthropods and earthworms), along a secondary succession in southwestern China, using an energy-flux approach. To assess whether forest restoration by planting follows natural succession, we also compared spruce and larch plantations with secondary birch forest of the same successional stage. 3. Supporting expectations of reduced energy turnover, the results showed an increasing animal biomass-to-energy flux ratio and a functional shift from herbivory-dominated (green) to detritivory-dominated (brown) energy channelling along succession. Soil food web compartments showed contrasting trends: macro-food webs shifted towards bacterial energy channels with decreasing predation, while micro-food webs maintained similar bacterial/fungal energy flux ratios and tended towards increasing predation. The larch plantation supported lower animal biomass than the secondary birch forest, whereas the spruce plantation did not differ. We further found that energy flux correlated positively with microbial biomass and soil animal diversity, but negatively with litter biomass during succession. 4. Overall, we expand successional theory by revealing the transformations in energy use and pathways within soil food webs along secondary succession, thereby advancing understanding of ecosystem functioning and guiding ecosystem restoration. Our results further suggest that tree plantations do not necessarily replicate the belowground development of natural succession, which should be considered in ecosystem restoration.

articles.title: Establishing an ex vivo platform for molecular profiling of skin structural cells using frozen human skin biopsies
articles.abstract: Skin structural cells, including keratinocytes, melanocytes, endothelial cells, and fibroblasts, play critical roles in the development of chronic inflammatory skin disease. Inflammatory stimuli induce transcriptional reprogramming and epigenetic changes in skin structural cells, which contribute to disease pathogenesis. Although two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) skin culture models have been widely used to investigate inflammatory responses in skin structural cells, ex vivo systems that maintain skin structure and cellular composition remain limited. To address this gap, we explored using frozen skin biopsies as an experimental platform to study the responses of skin structural cells to inflammatory stimuli. Using a simple air-liquid interface culture method on permeable Transwell inserts, we showed that viable skin structural cells that retain cell-type-specific transcriptional profiles can be recovered from frozen skin biopsies after prolonged in vitro culture. Stimulation with IFN-{gamma} induced robust transcriptional and chromatin accessibility changes that were largely resolved after stimulus removal, with transcriptional responses to secondary stimulation comparable to the primary stimulation. Treatment of cultured skin biopsies with histone-modifying enzyme inhibitors effectively altered global histone modification levels, but did not substantially affect the transcriptional resolution of IFN-{gamma}-induced responses. Collectively, these findings establish cryopreserved human skin biopsies as a scalable ex vivo platform that enables mechanistic studies of inflammatory responses of multiple populations of skin structural cells.

articles.title: Evolutionary dynamics of the pan-centromere architecture in oaks
articles.abstract: Centromeres ensure faithful chromosome segregation and genome stability, yet their DNA evolves rapidly, presenting a long-standing centromere paradox. Here we characterise the genomic and epigenomic architecture of >1,300 candidate centromeres from 111 high-quality Quercus (oak) genomes. We show that lineage-specific expansion of QuCEN146 satellite drives centromere turnover in oaks by displacing ancestral LTR-rich sequences into flanking regions, with genetic drift facilitating fixation of satellite-rich centromeres. Population-scale analyses in Q. serrata reveal extensive variation in satellite rich centromeres, generated by array expansion and contraction, strand-orientation shifts, and interspecific introgression. By contrast, LTR rich centromeres of Q. variabilis exhibit extremely low polymorphism and high collinearity across populations, sustained by suppressed local recombination, linked selection, and constrained LTR dynamics. We further demonstrate chromosome-independent evolutionary patterns for both satellite-rich and LTR-rich centromeres. Collectively, these findings demonstrate how evolutionary processes drive centromere turnover and shape contrasting centromeric sequence landscapes in forest trees.

articles.title: Examining urban weed response to elevated salt levels
articles.abstract: Stressors from the urban environment cause adverse effects on city-dwelling organisms. While there is evidence that some species are adapting to urban stressors, such as the urban heat island and impervious surfaces, other stressors such as road salt are less studied. We investigated whether plants are adapting to elevated salt concentrations with two common garden experiments using three common weed species: Veronica arvensis, Stellaria media, and Lamium purpureum. We collected plants from parks around Baltimore, MD, USA, collecting plant maternal lineages from roadside soils (i.e. higher soil salinity) and inner park soils (i.e. lower soil salinity). We hypothesized that roadside lineages would tolerate salt treatment better than park lineages. In our germination experiment on wild-collected seeds, we observed a non-significant trend where the germination rate of roadside L. purpureum lineages was reduced less by salt treatment than for park genetic lineages, while S. media had similar declines between groups. In our greenhouse experiment on the F1 generation, roadside V. arvensis lineages displayed a less adverse reaction to salt treatment than park V. arvensis lineages. L. purpureum did not display this difference, but roadside lineages of both species exhibited less tissue damage overall. The results of our experiments were likely influenced by the maternal environment, and work on F2 generations is required to confirm them. Our findings show some support for urban salt tolerance adaptation, and point to the heterogeneity of the urban environment and the complexity of plant reactions to salinity.

articles.title: FUSION PORE CLOSURE DETERMINES SUBQUANTAL KISS-AND-RUN SEROTONIN RELEASE FROM FULLY LOADED DENSE-CORE VESICLES
articles.abstract: During kiss-and-run exocytosis, a transient fusion pore opens, releases part of the vesicular quantum, and closes without full fusion. This report investigates two questions: first, whether dense-core vesicles undergoing kiss-and-run contain the same number of molecules as those undergoing full fusion; second, whether subquantal release results from pore closure or vesicle depletion. We analyzed amperometric recordings of extrasynaptic serotonin release from dense-core vesicles in cultured leech Retzius neurons. Full-fusion events released 91,585{+/-}34,428 molecules (n=14), whereas kiss-and-run events released 58,344{+/-}20,759 molecules, 64% of the quantum. We analyzed the biexponential dynamics of the filtered amperometric current using Ohmic equations for cylindrical and toroidal pores. Hydrated flux packing (HFP) independently estimated the minimum peak pore diameter from the number of hydrated serotonin molecules crossing the pore. Kiss-and-run peak diameters were 2.1 to 3.2 nm, corresponding to the passage of 4 to 10 hydrated molecules. The vesicular serotonin content of individual kiss-and-run events was estimated by a frozen pore extrapolation (FPE), in which pores were kept at the peak HFP diameter. FPE yielded 102,650{+/-}10,989 molecules per vesicle (n=15), similar to the quantum obtained by integrating full-fusion events. Therefore, kiss-and-run subquantal release did not reflect a smaller quantum. We then compared the decay of serotonin flux with that estimated through the frozen pore at its peak diameter. In every event, the flux decayed faster, reaching half its peak in 0.59 (0.23 to 0.95) of the time taken by the frozen pore flux. We conclude that subquantal release during kiss-and-run exocytosis is governed by fusion-pore closure rather than vesicle depletion.

articles.title: Galectin-9 drives thrombo-inflammatory circuits initiating venous thrombosis
articles.abstract: Background: Venous thromboembolism is increasingly recognized as a thrombo-inflammatory disease, yet the pathways linking inflammation to venous thrombus initiation remain incompletely defined. Galectin-9 (Gal-9), a {beta}-galactoside-binding lectin elevated in inflammatory disorders, has no defined role in venous thrombosis. Methods: Using plasma from patients with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), Gal-9-deficient mice, an inferior vena cava stenosis model, intravital microscopy, microfluidics, and ex vivo platelet and neutrophil assays, we assessed the functional contribution of Gal-9 to venous thrombosis. Results: Plasma Gal-9 was elevated in DVT patients, correlated with D-dimer at presentation, and declined over 3-month follow-up. Gal-9 deletion did not alter hemostasis but markedly impaired thrombus initiation, with reduced platelet and neutrophil recruitment to the vessel wall and reduced intra-thrombus neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation. TNF-/IFN-{gamma}-stimulated endothelial cells upregulated Gal-9 and promoted platelet adhesion and fibrin(ogen) deposition, which Gal-9 neutralization partially reversed. Under venous shear, immobilized recombinant Gal-9 potentiated platelet activation and thrombus formation, particularly alongside collagen, whereas Gal-9 inhibition suppressed these responses. Gal-9-activated platelets promoted NETosis and shifted thrombus composition toward a NET-rich inflammatory phenotype. Conclusions: Gal-9 is a previously unrecognized driver of venous thrombo-inflammation, linking vascular inflammation to platelet activation, NET formation, and thrombosis. Genetic deletion attenuated these responses in vivo, and antibody-mediated Gal-9 neutralization suppressed platelet activation and thrombus formation in vitro, identifying the Gal-9 glycan-binding pathway as a therapeutic target that disrupts thrombosis without impairing hemostasis.

articles.title: Generalizable sex differences in functional brain organization follow the cortical hierarchy in youth
articles.abstract: It remains unknown if sex differences in human functional connectivity follow a generalizable overarching principle. Here, we tested whether sex differences in functional connectivity during childhood and adolescence are organized along the sensorimotor-association (S-A) axis, a cortical hierarchy spanning unimodal sensorimotor to transmodal association cortex. We analyzed four large-scale, independent datasets of youth ages 5-23 years (total N = 3,355). Across datasets, males showed greater connectivity between functional networks, whereas females showed greater connectivity within networks, most prominently within the default mode network. More broadly, the sensorimotor and association ends of the S-A axis were more segregated in females and more integrated in males. This difference extended to macroscale cortical organization: the cortical hierarchy was expanded in females relative to males along the principal gradient of functional connectivity. Together, these findings identify the S-A axis as a generalizable organizing principle of sex differences in functional brain organization during youth.

articles.title: Generative 3D Spatial Reconstruction of Cellular Organization from Single Cell Expression
articles.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing profiles cellular states at scale but removes their three-dimensional (3D) spatial organization. Reconstructing this organization requires recovering not only individual cell positions but also the physical size, geometry, and neighborhoods of an entire tissue. Existing methods either map cells onto measured spatial references or reconstruct two-dimensional sections independently, leaving the joint reconstruction of a new 3D specimen unresolved. Moreover, predicting the average plausible position of each cell can reduce per-cell error while compressing tissue geometry. We introduce ORBIS, a generative framework that jointly reconstructs whole 3D specimens from single-cell gene expression without requiring a spatial reference at inference. ORBIS learns spatial organization through flow matching in a shared physical coordinate frame, using training views sampled from sparse serial sections, tissue blocks, and whole specimens. At inference, a shared spatial state is iteratively updated through dynamically regrouped windows, enabling the generation of millions of cell positions without independently reconstructing and stitching tissue regions. We evaluate physical size, cell-population shape, per-cell placement, and neighborhood organization separately to distinguish accurate tissue geometry from low per-cell error. Across eight held-out specimens spanning whole mouse brains, thick brain blocks, and Drosophila embryos, ORBIS achieves lower cell-population shape error than all five evaluated baselines on every test and reconstructs specimens containing up to 3.7 million cells. On a single GPU, ORBIS samples million-cell brains in 0.9-2.8 minutes, approximately 38 times faster than the sampler of LUNA-3D, our 3D extension of the state-of-the-art generative spatial reconstruction method LUNA. On two held-out brain tests, sampling reduces size error by 3.3-fold and shape error by 1.8-fold compared with a single-call variant. On an independent dissociated single-cell brain atlas, ORBIS returns on average 37.9% of each region's cells to their dissection region across 23 regions, compared with 28.5% for LUNA-3D.

articles.title: Generative Models for Novel Enzymatic Reactions: How Far Do They Go?
articles.abstract: Enzyme function prediction is a long-standing problem in biology, and deep learning methods have recently become popular to improve performance on this task. While most of these models focus on classifying enzymes or mapping them to known reactions, predicting unknown biochemical reactions remains underexplored. Here we thoroughly examine an approach that generates reactions absent from the training data from the enzyme alone. Existing methods such as BLASTp or CLIPZyme cannot, by design, output reactions that are absent from their training data or were not supplied at inference. The closest prior model, RxnPred, reports high fingerprint-similarity scores on held-out enzymes, a less stringent criterion than exact recovery, but fails to recover the correct answer on unseen reactions. We present a structure-conditioned generative model that outputs a complete reaction, reactants and products, and evaluate it on EnzymeMap_x, a reaction-disjoint benchmark in which no test reaction appears in training, under exact, stereo-respecting scoring. On this benchmark, within 400 sampled candidates, the model generates the complete, correct reaction for 25.0% of the subset of test enzyme--reaction pairs whose reaction is a new combination of metabolites seen in training. Surprisingly, it also correctly generates a few reactions composed of metabolites it has not seen in training (1.6%), though their embeddings are present in the vocabulary. With a lower budget, re-ranking places the correct reaction first for 5.6% of pairs and in the top ten for 12.4%, when the reaction is assumed not to be already known (0.2% and 8.1% without that assumption) along with confidence scores. Assessed more leniently, the model produces at least one correct reaction known for the enzyme (usually memorised from training) for 71.2% of test pairs. Going further, without any retraining, a sequence-only model given the reactants as well as the enzyme produces the correct product set for 9.5% of pairs within five candidates, without re-ranking. We also present head-to-head comparisons on these tasks with BLASTp, DIAMOND, RxnPred and Horizyn. Structure conditioning improves fingerprint similarity on homology-stratified splits, but a matched sequence-only ablation at the best configuration finds no measurable effect on exact recovery. Data coverage and chemical initialisation of the vocabulary seem to matter more than encoder geometry.

articles.title: Genome-wide Analysis of the VQ Gene Family and Expression Profiling in Sorghum bicolor
articles.abstract: Soil salinization severely restricts agricultural productivity, making the stress-tolerant sorghum an ideal model for studying crop adaptation. VQ motif-containing proteins are plant-specific transcriptional co-regulators vital for stress responses, yet their roles in sorghum remain underexplored. Here, we identified 35 VQ genes in sorghum, classifying them into seven subfamilies. Evolutionary analysis indicated that the family's expansion was primarily driven by segmental duplication. Notably, synteny analysis revealed a lack of collinearity between sorghum and Arabidopsis VQ genes, suggesting significant functional divergence during monocot evolution. Expression profiling showed distinct patterns among VQ members, with SbVQ34, SbVQ39 adn SbVQ40 significantly upregulated under salt stress. Furthermore, protein-protein interaction analysis highlighted SbVQ39 as a potential key regulator in sorghum salt tolerance. This study provides novel insights into sorghum's salinity tolerance mechanisms and establishes a foundation for utilizing VQ genes in breeding salt-tolerant crops.

articles.title: Genomic analysis of the Streptococcus anginosus group; taxonomic implications, evolutionary insights and clinical considerations
articles.abstract: Background: The Streptococcus anginosus group (SAG) (S. anginosus, S. intermedius, and S. constellatus) causes serious, potentially life-threatening, invasive infections, often in otherwise healthy individuals. However, the group's diversity is still poorly understood, and with it, the ability to identify prognostic markers of severe disease. Methods: Long-read sequencing produced closed genomes for 29 isolates from 25 patients hospitalised primarily for invasive SAG infections, and 21 isolates from 20 non-hospitalised controls. Genomes were classified with GTDB-Tk and combined with 211 reference genomes. After dereplication, 207 SAG genomes (38 isolate, 169 reference) representing 206 strains were analysed using: GTDB classification, average nucleotide identity, multi-marker and core-genome SNP phylogenies, recombination-aware analyses, mobilome, CAZyme and gapseq metabolic profiling, and lineage-aware genome-wide association testing for invasive phenotype. Results: Agreement between GTDB-Tk and MALDI-TOF taxonomic classifications was low (42.8%), including two S. massiliensis cases mis-identified by MALDI-TOF as SAG. S. anginosus resolved into four taxa (S. anginosus, S. hominis, S. whileyi and S. vaginalis). Phylogenies based on core genome single-nucleotide polymorphisms resolved these species into distinct clades, whereas 16S rRNA gene and multilocus sequence analysis phylogenies did not. The four ex-S. anginosus taxa showed a gradient of genomic cohesion, with S. vaginalis being near-clonal, in contrast to S. anginosus, which shared high levels of sequence ancestry with other neighbouring taxa. Carbohydrate utilisation was strongly lineage-associated, as was propensity for invasive disease. A ~15Kbp glycosaminoglycan utilisation locus was found in the three taxa of highest disease severity propensity (S. intermedius, S. constellatus, S. whileyi) which predicts a direct host glycosaminoglycan feeding mechanism that may contribute to invasive disease. No single functional feature, gene or core-genome SNP was associated with invasiveness however after lineage-adjustment. Combined feature analysis suggests S. vaginalis has undergone a niche restriction and has evolved for a primary existence in the female urogenital tract. Conclusions: Under-reported species may be mis-diagnosed as SAG invasive infections. SAG is more diverse than its current three-species definition, with the conventional S. anginosus species proposed to be classed into a complex of four distinct taxa. Invasive capacity appears to be an emergent system-level property rather than from individual features.

articles.title: Genomic signatures of positive selection and relaxed selective constraints associated with convergent dietary specialisation
articles.abstract: Island radiations provide ideal frameworks for studying the molecular basis of convergent evolution. The rapid diversification of Dysdera spiders in Canary Islands provides a striking example, with repeated dietary shifts towards specialisation on woodlice, accompanied by morphological, metabolic, and behavioural modifications that facilitate the exploitation of this heavy-metal-rich prey. Here, we investigate two independent events of dietary specialisation on different islands. By analysing six high-quality genome-assemblies, including three newly generated in this study, we investigate the genomic signals of positive selection and relaxed selection in protein-coding genes, upstream regulatory regions, and gene family turnover rates. We detected signatures of positive selection associated with the two specialists, accompanied by a twofold increase in gene loss rates relative to generalist ancestors. Notably, positive selection targeted a smaller, functionally coherent set of genes, potentially involved in detoxification likely through heavy metal excretion. In contrast, relaxation of selection affected a broader set of genes associated with functions that may have become dispensable under the new dietary regime. Furthermore, we found contractions in gene families associated with vesicular transport, potentially reflecting a reduced reliance on vesicle-mediated metal accumulation. Overall, our findings suggest that similar ecological pressures can drive parallel, yet non-identical, adaptive and non-adaptive responses, pointing to partially predictable evolutionary trajectories in an island radiation.

articles.title: Hide and seek in a rainforest canopy : when a fruit-eating carnivore (almost) met its top predator carnivore
articles.abstract: Prey-predator interactions in the wild are spectacular. Common reported cases come from ground-dwelling animals, in open areas and by daylight. Here, we report, for the first time, a sequence with the nocturnal arboreal kinkajou (Potos flavus), being followed ca. 20 minutes apart by one of its predators, the puma (Puma concolor), 33 m aboveground in a rainforest in French Guiana.

articles.title: Hierarchical Temporal Transformer for Cancer Grade Prediction and Cross-Cancer Transfer Learning from Pathology Reports
articles.abstract: Background: Language models for cancer reports usually read one document at a time and are tested on tumour types seen in training. Continuous-time sequence models address the first gap, but whether they use visit timing, not just order, is seldom tested. Methods: We developed the Hierarchical Temporal Transformer (HTT), which encodes reports with adapted BiomedBERT and reads the sequence with a cancer-type-conditioned temporal transformer. We evaluated it against best-possible AUROC ceilings on two synthetic benchmarks, one with the label stated in the text and one recoverable only from tumour sizes and visit intervals (ten seeds). Diagnostics led to an interval-aware time code (HTT-IA). On 4,786 TCGA pathology reports in 14 types, three types were withheld, and a text-only HTT was compared with a survival model. Results: On the phrase benchmark HTT reached AUROC 0.931 +/- 0.012 against 0.913 +/- 0.007 for a last-report baseline (+0.018, 95% CI -0.009 to +0.050); dates cannot raise the ceiling there. On the growth benchmark the initial time code scored 0.790, equal to a no-time model (0.787), whereas HTT-IA reached 0.843 (+0.053, 0.026 to 0.082) against ceilings of 0.894 without and 0.979 with dates. On unseen tumour types HTT reached 0.925 +/- 0.007, equal to in-distribution performance and to a single-report baseline. Text-only macro C-index was 0.592 (CALM 0.626-0.652). Conclusion: Cross-type transfer is carried by the pre-trained encoder. Visit timing is used only when the data make it identifiable and the time code is on a clinical scale. Ceilings, order-only ablations and re-dating probes are inexpensive checks for such models.

articles.title: Homeostatic fibroblast niche collapse in clinically uninvolved skin marks a pre-fibrotic stage of systemic sclerosis
articles.abstract: Systemic sclerosis, or scleroderma, is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by vasculopathy, immune dysregulation, and progressive fibrosis of the skin and internal organs. Heterogeneous clinical presentation and polygenic risk complicate our understanding of disease mechanisms and the path to effective therapy. Single-cell analyses have revealed substantial transcriptional diversity in skin, but disease-associated reprogramming remains poorly defined. To address this, we performed high-resolution spatial transcriptomic profiling of paired clinically uninvolved and clinically affected scleroderma donor skin alongside healthy controls. We identified a continuum of cellular, molecular, and spatial changes to the stroma that were already evident in clinically uninvolved tissue yet still distinct from the broader and more advanced changes in paired fibrotic samples. Uninvolved skin was comparable to healthy tissue by clinical and histopathological assessment, but distinguishable by the numerical reduction, transcriptional reprogramming, and spatial isolation of LGR5+SCARA5+PI16+ progenitor fibroblasts. In parallel, the dermal vascular smooth muscle compartment shifted from a contractile to a synthetic, activated state, suggesting reprogramming that begins before overt fibrosis. Cell neighborhood analysis revealed that progenitor fibroblasts occupy dense stromal niches in healthy skin that collapse in clinically uninvolved tissue, replaced by isolated, disease-associated cellular networks. These data indicate that clinically uninvolved skin occupies an intermediate stage along the pathologic continuum of scleroderma, establishing a framework for strategies to preserve homeostatic fibroblast niches before tissue remodeling and fibrotic commitment.

articles.title: How mutation rate evolves: Gene expression shapes genome-wide mutation rates in Drosophila melanogaster and Caenorhabditis elegans
articles.abstract: Mutation rates vary across the genome, linked to biochemical properties of local DNA sequences. However, mutation rate variation also associates with functional genomic features, raising the possibility that intragenomic mutation rate variation is shaped by adaptive evolution. In particular, recent studies in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana suggested that highly conserved genes under strong purifying selection also have reduced de novo mutation rates, suggesting that natural selection may have acted to reduce mutation rate specifically at important genes. However, whether this is true for wider taxa, including animals, remains unknown. Here we repurposed published mutation accumulation datasets from Drosophila melanogaster and Caenorhabditis elegans to investigate the determinants of de novo single nucleotide variant (DNV) rates genome-wide under minimal selection. Loci under stronger purifying selection accumulated fewer mutations, including intronic and synonymous mutations. Various sequence-specific (i.e. GC content) and regulatory features (e.g. chromatin modifications) were strongly correlated with mutation rate, but gene expression best explained the depletion of mutations within strongly conserved loci, even after accounting for correlations amongst variables. Using excision repair (XR)-sequencing data we determined that higher levels of transcription- coupled repair (TCR) were associated with reduced mutation rates, strongly suggesting that TCR lowers mutation rate of highly conserved genes. Furthermore, by comparing orthologs between C. elegans and its close relative Pristionchus pacificus, we found that altered gene expression across evolutionary time correlated with altered mutation rate. These findings support a model whereby developmental transcription modulates local mutation rates through TCR. A corollary is that adaptive mutation bias may emerge indirectly, downstream of gene regulation evolution, providing a mechanistic framework that reconciles non-random local mutation rate variation with established evolutionary theory.

articles.title: Hub labeling makes exact distance calculation practical for large human pangenome graphs
articles.abstract: Pangenome graphs are now a standard reference representation, and tools built on them depend on fast minimum-distance queries between graph positions, for example, when clustering seed matches during read alignment. The baseline distance index, previously used by the vg toolkit, answers such queries based on a decomposition of the graph into nested subgraphs called "snarls". Within each snarl, the index uses a dense all-pairs distance matrix. Because such a matrix is quadratic in a snarl's number of children, the large, complex snarls that often occur in many pangenome graphs dominate the overall index size. This means whole-genome graphs can be impractical to index. To mitigate this, the baseline distance index does not fully index the largest snarls, and thus cannot itself answer certain queries involving them. We replace the dense matrix with a hub labeling for snarls above a size limit. Because hub labeling and associated methods are defined for directed graphs, we introduce a directed representation of a snarl's bidirected internal "net graph", whose shortest path lengths are the net graph's minimum walk lengths. Hub labels are built using pruned landmark labeling, ordered by a contraction hierarchy. On four human chromosome pangenomes, our hub-labeling-based distance index indexes every snarl in 0.9 GB to 3.0 GB at a snarl limit of 500, an estimated 28x to 119x less space than dense distance matrices would need for those snarls with more than 500 children, and supports the 3-18.6% of node-to-node queries that the previous index cannot answer by itself. On the queries both indexes can answer, query time distributions broadly overlap. We explore the snarl limit parameter space and are able to build indexes under 50 GB for four human whole-genome pangenomes in under 6 hours, where we estimate dense matrices could have required multiple terabytes.

articles.title: Human organoid screen links transient translational modulation to progenitor progression in corticogenesis
articles.abstract: Human pluripotent stem cell-derived models are increasingly used to recapitulate aspects of human corticogenesis, including the emergence of diverse cortical cell types and their progression through developmental states. These systems offer an opportunity to dissect the molecular mechanisms regulating transitions between cell states, but methods for perturbing them systematically at scale remain limited. Here, we developed a semi-automated culture and high-throughput arrayed screening platform for human cortical organoids. Using a library of 1,280 small molecules designed to systematically target major signaling and regulatory pathways, we screened for modulators of EOMES, which encodes for the transcription factor TBR2, and identified Emetine, an inhibitor of translation elongation, as the top hit. The effect of Emetine on cortical cell-state progression was reproduced across human pluripotent stem cell lines, non-human primate cortical organoids, and primary human cortical tissue but not broadly across translation inhibitors. Moreover, transient exposure resulted in a shift from dividing radial glia towards cortical glutamatergic neurons. Mechanistically, nascent-proteome profiling revealed an early and coordinated remodeling of newly translated proteins that preceded detectable transcriptional changes, placing translational regulation upstream of the ensuing cell-state transition. Together, these findings highlight a role for specific translational inhibitors in promoting cortical cell-state progression and establish a scalable platform for systematic perturbation and discovery in human neural organoids.

articles.title: Hypoxia-inducible factor 2-alpha promotes fitness of cytokine-activated human natural killer cells
articles.abstract: Natural Killer (NK) cells are innate effector cells with potent antiviral, antitumor, and immunoregulatory functions that are relevant for the treatment of human diseases. There is a pressing need to better understand the mechanisms governing cellular fitness and functional persistence of NK cells to generate therapeutics regimens of sufficient durability to achieve meaningful clinical benefit. Given the central role of interleukin-2 (IL-2) and IL-15 in the survival and proliferation of NK cells, we sought to identify transcription factors induced by these cytokines that are essential for maintaining the fitness of human NK cells from healthy human blood donors. Culture in IL-2 or IL-15 increased protein expression of hypoxia inducible factor 2 alpha (HIF-2, encoded by EPAS1) but not HIF-1 in NK cells. Unexpectedly, induction of HIF-2 was not dependent on limited oxygen availability. CRISPR targeting of EPAS1 or pharmacological inhibition of HIF-2 protein expression markedly compromised the survival of cytokine-activated human NK cells. In contrast, inhibition of canonical HIF-2 transcription factor activity via blocking HIF-2/HIF-1{beta} heterodimer formation had no apparent effects on NK cell viability, function, or metabolism. These results suggest that cytokines, rather than hypoxia, activate an unconventional HIF-1{beta} independent, HIF-2 pathway that helps to maintain NK cells during cellular activation, revealing the potential promise of manipulating HIF-2 to improve the efficacy of adoptive NK cell therapies.

articles.title: Expectation-driven gain modulation of preparatory spatial attention
articles.abstract: The visual system can flexibly adjust attentional deployment to match task demands, but whether observers can proactively modulate the spatial scope of attention based on expectations about upcoming search difficulty remains unclear. According to the zoom lens model, attention can narrow or broaden its spatial extent, with narrower focus enhancing processing efficiency, a mechanism that would benefit target discrimination in crowded displays. We tested whether observers adjust attentional scope when expecting sparse versus dense search arrays by combining spatial cueing with block-wise manipulations of display density expectations. Participants performed a visual search task in which endogenous cues predicted target location, while blocks predominantly contained either sparse (1 target, 3 distractors) or dense (1 target, 7 distractors) displays. We applied inverted encoding models to broadband EEG data to reconstruct spatial channel tuning functions, enabling precise characterization of both the locus and breadth of attentional deployment. Behaviorally, expecting difficult searches selectively improved accuracy at cued locations without costs elsewhere. Consistent with this selective benefit, neural measurements revealed that expectancy enhanced the amplitude of spatially selective responses at the attended location but did not alter tuning width. These findings demonstrate that expectations about search difficulty modulate attention through gain-based signal enhancement rather than adjustments to spatial scope, revealing that preparatory attentional control operates via amplitude modulation within a stable spatial focus. This mechanism complements reactive attentional adjustments and provides an efficient means for the visual system to optimize processing under predictable task demands.

articles.title: Large inversions in Lake Malawi cichlids are associated with habitat, lineage, and sex determination
articles.abstract: Chromosomal inversions are an important class of genetic variation that link multiple alleles together into a single inherited block that can have important effects on fitness. To study the role of large inversions in the massive evolutionary radiation of Lake Malawi cichlids, we used long-read technologies to identify four single and two tandem inversions that span half of each respective chromosome, and which together encompass over 10% of the genome. Each inversion is fixed in one of the two states within the seven major ecogroups, suggesting they played a role in the separation of the major lake lineages into specific lake habitats. One exception is within the benthic sub-radiation, where both inverted and non-inverted alleles continue to segregate within the group. The evolutionary histories of three of the six inversions suggest they transferred from the pelagic Diplotaxodon group into benthic ancestors at the time the benthic sub-radiation was seeded. The remaining three inversions are found in a subset of benthic species living in deep waters. We show that some of these inversions are linked to XY sex-determination systems but are also likely limited to a subset of total lake species. Our work suggests that inversions have been under both sexual and natural selection in Lake Malawi cichlids and that they will be important to understanding how this adaptive radiation evolved.

articles.title: Simple methods to acutely measure multiple timing metrics among the sexual repertoire of male Drosophila
articles.abstract: Male Drosophila courtship behavior is a key model for studying temporal decision-making. While courtship index (CI) is widely used to quantify mating activity, other timing metrics like courtship latency, copulation latency (CL), and mating duration (MD) remain understudied. Traditional methods for quantifying these behaviors are often labor-intensive and prone to human error. In this study, we present a protocol combining a modular chamber system and automated software (DrosoMating) to quantify six key timing metrics during male courtship. Our image-based video analysis enables precise identification of courtship and copulation events, as well as quantification of their timing and duration under controlled conditions. Validation shows <0.05% error rates and 98–99% agreement with manual scoring for CL, CI, and MD. The protocol supports genetic and neural circuit manipulations, detecting subtle genetic, social, and environmental behavioral variations. By minimizing manual effort and standardizing data collection, this approach facilitates scalable, reproducible studies on adaptive trade-offs, learning, and neural mechanisms in mating behavior. This method streamlines timing analysis in male courtship, offering reproducible metrics for behavioral genetics.

articles.title: Spatial confinement induces oscillatory migration of epidermal keratinocytes and forms a three-compartment epithelial structure with epithelial–mesenchymal transition dynamics
articles.abstract: Epithelial cells undergo epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) during migration and regain their epithelial phenotype in the post-migration phase (mesenchymal–epithelial transition [MET]). We established an experimental system that reproduces a three-compartment epithelial structure comprising the original epithelium, its EMT state, and its MET state. Keratinocytes (KCs), skin epithelial cells, placed on a microporous membrane, migrated through 3.0 µm or larger micropores. The 3.0-µm-pored membrane induced an epithelial structure with three distinct states: stratified KCs above the membrane, KCs showing EMT within the micropores, and a new stratified epithelium under the membrane. The membrane with larger micropores failed to maintain the three-compartment epithelial structure. Live imaging revealed that KCs moved in an oscillatory manner, with actin-rich filopodia-like structures extending into and out of the 3.0 µm micropores, while the cells migrated unidirectionally into larger micropores. Piezo1 and keratin 6 were identified as negative modulators of KC entry into and exit from the 3.0 µm micropores. These results demonstrate that non-cancerous epithelial cells migrate through confined spaces in an oscillatory manner, which might contribute to the formation of a three-compartment epithelial structure that recapitulates key aspects of wound healing.

articles.title: The hypoxic response extends lifespan through a bioaminergic and peptidergic neural circuit
articles.abstract: A coordinated response to stress is crucial for promoting the short- and long-term health of an organism. The perception of stress, frequently through the nervous system, can lead to physiological changes that are fundamental to maintaining homeostasis. Activating the response to low oxygen, or hypoxia, extends healthspan and lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. However, despite some positive impacts, negative effects of the hypoxic response in specific tissues prevent translation of their benefits in mammals. Thus, it is imperative to identify which components of this response promote longevity. Here, we interrogate the cell-nonautonomous signaling pathway downstream of genetic activation of the hypoxic response. We find that HIF-1-mediated signaling in ADF serotonergic neurons is both necessary and sufficient for lifespan extension. Signaling through the serotonin receptor SER-7 in the GABAergic RIS interneurons is necessary in this process. Our findings also highlight the involvement of additional neural signaling molecules, including the neurotransmitters tyramine and GABA, and the neuropeptide NLP-17, in mediating longevity effects. Finally, we demonstrate that oxygen- and carbon-dioxide-sensing neurons act downstream of HIF-1 in this circuit. Together, these insights demonstrate a circuit for how genetic induction of the hypoxic response cell-nonautonomously modifies aging and suggests valuable targets for modulating aging in mammals.

articles.title: The resource elasticity of control
articles.abstract: The ability to determine how much the environment can be controlled through our actions has long been viewed as fundamental to adaptive behavior. While traditional accounts treat controllability as a fixed property of the environment, we argue that real-world controllability often depends on the effort, time, and money we are able and willing to invest. In such cases, controllability can be said to be elastic to invested resources. Here, we propose that inferring this elasticity is essential for efficient resource allocation, and thus, elasticity misestimations result in maladaptive behavior. To test this hypothesis, we developed a novel treasure hunt game where participants encountered environments with varying degrees of controllability and elasticity. Across two pre-registered studies (N=514), we first demonstrate that people infer elasticity and adapt their resource allocation accordingly. We then present a computational model that explains how people make this inference and identify individual elasticity biases that lead to suboptimal resource allocation. Finally, we show that overestimation of elasticity is associated with elevated psychopathology involving an impaired sense of control. These findings establish the elasticity of control as a distinct cognitive construct guiding adaptive behavior and a computational marker for control-related maladaptive behavior.

articles.title: A CBC-derived score associated with dengue NS1 antigen positivity among suspected dengue patients in Dhaka: a retrospective model-development study
articles.abstract: Background: Early diagnostic triage for suspected dengue is important in high-volume settings, yet confirmatory testing may be delayed or intermittently available. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a simple complete blood count (CBC)-derived score to estimate the likelihood of same-day dengue non-structural protein 1 (NS1) antigen positivity among suspected dengue patients in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Methods: We conducted a retrospective model-development study at Uttara Adhunik Medical College Hospital using data from patients with clinical suspicion of dengue between 19 August and 12 October 2023. The final analysis included 596 unique patients who underwent CBC and NS1 testing on the same day. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) penalized logistic regression was used for variable selection among routinely available demographic and hematological predictors. Selected predictors were refit using unpenalized logistic regression to derive a CBC score. Internal validation and calibration were assessed using bootstrap optimism correction with 400 resamples. Results: Among 596 patients, 306 (51.3%) were NS1 positive. The final parsimonious model retained platelet count rescaled per 10 x 109/L, white blood cell count, and monocyte count. The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.9429. At the Youden-derived cutoff of 11.825, the final integer score had sensitivity 0.833 (95% CI, 0.787-0.873), specificity 0.966 (95% CI, 0.938-0.983), PPV 0.962 (95% CI, 0.932-0.982), NPV 0.846 (95% CI, 0.802-0.883), and accuracy 0.898 (95% CI, 0.870-0.921). A rounded cutoff of 12 produced similar performance. In benchmark analysis, the final model showed a modest improvement over platelet count alone (AUC 0.944 vs 0.931; Delta AUC 0.012; DeLong p=0.00364). Conclusion: A three-parameter CBC score can estimate the likelihood of NS1 antigen positivity among suspected dengue patients in this single-center dataset. The score should be interpreted as a CBC-only triage adjunct, not as a replacement for confirmatory dengue testing. External validation in independent cohorts is needed before routine clinical use.

articles.title: A Cross-Dataset Audit of Discrimination and Conformal Prediction Coverage in Keystroke-Based Parkinson's Disease Classi cation
articles.abstract: Typing dynamics are being investigated as a digital behavioral marker for Parkinson's disease (PD), but the cross-dataset reliability of typing-based classi ers remains uncertain. We evaluated four public datasets (475 par ticipants; 270 with PD and 205 controls) across 12 transfer directions using split conformal prediction targeting 90% marginal coverage. In all three pri mary directions, coverage was below the 0.90 target and the one-sided tests remained signi cant after Holm correction: 0.598 (95% CI, 0.4830.704) for Tappy[->]MIT, 0.850 (0.7880.899) for MIT[->]Tappy, and 0.732 (0.6840.777) for clinical[->]self-reported transfer. Discrimination and coverage did not con sistently change together: LightGBM had lower AUC than logistic regression in all 12 directions but higher coverage in 11, with larger prediction sets. Class-conditional coverage varied by target cohort: PD-conditional cover age was 0.214 for Tappy[->]MIT, whereas healthy-control coverage was 0.700 for MIT[->]Tappy and 0.627 for clinical[->]self-reported transfer. Recalibration with 9 and 18 labeled target participants raised the lower condence bound above 0.80 in the latter two directions; in Tappy[->]MIT, it remained below 0.80 even with 25 labels. Weighted conformal prediction yielded coverage of 0.9181.000 without target labels but returned the full label set for 86% 100% of participants. Stress tests did not reproduce the observed coverage patterns, and black-box shift estimation did not support pure label shift as the dominant explanation for Tappy[->]MIT. Evaluating typing dynamics as a digital marker for PD requires cross-dataset assessment of discrimination, marginal and class-conditional coverage, and recovery costs. Clinical screen ing utility has not been established.

articles.title: A healthy donor kidney aging signature estimable from PAS histology and its association with progression of diabetic kidney disease
articles.abstract: Background. As kidneys age, their cells change in arrangement and gene expression. Whether these changes are also present in diabetic kidney disease (DKD), and whether they relate to how quickly kidney function is lost, is not known. Methods. Zero-time biopsies from 24 healthy living kidney donors (aged 36-66 years) and biopsies from 28 patients with DKD were profiled by single-cell-level spatial transcriptomics with a 5,101-gene panel. In the donors, we identified how cell neighborhoods and cell-type gene expression change with age and summarized the expression changes as tissue-aging scores. The scores were applied unchanged to DKD and related to the rate of eGFR decline after biopsy in 24 patients, with adjustment for age, sex, baseline eGFR, and proteinuria. We also estimated the scores from routine periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) slides, using models that did not include the patient being scored. Results. In older donors, immune cells were less often found next to tubular epithelium, and contacts between endothelial cells and podocytes and between stromal and epithelial cells were fewer, although cell proportions changed little. Expression of stress-response and cell-cycle regulators (FOXO3, CDKN1A, BBC3, PINK1, IRAK1, SOCS1) increased. Changes in cell contacts in DKD tissue largely followed the same direction as those in older donors. In DKD, higher tissue-aging scores were associated with faster eGFR loss independently of age, sex, baseline eGFR, and proteinuria (overall score, partial {rho} = -0.61); this held for tubular, endothelial, immune, and parietal epithelial cell scores but not for the podocyte score. Scores estimated from PAS slides correlated with the transcriptomic scores (mean {rho} = 0.62) and were also associated with faster eGFR loss (partial {rho}, -0.44 to -0.56). Conclusions. Healthy kidney aging involves a selective loss of cell contacts together with a coordinated stress-response program. DKD kidneys that carry this aging phenotype lose function faster, and the phenotype can be estimated in part from the routine diagnostic PAS slide.

articles.title: Additional tuberculosis case detection through repeat household contact investigation at 6 and 12 months: a retrospective cohort study in Kasama, a peri-urban district in Zambia
articles.abstract: Background: Tuberculosis contact investigation (TBCI) facilitates early detection of TB among household contacts. However, evidence on the additional contribution of repeat TBCI in high-burden settings remains limited. We assessed the contribution of repeat TBCI at 6 and 12 months to TB case detection in Kasama District, Zambia. Methods: We conducted a retrospective observational cohort analysis of routinely collected programme data from five purposively selected high-volume TB diagnostic facilities. Household contacts of bacteriologically confirmed TB patients notified between January 2023 and April 2024 underwent symptom-based TB screening at baseline and at 6 and 12 months. We estimated round-specific TB detection yields, the cumulative proportion diagnosed with TB, and the contribution of repeat investigations to overall case detection. Results: Among 1,250 index TB patients, 3,648 household contacts were identified and screened at baseline. TB was diagnosed in 143 (3.9%) contacts at baseline, 31 (0.9%) at month 6, and 25 (0.7%) at month 12. Overall, 199 (5.5%) contacts were diagnosed with TB across the three screening rounds, of whom 159 (79.9%) had bacteriologically confirmed disease. Repeat investigations identified 56 additional cases, representing 28.1% of all TB diagnoses. Conclusions: Repeat TBCI at 6 and 12 months identified additional TB cases beyond baseline screening, although detection yields declined across successive rounds. These findings support further evaluation of risk-based follow-up strategies and more sensitive baseline screening approaches to optimize TB case detection and resource utilization in high-burden settings.
