articles.title: Agentic Pipeline for Large-Scale Clinical Data Queries in Enterprise Electronic Health Records
articles.abstract: Using electronic health record (EHR) data to answer clinical research questions is challenging. It requires understanding the research question, finding relevant information across different sources, and combining that information to produce meaningful results. We developed an agentic large language model (LLM) pipeline that decomposes investigator-authored requests into source-specific tasks, generates and executes SQL on EHR, integrates structured and unstructured EHR evidence, and applies study-specific clinical note adjudication. We evaluated this workflow against data analyst-identified cohorts across 50 pediatric orthopedic clinical data query requests. Of these, 43 were included in manual-review-adjusted performance analyses. The median adjusted positive predictive value, sensitivity among patients identified by either approach, and corresponding F1 score were 0.93 (95% CI, 0.88-0.98), 0.92 (95% CI, 0.90-0.95) and 0.90 (95% CI, 0.87-0.94), respectively. These findings support the feasibility of translating natural-language research intent into executable, autonomous multi-stage EHR workflows.

articles.title: An explainable, bias-audited machine learning model to detect hidden hepatitis C from region-wide real-world health records
articles.abstract: Background: Although direct-acting antivirals have transformed hepatitis C virus (HCV) treatment, 25-30% of active infections in Spain remain undiagnosed. We aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine-learning model to identify undiagnosed HCV infection using only data already recorded within the health system. Materials and Methods: We conducted a retrospective, population-based cohort study using the Andalusian Population Health Database (BPS). Individuals diagnosed with HCV between 2017 and 2024 (n=25,028) were matched, up to 10:1, to controls by birth year, sex, and health district. An Explainable Boosting Machine was trained on 2017-2022 data, with a threshold set in a 2023 validation set to guarantee [≥]60% sensitivity, then evaluated unmodified in an independent, non-matched, population-representative 2024 sample approximating real-world screening. Predictors comprised chronic-disease diagnoses and laboratory summary statistics recorded [≥]30 days before the index date; age and sex were excluded as matching variables. Predictors reflecting socioeconomic proxies or matching artefacts (pharmaceutical co-payment category, a zone-level deprivation index) were removed after explainability review. Results: In the independent test set, the model achieved an AUC of 0.837 (0.826 in validation), sensitivity 63.5%, specificity 91.8%, positive predictive value 7.0%, and negative predictive value 99.6%. Leading predictors were minimum alanine aminotransferase, HIV infection, dependence on non-tobacco substances, and platelet-count statistics, forming a clinically coherent, laboratory- and comorbidity-driven profile. Conclusion: An explainable model built exclusively from routine electronic health record data can identify undiagnosed HCV infection with discrimination comparable to previously published tools, evaluated under conditions approximating true population prevalence. Bias-auditing was feasible without sacrificing interpretability, supporting a scalable, equity-conscious instrument for the final phase of HCV elimination.

articles.title: Association Between Anorexia Nervosa Severity and Social and Occupational Functioning across Adulthood
articles.abstract: Importance: Severe anorexia nervosa (AN) carries substantial mortality risk, but its consequences associated with social and occupational functioning remain poorly characterized, limiting the development of targeted interventions to improve functioning, prevent and reduce long-term social disadvantage. Objective: To determine whether AN severity is associated with educational attainment, employment, income, and cohabitation status. Design: Cohort study following social and occupational outcomes across adulthood until age 55. Setting: Population-based. Participants: All individuals born in Denmark from 1963 to 1994, alive and residing in Denmark at age 30. The AN group had a first AN diagnosis between ages 10 and 25 years, excluding those who died or emigrated within 5 years. The comparison group had no AN diagnosis. Exposure: Illness severity of AN, measured by the AN Register-based Severity Index 5 years after the first AN diagnosis. Main Outcomes and Measures: Educational attainment was assessed at age 25 (upper secondary education) and at age 30/35 (highest completed education). Employment status, income deficiency, and cohabitation status were assessed annually from age 30 to 55. Results: Among 2,442,916 individuals, 9,465 were diagnosed with AN, of whom 1,996 (21.1%) were classified as severe AN cases. At age 25, individuals with severe AN had increased odds of non-completion of upper-secondary education compared to the general population (odds ratio [OR]=3.07; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.72-3.46), and those with less severe AN (OR=1.39; 95% CI: 1.29-1.50). At age 30, severe AN was associated with higher odds of unemployment (OR=3.42; 95% CI: 3.03-3.86), income deficiency (OR=3.84; 95% CI: 3.42-4.31), and living alone (OR=2.43; 95% CI: 2.17-2.71) compared to the less severe AN group. The risk of unemployment and income deficiency diverged across time: individuals with less severe AN gradually approached the general population, whereas those with severe AN diverged further over time. Within the AN cohort, severity differences persisted after adjustment for active AN diagnosis, with minimal attenuation. Conclusions and Relevance: Greater lifetime AN severity was associated with significantly poorer long-term social and occupational functioning outcomes, and these functional difficulties may persist beyond periods of active illness. This vulnerable group needs substantial support in these areas throughout the course of illness.

articles.title: Association Between Parental Nativity and Mental Health Among U.S. Adolescents: Findings from the National Health Interview Survey, 2022 - 2024
articles.abstract: Introduction: Studies have shown a high prevalence of mental health problems among immigrants, but findings for their children are mixed. We examined the association between parental nativity and mental health among U.S. adolescents and assessed whether these associations varied by sex and race/ethnicity. Methods: We analyzed pooled cross-sectional data from the 2022-2024 National Health Interview Survey, including 12,540 adolescents aged 12-17 years. The exposure was parental nativity. The outcomes were adolescents' mental health, including anxiety, depression, behavioral difficulties, and peer relationships. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and nearest neighbor matching were used to control confounders. Survey-weighted logistic regression was used to estimate the association between parent nativity and each outcome. Subgroup analyses were conducted by sex and race/ethnicity. Results: Compared with adolescents with U.S.-born parents, adolescents with at least one foreign-born parent had lower odds of anxiety (Odds Ratio [OR]=0.62, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.54-0.71), depression (OR=0.71, 95% CI: 0.60-0.84), and behavioral difficulties (OR=0.56, 95% CI: 0.43-0.72), but not relationship difficulties (OR=0.97, 95% CI: 0.74-1.26), in the IPTW analysis. Findings from nearest-neighbor matching were consistent. In exploratory stratified analyses, inverse associations were observed among Hispanic adolescents and adolescents classified as other race/ethnicity. Conclusion: Parental nativity was associated with adolescent mental health, with adolescents of at least one foreign-born parent showing lower odds of anxiety, depression, and behavioral difficulties. Future studies are needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms and identify protective factors that help inform interventions to promote adolescent mental health.

articles.title: Benchmarking Structural Variant Detection in Whole-Exome Sequencing of 67 Multiple Myeloma Cell Lines
articles.abstract: Background. Although the majority of structural variant (SV) workflows have been derived based on whole genome sequencing (WGS) data, they continue to be applied to whole exome sequence (WES) data for which many studies have evaluated their performance in cancer. An equally important consideration that has not been well studied is the impact of cancer context specific features among WGS-derived SV callers applied to WES data. Similar to personalized medicine, not all SV callers are alike and optimal for use with all cancer types and sequence data types. In addition to sequencing related data features, cancer types have embedded features withing the sequencing data that should be considered. Herein, we performed an analysis of SV heterogeneity among WGS-derived SV callers to WES data in multiple myeloma (MM), a cancer known for its genetically heterogeneous nature. Using WES data derived from a panel of 67 Multiple Myeloma (MM) cell lines, we evaluated seven WGS-derived SV detection tools (Delly, SvABA, BreakDancer, Smoove, LUMPY and Manta) for their ability to identify cytogenetically known genetic abnormalities and to characterize overall differences in the number, length, type, and runtime of SVs called among them. Results. Among the seven tools, Smoove and Manta both had the shortest runtime, processing files in less than 2 minutes, in contrast to tools that required more than two hours to run such as SvABA and Pindel. Smoove was the only SV caller to identify a range of SV types, while SvABA was the most restrictive, calling only breakends. All tools differed in the length of SVs called, with SvABA's unfiltered output including the shortest length of less than 10 base pairs (bps), and Delly and BreakDancer's output including the longest, with SVs of less than 1,000 bps. At the chromosome level, SvABA's unfiltered output and Delly's output included 78% and 27.5% of known SVs, respectively, with the remaining tools (including SvABA's filtered output) achieved recall rates of less of less than 10%. By comparison, at the genomics coordinate level, no tool identified more than 20% of known SVs. Conclusions. As all evaluated SV detection tools achieved poor recall rates on this comprehensive catalog of MM cell lines, this study implies SVs detected by WGS-based SV callers on WES data should be confirmed experimentally before being declared legitimate. Heterogeneity in these tools' output lends support to their combined use in practice. Considering that many clinical grade sequencing panels continue to expand their repertoire of rearrangements with therapeutic implications, our results prompt the potential need for cancer type-matched workflows to evaluate the calling of such rearrangements.

articles.title: Beyond Perinatal Mood: Breadth of Psychiatric Symptoms and Delay Discounting as Correlates of Mothers' Relational Reports from Pregnancy Through Adult Children
articles.abstract: Maternal mental illness affects roughly one in five mothers in the United States, yet most evidence linking it to the mother-child relationship comes from the first postpartum year and relies on self-report measures of depression, anxiety, and stress. In 613 women spanning five family contexts - pregnancy and mothers whose youngest child was aged 0-2, 3-12, 13-17, or 18 and older - we examined twelve psychological constructs as correlates of mothers' relational reports. Eleven were associated with relational reports individually; entered together, only three retained independent associations surviving false discovery rate correction: cross-domain psychiatric symptom burden (beta = 0.38), delay discounting (beta = -0.11), and orienting sensitivity (beta = 0.10). To our knowledge, this is the first peer-reviewed study linking delay discounting to maternal relational reports. Depression, anxiety, anger, perceived stress, and negative affect fell to non-significance, and the symptom composite that displaced them contains none of those domains, indicating that breadth of psychiatric symptoms, not their type, tracked relational reports. A person-centered analysis converged: the latent profile with the poorest relational reports was defined by symptoms across multiple domains rather than by elevated stress alone. Associations varied across family contexts, though because each context used a different relational instrument, differences cannot be attributed to child age. These cross-sectional findings suggest that the psychological dimension most closely tied to maternal relational reports is broader than the perinatal mood constructs around which research and screening are organized, and that cross-domain symptom assessment warrants prospective evaluation as a complement to mood screening.

articles.title: Biomarker-Informed Phenotyping of the Heart Failure Continuum: A Population-Based Evaluation of the Second Universal Definition of Heart Failure
articles.abstract: Objective: To develop and evaluate a biomarker-informed, computable phenotype of the heart failure (HF) continuum, aligned with 2026 AHA/ACC/ESC/WHF Expert Consensus, using NHANES and linked mortality data, and to determine whether this phenotype identifies subgroups with distinct mortality risks. Methods: We analyzed 11,477 U.S. adults aged [≥]20 years from the 1999-2004 NHANES cycles who participated in the surplus-sera biomarker substudy and were linked to National Death Index follow-up. Participants were classified into four phenotypes according to the 2026 Universal Definition of Heart Failure: no apparent risk, Stage A (at risk), Stage B (elevated NT-proBNP without self-reported HF), and Stage C (self-reported HF). Survey-weighted Kaplan-Meier curves and nested, multiply imputed Cox proportional hazards models, with sequential adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, and cardiometabolic covariates, were used to estimate associations with mortality. Pairwise phenotype comparisons, standardized adjusted survival estimates, and restricted mean survival times were also calculated. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated by comparing discrimination and reclassification metrics between the full phenotype and a conventional three-level model that excluded NT-proBNP. Results: Weighted prevalences were 16.9%, 70.0%, 10.7%, and 2.4% for no apparent risk, Stage A, Stage B, and Stage C, respectively. In fully adjusted models, the hazard ratios (HRs) relative to no apparent risk were 1.58 (95% CI, 1.08-2.30), 2.88 (95% CI, 2.00-4.16), and 2.56 (95% CI, 1.61-4.09), respectively. Stage B was associated with significantly higher mortality risk than Stage A (HR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.62-2.07), whereas the difference between Stage C and Stage B was not statistically significant (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.71-1.11). The association for Stage B attenuated less across sequentially adjusted models than that for Stage C. Adjusted 10-year mortality risks were 15.2% for Stage B and 14.2% for Stage C. Incorporating Stage B into the conventional model yielded only marginal improvements in discrimination ({Delta}C-statistic, 0.002; 95% CI, 0.001-0.002). Conclusion: A biomarker-informed phenotype of the HF continuum can be operationalized using national survey data and identifies a pre-HF subgroup with an adjusted mortality risk not significantly different from that of individuals with overt HF, despite only marginal gains in prognostic discrimination.

articles.title: Brainstem functional connectivity integrates microbiome-gut-brain signals in healthy older adults: a cross-sectional evaluation and a randomised controlled probiotic trial
articles.abstract: Background: Despite increasing interest in the gut-brain axis, the role of the autonomic nervous system and the brainstem in human gut-brain signalling remain largely unknown. Objective: To characterise resting state functional connectivity (FC) of the brainstem in healthy older adults and to examine its association with a variety of factors relevant to ageing and the gut-brain axis, and to assess if brainstem FC is altered by probiotic intervention. Design: Randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial in 60-80-year-olds (55 women/28 men) with six-weeks Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus HN001 intervention in a non-encapsulated and microencapsulated formulation. Brainstem-optimised functional magnetic resonance imaging was performed before and after intervention. Results: At baseline, age correlated positively with FC of locus coeruleus (LC) and dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) with pre-/postcentral gyrus, as well as of periaqueductal gray (PAG) with temporal/supramarginal gyrus and planum temporale. FC of PAG with precuneus cortex and cingulate gyrus correlated with cognitive status and mood. Perceived stress correlated with FC between nucleus tractus solitarius and occipital cortex, angular/temporal gyrus. FC of DRN differed between men and women. All p<0.0063. Following probiotic intervention, a significant time*group interaction and main time effect were observed for FC of LC and ventral tegmental area. FC of both with occipital pole/cortex and cerebellum, and of LC with pre-/postcentral gyrus, superior parietal lobule, insular/opercular cortex, putamen, and planum polare showed within-group changes (non-encapsulated), no between-group differences were observed (all p<0.0056). Conclusion: Brainstem-to-cortex FC at rest correlates with several phenotypic characteristics implicated in healthy ageing and may be modifiable by probiotic supplementation.

articles.title: Can dental EHR data support a learning health system? Completeness, consistency, and accuracy of structured versus narrative diagnoses
articles.abstract: Introduction Electronic health record (EHR) data increasingly drive quality monitoring and research, yet their reliability in dentistry is uncertain. We compared the completeness, consistency, and accuracy of periodontal diagnoses captured in two different formats (structured fields versus narrative notes) across two academic dental centers sharing the same EHR platform and diagnostic terminology. Methods In this retrospective study of qualifying periodontal encounters (2021), structured diagnoses were extracted by SQL and narrative diagnoses by a fine-tuned RoBERTa NLP model. A random sample (~20%) was independently reviewed by two board-certified periodontists, with disagreements resolved by consensus, to form the gold standard. Outcomes were completeness (presence of a diagnosis), consistency (agreement between formats), and accuracy (agreement with the gold standard), with ordinal periodontal stage compared using quadratic weighted {kappa}. Results Across 4,542 encounters, completeness varied widely by site and format (34.7% - 84.5%), and neither format was consistently more complete; at one site, over one-third of encounters (35.8%) had no documented diagnosis in either format. Among dual-documented encounters, agreement between formats was substantial but imperfect ({kappa} = 0.86 and 0.80). Accuracy against the gold standard was modest for both sources (all near 50%), with narrative notes numerically higher at both sites and favored by the severity-weighted {kappa}, though raw differences were not significant. Pooled across sites, the formats diverged in 14.8% of dual-documented encounters, 8.4% by two or more stages, with the structured field carrying the milder stage in 67.9% of disagreements. Conclusions Structured and unstructured periodontal diagnoses each matched expert adjudication only about half the time, and neither was consistently more complete. Narrative notes held a small severity-weighted accuracy advantage, and coded fields more often carried the milder stage when the two disagreed. These convergent, cross-site patterns appear systematic rather than site-specific and expose latent risks for analytics and decision support. Improving dental EHR data quality will require workflows that combine the computability of coded entries with the fidelity of free text.

articles.title: Challenges and Health Disparities in Prostate Cancer: Healthcare Access as a Driver of Inequities in a Rural Hospital Network
articles.abstract: Background: Prostate cancer is the most common male cancer, and second most common cause of cancer mortality in the US. Disparities abound in this disease for reasons that need further study, including social and ethnic barriers, geographic barriers, and biological differences. North Carolina is the second largest state by rural population measures (3.5 million), which provides ample geography to study these disparities. Materials and Methods: A dataset containing all patients with a medical record documenting a diagnosis of and/or treatment for de novo prostate cancer within the mostly rural ECU Health 9-hospital system was characterized over a 20-year period for structural inequities, access barriers, and biological differences. Results: Stages and outcomes of prostate cancer changed temporally, reflecting changes in screening, treatment, and inclusion of prognostic factors such as prostate-specific antigen, Gleason score, and other factors. Late stage (4) prostate cancer disproportionately affected our system as a whole and smaller community hospitals, with higher death rates seen in community, mostly rural programs that lack access to all required components of care. Conclusion: Stages of prostate cancer changed considerably over the study period, reflecting changes in screening recommendations, and staging criteria. Late stage (4) disease increased over the analytic period, was higher than NCDB references by period, and disproportionately affected community programs where resources were sparse, correlating with worse outcomes.

articles.title: Circulating Tumor DNA in Patients with Early-Onset Systemic Sclerosis and Dermatomyositis
articles.abstract: Background: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) and dermatomyositis (DM) are autoimmune diseases that have been proposed as models of cancer immunoediting. Autoantibody-defined subsets show divergent cancer risks, yet malignancy often remains clinically occult. We tested whether circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) can reveal subclinical cancer in new-onset SSc and DM. Methods: We prospectively recruited adults with recent SSc or DM onset. Plasma ctDNA was assessed using a targeted next-generation sequencing panel covering commonly mutated cancer genes. Patients were followed for 18-24 months on average. ctDNA positivity was correlated with subsequent cancer diagnoses. Findings: Among 134 patients (69 SSc, 65 DM), cancer was diagnosed in six (4.5%; three SSc, three DM). ctDNA was detected in four of these six patients (67%) a median of 13 months (range 1.4-17) before clinical diagnosis; in three of four patients, mutations detected in plasma matched those subsequently identified in the same patients primary tumors. ctDNA was also detected in 16 of 128 patients without a cancer diagnosis. ctDNA positivity conferred an 11.4-fold higher risk of malignancy relative to ctDNA negativity and yielded a negative predictive value of 98% and a positive predictive value of 20% for cancer within the observation window. Interpretation: ctDNA testing identified most cancers that emerged within 18 months in new-onset SSc and DM and stratified near-term cancer risk. These findings support larger, interventional trials to determine whether ctDNA-guided surveillance improves timeliness of cancer detection, optimizes imaging and biopsy strategies, and enhances outcomes in patients with SSc and DM.

articles.title: Circulating insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) and short-term functional change in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS): exploratory evidence for systemic trophic-metabolic reserve.
articles.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) exhibit heterogeneous functional decline, potentially influenced by systemic metabolic reserve. We investigate whether circulating insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) is associated with subsequent functional change in ALS. Serum IGF-1 was measured in 37 participants with ALS and 25 healthy controls. Baseline levels were compared between groups, and across disease-duration defined progression categories. Lagged regression assessed whether prior visit IGF-1 level predicted change in Revised ALS Functional Rating Scale (ALSFRS-R) on the next visit, adjusting for inter-visit interval, body mass index, age and sex. Mixed-effects and sensitivity analyses assessed robustness. Baseline IGF-1 did not differ significantly between controls and ALS (mean + SD: 107.3 + 54.3 vs 132.2 + 68.3 ng/mL, p = 0.12), or across progression categories (F(2, 34) = 0.13, p = 0.88). Across 48 intervals from 23 ALS participants, each 1-SD higher IGF-1 from prior visit was associated with 1.40-point less subsequent {Delta}ALSFRS-R decline (95% CI: 0.03 to 2.77, p = 0.045). Generalised estimating equations yielded a similar association ({beta} = 1.50, p = 0.030), whereas small-cluster robust inference showed wider uncertainty (p = 0.084). Repeated IGF-1 showed an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.69, and the lagged association remained positive in all 23 leave-one-participant-out analyses. The IGF-1-by-time interaction was not significant in a random-slope mixed model (p =0.254). Higher circulating IGF-1 may reflect systemic trophic-metabolic reserve associated with short-term functional preservation in ALS, but limited precision precludes definitive prognostic or causal conclusions.

articles.title: Classical machine learning versus transformers for predicting daily psychological distress from passive smartphone sensing and self-report: a prospective cohort study
articles.abstract: Objective: We test whether data collected from daily passive smartphone sensing and self-reports can predict daily significant psychological distress with meaningful potential clinical utility, comparing across best-in-class machine learning algorithms. Methods: In this prospective cohort study, 169 community-dwelling adults completed baseline surveys followed by 7 days of passive smartphone sensing (accelerometer, GPS, power state) and end-of-day Brief Symptom Inventory-18 (BSI-18) assessments. Cases were defined as days (total n = 1,062) where participants' psychological distress measured with the sex-specific BSI-18 Global Severity Index T-score was [≥]63 (prevalence 11.2%). Four classical models (artificial neural network, elastic net, support vector machine [SVM], extreme gradient boosting [XGB]) and four transformers (sensor-only or multimodal; standard or fusion architecture) were tuned, Platt-calibrated and evaluated on held-out participants (210 records, 25 cases) with participant-level bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: The SVM (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC] 0.84; 95% CI 0.71-0.93), the multimodal fusion transformer (0.84; 0.69-0.95) and XGB (0.82; 0.63-0.94) discriminated best; sensor-only transformers performed at chance (0.49-0.50). At the default threshold of 0.50, elastic net logistic regression was the best classifier (sensitivity 0.56, positive predictive value 0.64). At 0.12 (near the outcome prevalence), the SVM detected all cases (negative predictive value 1.00), but positive predictive values were low for all models (0.13-0.26). Decision-curve analysis favored most models over treat-all and treat-none lines at thresholds between 0.05 and 0.25. Baseline survey items, mainly on functional impairment, had the largest feature importance. Conclusions: Compact classical models performed as well as transformers, which were considerably more computationally intensive. Decision-curve analysis supports further clinical exploration of these tools for triaging daily psychological distress, though our results suggest the relative value of psychosocial assessments and digital data should be carefully analyzed. External validation is needed before clinical use.

articles.title: Clonal Hematopoiesis and Incident Solid Cancers Resolved by Histologic Subtype: A Prospective Cohort Study
articles.abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) is a recognized precursor of myeloid malignancy and an independent cardiovascular risk factor, but its relationship with solid tumors is incompletely defined, particularly at histologic resolution. Here, we quantify the association between CHIP and incident cancer across hematologic and solid-organ sites, by clone size, mutation number, and histologic subtype in a prospective cohort of UK Biobank participants with baseline genetic sequencing and cancer ascertained by national registry linkage; those with pre-baseline cancer were excluded. Vanderbilt BioVU was used for replication. CHIP was associated with any incident cancer (HR, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.18-1.27) and with all solid tumors combined (HR, 1.13; 95% CI, 1.08-1.19). Among 17 endpoints, two survived multiple testing correction: lung adenocarcinoma (HR, 1.79; 95% CI, 1.48 - 2.16) and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (HR, 2.28; 95% CI, 1.37-3.81). Risk increased with clone size and multi-hit CHIP, most markedly for esophageal cancer (VAF [≥]30%: HR, 2.72), and the esophageal squamous association persisted in 5-year landmark analysis (HR, 2.57). In BioVU, CHIP was directionally associated with esophageal cancer and lung adenocarcinoma and its association with all solid tumors overall (HR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.17-1.32) was confirmed. These findings extend CHIP from a hematologic and cardiovascular risk marker to a risk marker of solid-organ cancer risk with histologic resolution and motivate clone-size aware risk models and mechanistic studies.

articles.title: Co-Design of the VIRtual physiotherapist-led Triage of referrals to shoUlder surgEons (VIRTUE) model of care: a study protocol
articles.abstract: Background: Rotator cuff-related shoulder pain accounts for up to 85% of shoulder pain. Guidelines recommend 6 months of non-surgical care before considering surgery, yet many are referred to a surgeon before trying it. High referral rates to public hospital shoulder surgery clinics in Australia mean many patients wait 1-2 years to see a surgeon, during which symptoms may become more complex and costly to manage. A promising solution is the VIRtual physiotherapist-led Triage of referrals to shoUlder surgEons (VIRTUE) model of care, in which physiotherapists screen new referrals and determine suitability for non-surgical care or surgical review. However, no such model has been co-designed to incorporate virtual care nor evaluated in a randomised controlled trial. Aims: The broad aim of this study is to co-design the VIRTUE model of care ready for evaluation in a randomised controlled trial conducted in public hospital shoulder surgery clinics in Australia. Specifically, this study has two aims (two stages): i) explore stakeholders perceptions of the feasibility, acceptability and implementation of the VIRTUE model of care for adults with rotator cuff-related shoulder pain who are referred to public hospital shoulder surgery clinics; and ii) co-design the VIRTUE model of care so that it is user-centred and acceptable to patients, clinicians and key stakeholders. Methods: Stage 1 is a qualitative descriptive study using semi-structured online interviews with patients, clinicians and key stakeholders, recruited using purposive, maximum variation sampling. Interviews will explore experiences of current care, perceptions of the proposed model, and barriers and facilitators to implementation, guided by the Theoretical Framework for Acceptability and Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research. Stage 2 will use Experience-Based Co-Design methodology and involves three online workshops: separate workshops for patients, and for clinicians and key stakeholders, then a combined workshop. Workshops will explore Stage 1 findings, perceptions of the proposed model, and refinements needed to finalise it, with data mapped to the Framework for Reporting Adaptations and Modifications-Expanded. Conclusion: Co-designing VIRTUE with patients, clinicians and key stakeholders will ensure it is user-centred, acceptable and feasible within Australian public health services, ready for evaluation in a randomised controlled trial. By facilitating timely and equitable access to evidence-based care, VIRTUE could improve outcomes for patients, ensure specialist services are available for those most in need, and improve health system performance.

articles.title: Cognitive Performance in Prodromal Neuronal α Synuclein Disease
articles.abstract: Importance: Cognitive abnormalities may emerge during prodromal neuronal a-synuclein disease (NSD), but their domain specificity and longitudinal course are uncertain. Objective: To characterize baseline cognition and longitudinal change in prodromal NSD compared with healthy controls, NSD-negative genetic carriers, and sporadic Parkinson disease (PD). Design: Longitudinal cohort study using Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI) data, with first visits from July 2010 through April 2026 and up to 4 years of follow-up. Setting: Multicenter cohort. Participants: Healthy controls (HC; n=244), GBA1 or LRRK2 nonmanifesting carriers without NSD (n=323), prodromal NSD participants recruited through hyposmia or isolated rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder cohorts (n=1640), and sporadic PD (n=824). Exposures: NSD status and clinical cohort. Main Outcomes and Measures: Cognitive summary scores for verbal memory, executive function, processing speed, language, and visuospatial function, and PPMI-defined mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Models adjusted for age, sex, education, and APOE {varepsilon}4 status. Results: Among 3031 participants (mean [SD] age, 66.6 [7.0] years; 1322 female [43.6%]), prodromal NSD participants had lower baseline verbal-memory performance than HC (adjusted difference, -0.20 SD; 95% CI, -0.34 to -0.07; adjusted P = .007); NSD-negative genetic carriers did not differ from HC. No other cognitive domain was lower than HC at baseline or longitudinally. In the primary age-adjusted analysis, verbal-memory trajectory differed from HC over 4 years (P = .009), whereas in a smaller age-matched sensitivity subset through year 3, it did not (P = .62); the baseline difference persisted (adjusted difference, -0.28 SD; 95% CI, -0.46 to -0.10; P = .003). Adjusted MCI probability increased from 10.2% to 15.1% in prodromal NSD, compared with 8.4% to 5.0% in HC and 13.4% to 17.7% in PD. The increase was greater than in HC (ratio of annual odds ratios, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.58; adjusted P = .04) but not PD (P = .62). Conclusions and Relevance: Prodromal NSD was associated with modestly lower verbal memory and increasing MCI probability relative to HC, without lower performance in other cognitive domains. The baseline verbal-memory difference was robust, whereas the longitudinal trajectory finding was not reproduced in the smaller age-matched sensitivity subset.

articles.title: Communication without dialogue? Framing patient-professional interaction in UK institutional discourse on pregnancy loss
articles.abstract: Communication failures are repeatedly implicated in harmful experiences and outcomes in pregnancy care, especially in contexts of loss, yet little is known about how communication itself is represented in the institutional texts that shape expectations of care. This study examines the extent to which communication is discussed, and how patient-healthcare professional interaction is framed, in publicly accessible UK discourse about pregnancy loss. Two corpora comprising texts from seven medical organisations (120,383 words) and eight charities (224,481 words) were divided into healthcare professional-facing and patient-facing sub-corpora. Frequency, semantic keyness, keyword and concordance analyses were conducted using Wmatrix7. In medical discourse, language and communicative interaction were underrepresented, while speech acts associated with unidirectional professional activities such as advising, recommending and referring were overrepresented. Compared with charity texts, medical outputs foregrounded clinical evidence, policy, risk and professional knowledge. Characteristic forms including 'confirmed', 'advised', 'recommended' and 'offered' frequently occurred in passive or agentless constructions that positioned patients principally as recipients of information; patient agency was most visible in 'reporting' symptoms or concerns. Charity discourse more often foregrounded talking, listening, feelings, preferences, wording, lived experience, and patient knowledge; representing communication as active and bidirectional. We argue that UK medical discourse constructs communication primarily as the transmission of authorised knowledge rather than as relational clinical practice, reinforcing a paternalistic distribution of communicative agency. Medical institutions should embed listening, reciprocal dialogue, sensitivity to language preferences, and checks on understanding as core standards of safe pregnancy care.

articles.title: Determinants of Prehospital Management of Superficial Burns in Pediatric Patients at Health Facilities in Mazabuka District: A Cross-Sectional Study
articles.abstract: Background Burn injuries in children are common in low-resource settings, yet little is known about how they are managed before reaching health facilities in Zambia. Early care at home plays a key role in recovery, but harmful practices are still widely used. We examined how caregivers manage superficial burns in children and identified factors linked to good prehospital care in Mazabuka District. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study between September and December 2025 among 337 caregivers of children aged 0-15 years presenting with superficial burns. The study was conducted at three health facilities in Mazabuka District. Data were collected using structured interviews and clinical records. Prehospital burn care was classified as good or poor based on the recommended first-aid practices. Associations were assessed using Firth penalised logistic regression, and results are reported as adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Only 13.1% (44/337) of caregivers provided good prehospital burn care. Urban residence was associated with lower odds of good management (AOR 0.22; 95% CI: 0.05-0.92; p=0.038). Older caregiver age reduced the odds of good care (AOR 0.92; 95% CI: 0.86-0.98; p=0.011), while increasing child age improved it (AOR 1.25; 95% CI: 1.10-1.43; p<0.001). Longer time to reach a facility was also associated with poorer care (AOR 0.96; 95% CI 0.94-0.98; p<0.001). Conclusion Good prehospital burn care was uncommon. It was associated with time to the health facility, caregiver age, child age, and urban versus rural residence, rather than with proximity to a facility alone. Programmes should promote cooling with running water, avoidance of harmful home applications, and prompt care-seeking. Messages in routine child health services may reach caregivers of young children; additional approaches are needed for older caregivers and urban communities.

articles.title: Development and Preliminary Evaluation of a Brief Health Chatbot Acceptability Scale (CAS): A Pilot Study
articles.abstract: Background. Conversational agents (chatbots) are increasingly used to deliver health information to middle-aged and older adults, a population in which the determinants of technology acceptance are known to diverge from those of younger users. However, acceptability is inconsistently defined and typically measured with ad hoc, unvalidated instruments. The psychometrically sound chatbot measures that exist assess usability rather than acceptability or were validated in student samples. Objective. To develop and conduct an initial psychometric evaluation of a brief, 10-item health chatbot acceptance measure grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). Methods. Twenty adults (mean age = 52.8 years, range 28-81; 85% aged 40 or older; 75% female) enrolled in a sleep-application pilot usability study completed the 10 candidate items, the System Usability Scale (SUS), and sleep measures (PROMIS Sleep Disturbance 8a; Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index). We examined item performance, internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha), dimensionality (exploratory factor analysis with oblique rotation), and convergent validity (correlations with the SUS). Results. A two-factor structure emerged and was invariant across rotation methods, resulting in an Information Quality factor and an Acceptance factor (interfactor r = .39). All items loaded ≥ .60 on their primary factor; mean communality was .83. Subscale reliabilities were high (Information Quality α = .96; Acceptance α = .94; full scale α = .93). Both subscales correlated with the SUS in the expected direction (r = .69 and r = .59), providing preliminary support for convergent validity. Conclusions. The measure shows a coherent and theory-consistent two-factor structure and shows preliminary evidence of reliability and convergent validity. Given the small pilot sample, these results must be viewed as provisional but identify the measure as a candidate for formal validation in a larger, independent sample.

articles.title: Digital Twin-Based Risk Stratification Integrating Aortic Shape and Wall Mechanics in Acute Uncomplicated Type B Aortic Dissection
articles.abstract: Objective This study evaluated whether patient-specific digital twins integrating 3D aortic anatomy and structural wall stress could identify patients with acute uncomplicated type B aortic dissection (AUTBAD) at high risk for adverse aortic events. Methods We analyzed CTAs from 50 patients extracted from a 400 AUTBAD patient database treated with optimal medical therapy from 1999-2025. Digital twin models were constructed, and statistical shape modeling and reduced-order fluid-structure interaction analysis were performed. Anatomic shape and biomechanical stress data were integrated into models predicting freedom from aortic events, defined as intervention or aortic-related death, using leave-one-out cross-validation. A cross-validated risk score was generated for each patient, with higher scores indicating higher event risk. Results At diagnosis, the median descending aortic diameter was 40.61 mm. During follow-up, 35 patients experienced an aortic event: 28 interventions (56%) and 7 aortic-related deaths (14%). Stratification by descending aortic diameter above or below 40.61 mm yielded higher- versus lower-risk aortic event-free survival of 72.0% versus 84.0% at 1 year and 27.8% versus 56.7% at 6 years (p=0.035; C-index=0.590). In the cross-validated multidimensional model combining morphology and structural stress, higher- versus lower-risk event-free survival was 60.0% versus 96.0% at 1 year and 12.5% versus 68.9% at 6 years (p<0.001; C-index=0.792). Conclusions Digital twin modeling integrating morphology and wall stress provided greater risk separation than univariable predictors in AUTBAD patients. With independent validation, patient-specific AUTBAD risk stratification using geometric and biomechanical data may ultimately contribute to identification of high-risk patients who may benefit from early endovascular repair.

articles.title: Disability-relevant demyelination in multiple sclerosis: five-year evolution following diagnosis
articles.abstract: Improved understanding of how myelin damage contributes to disability in multiple sclerosis (MS) is needed to inform targeted therapeutic strategies and improve clinical trial platforms. Magnetization transfer saturation ( MTsat ) and T 1 relaxometry provide in vivo quantitative MRI measures of myelin integrity, and may offer insights into disability-relevant pathology beyond inflammatory relapse. This longitudinal study explores the relationship between early demyelination and disability progression over the first five years following diagnosis. 62 people with relapsing-remitting (pwRR)MS (≤ 6 months post-diagnosis, 48 female, mean age 38 years) underwent baseline and one-year MRI and Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) assessment. At five-year follow-up, 56/62 (90.3%) completed EDSS and 40/62 additionally completed MRI (64.5%). Disability progression was defined as an increase of ≥ 1.5, ≥ 1.0 or ≥ 0.5 points for a previous EDSS score of < 1.0, 1.0 to 5.5, and ≥ 6.0, respectively. Baseline neurofilament light chain (NfL), glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and EBNA1 immunoglobulin (IgG) titres were also measured. MTsat was calculated within normal-appearing white matter (NAWM), white matter lesions (WML), cortical and deep grey matter (GM) structures. Associations between change in MTsat and disability progression were assessed with binomial logistic regression. Interactions with interval disease activity (i.e. new/enlarging lesions [NELs]) were investigated, and comparisons were made with healthy control test-retest data (n = 11). Exploratory analyses were performed for: (prolonged) T 1 ; baseline metrics; blood-derived markers; diffusion-weighted imaging; and, disability-associated differences in five-year microstructural MRI trajectories. Greater baseline-to-one-year decreases in NAWM and WML MTsat were associated with baseline-to-one-year disability progression (adjusted odds ratio [95% confidence interval] = 0.255 [0.078 to 0.602] and 0.261 [0.084 to 0.638]; false discovery rate [FDR]-corrected p -value = 0.015 and 0.015). NELs did not influence these associations (interaction p -values > 0.05). One-to-five-year changes in MTsat were not associated with one-to-five-year disability progression (FDR-corrected p -values > 0.05). Neither baseline nor baseline-to-one-year MTsat changes predicted future disability progression. No exploratory analyses reached FDR-corrected statistical significance. We show for the first time that progressive NAWM and WML demyelination measured with MTsat is associated with early disability progression in recently diagnosed RRMS, independent of radiological inflammatory disease activity. Neither MTsat nor T 1 are associated with longer-term progression over the subsequent four years. MTsat is sensitive to disability-relevant demyelination not visible on conventional MRI, indicates a potential early window of therapeutic opportunity in the year following diagnosis, and is a promising clinically applicable disease stratifier and surrogate endpoint for therapeutic trials.

articles.title: EIN-RECAP: Evidence-Grounded Multi-Agent Summarization and Retrieval of Infectious-Disease Expert Discussions
articles.abstract: Infectious disease experts exchange practical knowledge through clinical discussions, but identifying relevant information across years of conversations is difficult. These discussions often contain differing opinions and emerging observations that are not yet reflected in published evidence. We present EIN-RECAP, an AI-assisted platform developed with Emerging Infections Network (EIN) experts and deployed in beta to summarize and search historical discussions. The system combines retrieval-grounded summarization, citation validation, and hybrid search while distinguishing published evidence from community experience. We evaluated summarization methods across 3,185 threads and conducted blinded expert review on a recent subset. Although a multi-agent workflow achieved stronger automated scores, experts favored a simpler generation pipeline and identified repetition, inaccuracies, and overconfident recommendations in the more complex system. This feedback motivated an ensemble that improved discussion coverage and key clinical points on nine high-disagreement threads, although retrieval relevance remained a limitation. Our findings demonstrate the importance of expert involvement in clinical AI development and show why automated evaluation alone is insufficient to guide system selection.

articles.title: Effect of results-based financing on selected maternal and child health indicators in Mayuge District, Uganda: a comparative interrupted time series analysis
articles.abstract: Background Uganda continues to experience a high burden of maternal and child morbidity and mortality, partly due to suboptimal utilization and quality of reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health services. To address these challenges, the Ministry of Health of Uganda, with World Bank funding, implemented results-based financing (RBF) through the Uganda Reproductive, Maternal, and Child Health Services Improvement Project (URMCHIP) in selected districts. Although RBF has been implemented for nearly a decade, evidence on its impact on maternal and child health service indicators in Uganda remains limited. This study assessed the effect of RBF on selected maternal and child health indicators in Mayuge District, Uganda. Methods We retrospectively reviewed the records between July 2018 and June 2019 as the pre-intervention period, July 2019 to June 2021 as the intervention period, and July 2021 to June 2023 as the post-intervention period. We conducted multiple-group interrupted time-series analyses to compare trends in selected maternal and child health indicators between four intervention and three non-intervention health facilities. Results After the implementation of RBF, the number of births in the intervention facilities increased by 1.67 births per month (95% CI [0.19, 3.16]) as compared to the control facilities. The number of women receiving modern family planning methods in intervention facilities increased by 34.1 women per month (CI [25.8, 42.4] as compared to the control facilities. The number of children under five years seen at the outpatient department slightly decreased by -0.24 children per month (CI [-9.58, 9.10]). There was a decline in facility-based births and the number of clients receiving modern family planning methods following the discontinuation of results-based financing in the intervention health facilities. Conclusions There was an improvement in selected maternal and child health indicators in the intervention health facilities following the implementation of RBF, with a subsequent decline in facility-based births and the number of clients receiving modern family planning methods after RBF was discontinued. We recommend that policymakers consider allocating additional funds towards RBF to improve health service delivery.

articles.title: Electric and Magnetic Source Imaging in Epilepsy: Anatomical Insights from Realistic Simulations
articles.abstract: Neurosurgery is an effective treatment for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE), but its success depends on the accurate delineation of the epileptogenic focus, approximated noninvasively by electric and magnetic source imaging (ESI/MSI) of high-density electroencephalography (HD-EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG). These modalities have distinct sensitivity profiles; consequently, epileptiform activity detected by one modality may remain undetected by the other. However, the implications of these differences for spike detectability and localization accuracy, and the added value of combined electromagnetic source imaging (EMSI), remain insufficiently characterized under clinically realistic conditions. Here, we characterize HD-EEG and MEG sensitivity profiles and compare ESI, MSI, and EMSI, using realistic simulations with known ground truth. We generated HD-EEG and MEG datasets from cortical, insular, and hippocampal sources across multiple orientations, activated using patient-derived intracranial EEG spike waveforms. Spike sensitivity and localization accuracy were evaluated using dipole scanning, dynamic statistical parametric mapping (dSPM), and linearly constrained minimum variance (LCMV). EEG demonstrated higher spike detection rates and sensitivity for radially cortical sources at gyral crowns and sulcal bottoms (p<0.001), while MEG detected more spikes from tangential cortical sources along sulcal walls (p<0.001). MSI localized tangential sources more accurately than ESI across all methods (p<0.001), while dipole scanning outperformed dSPM and LCMV for cortical and insular sources (p<0.001). EMSI outperformed ESI (p<0.001) but did not improve localization over MSI. These findings suggest that complementary anatomical sensitivities of HD-EEG and MEG may improve epileptogenic source characterization, supporting simultaneous acquisition during the presurgical evaluation of patients with DRE.

articles.title: Epidemiological Modeling of Seasonal Influenza Through Periodic Mean-Reverting Stochastic Processes
articles.abstract: Seasonal influenza follows annual cycles, but variation in epidemic magnitude and timing complicates preparedness. We applied periodic mean reverting stochastic differential equations (SDEs) to seven seasons of weekly Texas influenza surveillance data. Missing observations were imputed using MissForest and compared with four alternative methods. Stochastic variability was modeled using {sigma}X(t) dW(t), with p = 1/2,2/3,5/6, and 1, representing square root, intermediate sublinear, and multiplicative diffusion. Each specification was evaluated for direct influenza modeling and within a susceptible, exposed, infectious , and recovered model incorporating waning immunity, where the SDE governed transmission. Parameters were estimated using least squares and approximate maximum likelihood for direct models and sample-proportion weighted least squares for stochastic SEIR models. Model-based parametric bootstrap assessed direct-model parameter uncertainty. For direct modeling, p = 1/2 achieved the lowest RMSE (712.8) and AIC (5383.0), with similar AIC for p = 2/3 (5383.2). For stochastic SEIR modeling, p = 1 achieved the lowest RMSE (0.02926), compared with 0.03506 for p = 1/2. The deterministic SEIR model yielded R = 1.158. Transmission peaked approximately 10 weeks before infectious prevalence, while stochastic transmission generated variation in epidemic peak timing. Bootstrap analysis identified dependence between mean-reversion and diffusion parameters. Overall, the appropriate diffusion structure depended on the epidemiological quantity modeled, supporting flexible characterization of seasonal transmission variability while requiring prospective validation before operational forecasting.

articles.title: Exercise reshapes cellular immunity toward anti-inflammation and diminishes CCR4 levels on LFA-1αhighCD4+ T cells in multiple sclerosis
articles.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) represents a multifaceted neuroinflammatory disease for which regular exercise is now recommended by many healthcare institutions. Although preclinical studies indicate robust immunomodulatory effects of exercise, evidence from human studies is lacking. In this randomized controlled trial, persons with MS (pwMS) were assigned to three months of high-intensity interval training or a passive control condition, with outcomes assessed at baseline, after intervention, and a fourweek follow-up. Additionally, a healthy matched control group was included. Besides exercise-induced sustained increases in physical fitness, systemic inflammation was diminished and the Treg-to-TH17.1 ratio improved after exercise. Untargeted proteomic analysis of peripheral blood mononuclear cells covering >7000 proteins revealed an exercise-induced decrease in proteins implicated in inflammatory diseases (i.e., MTHFD2). This was supported by inferred transcription factor activity analysis, which indicated enhanced polarization of immune cells toward anti-inflammatory phenotypes at follow-up. Using flow cytometry, we identified an LFA-1αhighCD4+ T-cell subset that was associated with disease biomarkers and exhibited increased CCR4 expression compared to healthy matched subjects which was reduced after exercise. Our findings significantly expand knowledge of how exercise training exerts immediate and sustained immunomodulatory effects in pwMS and thereby strengthens the mechanistic rationale for exercise recommendations made by healthcare professionals.

articles.title: Food-Group Intakes and Depression in Tangerang, Indonesia: An Exploratory Case-Control Study
articles.abstract: Background: Diet may be associated with depression, but evidence on locally consumed food groups in Indonesia is limited. Objectives: To compare food-group intake between people with and without a formal diagnosis of depression in Tangerang, Indonesia, and to explore whether BMI modifies any association. Methods: In this case-control study, cases were psychiatric outpatients with a formal diagnosis of depression. Controls had no formal diagnosis and were recruited through university and community networks. Daily intake of ten food groups was estimated with a semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire. Intakes were compared with independent-samples t-tests (Welch's test when variances were unequal), overall and stratified by BMI group. Logistic regression estimated the odds of depression per 100 g/day of sweetened beverage intake, adjusted for BMI group, sex, and age, with a sweetened beverage and BMI group interaction term. Results: There were 257 participants: 104 cases and 153 controls. Sweetened beverages were the only food group whose intake differed significantly between groups (approximately 214 vs. 153 g/day; mean difference 61 g/day; 95% CI 18-103; p=0.005). Each additional 100 g/day was associated with higher odds of depression after adjustment (OR 1.29; 95% CI 1.09-1.52). The association appeared stronger in underweight/normal-weight participants (ratio of ORs for overweight/obese vs. underweight/normal 0.70; 95% CI 0.49-0.99; p for interaction=0.046). Conclusions: Higher sweetened beverage intake was associated with depression in this sample, and there was modest evidence that the association differed by BMI group. Because the study is cross-sectional in timing, the case-control samples were selected differently, and many comparisons were made, these findings are exploratory. They do not establish causality.

articles.title: Foundation models capture human and environmental context to improve dengue forecasting
articles.abstract: Accurate and timely probabilistic dengue forecasts can support public health preparedness, but producing reliable forecasts across locations and time horizons remains challenging. We evaluated five statistical, machine-learning, deep-learning, and foundation-model approaches for forecasting monthly reported dengue cases across 5,570 Brazilian municipalities at 1-, 3-, 6- and 12-month horizons, with forecasts backtested from January 2020 to August 2025. The time-series foundation model TimesFM maintained comparatively stable probabilistic forecast performance at longer horizons, while most other models showed declining performance. We then tested whether spatial representations of human and environmental context from a Population Dynamics Foundation Model (PDFM) could improve forecasts through post-hoc residual adjustment. PDFM adjustment improved mean probabilistic forecast performance, measured by the Weighted Interval Score (WIS), in 19 of 20 model-horizon combinations, although the magnitude and frequency of improvements varied across models, horizons and municipalities. The largest improvements were observed for N-BEATS, including a reduction in mean WIS of 1.13 at the six-month horizon (95% CI [0.84, 1.48]; Diebold-Mariano p < 0.0001), with improvements also observed for XGBoost. The proportion of forecasts improved by PDFM generally increased with locally reported dengue case counts, although this relationship varied between models. Covariate selection, spatial fitting and forecast aggregation strategies showed strong model-dependent effects, while monthly model retraining provided no consistent advantage in the settings evaluated. Together, these findings highlight the potential of pretrained representations for dengue forecasting, with benefits dependent on forecasting architecture, horizon and modelling configuration.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Added to Statin Therapy and Cardiovascular Outcomes in ASCVD A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study
articles.abstract: Objective: To evaluate whether GLP-1 RA use added to statins is associated with lower all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction (MI), and ischemic stroke versus statin monotherapy in ASCVD patients with body mass index (BMI) 30 kg/m2. Approach and Results:Using the TriNetX Research Network (108 U.S. healthcare organizations), we identified ASCVD patients with BMI 30 kg/m2 on statins initiating a GLP-1 RA (n=166,278) versus statin-only controls (n=920,176). Propensity score matching on 34 covariates yielded 119,911 matched pairs followed 3 years. Prespecified analyses included a BMI 35 subgroup (62,385 pairs), four washout sensitivity analyses (30-120 days), and a familial hypercholesterolemia exclusion analysis (161,312 matched pairs). Results. GLP-1 RA use was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality (4.0% vs. 7.5%; HR 0.479; 95% CI: 0.463-0.496; p<0.001), MI (HR 0.762; 95% CI: 0.737-0.788; p<0.001), and ischemic stroke (HR 0.671; 95% CI: 0.588-0.766; p<0.001). Benefits were consistent across the BMI 35 subgroup and all washout analyses. GLP-1 RA users were more likely to achieve LDL <55 mg/dL by risk analysis (17.1% vs. 15.3%; RR 1.118; p<0.001); the Kaplan-Meier analysis was non-significant (HR 1.007; p=0.538). Mortality benefit was preserved in the FH exclusion analysis. Conclusion: ASCVD patients with obesity on statins, GLP-1 RA use was associated with substantially lower mortality, MI, and stroke, suggesting GLP-1 RAs may serve as cardioprotective adjuncts to statin therapy in this population.

articles.title: Genomic epidemiology reconstructs the pre-detection transmission and establishment of chikungunya virus in Guangdong, China
articles.abstract: In 2025, a chikungunya outbreak in southern China resulted in more than 25,000 confirmed cases, but its origins and transmission history remain unresolved. As part of the public health investigation, we generated 1,264 near-complete chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genomes from Guangdong Province and integrated genomic, epidemiological, entomological, and human mobility data to reconstruct the emergence and spread of this outbreak. Our analyses traced the outbreak to a single dominant introduction of a Reunion-associated East/Central/South African (ECSA) virus lineage and dated the origin of the sampled Guangdong outbreak lineage from late April to early May 2025. The interval between the estimated origin of the outbreak lineage and the first reported case was consistent with a period of undetected local transmission and exposed limitations in passive surveillance for early arboviral outbreak detection. Spatiotemporal reconstruction showed two distinct epidemic waves with contrasting transmission dynamics. The Foshan wave involved frequent medium- to long-distance viral movement, while the Jiangmen wave remained relatively localized. Together, these findings reconstruct the early establishment and spatially heterogeneous spread of the largest documented CHIKV epidemic in southern China to date and demonstrate the necessity of expanding active genomic surveillance in areas at the fringe of CHIKV endemic transmission for timely detecting and characterizing emerging epidemics.

articles.title: Genotypic infection endpoint analysis to understand efficacy and escape potential of the malaria monoclonal antibody CIS43LS
articles.abstract: Early-phase trials of candidate malaria interventions in endemic areas often use "time-to-first" infection as a primary efficacy endpoint. This approach does not assess infection risk after the initial infection, and its censoring of trial participants after their first infection can introduce bias by removing more high-risk participants from control than treatment arms over time. Efficacy estimate precision may also decline as risk set size decreases. Here we assessed the utility of genotyping all infections in an intervention trial to determine the total infection incidence in each participant for the full follow-up period. Specifically, we genotyped all Plasmodium falciparum infections detected in a previously-reported phase 2 trial of the antimalarial monoclonal antibody CIS43LS in 330 Malian adults. We determined the molecular force of infection (molFOI; rate of new P. falciparum strains) for each participant, expressing efficacy as the percent molFOI reduction in CIS43LS versus placebo arms (Eff molFOI ). Six-month Eff molFOI was 86.5% (95% CI: 80.1-90.8) and 70.7% (61.0-78.0) for the 40 mg/kg and 10 mg/kg doses, respectively. These estimates are similar to those from time-to-first infection analysis, but more precise when analyzing efficacy by trial-month and when stratifying by P. falciparum infection-status at enrollment. Participants infected at enrollment had lower Eff molFOI and acquired infections earlier in the trial, creating systematic differences in risk composition between arms over time. Genotyping showed no evidence for escape-polymorphisms in the CIS43LS epitope. These results demonstrate how genotypic endpoints can provide a more comprehensive understanding of candidate malaria interventions.

articles.title: Greater Stress Response Network (SRN) Connectivity is Associated with Higher Worry in Men and Women Especially in Later Life
articles.abstract: Background: Late-life anxiety is common and disabling, with pathological worry as a core feature. The Stress Response Network (SRN: amygdala, bed nucleus of the stria terminalis, paraventricular nucleus), which modulates threat and stress reactivity, and its interaction with the Executive Control Network (ECN), anchored by the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, which supports emotional regulation via top-down cognitive control, may underlie individual differences in worry severity. We hypothesize higher SRN connectivity to be associated with greater worry severity and that this relationship may be moderated positively by older age, and female sex. Methods: We recruited older adults with varying worry. Resting-state fMRI was used to compute SRN connectivity and SRN-ECN connectivity. Regression models tested associations between connectivity and worry (PSWQ), anxiety (HARS), and rumination (RSQ), adjusting for age, sex, race, and education. Exploratory models examined age and sex moderation and associations with emotion regulation/suppression and cognitive function. Results: Among 131 participants who were [≥] 50 years old, with varying levels of worry severity, SRN connectivity was significantly associated with greater worry severity (B=23.51 (SE = 12.12), p<0.05), whereas SRN-ECN connectivity was not. SRN connectivity was lower with greater age (B=-0.003 (SE=0.001), p=0.04), yet older individuals reported greater worry than younger with comparable connectivity. Greater language domain cognitive function was associated with lower SRN connectivity but higher SRN-ECN connectivity, while greater overall cognitive function was associated with lower SRN-ECN connectivity. Women reported lower use of daily expressive suppression and higher performance across cognitive measures than men. Higher daily use of expressive suppression was not significantly associated with either connectivity measure. Discussion: SRN connectivity, rather than SRN-ECN connectivity, may serve as the primary neural correlate of worry, shaped by age and cognitive function.

articles.title: Greater than the sum of its parts: A novel psychiatric multimorbidity metric applied to rare disease
articles.abstract: Importance: Rare genetic syndromes are often drivers of complex multimorbidity. However, current methods consider multimorbidity as the sum of chronic diagnoses, which does not account for subthreshold impairment. Objective: To develop a quantitative multimorbidity score (MMS) for rare genetic syndromes that summarizes the neurodevelopmental and psychiatric multimorbidity landscape, including subthreshold symptoms, using 3q29 deletion and 3q29 duplication syndromes as hallmark examples. Design: We developed a multimorbidity metric and applied it to cross-sectional data. Remote phenotyping from 2023-2026. In-person phenotyping from 2017-2020. Setting: Remote phenotyping conducted at Rutgers University. In-person phenotyping conducted at Emory University. Participants: Participants were 6 years of age and older. 3q29del and 3q29dup recruited from the 3q29 registry and direct referrals and contacts. Syndrome status confirmed by genetic report review. Typically developing controls recruited from community sources and ResearchMatch. Main Outcomes and Measures: We developed a quantitative MMS across five distinct domains of functioning, operationalized as the sum of z-scores across six standardized assessments. The MMS was calculated for each study participant and compared across groups. Within 3q29del, we evaluated the relationship between MMSs and Vineland-3 adaptive behavior. Results: 96 individuals with 3q29del (52.08% male, 18.01+/-11.47 years old), 28 individuals with 3q29dup (50.00% male, 20.82+/-13.64 years old), and 53 controls (41.51% male, 17.77+/-10.74 years old) were included. 3q29del and 3q29dup participants had significantly lower MMS scores compared to controls (3q29del mean=-8.22+/-4.67, 3q29dup mean=-6.47+/-4.66, control mean=1.36+/-2.35, 3q29del p<2E-16, 3q29dup p=4.89E-16). Within 3q29del, subjects with more severe multimorbidity had greater impairment in adaptive behavior (R2=0.589, p<2E-16). The quantitative MMS is more highly correlated with adaptive behavior than traditional diagnosis-based multimorbidity metrics (quantitative MMS R2=0.589, diagnosis-based multimorbidity R2=0.447). In a subset of 24 3q29del participants with longitudinal data (58.33% male, 13.17+/-9.08 years old at first evaluation, average time to follow up=5.17+/-0.87 years), the MMS is stable over time (R2=0.858, p=8.34E-8). Conclusions and Relevance: Our novel quantitative MMS is an improved metric for measuring psychiatric multimorbidity in high-risk populations, and accounts for the impact of subthreshold impairments. When applied to 3q29del and 3q29dup, it quantifies the individual burden of multimorbidity, is stable over time, and is associated with clinical outcome measures.

articles.title: Hidden overweight and adverse birth outcomes among Asian mothers in the United States, 2016-2023: a population-based repeated cross-sectional study
articles.abstract: Background: Standard body mass index (BMI) categories may understate risk in Asian individuals. Lower Asian action points exist, but their relevance to birth outcomes is unclear. Objectives: To estimate the proportion of normal-weight Asian mothers with BMI 23.0-24.9 kg/m2 and its association with birth outcomes, overall and by Asian subgroup, and to compare Asian and White mothers. Methods: Repeated cross-sectional study of US singleton live births, 2016-2023 (National Vital Statistics System). Outcomes were hypertensive disorders, caesarean delivery, preterm birth, and low birthweight. Modified Poisson regression, adjusted for confounders and Asian subgroup, estimated risk ratios (RRs), standardized risks, and risk differences (RDs). We tested for a change in slope at 23.0 kg/m2, subgroup heterogeneity, and race x BMI interaction. Results: Among 1,758,116 non-Hispanic Asian mothers, 314,510 (17.9%) had BMI 23.0-24.9 kg/m2, 30.4% of normal-weight mothers. Compared with BMI 18.5-22.9, standardized risk of hypertensive disorders was 4.5% versus 3.2% (RD 1.4 percentage points, 95% CI 1.3, 1.5; RR 1.44, 95% CI 1.40, 1.47), and of caesarean delivery 32.4% versus 28.6% (RR 1.14, 95% CI 1.13, 1.14). Preterm birth risk was 7.2% versus 6.6% (RR 1.08, 95% CI 1.06, 1.10); low birthweight risk was not higher (7.1% versus 7.5%; RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.93, 0.97). The hypertensive-disorder slope showed no evidence of change at 23.0 (ratio of per-unit RRs 0.99, 95% CI 0.98, 1.01); the hypertensive-disorder RR ranged from 1.24 (95% CI 1.18, 1.29) among Asian Indian to 1.70 (95% CI 1.60, 1.81) among Chinese mothers. BMI-outcome associations differed between Asian and White mothers. Conclusions: Nearly one in three normal-weight Asian mothers had BMI 23.0-24.9 kg/m2, associated with higher risks of hypertensive disorders and caesarean delivery but not low birthweight. The hypertensive-disorder gradient showed no evidence of change at 23.0 kg/m2, and associations varied across Asian subgroups.

articles.title: Hypoxic Burden Predicts Symptomatic but Not Sleep Architecture Response to CPAP Therapy in Obstructive Sleep Apnea
articles.abstract: The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) remains the standard metric for assessing obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity, although it does not fully capture the physiological consequences of respiratory events. Hypoxic burden (HB), which integrates the frequency, depth, and duration of oxygen desaturations, has been proposed as a more comprehensive measure of OSA-related hypoxic stress. This study compared the prognostic value of HB and AHI for subjective and objective treatment outcomes in patients undergoing continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. Data from 412 patients with OSA who underwent diagnostic and CPAP-treated polysomnography were analyzed, including 52 patients with available follow-up questionnaires. HB was calculated using a validated event-based algorithm. Multivariable regression models were used to predict patient-reported outcomes and changes in sleep architecture, adjusted for age, sex and body mass index. HB consistently demonstrated stronger associations with symptomatic outcomes than AHI. Models including HB showed improved model fit and explained variance. HB remained independently associated with lower follow-up fatigue and better sleep quality after adjustment for AHI. In contrast, AHI was the dominant predictor of objective sleep architecture improvements, including increases in N3 sleep, reductions in N1 sleep, and reductions in arousal index. HB provided additional independent information only for changes in arousal burden. These findings suggest that HB and AHI capture complementary dimensions of OSA severity. While AHI primarily reflects sleep fragmentation and physiological response to CPAP, HB appears more closely related to subjective treatment benefit. Incorporating HB alongside AHI may improve clinical phenotyping and prediction of treatment response in OSA.

articles.title: Individualised and Time-Dependent Prediction of Recurrence After Colorectal Cancer Liver Metastases Resection
articles.abstract: Introduction: Treatment strategies for colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) are increasingly complex, driving interest in advanced prognostic tools. Externally validated benchmarks based on established clinical risk scores are needed to contextualise emerging models. However, existing scores remain difficult to apply and compare, because they provide categorical risk strata rather than individualised probabilities, and because model parameters are rarely published. Here, we validate and recalibrate seven established risk scores to derive individualised recurrence probabilities for future score benchmarking. Method: Patients undergoing index CRLM resection from two tertiary centres were included: Karolinska University Hospital (retrospective KaroLiver cohort [2013-2021, follow-up to 2025, n=709]) and Oslo University Hospital (OSLO-COMET trial cohort [2012-2016, follow-up to 2022, n=198]). Performance of the GAME, m-CS, Fong, Nordlinger, Nagashima, Konopke and Helsinki scores was assessed using recurrence-free survival as the primary outcome. Results: Among 709 patients in KaroLiver (median age 67 years [IQR 59-74]; 434 men [61%]), 422 (60%) had synchronous metastases and 444 (63%) received neoadjuvant chemotherapy. All scores significantly stratified recurrence risk (log-rank P<0.001; time-dependent AUC 0.63-0.74 at 3 years), albeit with performance differences across time points. Recalibrated models showed good agreement between predicted and observed recurrence and were externally validated in OSLO-COMET with broadly comparable net benefit. Models were implemented in the online tool PLATO (Personalised Liver metastases risk AssessmenT in Oncology). Conclusion: Established CRLM risk scores can be translated into individualised probabilistic recurrence estimates at clinically relevant time points, supporting patient communication, risk-adapted surveillance and transparent benchmarking of next-generation prognostic models.

articles.title: KNOWLEDGE, ATTITUDES AND PRACTICES OF REFUSE DISPOSAL IN OKELELE, ILORIN, NIGERIA
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Improper refuse disposal remains an environmental health concern in many Nigerian communities. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes and practices relating to refuse disposal among adult residents of Okelele community, Ilorin East Local Government Area, Kwara State, Nigeria. METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional community-based study was conducted among 180 adults. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge, attitudes and disposal practices. Descriptive statistics summarised responses, and chi-square tests assessed associations between categorical variables at a 5% significance level. RESULTS: Of 180 respondents, 102 (56.7%) had good knowledge, while 87 (48.3%) had negative attitudes and 99 (55.0%) had poor refuse-disposal practices. Commonly reported practices included incineration (50.6%), disposal into drains (30.6%) and open burning (21.7%). Absence of waste containers (37.2%) and distance to available containers (28.9%) were the leading reported barriers. Knowledge was associated with practice (chi-square=22.122; p<0.001) and attitude (chi-square=8.221; p=0.016); practice was also associated with attitude (chi-square=5.970; p=0.015). CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS FOR TRANSLATION: Despite generally good knowledge, poor disposal practices were common. Improving access to reliable waste-collection infrastructure, alongside community education and enforcement of local waste-management measures, may help translate knowledge into safer practices. Keywords: Solid waste; Waste management; Knowledge; Attitude; Health behavior; Nigeria

articles.title: Late-Stage Concentration of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Burden in US Adults: Disability-Adjusted Life Years Across AHA Stages, 2005 to 2023
articles.abstract: Background: Cardiovascular prevention is increasingly prioritised using burden estimates, yet disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) reward late-stage treatment by construction. Whether that bias is large for cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, and where the population is accumulating relative to where the burden sits, is unknown. Methods: We pooled nine National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cycles (2005-2023) and assigned CKM stages 0-4 from measured blood pressure, adiposity, glycaemia, lipids, kidney function, urine albumin, self-reported cardiovascular disease, and 10-year PREVENT risk. Years lived with disability used GBD disability weights. Years of life lost combined national death counts, stage-specific mortality from linked mortality files (1999-2018), and period life tables. A second aim attributed burden to smoking and physical inactivity, two exposures outside the CKM definition.
