articles.abstract: We provide the first characterization of Magnesium–Vacancy (MgV) color centers under hydrostatic high‐pressure conditions. The luminescent defects were fabricated upon ion implantation into a diamond anvil, which was subsequently assembled into a Diamond Anvil Cell (DAC). The photoluminescence study, performed at 87 K, reveals a blueshift of the Zero‐Phonon Line (ZPL) induced by increasing compressive stress, with a slope of 2.1 meV/GPa. A theoretical model of the electronic level structure of the MgV−${\rm MgV}^-$ center has been developed to support the experimental findings, showing good compatibility with the measured shift. In addition, the optical response of MgV−${\rm MgV}^-$ centers was investigated upon temperature variations.The results obtained further confirm the previously reported temperature‐induced shift of the ZPL, which undergoes a redshift during cool down, in the opposite direction with respect to that observed in other color centers explored under changing temperature. The theoretical calculations reproduce this temperature dependence as well, complementing the characterization of MgV−${\rm MgV}^-$ centers as temperature sensors. These results are discussed in relation to existing studies on MgV−${\rm MgV}^-$ centers, expanding the understanding of this recently discovered quantum emitter and unlocking its employment as an all‐optical sensor of pressure and temperature.

articles.title: Analog‐Tunable Nonvolatile Memristors with Self‐Compliance Behavior via a MoSx‐Interlayer Strategy for Neuromorphic Recognition and Zero‐Trust Image Encryption
articles.abstract: The von Neumann memory wall severely restricts the performance of traditional computing systems, and memristors have emerged as premier candidates for neuromorphic computing by virtue of their ability to integrate storage and computation functions. However, conventional HfOx memristors suffer from abrupt resistive switching and lack of intrinsic self‐protection, limiting their synaptic emulation performance. Herein, a novel nonvolatile HfOx/MoSx/HfOx trilayer heterostructure memristor with intrinsic self‐compliance and analog conductance modulation was constructed. The optimized device exhibits stable cycling endurance, multilevel retention stability and fast response speed, and achieves linear and symmetric conductance potentiation and depression. Furthermore, the proposed memristor successfully emulates diverse biological synaptic plasticities, including EPSC, IPSC, PPF, and PPD. A constructed neural network based on this device achieves a high handwritten digit recognition accuracy of 93.84% on the MNIST dataset, with excellent noise immunity and device variation robustness. Furthermore, the memristor acts as an irreplaceable physical entropy source for zero‐trust XOR‐based image encryption, generating ciphertext images with near‐optimal information entropy reaching 7.978 bits. This work presents a feasible MoSx interlayer modification strategy to optimize high‐performance artificial synapses on oxide memristors, enabling co‐integration of neuromorphic computing and hardware security.

articles.title: Architected Bio‐Based Iontronic Skin With Dual‐Mode Pressure and Strain Sensing
articles.abstract: Human skin encodes pressure and stretch through the motion of ions, a principle soft iontronics reproduce but rarely on sustainable terms. Additive manufacturing has lifted ionogels from cast slabs into architected sensors, yet this progress rests on fossil‐derived acrylates, because plant‐based networks expel the polar ionic liquids that carry charge. Here we print an ionogel whose matrix exceeds 80% bio‐based carbon while stably hosting a hydrophobic imidazolium ionic liquid, resolving a long‐standing compatibility barrier. A single monomer ratio tunes stiffness 30 fold (9 to 0.3 MPa) and nearly doubles ionic conductivity to 0.53 mS cm−1. Printed as gyroid lattices, the material senses pressure capacitively and strain resistively through separable channels: near‐incompressibility pins the gauge factor near 2 irrespective of geometry, whereas the lattice amplifies low‐pressure sensitivity eightfold and accelerates the strain response 4.6‐fold. On the body, both modes track joint motion with complementary signatures. Chemistry and printed architecture thus act as independent levers for renewable iontronic skin.

articles.title: Asymmetrically Coordinated Dysprosium (Dy) Single Atoms/Clusters Synergistic Catalysts Promote High‐Performance Aqueous Zn–I2 Batteries
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc–iodine batteries have attracted considerable attention owing to their environmental friendliness and high theoretical capacity. However, the iodine cathode inevitably suffers from the formation of soluble polyiodides during charge/discharge processes, resulting in active material loss and heavy shuttle effects. In this manuscript, asymmetrically coordinated dysprosium (Dy‐N3O5) single atoms and clusters (DySA+C–NC) were designed and synthesized through high‐temperature annealing of its ZIF precursor. The optimized DySA+C–NC contains highly dispersed Dy‐N/O single atom sites together with Dy cluster sites, which collectively strengthen polyiodide confinement and accelerate reversible iodine conversion. In addition, the nitrogen‐doped carbon host offers continuous electron transport pathways and pore‐confined spaces, contributing to electrolyte wetting, ion diffusion and iodine utilization. In situ Raman, in situ UV–vis and DFT calculation support that the Dy single atoms/clusters effectively confines iodine species and promotes rapid polyiodide conversion. Particularly, PDOS analysis reveals that the overlap between I‐5p and Dy‐5d states enhances interfacial electronic coupling for iodine activation, while the localized Dy‐4f states regulate the electronic environment of Dy centers. The DySA+C–NC@I2 cathode delivers a high discharge capacity of 200.46 mAh g−1 at 5 A g−1 after 25 000 cycles. This work provides a strategy for the design of rare‐earth single atoms/cluster for long‐life aqueous zinc–iodine batteries.

articles.title: Atomic Samarium Doping Reinforces Ir/IrO2 Heterointerface for Efficient Acidic Overall Water Splitting
articles.abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is constrained by the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics and the intrinsic activity-stability trade-off of Ir-based anodes. In this work, an atomically Sm-doped Ir/IrO2 heterointerface catalyst is fabricated via a facile ligand-assisted foaming strategy. The optimized catalyst achieves overpotentials of 246 mV for OER and 19 mV for HER at 10 mA cm−2 in an acidic electrolyte, with a remarkable mass activity of 835.91 A gIr −1 at 1.53 V and long-term stability for 500 h. In PEM electrolyzer, the catalyst delivers 1 A cm−2 at 1.70 V and maintains stability for 325 h, demonstrating great promise for practical acidic water splitting. Combining in-situ spectroscopy and DFT calculations reveals that Sm, with its unique 4f electronic configuration, serves as an electron donor to downshift the d-band center of Ir and strengthen the Ir–O covalent bond. Such electronic modulation tends to the AEM pathway and optimizes the adsorption energetics of oxygenated intermediates. The rate-determining step shifts from *OOH formation to *OH dehydrogenation, thereby reducing the reaction free-energy and mitigating irreversible Ir overoxidation. This work establishes lanthanide doping at heterointerfaces as a powerful strategy to break the activity-stability trade-off in acidic water splitting.

articles.title: Breaking Quasi‐Chelation in Thioether Electrolytes for Synergistic Interfacial Stabilization in Lithium‐Sulfur Batteries
articles.abstract: Lithium‐sulfur batteries (LSBs) have attracted extensive attention owing to their high energy density. However, their development remains severely hindered by sluggish interfacial reaction kinetics, unstable electrode–electrolyte interphases, lithium dendrite growth, and polysulfide shuttling. In this work, we identify a hidden quasi‐chelation effect in ether‐based nitrile solvents, which undermines the effectiveness of weakly solvating electrolyte design, and demonstrate that this limitation can be effectively overcome through a thioether‐substitution strategy. Specifically, replacing the ether oxygen in methoxyacetonitrile with sulfur to form (methylthio)acetonitrile disrupts the quasi‐chelating coordination motif and weakens solvent‐Li+ interactions, and induces anion‐rich solvation structures. Spectroscopic characterizations combined with molecular dynamics simulations reveal that breaking this quasi‐chelation effect lowers the Li+ desolvation barrier and accelerates ion‐transport kinetics. Meanwhile, the preferential decomposition of the thioether solvent promotes the formation of sulfur‐rich, inorganic‐dominated interphases, thereby enabling simultaneous stabilization of both the lithium metal anode and the SPAN cathode. As a result, lithium dendrite growth and polysulfide shuttling are effectively suppressed, and Li||SPAN full cells retain 86% of their initial capacity after 600 cycles under high‐loading conditions. This work demonstrates that quasi‐chelation breaking can serve as an effective molecular design principle for constructing weakly solvating electrolytes toward practical lithium‐sulfur batteries.

articles.title: Breaking the Aperture Limit: Interference‐Enhanced Stacking and Constraint‐Driven Design of Metallic Meshes
articles.abstract: Achieving high optical transmittance and shielding effectiveness (SE) remains challenging for transparent electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials. Herein, a physics‐guided, constraint‐driven design strategy for metallic meshes is developed through electromagnetic simulations, machine learning, and experiments. Single‐layer SE approaches saturation with increasing conductivity at a level set by the mesh geometry, dominated by the period, while the conductivity required for saturation decreases with increasing conductor cross‐section. At a fixed cross‐sectional area, a narrow‐and‐high cross‐section (w < t) improves both SE and transmittance relative to a square one. Interference‐enhanced stacking allows double‐ and triple‐layer SE to reach approximately 2.17 and 3.40 times the single‐layer value expressed in dB, respectively, with equal metal allocation maximizing SE under a fixed metal budget. XGBR and response‐surface models enable rapid screening of structures that meet prescribed SE requirements while balancing transmittance, total interlayer spacing, and metal cross‐sectional area. The selected triple‐layer design achieves 88% transmittance, 10.86% haze, and an average experimental SE of 92.17 dB in the X‐band, and its assembly tolerance and conductivity sensitivity are further analyzed. This strategy links quantitative electromagnetic analysis with requirement‐driven design of transparent metallic meshes.

articles.title: Building‐Block Design of Nonflammable Quasi‐Solid Electrolytes for Ampere‐Hour‐Scale Sodium‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a competitive technology for large‐scale energy storage; however, their commercial viability remains severely hindered by the inherent flammability and high volatility of liquid electrolytes (LEs). Herein, we propose a modular assembly strategy inspired by the building‐block principle to architect a quasi‐solid electrolyte (QSE). By synergistically integrating vinylene carbonate (VC) and 2,2,3,4,4,4‐hexafluorobutyl acrylate (HFBA) monomers, we modulate the electron density distribution within the polymer matrix. The resulting PVH QSE lowers the Na+ desolvation barrier and provides continuous ion migration pathways, thereby achieving exceptional ionic conductivity of 5.60 mS cm−1 and a sodium‐ion transference number of 0.58. Furthermore, the spatially locked polymer architecture drives the formation of ion‐solvent aggregates and a robust NaF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase, synergistically suppressing solvent decomposition and eradicating sodium dendrite growth. Consequently, the Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells exhibit an outstanding capacity retention of 94.9% after 3000 cycles alongside superior temperature adaptability. To demonstrate practical feasibility, the hard carbon||NaNi0.33Fe0.33Mn0.33O2 pouch cells maintain stable cycling over 200 cycles. Crucially, nail penetration and accelerating rate calorimetry (ARC) tests verify the exceptional safety of the pouch cells. By linking molecular microenvironment regulation to macroscopic battery safety, this work illuminates a viable pathway toward the commercialization of intrinsically safe SIBs.

articles.title: Chemical Compatibility Enables Dual‐Role Carbonized Polymer Dots for Robust, Highly Stretchable, and Rapidly Self‐Healing Room‐Temperature Phosphorescent Elastomers
articles.abstract: Achieving persistent room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP), mechanical robustness, high stretchability, and rapid self-healing in a single elastomer is challenging because triplet confinement and load bearing require restricted interactions, whereas deformation and repair require chain mobility and reversible bonding. Here, low-carbonization carbonized polymer dots (CPDs) are directly incorporated into a chemically compatible poly(N,N-dimethylacrylamide-co-methoxy poly(ethylene glycol) acrylate) elastomer (DM 6 ). Chemical compatibility activates the native dual role of CPDs: their partially carbonized domains serve as intrinsic RTP centers, while their polymer-like surfaces form reversible hydrogen bonds with DM 6 , simultaneously providing local triplet confinement and dynamic physical crosslinking. The resulting DM 6 /CPDs-8 exhibits a tensile strength of 6.14 MPa, a fracture strain of 923%, and 94.1% strength recovery after only 30 s of contact at room temperature without heating or external healing agents. Across the composition series, the phosphorescence lifetime reaches 538.1 ms, and the fracture energy reaches 43.2 kJ m− 2, while DM 6 /CPDs-8 maintains tan δ > 1 from 0.02 to 300 Hz. This compatibility-enabled integration provides a direct route to mechanically robust, highly stretchable, rapidly self-healing RTP elastomers with high crack tolerance and broadband damping.

articles.title: Competition Between Weak Localization and Antilocalization of Dirac‐Like Fermions in a Spin‐Polarized Two‐Dimensional Electron Gas at KTaO3 (111) Interface
articles.abstract: Quantum transport phenomena in two‐dimensional electron gases (2DEGs) at oxide interfaces have garnered significant interest owing to their potential in spintronic and quantum information technologies. Here, we systematically investigate the quantum conductance corrections of spin‐polarized 2DEGs formed at the interfaces between two insulating oxides, ferromagnetic EuTiO3 (ETO) films and (111)‐oriented KTaO3 (KTO) substrates. The anomalous Hall effect and hysteretic magnetoresistance provide evidence for long‐range ferromagnetic order in the 2DEGs, which could be attributed to interfacial Eu doping in combination with the magnetic proximity effect of the ETO layer. The breaking of time‐reversal symmetry by ferromagnetism in the 2DEGs, and with the assistance of the spin‐orbit coupling effect, leads to a non‐trivial Berry phase. These results are explained by the competition between weak localization (WL) and weak antilocalization (WAL) in quantum transport due to Dirac‐like fermions at the KTO (111) interfaces, strikingly similar to that observed in spin‐polarized 2DEGs in LAO/ETO/STO (111) heterostructures and magnetically doped topological insulators. Moreover, we find that this competition can be tuned by optical stimuli via a photo‐excitation‐induced shift of the Fermi level. Our findings demonstrate a controllable platform based on spin‐polarized oxide 2DEGs for quantum transport, opening new avenues for spin‐orbitronic and topological electronic applications.

articles.title: Conformational Restriction Unlocks Record Birefringence in Sulfonate Ultraviolet NLO Crystals
articles.abstract: Optimizing second–harmonic generation (SHG), birefringence, and bandgap simultaneously within a single material remains a formidable challenge due to their intrinsic mutual trade‐offs. Herein, we propose a conformational restriction strategy that replaces a flexible monocyclic cation with a rigid polycyclic analogue, which affords two organic ionic sulfonate crystals, [C5H6NO][SO3(C7H5O3)]·2H2O (HPSA) and [C12H9N2][SO3(C7H5O3)] (OPSA). HPSA adopts a highly ordered centrosymmetric (CS) crystal structure, Pbca, stabilized by strong and directional hydrogen bonds. Whereas OPSA crystallizes in a noncentrosymmetric (NCS) space group P21 arising from steric hindrance and weak, asymmetric supramolecular interactions, thereby endowing OPSA with a stable SHG response (1.1 × KDP), with no observable intensity degradation upon heating up to 533 K. Both compounds possess wide bandgaps and pronounced optical anisotropy, notably OPSA with record‐high birefringence (Δn = 0.93@546 nm) among all known NLO crystals containing π‐conjugated groups with bandgap exceeding 3.1 eV. Moreover, OPSA achieves single‐phase white light with an ultrabroad dual‐band spectrum spanning 400–800 nm, enabling a prototype white‐light‐emitting diode with a color rendering index of 87, CIE chromaticity coordinates of (0.31, 0.32), and correlated color temperature of 7185 K. This work expands the structural diversity of sulfonate‐based materials and establishes a rational design strategy for multifunctional optical crystals.

articles.title: Core–Shell Solvation Structure Engineering Enables Practical Lithium Metal Batteries With 475 Wh Kg−1
articles.abstract: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) offer extremely high theoretical energy densities, but face significant challenges in terms of electrolyte compatibility and interface stability. Existing low‐concentration electrolytes struggle to form a robust solid‐electrolyte interface to maintain stable cycling. Here, we designed a low‐concentration electrolyte based on a functionally partitioned core–shell solvation strategy. Methyl sulfone, possessing a relatively high donor number, dominates the primary Li+ coordination domain, while fluoroethylene carbonate, with a low donor number and low viscosity, primarily regulates the outer solvation environment and interfacial chemistry. This design facilitates rapid desolvation, high ionic conductivity (4.42 mS cm−1), and an exceptionally high Li+ transference number (0.74). The core–shell structure induces a gradient SEI, promoting uniform lithium deposition. Consequently, the LiFePO4 (LFP)||Li cell achieved capacity retention of 85.9% after 5000 cycles at 1 C, along with cycling stability from −10°C to 50°C. Practical application was further confirmed by stable cycling of NCM811||Li pouch cells (200 cycles, 95.7%) and NCM811||graphite pouch cells (650 cycles, 88.5%). Furthermore, a 2.2 Ah NCM811||Li pouch cell achieves a gravimetric energy density of 475 Wh kg−1. This work presents a scalable approach to engineering solvation chemistries for high‐voltage and high‐energy‐density LMBs.

articles.title: Correction to “GSH‐Responsive Shape‐Transformable Nanotheranostics for Dual‐Modal T1/T2 MRI‐Guided Enhanced PDT of Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma”
Coupling Ionic Network Reconstruction With Interfacial Electrostatics Shielding Resolves the Interphase Stability‐Transport Trade‐Off for High‐Temperature Durable Li‐SPAN Batteries
articles.abstract: High‐performance lithium‐sulfurized polyacrylonitrile (SPAN) batteries require an electrolyte that simultaneously delivers robust lithium metal stability and efficient bulk ionic transport. However, existing electrolyte engineering strategies generally improve interfacial stability at the expense of bulk transport properties. Herein, by introducing 1‐methyl‐1‐propylpyrrolidinium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (PY13FSI), we achieved a reconstruction of the ionic network, coupled with the electrostatic shielding effect at the interface, breaking the traditional trade‐off between interphase stability and bulk transport kinetics. While forming inorganic‐rich LiF/Li3N interphases on both the cathode and anode to block lithium polysulfide shuttling and homogenize lithium deposition, the electrolyte simultaneously delivers a high ionic conductivity approaching 10 mS cm−1 and an impressive Li+ transference number of 0.71. Consequently, Li||SPAN cells deliver outstanding long‐term cycling stability and rate capability, retaining 94.1% capacity retention after 1100 cycles at 1 C. Meanwhile, stable cycling performance is observed at 60°C. Commercially viable full cells (with a thin Li anode and high‐loading cathode) still demonstrate exceptional performance with a capacity retention of 90.8% after 200 cycles. This work presents an effective strategy to break the conventional trade‐off between interphase stability and bulk ionic transport, offering fresh insights into the future design of advanced electrolytes for high‐energy‐density battery systems.

articles.title: Defect‐Engineered N‐Doped ZnO as a Dual‐Functional Platform for PENG‐Driven Memristive Sensory Memory
articles.abstract: Energy‐efficient computing is a critical challenge for artificial intelligence and edge applications. Although self‐powered memory systems that integrate sensing, energy harvesting, and storage are promising, they often suffer from high leakage currents, poor reproducibility, and material incompatibility. Here, we present a dual‐functional N‐doped ZnO (NZO) platform that electrically couples an interface‐type memristor with a piezoelectric nanogenerator (PENG), enabling self‐powered memory programming. Uniform N‐doping via low‐temperature atomic layer deposition passivates oxygen‐related defects, suppresses leakage currents, and stabilizes resistive switching. A thin TiO2‐x interfacial layer acts as an oxygen reservoir and enables precise barrier engineering for reversible, low‐power multilevel operation. At the same time, the reduced carrier concentration in NZO enhances PENG performance through suppression of electrostatic screening effects. Density functional theory (DFT+U) calculations further predict N‐induced changes in elastic stiffness and compliance, suggesting a possible secondary contribution to the electromechanical response through modified strain accommodation. As a result, the rectified PENG output directly programs the memristor without an external bias. The coupled system exhibits stable multilevel storage, robust endurance, and synaptic plasticity. By co‐designing energy harvesting, sensing, and memory on a unified oxide platform, this work establishes a practical pathway toward energy‐autonomous neuromorphic computing and intelligent tactile memory systems.

articles.title: Defect‐Free Transfer Principles for Scalable, Thin Garnet‐Based Hybrid Solid Electrolytes in Solid‐State Batteries
articles.abstract: The scalable fabrication of thin, uniform, and defect‐free hybrid solid electrolytes (HSEs) remains a critical challenge for solid‐state batteries due to the lack of quantitative design principles governing interfacial interactions during coating, transfer, and impregnation. Here, we establish thermodynamic criteria for Li6.75La3Zr1.75Ta0.25O12‐based hybrid layers (LLZTO‐HLs) fabrication using Hansen solubility parameters to correlate interfacial compatibility with process behavior. Uniform coating requires sufficiently high slurry–substrate compatibility, whereas clean transfer demands low binder–substrate adhesion. Furthermore, binder–polymer electrolyte compatibility governs impregnation behavior, enabling rational combination selection. Based on this framework, defect‐free, 15 µm‐thin LLZTO‐HLs are fabricated over large areas (120 cm2) via transfer printing and integrated into transfer‐printed HSEs (THSEs). Compared with direct coating, transfer printing enables uniform electrolyte layers and electrode interfacial stability owing to the absence of slurry infiltration into the porous anode. Consequently, THSEs exhibit enhanced Li+ transport, superior rate capability, and improved cycling stability in coin‐type hybrid solid‐state batteries. Notably, comparable cycling performance is retained in pouch‐type cells despite increased cell area, highlighting the excellent uniformity and scalability of the THSE. The THSE demonstrates superior thermal stability under elevated temperatures. The thermodynamic design principles established herein provide a generalizable framework for scalable manufacturing of high‐performance HSEs.

articles.title: Defect‐Induced Symmetry Breaking Activates Fullerene Acceptors for Self‐Powered Organic Photodetection
articles.abstract: Pristine C60 suffers from symmetry‐induced forbidden transitions, resulting in limited visible‐infrared photoresponse and restricting its application in organic photodetectors (OPDs). Here, we report a biomass‐assisted thermal reconstruction strategy to break the intrinsic symmetry of C60 through heteroatom‐induced defect engineering. By calcining chitosan oligosaccharide with C60, a novel fullerene derivative (CC) was obtained, exhibiting reconstructed electronic states and narrowed energy gaps. Incorporating CC into the P3HT active layer induces intermediate states that facilitate low‐energy photogeneration, overcoming the limited visible‐light response of conventional C60‐based OPDs to enable broadband photoresponse. The optimized P3HT: CC OPD achieved a detectivity of 1.15 × 1013 Jones, an ultra‐high on/off ratio of ≈3 × 106, and an outstanding linear dynamic range of 108.3 dB, rivaling silicon or PCBM‐based devices. Benefiting from enhanced broadband absorption and optimized carrier transport, the CC devices further demonstrate excellent operational stability and potential for flexible biomimetic imaging and wireless optical communication. CC also exhibits high versatility in OPDs incorporating other organic donor materials. This work provides a sustainable and low‐cost strategy for reactivating fullerene‐derived materials toward next‐generation broadband organic optoelectronics.

articles.title: Disorder‐Assisted Topological States and Critical Couplings in Continuous Elastic Metaplates
articles.abstract: Precise manipulation of elastic waves in continuous solid‐state media is important for enhancing wave‐matter interactions and enabling applications such as energy harvesting, nondestructive testing, sensing, and on‐chip signal processing. Disorder is typically regarded as detrimental to wave propagation. However, disorder can drive a trivial phase into a nontrivial one, leading to the emergence of a topological Anderson insulator (TAI). While existing TAI studies mainly focus on idealized systems such as discrete lattice models or resonator arrays, here we realize the disorder‐engineering principle in a scalable continuous elastic plate for topological states and waveguide‐cavity critical couplings. Disorder is introduced by randomly rotating perforated elliptical holes in a continuous plate. The disorder‐assisted bandgap closing and reopening, and interface states with suppressed backscattering, are verified experimentally. We also develop a super‐periodic equivalent model that quantitatively predicts the disorder‐driven bandgap evolutions and topological transitions. Beyond robust transport, we realize disorder‐assisted critical couplings in a TAI waveguide‐cavity system, whereby most waveguide energy is coupled into the resonator, with possible applications in signal filtering and multiplexing. Our work introduces a disorder‐engineering strategy for manipulating wave phenomena in continuous solid‐state media. We expect these results to inspire further advances in integrated phononic circuits and on‐chip technologies.

articles.title: Drop‐on‐Demand Printed Negative Dielectric Anisotropy Liquid Crystal Droplets for Adaptive Complex Beam Manipulation and Assessment
articles.abstract: Adaptive manipulation of vectorial optical fields is important for optical metrology, imaging, and structured light‐related applications, yet existing approaches often rely on bulky or sequentially operated systems. Here we demonstrate an inkjet‐printed negative dielectric anisotropy nematic liquid crystal droplet platform that unifies adaptive complex beam generation and full‐vectorial optical field sensing within a single printed architecture. For complex beam generation, electric‐field‐driven director reconfiguration in the droplets produces tunable birefringence and wavelength‐dependent polarization textures, including skyrmionic‐like optical fields. For adaptive full‐vectorial optical field sensing, the same droplet array enables spectral and polarization retrieval through wavelength‐dependent intensity patterns and division‐of‐wavefront polarimetry, while also functioning as a microlens array for Shack–Hartmann wavefront sensing to reconstruct phase. These results establish negative dielectric anisotropy liquid crystal droplets as a scalable soft‐matter photonic system for adaptive beam manipulation and multidimensional optical field characterization.

articles.title: Dual‐Functional PDA/CMC‐Li Supramolecular Bridging Networks Unlock Trans‐Phase Li+ Conduction in Composite Solid Electrolytes for High‐Performance Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Composite solid electrolytes (CSEs) hold immense promise for high‐energy‐density solid‐state lithium metal batteries, yet their practical application remains severely hampered by filler agglomeration and sluggish interfacial Li+ transport. Herein, dual‐functional supramolecular bridging networks are constructed by employing lithiated carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC‐Li) as dynamic bridges to interconnect polydopamine (PDA)‐modified Li6.28Al0.24La3Zr2O12 (LLZAO) fillers within a PVDF‐HFP matrix. This synergistic architecture helps promote a more uniform filler dispersion and actively mediates ion solvation dynamics via simultaneous anion trapping and cation extraction. Crucially, this dual‐regulation fundamentally mitigates the space‐charge layer (SCL) effect at organic‐inorganic boundaries, actively unlocking a highly efficient trans‐phase Li+ percolation pathway through the LLZAO ceramic bulk, thereby bypassing conventionally sluggish interfacial routes. The resulting spatially homogeneous ion flux may reduce localized current hotspots and suppress lithium dendrite proliferation. Consequently, the optimized PVPL electrolyte empowers Li||Li symmetrical cells to maintain stable plating/stripping over 1400 h. Furthermore, LiFePO4||PVPL||Li full cells deliver 83% capacity retention after 400 cycles at 2 C, while NCM811||PVPL||Li cells maintain 88% capacity retention over 200 cycles. This dual‐functional bridging strategy establishes a generalizable and effective paradigm for engineering advanced CSEs with optimized structural and Li+ transport kinetics.

articles.title: Dual‐Interface Management Modulated by Functional Cationic Ligands Enables Robust and Efficient Perovskite Photovoltaics
articles.abstract: Despite the effectiveness of surface passivation, simultaneous optimization of buried interface and top surface in perovskite solar cells (PSCs) remains challenging due to incompatible additive functions and uncontrolled crystallization kinetics. Here, we present a dual‐interface regulation strategy that deploys phenyltrimethylammonium chloride (THPA) treatment on the top surface and 5‐amino‐1‐pentanol (5‐APT) treatment at the buried interface of the perovskite film. This approach achieves multiple collaborative regulation effects of dual interfaces: (i) THPA reduces trap density at the top surface of perovskites and promotes n‐type character. (ii) 5‐APT forms hydrogen and ionic bonds with the substrate, enhancing bottom crystallinity via cation exchange with FA+/Cs+ and facilitating hole extraction. Besides, in‐situ photoluminescence reveals that 5‐APT retards the crystallization process, promoting grain merging and yielding uniformly sized grains. As a result, the optimized PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.24% with excellent stability. This straightforward strategy transcends conventional spacer cation engineering, bridging the efficiency‐stability divide and providing a generalizable paradigm for interface passivation in perovskite optoelectronics.

articles.title: Dynamic Fe3+‐Cellulose Coordination Enables Ambient‐Temperature Fabrication of Water‐Resistant, Weldable, and Moldable Bioplastics
articles.abstract: The inherent trade‐offs among processability, wet stability, and environmental footprint of biomass‐derived materials hinder the development of sustainable alternatives to petroleum‐based plastics. Here, we report an ambient‐solvent‐regulated strategy that transforms native cellulose paper into a robust, weldable, and rapidly biodegradable plastic using a ternary iron(III) chloride/zinc chloride/water (FeCl3/ZnCl2/H2O) molten salt hydrate system. Leveraging the small ionic radius and high charge density of Fe3+, this system achieves rapid, ambient‐temperature partial dissolution of cellulose rather than full homogeneous disassembly, preserving the native microfiber skeleton while Fe3+ ions serve as permanent yet dynamic molecular rivets within the regenerated matrix during in situ reconstruction. The resulting Fe3+‐enhanced multiscale cellulose paper delivers 41.6 MPa dry tensile strength and 11.2 MPa wet strength. Dynamic Fe3+–O coordination bonds enable vitrimer‐like water‐assisted welding and binder‐free straw fabrication. Notably, the solvent remains effective over ten reuse cycles, with 75% strength retention. Life cycle assessment reveals a global warming potential of 1.82 kg CO2‐eq/kg, 40% and 21% lower than polylactic acid and polyethylene, respectively. Furthermore, the integrated Fe3+ centers trigger Fenton‐like self‐destruction in soil, achieving complete degradation within 35 days. This work establishes a coordination mechanochemistry strategy for designing high‐performance bioplastics with closed‐loop life cycles.

articles.title: Electrolyte‐Enabled Suppression of Static Corrosion for Long‐Cycle Calendar Life in Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: The calendar life of lithium (Li) metal batteries is commonly evaluated through cycling performance, implicitly assuming that storage-induced degradation follows the same interfacial processes. However, this work reveals that Li metal undergoes continuous non-Faradaic interfacial corrosion under open-circuit conditions, defining a distinct degradation pathway governing calendar aging, distinct from cycling-induced failure. To quantify this process, we introduce a kinetically defined descriptor based on the degradation rate constant (λ), enabling direct evaluation of time-dependent capacity loss during storage. This framework treats calendar aging as a corrosion-driven kinetic process rather than an extrapolation of cycling behavior. We further show that static corrosion can be actively regulated via electrolyte design. Based on the degradation rate constants derived from capacity decay fitting, the LiNO3-15C5-CsBr electrolyte projects a 2.7-fold extension in storage lifetime at 100% SOC and a 3.4-fold extension at 0% SOC versus the baseline electrolyte. Mechanistically, Cs+-mediated electrostatic shielding, Br−-induced interfacial polishing, and NO3 −-derived inorganic passivation cooperatively stabilize the Li interface, suppress corrosion kinetics, and reduce irreversible Li loss, leading to a marked decrease in λ. These findings establish static corrosion as a distinct degradation mode in Li metal batteries and provide a quantitative framework for evaluating and regulating calendar aging beyond cycling metrics.

articles.title: Engineering Core–Shell Interfaces with Hierarchical Mass Transport for Dendrite‑Free and Highly Reversible Zn Anodes
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc batteries are plagued by dendrite growth and parasitic reactions, calling for a rational interfacial design. Herein, we construct a core–shell ZIF-8@SiO2 architecture on the Zn anode (ZFSI@Zn) via a self-nucleation route. The hydrophilic SiO2 shell and anion-affinitive ZIF-8 core synergistically facilitate Zn2+ desolvation and transport, enhancing the 3D diffusion contribution while effectively suppressing interfacial concentration polarization. Consequently, the ZFSI@Zn anode delivers an extended lifespan of 1800 h at 1 mA cm−2/1 mAh cm−2 and maintains remarkable stability even at an ultrahigh current density of 50 mA cm−2. Beyond anode protection, strong SO4 2− adsorption confers a negative surface charge that electrostatically repels I3 −, thereby eliminating the shuttle effect in Zn-I2 batteries. This enables a maximum specific capacity of 202.3 mAh g−1 at 0.2 A g−1 and an outstanding capacity retention of 89.8% over 65 000 cycles at 5 A g−1, corresponding to an ultralow capacity decay of merely 0.00015% per cycle. The superior performance is further validated under high cathode loadings and in pouch‑cell configurations. Overall, this work establishes core–shell interfacial engineering as a versatile platform for tackling the multiple challenges in zinc‑based energy storage.

articles.title: Engineering Multifunctional Microneedle Devices: From Advanced Micro‐Nano Manufacturing to Closed‐Loop Theranostics
articles.abstract: As a turnover technology capable of painlessly breaching the transdermal barrier, microneedles (MNs) have overcome the limitations of solitary transdermal drug delivery, progressively evolving into highly integrated theranostic platforms. Tracing the evolution of bio‐interfacial mass transfer and systemic integration, this review systematically categorizes MN architectures into solid, hollow, coated, dissolving, hydrogel, and layered types, highlighting the critical roles of micromolding, high‐resolution lithography, and three‐dimensional printing in the precise fabrication of MN arrays. In alignment with this technological trend, this review systematically delineates two core trajectories of MN functional evolution and provides an in‐depth discussion on intervention strategies that overcome complex pathological microenvironments to achieve precise targeted drug delivery, while analyzing their sensing potential in situ extraction of dermal interstitial fluid and dynamic monitoring of biochemical biomarkers. Finally, the review explores the manufacturing and production barriers hindering the bench‐to‐bedside clinical translation of MN systems and envisions their promising future evolution toward intelligent closed‐loop theranostic platforms integrating sensing, decision‐making, and therapeutics. Ultimately, an overarching research framework for the MN field that combines systemic comprehensiveness, broad applicability, and introductory guidance is established.

articles.title: Exciting Dual‐Carriers in Two‐Dimensional Metallic Van Der Waals Fe3GeTe2/FeTe Heterostructure
articles.abstract: The advantage of dual‐carriers heterostructures has expanded the functional boundaries of semiconductor devices in bidirectional control, logical operations, high‐frequency communication, and precision medicine, which stand as a cornerstone for development of next‐generation information technologies and renewable energy systems. The excitation of dual‐carriers is usually realized in semiconductor heterostructures but suffers a significant challenge in real applications because of complex interface design and band structure modulation limitations. The dual‐carriers excitation in metallic heterostructures is strongly expected. In this work, we realized dual‐carriers excitation in a metallic transport van der Waals heterostructure. Compared with the single‐layer film, the heterostructure sample exhibits a pronounced nonlinear ordinary Hall curve. This transport phenomenon provides key material support for core technologies in fields such as electronic information, energy conversion, and optoelectronics.

articles.title: Facet‐Induced Electron‐Bridge Enables Enhanced LiO2‐Mediated Reaction Kinetics for Stable Lithium‐Oxygen Batteries
articles.abstract: Lithium oxygen batteries hold great promise as high‐energy‐density storage technologies, yet their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish cathode redox kinetics. A key bottleneck lies in the inefficient electron transfer associated with the formation and decomposition of the LiO2 intermediate, which leads to severe polarization and rapid capacity fade. Herein, we propose a facet‐induced electron‐bridge engineering to boost LiO2‐mediated reaction kinetics. By harnessing a Mott–Schottky built‐in electric field across the heterointerface, we drive directional charge separation that simultaneously tailors electron density and sorption microenvironments. The resulting intermediate‐binding energetics reprogram the reaction trajectory, affording precise manipulation over Li2O2 nucleation kinetics and the subsequent pathways governing its growth and decomposition. Consequently, the engineered cathode thus delivers extended cycle life with a substantially reduced overpotential. This work provides a general principle for regulating reaction intermediates and accelerating electron transfer via crystal plane optimization and interfacial engineering, offering a reliable strategy for high‐performance electrocatalysts.

articles.title: First‐Principles Insights Into Fe2O3/In2S3 Heterojunction and Its Application in Dispersion‐Managed Fiber Lasers
articles.abstract: Heterostructure materials have garnered substantial interest across optics, medicine, optoelectronics, and electromagnetics due to their ability to combine advantageous characteristics from multiple constituent phases. Notably, Fe2O3/In2S3 heterojunctions have demonstrated enhancement mechanisms for both photogenerated charge carrier separation and nonlinear optical response. However, their optoelectronic properties from a theoretical perspective and their potential in ultrafast photonics have not been extensively explored. Herein, robust S─O covalent‐bonded Fe2O3/In2S3 heterojunctions were successfully synthesized via heat treatment technology. First‐principles calculations were conducted to examine thermal stability, electronic band structures, density of states distributions, electron localization functions, and dielectric responses, thereby establishing a fundamental understanding of intrinsic material properties while informing future optoelectronic implementations. By employing the Fe2O3/In2S3 heterojunction in a fiber cavity with negative dispersion, passive mode‐locking operation was realized, delivering a pulse width of 300 fs. Moreover, the incorporation of the Fe2O3/In2S3 heterojunction into a net positive dispersion fiber cavity resulted in the achievement of mode‐locked operation with a pulse duration of 123 fs. Compared with previous studies, these lasers show improved performance. This work advances the understanding of Fe2O3/In2S3 structure‐property relationships from a theoretical perspective and highlights their potential as promising nonlinear optical materials for advanced optoelectronic devices from an experimental standpoint.

articles.title: Freestanding Membrane Enabled Multi‐Stimulus Ferroelectric Switching
articles.abstract: Substrate clamping constrains lattice deformation in epitaxial ferroelectrics, limiting the ability of weak non‐electrical stimuli to reconfigure polarization. Here, we show that releasing epitaxial PbTiO3 into a freestanding membrane reshapes its switching landscape and enables polarization control through electrical, mechanical, and optical stimuli. Whereas substrate‐clamped PbTiO3 remains stable under local mechanical loading up to 4000 nN and 405‐nm illumination, freestanding PbTiO3 integrated on silicon exhibits force‐driven polarization reconfiguration from ∼2000 nN and pronounced light‐assisted modification of the written polar state. Mechanical release enhances the piezoresponse by ∼80%, reduces the switching voltage by ∼45%, and produces a strongly force‐tunable electromechanical response. Optical excitation further induces asymmetric switching and a positive hysteresis shift in the freestanding membrane, consistent with a photoinduced internal bias field. Kelvin probe force microscopy reveals photoinduced surface‐potential modulation in both clamped and freestanding geometries, yet corresponding polarization reconfiguration occurs only in the mechanically released membrane. This contrast demonstrates that photoinduced electrostatic perturbation alone is insufficient to drive polarization reconfiguration and that its effectiveness is governed by the mechanical boundary condition. Our findings establish mechanical release as a strategy for engineering the accessibility of ferroelectric switching pathways and enabling multi‐stimulus control in reconfigurable oxide membranes.

articles.title: From Glass Waste to High‐Performance Solid Composite Electrolytes for Sustainable Solid‐State Lithium Batteries
articles.abstract: Solid‐state lithium batteries (SSLBs) are promising next‐generation energy storage devices, but their widespread deployment is largely hampered by costly, resource‐intensive solid electrolytes. Here we report a low‐cost, high‐performance, and sustainable solid composite electrolyte (SCE) membrane that comprises commercial high‐alkali glass fiber (GF) separators as scaffolds for in situ polymerization of the PEGDA/LiTFSI/FEC matrix. The alkali‐doped silicate framework in GF provides abundant Lewis acid‐base sites that promote lithium salt dissociation and enhance directional Li+ transport. The resulting GF‐SCE exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.89 × 10−4 S cm−1 at 25°C, a wide electrochemical stability window up to 5.0 V, and extensive dendrite‐free cycling, enabling the formation of a stable LiF‐rich solid‐electrolyte interphase. When GF‐SCE is used in a cell containing high‐Ni LiNi0.96Co0.03Mn0.01O2 cathode and Li metal anode, a large specific capacity of 253.6 mAh g−1 and stable cycling are achieved. Techno‐economic analyses show that the production cost of GF‐SCE membranes is only $8.98–$17.15 m−2 via solvent‐free roll‐to‐roll processing with earth‐abundant precursors, favorably competitive relative to other inorganic electrolyte counterparts. By combining high electrochemical performance, potential scalability, and favorable recyclability, the glass‐fiber‐based SCEs reported in this work offer a practical, cost‐effective pathway toward circular and high‐voltage solid‐state lithium batteries.

articles.title: A Hybrid Ultramicroporous Material Family With Metal‐Controlled Dynamic Behavior
articles.abstract: Hybrid ultramicroporous materials (HUMs) are comprised of combinations of inorganic and organic linker ligands as exemplified by the prototypal pcu topology variant [Zn(pyrazine)2(SiF6)]n, SIFSIX-3-Zn, and its recently reported first-generation derivatives [M(3,3’-bipyridine)2(SiF6)] n (M = Cu, Zn). Herein, we report the synthesis, structure, and sorption properties of a second-generation family of HUMs of general formula [M(3,3’-bipyridine)2(NbOF5)] n , NbOFFIVE-3,3'-bpy-M, M = Co, Ni, Cu, Zn. The four HUMs are structurally characterized by single crystal x-ray diffraction, revealing the expected pcu topology of the isostructural as-synthesized phases. All variants initially crystallized in large-pore (lp) phases with water molecules occupying 1D channels. Upon dehydration, Cu and Zn transformed from water-loaded lp phases into narrow-pore (np) guest-free phases, whereas Co and Ni retained their lp structures after desorption. Water vapor sorption isotherms (300 K) revealed stepped isotherms corresponding to structural transformations (np→lp) for Cu and Zn, and rare examples of induced-fit (lp→np→lp) from guest-free lp to np to water-loaded lp phases for Co and Ni. The NbOFFIVE-3,3'-bpy-M family exhibits uncommon examples of metal-dependent dynamic behavior in HUMs.

articles.title: A Multi‐Topologically Superposed Mechanically Interlocked Polymer
articles.abstract: Mechanically interlocked structures (MIS) provide a powerful platform for creating advanced materials with unprecedented topological architectures. Nevertheless, current related studies have predominantly focused on the construction of MIS with single topological motifs, and the integration of multiple topologies into a single MIS remains a grand challenge. Herein, we harness ligand conformational constraints to regulate the flexible coordination behavior of alkali metal ions, enabling the construction of a multi‐topologically superposed mechanically interlocked polymer (MIP) featuring the unprecedented incorporation of four distinct topological motifs. This incorporation imparts MIP with exceptional mechanical strength and efficient Na+ transport capability. As an artificial solid electrolyte interphase (ASEI) for sodium metal batteries, MIP delivers remarkable ultralong cycling stability, maintaining 87.8% capacity retention after 10 000 cycles at 20 C. This work breaks the boundaries of conventional MIS by enabling the creation of multi‐topologically superposed MIS, thereby unveiling new topological landscapes and opening unexplored opportunities for advanced functions.

articles.title: Aminophosphonium Dihydrogen Phosphate: A Structurally Modified KDP Analogue With Room‐Temperature Ferro‐ and Piezoelectric Properties
articles.abstract: Potassium dihydrogen phosphate is well-known to exhibit ferroelectricity, while ammonium dihydrogen phosphate is an antiferroelectric material, with both of them exhibiting a phase transition to paraelectric phase below room temperature. In this work, we report the synthesis and room-temperature ferroelectric behavior of an aminophosphonium dihydrogen phosphate of formula, [{P(NHPh)4(H2PO4)·(CH3OH)0.5] (TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5 ) that exhibits a three-dimensional pillared-layered hydrogen bonding network. (TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5 crystallizes in the polar monoclinic P21 space group, and its non-centrosymmetric structure was confirmed by second-harmonic generation (SHG) measurements. The ferroelectric behavior was further verified through polarization–electric field (P–E) loop measurements, with a saturation polarization of 21.40 µC cm−2. Structural analysis combined with preliminary density functional theory calculations indicates a ferrielectric-type ordering in which the adjacent layers exhibit different polarization directions but with unequal dipole moments. Furthermore, the electromechanical energy-harvesting properties of TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5 were explored in its composites with the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) polymer. The 10 wt% TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5–PDMS device exhibited a maximum peak-to-peak open-circuit voltage (𝑉oc) of 10.69 ± 0.04 V and the output work efficiency parameter (OWE) of 9.63%. Owing to the superior signal sensitivity of this device, a contact-type sensor was developed to measure a motor's revolutions per minute (RPM) at both low and high speeds.

articles.title: Conjugation Interruption in 1D COFs for Boosted Charge Separation and Photocatalytic 2,3‐Dihydrobenzofuran Synthesis
articles.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are appealing photocatalyst platforms because of their structural designability and tunable optoelectronic properties. However, the traditional strategy of extending π‐conjugation to improve light absorption often increases exciton binding energy and suppresses charge separation, creating a trade‐off that limits catalytic performance. Here, we introduce a conjugation‐interruption strategy for the first time to construct efficient COF‐based photocatalysts, where methylene (sp3) bridges are incorporated into one‐dimensional (1D) framework backbones to moderately disrupt long‐range conjugation, localize electrons and reduce exciton binding energy. Schiff base condensation of the 4‐connected thiadiazole‐containing tetra‐aldehyde with 2‐connected angular diamine precursors consisting of naphthyl, phenyl, and methylene bridges afforded BT‐NDA‐COF, BT‐TDA‐COF, and BT‐MDA‐COF, respectively. BT‐MDA‐COF with the weakest conjugation, exhibits the longest fluorescence lifetime (1.57 ns) and the lowest exciton binding energy (63.21 meV), clearly outperforming its fully conjugated counterparts (BT‐TDA‐COF and BT‐NDA‐COF). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the methylene bridges induce structural distortion and weaken exciton confinement, thereby promoting charge separation. This superior charge separation enables gram‐scale photocatalytic synthesis of bioactive 2,3‐dihydrobenzofurans with 98% yield, demonstrating the practical potential of conjugation interruption in COFs for green, high‐efficiency photocatalytic organic synthesis.

articles.title: Electrochemical Indicators for Designing Durable Low‐Pt Fuel Cell Catalysts
articles.abstract: Improving the durability of platinum (Pt)-based catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) remains a central challenge in the commercialization of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), yet simple and effective indicators to guide the rational design of highly stable Pt-based catalysts are still lacking. Herein, we identify initial electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) and dry proton accessibility (DPA) as two key indicators for unraveling cathodic Pt/C catalyst degradation. Systematic studies on a library of Pt/C catalysts with a wide range of initial ECSA (49–114 m2 gPt −1) and DPA (27%–91%) reveal clear relationships between these two indicators and ECSA loss: at a comparable DPA, ECSA loss decreases significantly with the reduction in initial ECSA; at a similar initial ECSA, lower DPA effectively mitigates ECSA loss; and the influence of DPA on ECSA loss becomes increasingly prominent as initial ECSA decreases. Regression analysis further clarifies the respective roles of these two indicators: initial ECSA is the dominant factor associated with ECSA loss within the catalyst library, while DPA further modulates degradation depending on the initial ECSA level. These findings suggest that catalyst durability can be improved by prioritizing the reduction of initial ECSA, with further benefits achieved by lowering DPA.

articles.title: Electrochemically Tunable Ring‐Contracting Cyanation and Imination of Saturated Cyclic Amines
articles.abstract: The green and facile protocol for the tunable transformation of alicyclic amines is meaningful due to the immense importance of the functionalized azaheterocycles in pharmaceuticals. In this work, electrochemically selective synthesis of α‐cyano amines and cyclic amidines from the reaction of saturated cyclic amines with TMSN3 is developed. Using thiomorpholines as amine substrates, the regioselective cleavage of C(sp3)─S bond, followed by recombination and cyanation, enables the construction of α‐cyano thiazolidines via a ring contraction process. In the presence of sodium sulfinate, alicyclic amines undergo cycloaddition, N2 extrusion, hydride transfer, and sulfonylation to give sulfonyl amidines. Notable features of the methods developed herein include simple and broad tertiary/secondary cyclic amine substrates, diverse novel transformations, catalyst‐free and external oxidant‐free conditions. Importantly, these reaction systems are amenable to the late‐stage functionalization of complex targets containing basic N‐heterocyclic moieties that are prevalent in medicinally active agents. In addition, electrolysis of the N‐aryl sulfonyl amidine triggers further cleavage of the N─S bond and coupling of C(sp2)─N bond to provide fused amines.

articles.title: Fluoroalkylated Azobenzenes with Photoswitchable Solid–Liquid States Enabling Spatiotemporally Controlled Lubrication for Liquid Motion Manipulation
articles.abstract: The precise control of liquid motion with light is fundamental to advancing next‐generation microfluidic devices and microreactors. Fluoroalkylated photoswitches that combine low surface tension with photoinduced reversible solid‑to‑liquid transitions would be ideal for this purpose, yet they have remained unrealized because fluoroalkyl chains typically suppress solid‑state photoisomerization. Here, we overcome this limitation by designing fluoroalkylated azobenzenes that exhibit low surface tension and photoinduced reversible solid‑to‑liquid transitions. This dual functionality stems from tailored molecular and crystalline structures that enable efficient trans‐cis photoisomerization in the solid state. The fluoroalkylated azobenzenes function as non‑lubricating solids in their trans form and become liquid lubricants upon photoconversion to their cis form. By infusing them into microstructured substrates, we create surfaces that can be optically switched between a liquid‐pinning state and a slippery state. This photoswitching capability enables the on‑demand creation and reconfiguration of guiding pathways to control the sliding of various liquids. This work establishes spatiotemporally controlled lubrication via photoinduced reversible solid‑to‐liquid transitions as a new mechanism for designing microfluidics, microreactors, and adaptive surfaces.

articles.title: Heterogeneous Palladium‐Catalyzed Trideuteromethylation and 13C‐Trideuteromethylation of Arylboron Compounds via D2O as the Deuterium Source
articles.abstract: Integrating the “magic methyl” effect and deuterium kinetic isotope effect, trideuteromethyl (CD3) modification is a robust strategy for pharmaceutical development. Accordingly, the development of cost‐effective and practical methods to install CD3 moieties into drug‐like molecules is highly desirable. Herein, we develop a reusable heterogeneous Pd‐catalyzed trideuteromethylation of arylboron esters, with D2O serving as the sole deuterium source. Methylthianthrenium salts (TT‐Me) act as key precursors, undergoing facile H/D exchange to in situ produce CD3 synthons for efficient one‐pot cross‐coupling with arylboron esters. This protocol features outstanding functional group compatibility and an extraordinarily broad substrate applicability. It enables the trideuteromethylation of diverse biologically relevant scaffolds, as well as the modular two‐step synthesis of aryl‐CD3 skeletons starting from commercially available aryl chlorides, phenols, anilines, and benzoic acids. It also facilely affords 13CH3/13CD3 dual‐labeled analogs for pharmaceutical and analytical use. Combined with C─H borylation, this one‐pot platform achieves direct trideuteromethylation of inert aryl C─H bonds, allowing divergent installation of two site‐specific CD3 moieties into lidocaine isotopologues. Mechanistic investigations reveal a surface‐mediated heterogeneous pathway, where K2CO3 dually activates TT‐Me and arylboron esters. This work offers a practical, scalable and sustainable route for constructing aryl–CD3 isotopic architectures.

articles.title: Heterometallic Polarization Enabling Precise Intermediate Regulation for Selective CO2 Photoreduction
articles.abstract: Achieving high selectivity in photocatalytic CO2 reduction remains a fundamental challenge, as competing pathways share similar thermodynamic potentials but differ in their intermediate adsorption behavior. Here we introduce a heterometallic polarization strategy based on bimetallic metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), where asymmetric charge redistribution between distinct metal centers tailors the local electronic structure and modulates CO* binding energetics. Taking MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni) as a model system, the incorporation of Ni induces intermetallic electronic coupling, creating polarized Fe─Ni sites that synergistically enhance CO2 activation and charge transfer. As a result, MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni2.5) achieves a CO production rate of 1517.4 µmol g−1 h−1—10.8 times higher than MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni0)—with a selectivity of 97.9%. Increasing the Ni content strengthens CO* adsorption, thereby steering the reaction from CO evolution to deep hydrogenation toward CH4. MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni7.5) delivers a CH4 production rate of 255.0 µmol g−1 h−1—28.3 and 14.5 times that of MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni0) and MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni2.5), respectively—with an electron selectivity of 81.3%. These results demonstrate that heterometallic polarization provides a powerful design principle for regulating intermediates and achieving tunable product selectivity in photocatalytic CO2 conversion.

articles.title: Hydroxyl‐Mediated Proton Transfer Over Cu Single Atoms Decorated TiO2 for Selective Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction to Ethanol
articles.abstract: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction to hydrocarbon fuels represents a sustainable route toward carbon neutrality, yet selective and efficient C2 production remains a formidable challenging due to the high thermodynamic barrier and sluggish C–C coupling kinetics. In this study, we report a hydroxyl (–OH)‐rich TiO2 photocatalyst decorated with Cu single atoms (SAs) (Cu/HTO) that addresses this challenge through synergistic active site—surface group engineering. The electronic interplay between surface –OH groups and Cu SAs promotes charge separation and strengthens CO2 chemisorption/activation at Cu sites, facilitating *CO intermediates formation and subsequent protonation for selective C2H5OH and CO prodution. Under sacrificial agent free conditions, Cu/HTO delivers CO at 90.1 µmol g−1 h−1 with 88.3% yield‐based selectivity in a gas–solid (GS) system. Notably, in a gas–liquid–solid (GLS) system with water supplying abundant protons, Cu/HTO efficiently yields C2H5OH at 361.5 µmol g−1 h−1 with 99.4% yield‐based selectivity, which is related to Cu2+ sites stabilized *CO intermediates thermodynamically favoring C–C coupling and the surface –OH groups mediated proton transfer kinetically facilitating multistep protonation. This work not only establishes a high‐performance and low‐cost photocatalyst for CO2‐to‐C2 conversion but also provides a rational design paradigm for engineering single‐atom–surface‐group synergy in solar fuel synthesis.

articles.title: Interfacial Carbonate‐Mediated Activation of Pre‐Catalysts for Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Pre-catalyst reconstruction fundamentally governs the local structure and solid–liquid interface of the derived phase, significantly influencing water electrolysis performance. However, fully unlocking the intrinsic potential of pre-catalysts remain a persistent bottleneck, as conventional electrolytes cannot functionalize the interface during reconstruction. Herein, we propose an interfacial carbonate-dominated activation strategy to simultaneously tune the derived NiOOH structure and its interface, enabling efficient oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Using Ca-Ni3S2 as the model pre-catalyst and K2CO3 to replace KOH as the reconstruction electrolyte, the carbonate-dominated interface kinetically and thermodynamically impedes the transformation of Ni3S2 into NiOOH, enabling surface-confined reconstruction at elevated potential that preserves the interior Ni3S2 while forming the functionalized NiOOH phase on the surface. This functionalized surface, induced by the retained CO3 2− from reconstruction, optimizes the electron distribution, interface water framework, and establishes a stable buffer layer, facilitating water oxidation and suppressing NiOOH deactivation. Resultantly, the reconstructed catalyst (Ca-Ni3S2-RC) shows an overpotential of only 261 mV at 100 mA cm−2, a remarkable reduction of 198 mV compared to its KOH-reconstructed counterpart. Integrated into an alkaline water electrolyzer (AWE), Ca-Ni3S2-RC presents a competitive energy consumption of 4.21 kWh m−3 H2 to deliver 4000 A m−2 over 900 h, highlighting its promise for industrial applicability.

articles.title: Novel Fused‐Ring Electron Acceptors Based on Double Electron‐Deficient Central Core for High‐Performance Organic Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Rapid advances in A-DA'D-A fused-ring electron acceptors have significantly boosted organic solar cells (OSCs), yet non-radiative energy loss (ΔE 3) remains a persistent bottleneck, and reliance on single electron-deficient cores limits further molecular diversification. Herein, we report CBT-4F, a novel acceptor featuring a double electron-deficient bis([1,2,5]thiadiazolo)[3,4-c:3′,4′-g]carbazole (CBT) core constructed via stepwise intramolecular Cadogan reductive cyclization. This synthetic strategy circumvents the challenges of carrying multiple nitro groups through key cross-coupling steps and offers an extensible route to multi-electron-deficient-core acceptors. Compared with the benchmark acceptor Y6, CBT-4F exhibits extended π-conjugation, increased backbone curvature, a lower average molecular electrostatic potential, and a distinct packing motif. These coupled molecular and solid-state characteristics, together with optimized blend morphology and recombination behavior, are associated with significantly suppressed ΔE 3 in PM6:CBT-4F devices (0.220 vs. 0.262 eV for PM6:Y6). Benefiting from a wider photovoltaic bandgap and reduced ΔE 3, PM6:CBT-4F achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.02% with a high open-circuit voltage (V OC) of 0.923 V, substantially outperforming the PM6:Y6 counterpart (17.63%, 0.834 V). Furthermore, incorporating CBT-4F as a third component into the PM6:BTP-eC9 system boosts the ternary PCE to 20.57%. This work establishes CBT-4F as a high-performance molecular platform and expands synthetic accessibility to multi-electron-deficient-core acceptors.

articles.title: Orchestrating Tumor‐Immune Interface and Microenvironment Remodeling via a Tumor‐Preferential DNA Nano‐Regulator for Metabolic‐Immunotherapy
articles.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming in malignant cells drives tumor progression and impairs immunotherapy efficacy, highlighting the urgent need for synergistic metabolic‐immunotherapy. However, the pharmacokinetic disparity and systemic toxicities pose significant challenges on this synergy. We develop a tumor‐preferential, multifunctional DNA nano‐regulator assembled on a DNA origami‐based framework with two functional layers for the integration of immune cues and metabolic modulation at the tumor‐immune interface. The inner layer is precisely functionalized with anti‐CD3/CD28/PD‐L1 antibodies and glutamine synthetase, enabling in situ T‐cell engagement, PD‐L1 blockade, and metabolic environment improvement. The outer layer combines albumin‐binding domains with pH‐responsive i‐motif switches to form a pH‐sensitive albumin coating in vivo, which shields the inner antibodies during systemic circulation and specifically exposes them within the tumoral acidic microenvironment. In the xenograft and syngeneic mouse models, the regulator‐mediated broad remodeling of the intratumoral immune and metabolic landscapes results in enhanced T‑cell infiltration and activation, potent tumor‐growth suppression, and a favorable safety profile. This study combines metabolic intervention with immunotherapy by integrating the synergism and tumor preference of therapies.

articles.title: Outside Back Cover: Sustainable Low‐Valent Iridium Active Sites in Rhenium Doped Perovskite Iridates for Efficient Acidic Oxygen Evolution Reaction via Hybridized Reaction Pathways
articles.abstract: In a rhenium‐doped SrZrxIr1−xO3 perovskite, high‐valent Re stabilizes low‐valent iridium active sites against overoxidation during acidic oxygen evolution. Dynamic Re–Ir–O interactions open a hybrid adsorbate‐evolution/oxide‐path mechanism, delivering a 250 mV overpotential, >1,300 A gIr−1 mass activity, and 600 h durability for low‐iridium PEM water electrolysis. More in the Research Article e1466065, Jung Kyu Kim, Young‐Min Kim, Byung‐Hyun Kim, HyukSu Han, and co‐workers.

articles.title: Ping–Pong Energy Transfer in a Heteroleptic Mixed‐Chromophore Coordination Cage
articles.abstract: Gaining control over chromophore-functionalized multicomponent architectures sets the stage to construct modular libraries of tunable emitters, light-harvesting complexes, and photo-redox catalysts. Based on a “Shape Complementary Assembly” (SCA) approach, we report two luminescent heteroleptic coordination cages built from Pd(II) cations, a diketopyrrolopyrrole ligand (LA ) and matching counter ligands with either a fluorenone (L1 ) or carbazole (L2 ) π-system. Transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy reveals an energy transfer from either L1 or L2 to LA , however, only for cage Pd2 LA 2 L1 2 do the TA data show a subsequent (re)population of L1 -centered (triplet) states, which we attribute to an intra-assembly excitation back-transfer from LA to L1 , accompanied by a prolonged overall excited-state lifetime. Computations suggest that different extents of vibrational relaxation of the donors’ S1 states enable excitation back-transfer in only one of the two cages and propose a Förster-type mechanism for it, indicating that the energy-transfer pathway can be selected through the choice of the co-ligand. As a nanosized cage, this system allows guest molecules to be closely bound within an outer shell of photoactive ligands. Hence, the encapsulation of a chiral guest bestows both cages with circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL).

articles.title: Potential‐Driven In‐Situ Reconstruction of Layered Bismuth Oxychloride for Efficient Electrosynthesis of H2O2 at Large Current Density
articles.abstract: Bismuth-based electro(pre)catalysts are emerging as promising systems for the selective two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR), yet a clear understanding of their structure–property relationships remains limited. Here, we demonstrate that selective electrochemical potential control under alkaline conditions can deterministically direct the reconstruction of layered BiOCl precursors, establishing a direct link between applied bias and catalyst structure. Comprehensive in situ/ex situ characterization coupled with theoretical calculations reveal strong potential-dependent behavior, where at 0 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), BiOCl undergoes deep reconstruction to metallic Bi with surface Cl adsorption (BiOCl-0 V), whereas at 0.5 V versus RHE, the structure is largely preserved (BiOCl-0.5 V). The reconstructed BiOCl-0 V exhibits significantly enhanced activity, H2O2 selectivity, and a near-ideal 2e− ORR pathway compared to BiOCl-0.5 V and commercial Bi, achieving >95% selectivity over a wide potential range, with a peak value exceeding 99%. In a three-electrode flow cell, BiOCl-0 V sustains 150 mA·cm−2 over 160 h, with Faradaic efficiency above 90% and H2O2 productivity of 5.56 mol·gcat −1·h−1. This superior performance stems from reconstruction-induced porosity and an optimized electronic structure, which enhance mass transport and active-site accessibility. These findings establish a direct link between Bi redox chemistry, potential-driven reconstruction, and catalytic performance, offering a general strategy for designing efficient 2e− ORR catalysts.

articles.title: Quantifying the Dissolution of Organic and Inorganic Components in Solid Electrolyte Interphase for Sodium‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Anode interphase dissolution is a major cause of instability in sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) because Na‐based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) compounds are more soluble than their Li analogues. Here, glyme electrolytes with varied chain lengths are used to regulate Na+ solvation structure and clarify its effect on SEI dissolution. A component‐resolved framework combining ion chromatography, mass spectrometry, electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance, and X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy is developed to quantify the dissolution and retention of organic and inorganic SEI species. This approach determines absolute SEI retention rather than relying on aggregate interphase loss. Compared with the glyme, tetraglyme reduces total SEI dissolution from 75% to 53% and increases the retention of inorganic F‐containing species from 18% to 30%. This improvement arises from an anion‐enriched Na+ solvation shell, which promotes the formation of a thinner, denser, and more inorganic‐rich SEI. Consequently, 1.25 Ah NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2||hard carbon pouch cells using the tetraglyme‐based electrolyte retain 91.2% capacity after 500 cycles and exhibit stable voltage retention during 21‐day aging at 60°C. These results establish a quantitative methodology for distinguishing the dissolution behavior of organic and inorganic SEI components, reveal the role of ether chain length in interphase stability, and provide practical guidance for designing durable SIBs.

articles.title: Quantum Dot Visible‐Light Photocatalysis Programs CO2 for Hydrocarboxylation and Carbonylation Reactions
articles.abstract: Homogeneous photocatalysis has greatly expanded the use of CO2 as a renewable one-carbon (C1) feedstock in organic synthesis, yet, controlling sequential proton/electron transfer kinetics and recovering the photocatalyst remain challenging. Here, we report that semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) provide a visible-light-driven heterogeneous platform that directs CO2 activation toward either one-electron radical anion (CO2 •–) or carbon monoxide (CO). Regulating interfacial proton transfer kinetics governs the fates of surface-bound CO2 •– intermediate. Slowing the first proton transfer prolongs CO2 •– lifetime, enabling its in situ interception by aromatic and aliphatic alkenes to afford carboxylic acids with exclusive β-selectivity. Meanwhile, the remaining CO is used as an ex situ C1 feedstock in carbonylation reaction. Moreover, facilitating sequential proton transfer promotes the transformation of CO2 •– intermediate to CO, the diverse carbonylation reactions proceed with good to excellent yields. This strategy can also enable 13C-labeled product and gram-scale synthesis. This work establishes QDs as a versatile and tunable heterogeneous platform for CO2 valorization in organic synthesis, offering complementary advantages over homogeneous systems for divergent C─C bond formation.

articles.title: Record‐High Toroidal Blocking in a {Cu6Dy3} Single Molecular Toroid
articles.abstract: Single-molecule toroids (SMTs) are promising for quantum technologies because their vortex-like spin arrangement generates magnetically silent ground states with minimal stray fields and enhanced protection against decoherence. However, their technological potential requires toroidal states that remain stable under strong external magnetic fields, since weak intramolecular interactions can induce spin flips and destroy toroidal order. In this study, we report heterometallic {3d–4f} complexes, [Ln3Cu6L6(µ3-OH)6(µ1-H2O)6]3+ (Ln = Dy (1), Y (2); L2− = (S,E)-N-(2-(λ 1-oxidaneyl)-1-phenylethyl)-1-(3-methoxy-2-(λ 1-oxidaneyl)phenyl)ethan-1-imine)). Remarkably, the Dy(III) analogue retains its magnetically silent toroidal ground state up to 1.3 T, establishing an unprecedented benchmark for toroidal magnetization blocking and extending the field stability of molecular toroidal states beyond previous limits. Sub-kelvin µ-SQUID measurements, high-frequency EPR spectroscopy, and theoretical modelling show that this high blocking field originates from an unexpectedly strong Dy–Dy exchange interaction, suggested to arise from neighboring Cu(II) ions, whereas direct ferromagnetic Cu–Dy exchange weakly destabilizes the toroidal state. These results reveal a new strategy for stabilizing toroidal states at high fields through targeted control of intramolecular exchange interactions, opening opportunities for electrically addressable molecular nanomagnets and quantum technologies.

articles.title: Self‐Assembled Macrocyclic Nanocarriers for Rapid Ratiometric Loading and Dosing of Multidrug Combinations
articles.abstract: Screening optimal drug combinations and dosing ratios is crucial for achieving and maximizing the synergistic therapeutic benefits in combined treatments. Traditional drug loading methods lack the precision to control drug ratios or involve complex technologies, failing to meet the demands of large‐scale screening in accuracy, convenience, and applicability. To address this, we developed a thermodynamically programmable macrocyclic nanoplatform based on amphiphilic calixarenes that overcomes the kinetic limitations on drug loading accuracy and reproducibility. This platform achieved precise drug loading and release with convenient tunability and broad‐spectrum applicability. For a series of drugs across various ratios, the actual loading ratio is > 95% consistent with the assigned values, and the consistency in delivery into cells and tumor tissues is also > 95%, enabling physicochemical control over the combination ratios. This work illustrates a feasible paradigm to screen for optimal drug ratios, providing a high‐throughput approach for advancing combinatorial therapeutics.

articles.title: Scope
articles.abstract: Scope taking is one of the most characteristic, distinctive, and ubiquitous phenomena in natural language. When an expression takes scope, it combines with surrounding material as its semantic argument. For instance, in Amy gave everyone a book , the semantic argument of everyone is an abstraction over the entire rest of the sentence, namely, λ x . Amy gave x a book , the property an individual has if Amy gave that individual a book. This ability to operate on surrounding context dramatically enriches (and complicates) the ways that meanings can be expressed. Although there are many formal theories of scope taking, Quantifier Raising—often thought of as a covert (silent) version of overt syntactic movement—is by far the dominant approach. There are many constraints on the availability of scope taking that depend on the identity of the scope taker as well as on its surrounding context.

articles.title: Voice Conversion, Voice Morphing, and Speech Style Modification
articles.abstract: A speech sample can be morphed from one voice to another by computing a sufficiently detailed time-frequency parameterization of the signal, optionally decomposing it into speaker-dependent and speaker-independent signal components, editing the parameterization or signal components, and then generating a speech signal based on the edited parameterization. Fine-grained control of time-frequency parameters has found applications in the scientific study of speech perception and in artistic applications such as voiceover and music. Coarse-grained control of speaker identity, emotion, and second-language accent have been applied to various tasks, including the training of speech recognizers and speaker anonymization.

articles.title: What Is Singular They and How Do We Use It? The Psycholinguistics of Singular They
articles.abstract: Singular they is valuable to psycholinguistic research because it has a long-standing usage in English that is currently undergoing changes, both in how often it is used and in what conditions. As a result, singular they is an informative testing ground for the cognitive mechanisms behind language change, which include both top-down intentional change and implicit learning and adaptation. Singular they is also an unusually socially salient function word that provides opportunities to examine how automatic psycholinguistic processes intersect with sociolinguistic issues like gender-fair language, linguistic prescriptivism, and the emerging use of they as a personal pronoun. Developments in the use of singular they are linked to broader shifts in concepts of gender. We suggest that there are two main varieties of singular they that currently differ in acceptability and processing characteristics.
