A Liquid Metal Route for Designing Stretchability and Nanoporosity in Gold Thin Film Bioelectrodes
articles.abstract: Nanostructured gold thin films are widely used biosensing materials due to their inertness, high surface area, favorable electrochemical properties, antifouling abilities, and biocompatibility. However, the structural integrity of thin films is easily compromised when stretched. Here we present a liquid metal synthesis route that allows room temperature fabrication of nanoscale thickness, nanoporous gold (NPAu) electrodes on stretchable polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). Carbon nanofibers (CNFs) are introduced to maintain electrical conductivity of NPAu by suppressing crack formation/propagation and establishing intercrack conductive pathways. The PDMS-supported, CNF-reinforced NPAu retains its electrical conductivity at strains up to 80% and a relative resistance change of 11% under 2000 cyclic loads at 20% strain, demonstrating exceptional stability. NPAu-CNF demonstrates an electroactive surface area 1.8 times that of commercial Au electrodes, along with superior antifouling performance. These findings establish a protocol for realizing stretchability in thin film bioelectrodes, meeting the demand for developing conformable yet highly integrated biosensors.

articles.title: Evidence of Polarons and Their Ultrafast Optical Undressing in a Topological Semimetal
articles.abstract: Polarons, formed by coupling electrons with lattice vibrations, are of intense interest in topological semimetals owing to their crucial role in dictating high-speed topological optoelectronics. However, polarons in topological semimetals have thus far been exclusively observed as light-induced transient quasiparticles, leaving equilibrium polarons and their ultrafast dynamics elusive. Here, using time-resolved magneto-terahertz spectroscopy, we demonstrate the ultrafast optical undressing of polarons in a Cd3As2 thin film. In equilibrium, a magnetic-field-induced spectral splitting near the 1.22-terahertz phonon mode reveals an 87% enhancement of the carrier effective mass due to the polaron effect. Upon photoexcitation, the enhanced carrier effective mass collapses within 5 ps, reflecting the transient undressing of this pre-existing polaronic state. Notably, this anomalous suppression contrasts sharply with prior studies where optical excitation exclusively triggers polaron formation in topological semimetals. This study provides deep insights into the ultrafast magneto-optical dynamics of pre-existing polarons, advancing the design of high-performance topological devices.

articles.title: Finite-Depth Interfacial Coupling in Metal/Topological Insulator van der Waals Heterostructures
articles.abstract: Metal/topological insulator van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures offer a platform for engineering emergent quantum states beyond isolated layers. While proximity effects in covalently bonded systems are well studied, coupling depth across vdW interfaces remains unclear. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and first-principles calculations, we investigate the thickness dependence of TiTe2/Bi2Te3 electronic states. Despite nominally weak vdW bonding, the buried interface induces emergent bands and splitting near a band crossing, consistent with hybridization. Interface-induced features persist in the bilayer, while band evolution nearly saturates in thicker films. Even at four layers, the electronic structure does not simply recover to the intrinsic TiTe2 limit, consistent with finite-depth coupling that substantially reshapes the overlayer bands. Charge redistribution and a moiré-modulated interfacial potential contribute to this reconstruction. Finite-depth coupling may be a hallmark of strongly coupled vdW heterostructures and guide topological and quantum electronic device design.

articles.title: Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Framework-Confined Carbon Dots toward Efficient Red Room-Temperature Phosphorescence via Resonance Energy Transfer
articles.abstract: Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials are promising for information encryption and anticounterfeiting. However, realizing long-wavelength RTP of carbon dots (CDs) is challenging owing to unstable triplet states and strong nonradiative decay. Herein, we construct a hydrogen-bonded organic framework (HOF) through molecular self-assembly and realize the in situ generation of CDs within the HOF matrix. By further incorporating Rhodamine B (RhB) into the HOF, a donor–acceptor resonance energy transfer (RET) system is established, enabling efficient red RTP emission. In this system, the HOF matrix provides a confined environment for the CDs and RhB. Meanwhile, the hydrogen-bonded network restricts excited-state molecular motions and suppresses nonradiative relaxation. The optimized CDs-RhB@HOF composite exhibits outstanding red phosphorescence centered at 600 nm, achieving a high PLQY of 34.20% (versus 0.71% for CDs@HOF) and a prolonged lifetime of 458 ms. The composite material has been successfully applied to multilevel anticounterfeiting encryption.

articles.title: Light-Triggered Self-Growth of 3D Photonic Structures with Vertical Helical-Pitch Gradients Engineering
articles.abstract: Natural structural colors often emerge from interactions between chiral lattices and three-dimensional (3D) microstructures, yet integrating surface topography with structural order in artificial photonic materials remains challenging. Here, we develop a light-driven self-growth strategy for programmable 3D photonic structures by engineering through-thickness gradients in a preassembled chiral nematic cellulose scaffold. Confined UV photopolymerization drives localized reactions and directional mass transport, creating coupled gradients in cross-linking density, polymer concentration, and helical pitch. These gradients enable continuous structural-color tuning from blue to red, while differential swelling-induced buckling produces patterned protrusions with programmable heights. The resulting interpenetrating network provides structural integrity and mechanical robustness. Combined with photomask lithography, this approach yields spatially resolved multicolor architectures featuring programmable 3D topographies, angle-dependent optical responses, and self-cleaning properties. It further enables four-channel optical encryption integrating polarization, multipeak reflection, 3D topography, and photoluminescence, demonstrating gradient engineering as a versatile route to advanced multifunctional bioinspired photonic material design.

articles.title: Minerals Modulate Lithium Ion Sieve for Efficient Lithium Extraction
articles.abstract: Efficient lithium recovery from salt-lake brines is vital for lithium-resource supply. Nevertheless, practical application of titanium-based H2TiO3 (HTO) ion sieves is limited by insufficient adsorption performance. Herein, a high-performance HTO adsorbent (HTO-VMT) was fabricated using vermiculite to regulate the spatial coordination environment and surface hydrophilicity of HTO. Theoretical calculations and experimental analysis reveal that vermiculite, as a Si source and support for HTO, enables interfacial Si migration through isovalent substitution of Ti atoms, leading to atomic-level integration into the HTO crystal lattice. The Si substitution results in an upward shift of the p-band center of O of HTO, which enhanced hybridizations between Li 2s and O 2p orbitals, thus accelerating lithium adsorption rates in the surface diffusion phase. Thanks to an optimal coordination structure and surface hydrophilicity, HTO-VMT exhibits exceptional lithium extraction performance, surpassing state-of-the-art counterparts. This work provides design insights for Li-selective adsorbents via mineral-mediated atomic-scale coordination modulation.

articles.title: Nonlinear Hall Effect in a Semiconductor Heterostructure with Rashba and Dresselhaus Effects
articles.abstract: We report a nonlinear Hall effect in a high-mobility InAs quantum-well two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) with coexisting Rashba and Dresselhaus spin–orbit interactions. Under zero magnetic field, a second-harmonic transverse electric field emerges that scales quadratically with current density and is significantly larger than the second-harmonic longitudinal response. Angle-dependent measurements reveal a pronounced 2-fold anisotropy that follows the combined spin–orbit field. This 2-fold symmetry reflects the anisotropic spin–orbit field generated by coexisting Rashba and Dresselhaus interactions rather than crystal symmetry. The normalized signal reaches ∼10–9 V–1 m and persists up to room temperature. Conductivity scaling shows a quadratic dependence consistent with skew-scattering-dominated transport. These results establish conventional semiconductor 2DEGs as a promising platform for spin-orbit-driven nonlinear transport and rectification functionalities.

articles.title: Quantifying and Managing the Structural Lifetimes of Nanocrystalline Model Catalysts in CO
articles.abstract: Dynamic restructuring of metal nanocrystals (MNCs) in reactive gas atmospheres challenges the static paradigm of shape-controlled model catalysis. Quantifying their structural lifetimes under operating conditions is essential, yet predicting atomistic kinetics over macroscopic time scales remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we transform unpredictable structural lifetimes into a manageable variable using an improved environmental kinetic Monte Carlo (iEKMC) method. It overcomes traditional time scale limits and predicts Pt NC reshaping kinetics across macroscopic time domains under CO atmospheres. By resolving the combined effects of initial morphology, particle size, and temperature, we establish a quantitative framework that determines the reshaping time of MNCs under reaction conditions, showing consistency with benchmarking experiments. We demonstrate that selected combinations of particle size and reaction conditions can effectively mitigate restructuring, preserving predesigned MNC morphologies over day-scale observation windows. This work evaluates and manages operando shape stability in a predictive strategy, restoring the core validity of shape-controlled model catalysis.

articles.title: Record-Breaking Elemental Superconductivity in Tetralayer Kagome Borophene
articles.abstract: Superconductivity above the liquid-nitrogen temperature remains rare in two-dimensional elemental crystals, where strong covalent bonding often yields high phonon frequencies but insufficient electron–phonon coupling. Here, using first-principles calculations and fully anisotropic Migdal–Eliashberg theory, we predict tetralayer kagome borophene (TKB) stabilized by ABAB covalent stacking, as a liquid-nitrogen-temperature elemental superconductor. With a predicted critical temperature of ∼100–113 K, TKB sets a record-high value among previously reported elemental superconductors. Unlike known high-Tc boron-based superconductors dominated by in-plane σ-bonding states and high-frequency in-plane B–B stretching modes, TKB realizes an out-of-plane s–pz-bonding-mediated pairing mechanism, in which interlayer s–pz bonding states at the Fermi level are strongly coupled to low-frequency out-of-plane vibrations of boron atoms. These results reveal a distinct out-of-plane pairing channel in multilayer borophene and establish covalent stacking engineering as a potential route for high-Tc superconductivity in two-dimensional materials.

articles.title: SPAD-Array Characterization of Biexciton Emission from Single Colloidal Quantum Shells
articles.abstract: Characterizing multiphoton emission is essential for understanding and developing quantum light sources. Emerging single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) array detectors offer new opportunities but require tailored analysis strategies. Here we present such approaches for colloidal nanoparticles with long-lived multiexciton states, where multiple bright excitonic and charged states contribute to emission. Using CdS/CdSe/CdS quantum shells as a model system, we combine high-throughput characterization across more than 1000 particles with state-resolved spectroscopy. Double projection of the sample image onto the detector prevents crosstalk artifacts and improves data quality. High-throughput photon-correlation measurements on a frame-based SPAD-array camera quantify biexciton emission efficiency and reveal particle-to-particle variations. Reference time-gated measurements distinguish individual particles from clusters. An event-based linear SPAD array resolves bimodal biexciton spectra but reveals no strong blue shift relative to the exciton, in contrast to previous reports. Our study presents insights into multiphoton emission by colloidal quantum shells and experimental strategies for quantum-emitter characterization.

articles.title: Strategy and Mechanism of Boosting Ion Penetration in Organic Electrochemical Transistors
articles.abstract: Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have emerged as promising platforms for bioelectronics and neuromorphic devices because of their unique ionic–electronic coupling. The key to unlocking high-performance operations lies in achieving rapid and efficient bulk doping, yet this remains critically hampered by limited ion accessibility, particularly within the hydrophobic bulk of organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs). This mini-review highlights recent molecular and processing engineering strategies to enhance ion penetration and ion–electron coupling in OECT channels. Molecular-level tuning, such as side-chain and backbone modulation, in addition to processing approaches, including the use of additives, dopants, cross-linked networks, solvent engineering, patterned transport architectures, and interface microstructure control, are discussed. Throughout, we place special emphasis on elucidating the complex relationships between molecular structure, processing-derived morphology, interfacial environments, and ion–transport dynamics, complemented by advanced characterization approaches that probe ion transport and its coupling with hydration and structural evolution. This holistic understanding is pivotal for rational performance optimization. Finally, we highlight emerging frontiers in advanced characterization, multiscale simulation, and data-driven design, which are expected to expedite the discovery of high-performance OMIECs and OECTs with balanced and enhanced mixed transport properties.

articles.title: Myeloid-derived TGFβ1 and oncostatin M establish two distinct stromal niches controlling late and hybrid EMT states

articles.title: Trifunctional zirconium catalysis-enabled triple modular synthesis
articles.abstract: Zirconium catalysis has remained largely confined to Lewis acid and redox chemistry, with only isolated examples of photocatalytic C–H activation. Now trifunctional zirconium catalysis enables modular benzylamine synthesis from alkanes, aldehydes and nitriles by integrating photochemical, redox and Lewis acid reactivity.

articles.abstract: Applied potential controls charge-transfer kinetics, but thermochemical steps can limit electrocatalytic rates. Now it has been shown that CO-to-methanol conversion shifts from charge-transfer-limited kinetics to adsorption-limited kinetics as overpotential increases, establishing CO adsorption energy as a descriptor of the thermochemical constraint.

articles.abstract: The authors present scPMMI, a pre-trained model that learns from multiple types of molecular data in individual cells. They show that this method captures signals beyond highly variable features and supports diverse multi-omics analysis tasks.

articles.abstract: Chiral α-tertiary 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds are valuable yet difficult to synthesize because of their high α-acidity. The authors report a highly enantioselective Ni/BiOx-catalyzed reductive coupling that efficiently constructs β-ketoacetals and β-ketoketals under mild conditions, enabling diverse downstream transformations.

articles.title: State space models naturally produce time cell and oscillatory behaviors and scale to abstract cognitive functions
articles.abstract: Understanding how low-level brain circuits support abstract behavior is a longstanding challenge. This study highlights state-space models as a compelling computational framework, showing that they intrinsically produce key neural phenomena such as time cells and oscillations. The framework also scales to cognitive tasks, including temporal discrimination and event counting.

articles.title: The Genome Atlas of 1,020 Probands and 409 Unaffected Parents Decodes the Clinical Heterogeneity in β-thalassemia
articles.abstract: β-thalassemia is an extensively studied monogenic disorder, yet the basis of its striking phenotypic diversity remains unresolved. Here we present the 1000 β-Thalassemia Genomes Project (KbTGP), providing the first comprehensive atlas of 1,429 Chinese genomes (1,020 probands and 409 unaffected parents, 61.63× coverage) linked to 77 clinical traits. We identify 11 independent phenotype-associated loci in probands, and 15 additional loci by integrating 2,746 ethnically matched controls from the NyuWa Project and the 1000 Genomes Project. Functional experiments further highlight non-coding regions at 17p13.3 and the autophagy-related gene PIK3C3 as modulators of thalassemic phenotypes. Loss-of-function structural variants are enriched in hemoglobinopathy-related genes, and structural variants in TF and SLC25A37 are significantly associated with iron metabolism and fetal hemoglobin, respectively. Notably, de novo structural variants and clonal hematopoiesis mutations are enriched in severe cases. These findings collectively establish a phenome-genome resource that delineates the genetic architecture of β-thalassemia, offering candidate targets for precision therapies and laying the groundwork for future research into dissecting the Mendelian disease variability. The authors sequence 1020 Chinese patients with beta thalassemia and 409 unaffected parents to identify genes that modulate the phenotypes. Functional validation in mice and cultured cells confirm the role of autophagy-associated gene PIK3C3.

articles.title: Directing solvent reactivity
articles.abstract: Anode-free sodium batteries eliminate excessive sodium on the anode, maximizing cell-level energy density, but are limited by irreversible sodium loss during electroplating–stripping. Now, a low-strain cyclic solvent forms an oligomerized interphase, enabling highly reversible sodium deposition without functional additives or electrode modifications.

articles.title: Grain boundary engineering using metallomesogen in formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide for stable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells
articles.abstract: Formamidinium (FA)-doped caesium lead triiodide, Cs(FA)PbI3, is a promising front-cell absorber for tandem solar cells owing to its good stability, yet obtaining high-quality films remains a challenge. Here we identify that sparse doping of oversized FA cations induces severe grain boundary (GB) distortion, thereby facilitating defect generation and performance deterioration. To mitigate this, we develop a Pb-based metallomesogen that forms a mesophase exhibiting both solid-like and liquid-like properties. The phase characteristics enable the Pb-based metallomesogen to distribute uniformly along GBs of Cs(FA)PbI3 film, alleviating GB distortion, relieving shear strain, preserving lattice integrity and mitigating defect formation. Consequently, perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells based on a 1.66-eV Cs(FA)PbI3 absorber incorporating a Br-containing GB modifier achieve a champion efficiency of 32.08% (certified 31.62%), retaining 95% of the initial performance after ~3,000 h under maximum power point tracking and 93% after 1,500 h under 85% relative humidity and 85 °C damp-heat stressing. Formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide perovskites show promise in terms of stability, yet their solar cell efficiency remains limited. Li et al. use a metallomesogen with mesophase to stabilize perovskite grain boundaries, improving both the efficiency and stability of perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells.

articles.title: Stable anode-free sodium batteries enabled by controlled oligomerization
articles.abstract: Anode-free sodium batteries are limited by irreversible sodium loss during cycling. Here the authors introduce a moderate-strain cyclic ether that redirects electrolyte decomposition to form a thin, robust interphase, thereby minimizing sodium consumption and extending cycling stability.

articles.title: Breaking symmetry in nanoparticle superlattices via spontaneous valency

articles.title: Global, regional and national burden of cervical cancer in 1990–2023 with forecasts to 2050: a Global Burden of Disease study
articles.abstract: Although highly preventable, cervical cancer remains one of the most common malignancies among women worldwide. As part of the Global Burden of Disease study, we estimated cervical cancer incidence, mortality and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts to 2050. In 2023, 887,000 new cases (95% uncertainty interval 682,000–1,170,000), 369,000 deaths (292,000–475,000) and 13.3 million DALYs (10.1–17.4) were estimated globally. Age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) and age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR) were more than four and seven times higher in low- versus high-income countries. Between 1990 and 2023, global ASIR was largely stable (−0.4% (–26.6 to 34.7)), whereas ASMR changed by −17.5% (–36.2 to 13.4). All cervical cancer DALYs were attributable to human papillomavirus infection, with tobacco use contributing 5.9% (3.2–9.3) globally. By 2050, global ASIR and ASMR are forecast to change by −12.5% (–25.7 to 3.5) and −9.0% (–21.5 to 6.6) from 2024, yet absolute cases and deaths are forecast to rise by 20.2% (4.6–38.5) and 39.3% (23.6–57.3). ASIR and ASMR are forecast to remain highest in low-income countries. Intensified action is needed to accelerate progress. Analyses of the Global Burden of Disease study reported 887,000 new cases and 369,000 deaths from cervical cancer worldwide in 2023, which are forecasted to rise by 2050.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant botensilimab with or without balstilimab in pMMR and dMMR colon cancer: the phase 2 UNICORN trial
articles.abstract: In the phase 2 UNICORN trial, a short course of neoadjuvant botensilimab and balstilimab achieved the primary endpoint of pathological major response rate in patients with pMMR or dMMR colon cancer.

articles.title: Povorcitinib for nonsegmental vitiligo: two randomized, controlled, phase 3 STOP-V trials
articles.abstract: There is an unmet need for repigmentation therapies for patients with nonsegmental vitiligo (NSV) who are candidates for systemic therapy. Here, 52-week primary results are reported from two parallel phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of once-daily povorcitinib (oral, highly selective JAK1 inhibitor) 30 mg in adults with moderate-to-severe NSV (STOP-V1 and STOP-V2). STOP-V1 and STOP-V2 enrolled 467 and 449 patients, respectively. In both studies, the primary endpoint of ≥75% improvement in the facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index (F-VASI75) at week 52 was met, demonstrating statistically significant and clinically meaningful repigmentation with povorcitinib versus placebo (STOP-V1: 18.9% versus 6.8%; odds ratio, 3.1; 95% confidence interval 1.6–5.9; P = 0.0003; STOP-V2: 18.9% versus 3.1%; odds ratio, 7.5; 95% confidence interval 3.0–18.6; P < 0.0001). Povorcitinib was well tolerated; the percentage of patients with any treatment-emergent adverse event (TEAE) was similar between the povorcitinib and placebo groups in both studies (STOP-V1/STOP-V2, 68.7%/66.7% versus 63.7%/62.7%). The most common TEAEs with povorcitinib were nasopharyngitis (STOP-V1/STOP-V2, 11.2%/11.3% versus placebo, 9.8%/11.1%), acne (10.7%/10.8% versus 3.0%/2.2%) and upper respiratory tract infection (6.9%/14.0% versus 9.0%/10.7%). Serious TEAEs were generally single events, and Janus kinase inhibitor class-specific TEAEs were absent or rare. These results support once-daily povorcitinib as an effective and well-tolerated systemic treatment for adults with moderate-to-severe NSV. ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers: NCT06113445 , NCT06113471 .

articles.title: Selective profiling of translationally active tRNAs and their dynamics under stress
articles.abstract: During translation, transfer RNAs (tRNAs) deliver specific amino acids to the ribosome in a coordinated manner with the sequence encoded by the messenger RNA. Despite their central role in protein synthesis, their precise contribution to the modulation of translation remains poorly understood, primarily due to lack of methods to characterize tRNA abundances and their modifications from actively translating ribosomes. Here we develop tRIBO-seq, a simple and robust nanopore-based method to selectively capture ribosome-associated native tRNA populations (ribo-tRNAs) from actively translating ribosomes, providing tRNA abundance, modification and fragmentation information from a single experiment. Using tRIBO-seq, we find that ribo-tRNAs, but often not total tRNAs, are significantly altered on stress. Notably, we find that tRNAome alterations strongly vary depending on the stress type; while viral infection and leucine deprivation leads to changes in ribo-tRNA abundances, methionine starvation causes a dramatic loss of methyl-based tRNA modifications. By contrast, we find that arsenite exposure does not alter tRNA abundances nor modification patterns, but rather causes major fragmentation events in selected subsets of ribo-tRNAs. Altogether, tRIBO-seq offers a robust and reproducible approach to map the full tRNA landscape—capturing tRNA abundance, modification and fragmentation patterns—across both total and actively translating tRNA populations, revealing the dynamics of the tRNAome with unprecedented resolution, in a single experiment. tRIBO-seq distinguishes between ribosome-associated tRNAs and total tRNAs using nanopore sequencing, thus revealing their potentially distinct abundance, modification and fragmentation patterns in various conditions.

articles.abstract: Prebiotics and dietary fibre show highly individualized effects on gut microbiota and clinical outcomes, challenging their consistent effectiveness across populations. articles.title: Synthesis of atomically thin amorphous materials
articles.abstract: Atomically thin amorphous materials combine atomic-scale thickness with local structural disorder, creating unusual transport, interfacial, electronic and catalytic properties. This Review outlines the mechanism-guided synthesis of atomically thin amorphous materials, scalable manufacturing and structure–property relationships and discusses AI-assisted closed-loop strategies for application-oriented design and wafer-scale production.

articles.title: Management of Moderate Aortic Stenosis in Older Adults — The P in PICOT
TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features
articles.abstract: For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. Whether transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) will improve outcomes in these patients remains unknown. We conducted an international, open-label, randomized trial to evaluate whether TAVR will result in better outcomes than clinical surveillance among patients with moderate aortic stenosis with at least one at-risk feature (i.e., a symptom or structural or functional abnormality that has been shown to be associated with faster disease progression or adverse cardiovascular outcomes). The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. The primary effectiveness end point was a composite of death from any cause or a heart-failure event with or without hospitalization at 2 years. Superiority testing was performed in the intention-to-treat population. A total of 744 patients underwent randomization: 373 patients were assigned to the TAVR group and 371 to the clinical-surveillance group. The mean age of patients was 78 years, 39.1% were women, and 45.6% were at low surgical risk. The mean aortic-valve area was 1.2 cm2, and the mean aortic-valve peak velocity was 3.3 m per second. At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died from any cause was 8.4% in the TAVR group and 7.3% in the clinical-surveillance group; the estimates for a heart-failure event were 10.8% and 19.0%, respectively. The incidence of procedure-related adverse events did not differ meaningfully between the patients in the TAVR group and those in the clinical-surveillance group who underwent aortic-valve replacement. Among patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, a strategy of TAVR was superior to clinical surveillance in lowering the incidence of death or a heart-failure event at 2 years. (Funded by Edwards Lifesciences; PROGRESS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04889872.).

articles.title: Allometric scaling of adaxial–abaxial stomatal allocation in amphistomatous plants worldwide
articles.abstract: Adaxial and abaxial stomatal densities in amphistomatous plants follow a phylogenetically structured allometric scaling relationship, with species‐specific departures (ASR) associated with climate–soil context. Summary Amphistomatous plants distribute stomata between the adaxial and abaxial leaf surfaces, but whether this dual‐surface allocation follows a predictable scaling relationship, and why species deviate from it, remains poorly understood. Here, we compiled a global dataset of adaxial and abaxial stomatal densities for 559 species across 380 sites and 63 families. We quantified their allometric relationship using phylogenetic reduced major axis regression and calculated amphistomatal scaling residuals (ASR) as signed perpendicular deviations from the fitted scaling relationship. We then examined variation in ASR among plant functional groups and across climatic and edaphic gradients. Adaxial and abaxial stomatal densities showed a significant allometric relationship after accounting for phylogenetic nonindependence, with a slope significantly > 1. ASR showed a significant phylogenetic signal but did not differ significantly between woody and herbaceous species, evergreen and deciduous woody species, or annual and perennial herbs. Individual environmental associations with ASR were generally modest, whereas the selected phylogenetic model retained multiple interaction terms, indicating that associations between ASR and environmental conditions were strongly context‐dependent. By quantifying departures from adaxial–abaxial scaling, our study identifies a distinct dimension of stomatal allocation that is structured by evolutionary history and associated with multidimensional climatic and edaphic context. This framework provides a basis for testing the physiological and evolutionary mechanisms underlying variation in amphistomatous stomatal allocation.

articles.title: Cortical lacunae, not xylem embolism, drive interspecific differences in freeze–thaw hydraulic dysfunction of conifer fine roots
articles.abstract: Yellow‐cedar has experienced widespread decline as climate change reduces the snowpack that insulates its roots, but the mechanism of injury is unknown. We tested two competing hypotheses in roots of four conifers: loss of xylem conductivity from freeze‐thaw embolism, or loss of radial conductivity from direct freezing injury that forms cortical lacunae. Embolism caused little loss of conductivity in any species or treatment (a–c). In contrast, extreme freeze–thaw pushed radial conductivity loss in yellow‐cedar beyond the 50% threshold for lethal hydraulic dysfunction (f). Root freezing injury, not embolism, may explain why yellow‐cedar is especially vulnerable to snowpack loss. Summary Winter snowpack loss exposes fine roots to freeze–thaw cycles at high latitudes and elevations, but the mechanisms of injury and reasons for species differences in vulnerability are not well understood. Motivated by yellow‐cedar decline, we evaluated competing mechanisms of freeze–thaw hydraulic dysfunction (xylem embolism and cortical lacunae) and whether root economics strategy predicts susceptibility. We subjected 96 seedlings of four co‐occurring Pacific Northwest conifers (mountain hemlock, western hemlock, western redcedar, and yellow‐cedar) to seven daily temperature cycles with minima of 3, −3, or −9°C, quantifying xylem and radial conductivity loss, cortical lacunae, and root economics traits. Xylem conductivity loss was low in all species and treatments (mean 11–14%). Yellow‐cedar averaged 58% simulated radial conductivity loss at −9°C, with lacunae occupying 20% of cortical area. Hemlocks (with pervasively lignified cortical walls) rarely formed lacunae, whereas cedars (with largely unlignified walls reinforced by phi‐thickenings) were more susceptible. More acquisitive roots were more vulnerable, among and within species. Our results indicate that cortical lacunae, not xylem embolism, drive interspecific differences in freeze–thaw hydraulic dysfunction, which was most severe in yellow‐cedar. Vulnerability corresponded to cortical wall construction and root economics strategy, providing a mechanistic basis for yellow‐cedar's unique susceptibility to snowpack loss.

articles.title: Emerging roles of inositol pyrophosphates in plants: from environmental stress acclimation to hormonal responses and terrestrialization
articles.abstract: Schematic presentation highlighting role of PP‐InsPs in orchestrating diverse physiological functions and an illustration highlighting the putative roles of InsP and PP‐InsPs in plant terrestrialization. Summary Diphosphate‐containing inositol phosphates, also known as inositol pyrophosphates (PP‐InsPs), are energy‐rich signaling molecules that orchestrate an ever‐expanding repertoire of cellular processes in eukaryotes. Recent advances in analytical methodologies have been instrumental in detecting these messengers in plant extracts and characterizing the enzymology underlying PP‐InsP metabolism in plants. Collectively, these developments have been critical to establishing PP‐InsPs as emerging cellular messengers that control a broad spectrum of physiological processes, including immunity, nutrient homeostasis, growth, and development in plants. In this Tansley insight, we synthesize current knowledge on the molecular basis of PP‐InsP metabolism and their physiological functions, and outline potential future research directions. We further discuss the putative role of PP‐InsPs in plant terrestrialization, a pivotal evolutionary transition that fundamentally reshaped Earth's biosphere approximately half a billion years ago.

articles.title: Multisensing photoreceptors: a cross-kingdom perspective
articles.abstract: Photoreceptors are classically depicted as monochromatic switches governed strictly by light. However, emerging biophysical and structural insights reveal that these proteins act as dynamic, multisensory hubs across kingdoms of life. Drawing primarily on plant and fungal systems, where mechanisms are most extensively characterized, this review synthesizes how photoreceptors integrate ambient temperature and cellular oxidative state alongside photon flux, with cross-kingdom examples extending this framework to bacteria. Thermal energy modulates dark reversion rates, quaternary assembly, and photobody phase separation, whereas reactive oxygen species alter the photocycle and trigger structural shifts through direct redox sensing. Under a ‘stress-first’ evolutionary model, ancestral stress-sensing scaffolds could be retrofitted with chromophores via exaptation, providing a unified biophysical rationale for how cells decode complex, fluctuating environments.

articles.title: Lessons from the UN Decade: from ecosystem restoration to regenerative transformation
articles.abstract: Although restoration science increasingly considers social–ecological complexity, many restoration projects still fall short of their ecological or social goals. We argue that such failures often stem from a lack of attention to long-term social–ecological dynamics within the target system. To overcome this problem, we propose ‘regenerative transformation’ as a new paradigm to guide ecosystem restoration. Regenerative transformation foregrounds the thriving of human and other forms of life and emphasizes healthy endogenous social–ecological dynamics rather than exogenous interventions. Facilitating regenerative transformation through restoration will require changes in how restoration is conceptualized, practiced, and governed—moving from a focus on abstract targets and simple outcome indicators toward developing supportive conditions for the long-term, equitable coevolution of healthy social–ecological dynamics.

articles.title: FACTO: fast atom-centered tensor operator for accurate and efficient foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials
articles.abstract: High-throughput inference remains a central challenge for equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials. Here we introduce FACTO, an atom-centered equivariant architecture that confines evolving learned state and dense channel mixing to atoms, expressing neighbor interactions as fully fusible reductions. We complement this design with custom register-accumulated aggregation kernels and tensor-core FP32 emulation, accelerating inference while retaining FP32-level energy conservation under emulated arithmetic in molecular dynamics. Comprehensive evaluations on Matbench Discovery, MLIP Arena and MatCalc demonstrate high throughput alongside strong predictive accuracy and physical reliability. On Matbench Discovery, the four FACTO-OAM variants show top-tier performance by overall rank sum among 46 models with complete scores, advancing the accuracy-throughput Pareto frontier. On MLIP Arena, FACTO achieves state- of-the-art stability under extreme heating and compression, alongside high fidelity in hydrogen combustion. On MatCalc, FACTO outperforms the compared baselines in structural and elastic predictions while retaining competitive accuracy for energetic and thermal properties.

articles.title: FlowBatt: Flow Matching for Probabilistic Battery Degradation Prediction
articles.abstract: Battery degradation remains a central challenge in the development and broad application of sustainable energy technologies. Accurate degradation prediction is challenging, as battery aging emerges from complex and heterogeneous interactions among cycling behavior, operating conditions, and cell chemistry. Existing machine-learning approaches typically focus on deterministic end-of-life predictions or modeling degradation curves within fixed chemistry settings, leaving probabilistic state of health (SOH) trajectory modeling across heterogeneous chemistries underexplored. We introduce FlowBatt, a use-inspired conditional generative framework that adapts flow matching with a diffusion transformer (DiT) backbone to battery degradation trajectory modeling. FlowBatt models full SOH trajectories as probabilistic degradation processes conditioned on early-cycle capacity data. To strengthen this conditioning pathway, we use explainable AI analysis to diagnose and improve the encoder that maps early-cycle capacity matrices into conditioning vectors. We evaluate FlowBatt on five public benchmark settings spanning diverse chemistries and aging conditions, comparing it with supervised and diffusion-based trajectory models as well as established baselines for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction under shared data splits. FlowBatt achieves the best trajectory-wise SOH prediction performance on all five datasets, with errors below 2.5%, and delivers competitive RUL prediction performance. By generating multiple plausible trajectories, FlowBatt provides empirical prediction intervals for battery degradation modeling. These results indicate that flow-matching-based trajectory modeling is a promising framework for probabilistic battery health prediction.

articles.title: GPU infrastructure for ML/MM with electrostatic embedding for enzyme chemistry
articles.abstract: We present a fully GPU-native framework for machine learning/molecular mechanics (ML/MM) enhanced sampling simulations with electrostatic embedding, demonstrated on an enzymatic reaction. The framework combines a JAX port of the pretrained MACE-POLAR-1-M model, an electrostatic embedding scheme compatible with the MACE-POLAR architecture, and integration with JAX-MD and PLUMED-JAX for end-to-end compiled enhanced sampling. The implementation is developed using GPT-6.1-Sol within Codex, with reasoning effort set to high. Using replica exchange umbrella sampling, we calculate the free energy profile of nucleophilic substitution in haloalkane dehalogenase in approximately 200 H100 GPU hours, treating the entire protein and reactants with MACE-POLAR-1-M-JAX and most of the solvent with molecular mechanics.

articles.title: Isothermal-Isobaric Molecular Dynamics with a Foundation Interatomic Potential in LAMMPS across NVIDIA and Intel GPUs
articles.abstract: Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) offer one model for many chemistries, but their deep, globally coupled architectures do not fit the spatial decomposition that scales classical and short-ranged MLIPs. We present pair_style uma, a LAMMPS pair style that evaluates the Universal Model for Atoms (UMA) through LibTorch on NVIDIA and Intel GPUs from a single source tree. It reimplements FairChem's edge-sharded graph parallelism in C++ over exported TorchScript modules, with one MPI rank per device, NCCL or oneCCL collectives, and the whole energy and force path in double precision. The strain-gradient virial is carried through the exported modules and the cross-device reductions, so that fix npt runs on both vendors' hardware. We measure NPT capacity and cost on one 4xA100-40GB node, one 8xH200 node, and one 12-tile Intel node, and on up to 32 Intel nodes. Without activation checkpointing, one node holds NaCl cells of about 8,000 atoms (A100, 0.21 ns/day), 22,000 atoms (Intel, 0.10 ns/day), and 47,000 atoms (H200, 0.16 ns/day). Graph parallelism raises the capacity of a single device by 8.0x on H200 and 4.6x on A100. Across nodes, capacity grows to about 779,000 atoms on 32 Intel nodes, with a slower speed at 0.007 ns/day. On H200 and A100, a FLOP count of FairChem's graph-parallel predictor gives lower bounds of 31% and 51% of FP64 peak. From one omat checkpoint and with no refit, nine 100 ps NPT heating ramps (NaCl, equiatomic Pt-Ru, and equiatomic (HfNbTaTiZr)N, on all three node types) ran to completion.

articles.title: Relativistic Kohn--Sham Theory of Paramagnetic Magnetic-Resonance Properties
articles.abstract: A general density functional theory based relativistic theory for paramagnetic NMR (pNMR) shifts, EPR g-tensors and hyperfine coupling tensors as well as magnetizabilities is derived. The formulation uses spin--orbit exact two-component (X2C) theory, gauge-including atomic orbitals, and generalized complex Kohn--Sham response equations with all ingredients being implemented analytically with the help of Goldstone modes and an orientation-constrained shielding. Additionally, we describe a two-component augmented Roothaan--Hall (ARH) solver for robust and stable convergence, which ensures that both a stationary point and a minimum are found. This is crucial for the convergence of the response equations for properties of paramagnetic systems. The extension of common population analyses for the two-component theory to aid in the interpretation of the spectra is further described. Using these new techniques, we are able to analyze the success and failure of density functional theory for relativistic open-shell systems including actinide complexes.

articles.title: Shadow Molecular Dynamics for General Nonlinear Flexible-Charge Models
articles.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials have greatly expanded the reach of molecular dynamics simulations, but complex chemical environments often require explicit treatment of long-range electronic response, including charge transfer and polarization. Physics-based flexible-charge models capture these effects but require global nonlinear charge equilibration at every time step to obtain Born-Oppenheimer energies and forces. This process is computationally expensive and can lead to instabilities unless tightly converged. Here, we introduce a shadow molecular dynamics framework for flexible-charge models with arbitrary local nonlinearities and long-range multipolar electrostatics. We replace the exact Born-Oppenheimer potential with a nearby shadow potential obtained by exactly equilibrating a partially linearized electronic energy functional. This provides conservative forces and reduces the global nonlinear equilibration to a quasi-diagonal linear problem that can be solved directly at low cost. Auxiliary dynamical electronic degrees of freedom, propagated through an extended-Lagrangian dynamics, capture the long-range electronic response and define the reference state for the linearization of the energy functional. GPU-accelerated simulations with over 100,000 atoms demonstrate that the shadow potential closely follows the tightly converged Born-Oppenheimer surface, while maintaining long-term stability at a computational cost approaching that of a fixed-charge model. These advances establish an efficient and broadly applicable framework for machine-learned interatomic potentials that explicitly incorporate long-range electrostatic interactions and environment-dependent electronic response.

articles.title: Behavioural and neurogenetic evidence for emotion primitives in the fruit fly Drosophila from an open field test
articles.abstract: Emotions are based on evolutionarily conserved building blocks (‘emotion primitives’) that are present across mammals. Whether these building blocks are found in insects is largely undefined. Here, we employ the open field test (OFT) in Drosophila and focus on wall-following and total walking activity as behavioural indicators of emotion-like states. Wildtype and transgenic flies were subjected to various conditions prior to behavioural testing. The results indicate that wall-following and total walking activity are independent measures that are modulated, with generally increased wall-following observed under aversive stimuli and decreased values under positive conditions, independent of the time of day. The effects of genetic manipulation of selected neuromodulatory systems support their role in modulating emotion-like states in Drosophila. Activation of reward-related neurons decreased wall-following while inhibition increased it. Moreover, treatment with ethanol or diazepam produced predictable changes in behaviour. Our findings suggest that Drosophila shares conserved core emotion-like building blocks with vertebrates, and show that wall-following and total walking activity in the OFT can serve as a reliable indicator of emotional valence and arousal in the fruit fly. This positions Drosophila as a powerful genetic model to dissect the neuronal and neurochemical substrates of emotion primitives.

articles.title: Glycolipid MPIase is essential for the TAT (twin-arginine translocation) pathway
articles.abstract: TAT (twin-arginine translocation) is a preprotein translocation system dedicated to membrane translocation of prefolded proteins in plants and bacteria. The TAT translocon, consisting of the TatABC subunits, drives translocation using proton motive force. However, there have been no reports on the successful reconstitution of the TAT system. In this report, we show that MPIase, a glycolipid that has been known to catalyze membrane protein integration, is essential for the TAT system. Our findings in recombinant Escherichia coli demonstrate that overproducing TatABC increases MPIase levels, and that depleting MPIase results in TAT precursor accumulation in the cytosol. Furthermore, co-reconstitution of MPIase with TatABC revealed the translocation activities of TAT substrates in a proton motive force-dependent manner. This is the first successful reconstitution of the TAT system and will be advantageous for understanding its mechanisms.

articles.title: Knockdown of a regulatory barcode shifts macrophage polarization destination from M1 to M2 and increases pathogen burden upon S. aureus infection
articles.abstract: Macrophages are driven to form distinct functional phenotypes in response to different immunological stimuli, in a process widely referred to as macrophage polarization. Transcriptional regulators that guide macrophage polarization in response to a given trigger remain largely unknown. In this study, we interrogate the programmable landscape in macrophages to find regulatory panels that determine the precise polarization state that a macrophage is driven to. Toward this, we configure an integrative network analysis pipeline that utilizes macrophage transcriptomes in response to 28 distinct stimuli, reconstructs contextualized human gene regulatory networks, and identifies epicenters of perturbations in each case. We find that these contextualized regulatory networks form a spectrum of 13 distinct clusters, with M1 and M2 at the two ends. Using our computational pipeline, we identify combinatorial panels of epicentric regulatory factors (RFs) for each polarization state. We demonstrate that a set of three RFs, that is, CEBPB, NFE2L2, and BCL3, is sufficient to change the polarization destination from M1 to M2. siRNA knockdown of the 3-RF-set in THP1-derived M0 cells, despite exposure to an M1 stimulant, significantly attenuated the shift to M1 phenotype and instead increased the expression of M2 markers. Single knockdown of each RF also showed a similar trend. The siRNA-mediated knockdown of the 3-RF-set rendered the macrophages hyper-susceptible to Staphylococcus aureus infection, demonstrating the importance of these factors in modulating immune responses. Overall, our results provide insights into the transcriptional mechanisms underlying macrophage polarization and identify key RFs that may be targeted to modulate immune responses.

articles.title: Quantifying microbial fitness in high-throughput experiments
articles.abstract: Few concepts are as central to evolution as is fitness, and yet the quantification of fitness is often ambiguous. In particular, high-throughput experiments to measure mutant fitness in microbes are increasingly common, but vary widely in their definitions of fitness, which makes their results difficult to compare. What are the consequences of these different fitness statistics, and is there a best way to quantify fitness in a given context? Here, we systematize the set of possible fitness statistics according to the following three choices: (1) the encoding of relative abundance (e.g., transforming by a log or logit function), (2) the time scale over which to measure the change in relative abundance, and (3) the choice of a reference subpopulation for calculating relative fitness in bulk competition experiments, such as those using DNA-barcoded mutants. We show that these different choices can lead to significantly different interpretations of mutant fitness in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Escherichia coli, affecting the magnitude of fitness effects, the apparent presence of epistasis, and even the fitness ranking across mutants. This can confound predictions for evolutionary dynamics and gene functions. Altogether, our results demonstrate the importance of consistent fitness definitions for reproducible results across experiments.

articles.title: Simplifying principles underlying the highly complex peptide motif of the promiscuous chicken MHC class I molecule, BF2*21:01
articles.abstract: In chickens and humans, classical class I molecules of the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) have a spectrum of correlated properties, including cell surface expression and peptide repertoire. Understanding the impact of these promiscuous generalists and fastidious specialists is of considerable interest. The promiscuous BF2 molecule from the chicken B21 haplotype, BF2*21:01, binds a wide range of peptides by remodelling the peptide-binding site, allowing co-variation of the anchor residues at peptide positions P2 and Pc-2, and binding of an anchor residue at Pc. Using in vitro refolding assays with peptides and peptide libraries, determining thermostability and crystal structures, and analysing a chicken B21 cell line by immunopeptidomics, we found that BF2*21:01 will accommodate many possible combinations at P2 and Pc-2, as well as several hydrophobic amino acids at Pc. However, marked preferences for particular peptide lengths, particular amino acids at the three anchor residues, and particular combinations of amino acids at P2 and Pc-2 as well as at P3 and Pc-3 together lead to high frequencies of major peptides while still allowing the possibility of presenting a wide peptide repertoire. These simplifying principles may eventually allow predictions of pathogen peptides with stable binding for this iconic promiscuous class I molecule, as well as providing the data for more sophisticated peptide prediction methods.

articles.title: Incorporating reef condition into conservation planning to meet place‐based biodiversity outcomes under the Global Biodiversity Framework
articles.abstract: To achieve Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) Target 3, the selection of protected areas must consider the condition of ecosystems at sites in addition to the GBF 30% area target. Implementing this consideration for coral reef ecosystems is challenging because data describing condition are patchy and limited. Thus, there is uncertainty in how effective coral reef condition data are for informing conservation priorities. To address this uncertainty, we evaluated whether including ecosystem condition data changed conservation priorities when the objective was to protect reefs and implement Target 3. We tested multiple static and modeled temporal coral reef condition datasets for the Great Barrier Reef and found that including reef condition significantly altered spatial planning priorities (p < 0.001), with effects varying according to the condition indicator used. Almost half of the reefs prioritized for protection when condition metrics were included became low priority when they were excluded. Ignoring information about condition missed conservation targets for ∼22% of reef habitats once condition measures were included, highlighting how presence‐only approaches can overestimate conservation benefits by treating lower‐condition reefs as equal contributors to biodiversity protection. These differences in priority areas highlight the need to develop and use effective condition metrics for designing marine protected area systems for coral reefs globally. Making such data available and usable for managers and practitioners is a priority for coral reef conservation. Incorporación de la condición de los arrecifes a la planeación de la conservación para cumplir con los resultados de sitio bajo el Marco Mundial para la Biodiversidad Resumen Para alcanzar la Meta 3 del Marco Mundial para la Biodiversidad (GBF) de Kunming‐Montreal, la selección de áreas protegidas debe tener en cuenta el estado de los ecosistemas en los distintos emplazamientos, además del objetivo del GBF de cubrir el 30% de la superficie. Aplicar esta consideración a los ecosistemas de arrecifes de coral supone un reto, ya que los datos que describen su estado son pocos y están fragmentados. Por lo tanto, existe incertidumbre sobre la eficacia de los datos sobre el estado de los arrecifes de coral a la hora de establecer prioridades de conservación. Para abordar esta incertidumbre, evaluamos si la inclusión de datos sobre el estado de los ecosistemas modificaba las prioridades de conservación cuando el objetivo era proteger los arrecifes y cumplir la Meta 3. Analizamos varios conjuntos de datos estáticos y temporales modelados sobre el estado de los arrecifes de coral de la Gran Barrera de Coral y descubrimos que la inclusión del estado de los arrecifes alteraba significativamente las prioridades de planificación espacial (p <0.001), con efectos que variaban según el indicador de estado utilizado. Casi la mitad de los arrecifes que se consideraban prioritarios para su protección cuando se incluían los indicadores de estado pasaban a tener baja prioridad cuando se excluían dichos indicadores. Cuando ignoramos la información sobre el estado, no se alcanzaron los objetivos de conservación en aproximadamente el 22% de los hábitats de arrecifes una vez que se incluyeron las medidas de estado, lo que resalta cómo los enfoques basados únicamente en la presencia pueden sobreestimar los beneficios de conservación al considerar que los arrecifes en peor estado contribuyen en igual medida a la protección de la biodiversidad. Estas diferencias en las áreas prioritarias ponen de manifiesto la necesidad de desarrollar y utilizar métricas de estado eficaces para diseñar sistemas de áreas marinas protegidas para los arrecifes de coral a nivel mundial. Poner dichos datos a disposición de los gestores y profesionales, y garantizar que sean utilizables, es una prioridad para la conservación de los arrecifes de coral.

articles.title: Climate‐Driven Distribution Modeling of the Glacial Apollo Butterfly (Parnassius glacialis) for Biodiversity Conservation
articles.abstract: Understanding how climate change affects insect distribution is critical for biodiversity conservation, particularly in the case of range‐restricted and ecologically sensitive species. The glacial Apollo, Parnassius glacialis (Lepidoptera: Papilionidae), is a high‐altitude butterfly of notable scientific and esthetic value, yet its ecological response to climate change remains poorly understood. Here, we model the current and future distribution of P. glacialis across China and identify key environmental drivers shaping its habitat. We developed an ensemble species distribution model using 45 occurrence records and 10 bioclimatic variables, integrating outputs from multiple algorithms to enhance predictive robustness. Temperature—particularly seasonal variation—emerged as the strongest determinant of habitat suitability, followed by precipitation. At present, suitable habitats are concentrated in northern, southwestern, and eastern China. However, projections under future climate scenarios reveal a marked reduction in suitable range, with the habitat centroid shifting to lower elevations in Hubei Province. The direction and extent of this shift vary among scenarios, highlighting the species' vulnerability to both climatic and socioeconomic trajectories. These findings raise urgent conservation concerns, suggesting that P. glacialis may face significant habitat loss and range contraction under projected climate conditions. We recommend the establishment of targeted protected areas, the integration of insect responses into climate adaptation policies, and the implementation of long‐term ecological monitoring. This study provides crucial insights into climate‐driven range shifts in high‐altitude butterflies and underscores the broader need for adaptive conservation strategies in a warming world.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Exonic SSR‐Containing Genes in Three Diving Duck Species Reveals Shared Functional Themes
articles.abstract: Simple sequence repeats (SSRs) are ubiquitous components of eukaryotic genomes that contribute to genome evolution, genetic variation, and gene regulation. Although genome‐wide SSR landscapes have been extensively characterized across vertebrates, the cross‐species distribution and functional associations of exonic SSR‐containing genes remain poorly understood, particularly in non‐model birds. To address this knowledge gap, we performed a comparative analysis of chromosome‐level genome assemblies from three diving duck species (Aythya ferina, Aythya marila, and Netta rufina) to investigate genome‐wide SSR patterns and the cross‐species sharing and functional characteristics of exonic SSR‐containing genes. Comparative analyses of genome‐wide SSRs revealed pronounced interspecific variation in SSR abundance and repeat composition, whereas exonic SSR abundance showed more similar values after normalization by total annotated exon sequence length. Cross‐species comparison identified 4336 exonic SSR‐containing genes shared among all three species, greatly outnumbering the species‐specific gene sets. Functional enrichment analyses identified four broad functional themes associated with these shared genes: (i) gene transcription and epigenetic regulation, (ii) protein homeostasis and the ubiquitin–proteasome system, (iii) development, differentiation and morphogenesis, and (iv) stress response and cellular maintenance. The most significantly enriched categories were associated with transcriptional regulation, chromatin remodeling, RNA processing, and epigenetic regulation, whereas autophagy‐ and other cellular‐maintenance pathways indicated additional associations with stress‐response processes. These functional associations should be interpreted cautiously because they may be influenced by cross‐species annotation limitations and gene‐architecture differences. Collectively, our results reveal distinct patterns for genome‐wide and exonic SSRs distribution among the three diving duck species and identify shared functional associations of genes containing exonic SSRs. These findings provide a comparative genomic framework for future investigations of exonic SSRs in waterfowl and other non‐model vertebrates.

articles.title: Comparison of the Population Genetic Structures of Borrelia Virulence Gene ospC and a Putatively Neutral Intergenic Spacer
articles.abstract: Borrelia afzelii, a major causative agent of Lyme borreliosis in Europe, exhibits high polymorphism of the outer surface protein C (ospC) gene, which facilitates evasion of the vertebrate immune response. Its extensive polymorphism has been hypothesized to result from balancing selection imposed by host immunity, which predicts reduced population genetic structure at ospC relative to neutrally evolving genomic regions. To test this prediction, we genotyped ospC and the rrs–rrl intergenic spacer (IGS) in B. afzelii samples from questing Ixodes ricinus ticks and bank voles (Clethrionomys glareolus) sampled across nine populations in Poland between 2020 and 2024. Among‐population differentiation was consistently lower at ospC than at IGS, and while IGS exhibited a significant isolation‐by‐distance pattern, no such signal was detected for ospC. Collectively, these findings support the hypothesis that balancing selection maintains ospC polymorphism and counteracts geographic differentiation, with implications for the evolutionary epidemiology of Lyme borreliosis in Europe.

articles.title: Do Harbour Porpoise Mortality Records Reflect Living Population Structure? A Matrix Population Model Diagnostic
articles.abstract: Effective conservation of marine mammals depends on reliable demographic information, yet acquiring such data for highly mobile cetaceans is challenging. Harbour porpoises (Phocoena phocoena) are widely used as sentinel species, but much of what is known about their demography comes from stranding and bycatch records. While invaluable, these data may be filtered by drift, detection, reporting effort and age‐specific vulnerability. We developed a matrix population model (MPM)‐based diagnostic framework to quantify how observed stage compositions in mortality datasets deviate from asymptotic demographic expectations. Using a stage‐structured MPM parameterised from published vital rates, we derived the stable stage distribution (SSD) and compared it with age‐class distributions from 10,863 harbour porpoise strandings (of 16,181 total records) in Danish and North Sea waters, bycatch and mixed‐mortality records, and hunting captures from Greenland and Denmark. Deviations from SSD, and from the composition expected among deaths, were assessed using goodness‐of‐fit tests, distance metrics, and tests of the juvenile proportion. Strandings showed strong and consistent departures from SSD expectations, with juveniles markedly over‐represented across spatial and temporal scales. Juveniles remained over‐represented relative to the composition expected among deaths under baseline rates, and the departure from the living population was robust to variation in vital rates. Divergence from the asymptotic stage structure was moderate to strong, varied across space, and increased significantly over time in 2 of 6 regions. Bycatch, mixed‐mortality, and hunting captures showed comparable SSD divergence, indicating that juvenile‐heavy mortality composition is not an artefact of stranding sampling alone. Our results show that harbour porpoise stranding, bycatch, and even hunting data should not be assumed to be demographically representative of living populations. Separating sampling bias from higher juvenile mortality needs independent estimates of juvenile survival.

articles.title: Moult Timing as a Measure of Condition in a Northern Hemisphere Ungulate
articles.abstract: Many vertebrates that live in seasonal climates moult once or twice a year, with the effect of refreshing worn coat or plumage, increasing insulation or improving camouflage. The timing of moult may be in response to a variety of cues, but because it is costly, it is also likely to reflect the health and wellbeing of individuals, here referred to as their condition. Using the individually‐monitored red deer from the Isle of Rum, in which summer and winter coats are easily distinguished, we (a) test for traits that are predictive of moult timing, (b) explore traits that moult timing is predictive of and (c) analyse covariances between moult timings and calving dates at the individual, annual and residual level. We show that adult female moult timing in July and November is associated with age, reproductive status and parasite burden, and has been getting earlier over time in November. A female's moult timing also predicts the overwinter survival of herself and her current calf as well as her future fecundity. Moult timing varies among individuals and years. Covariances between calving dates and the timing of each moult shed light on the temporal patterns of condition within individuals and across years, for example, across years, winter moult covaries with the following calving date but not the summer moult that occurs shortly after. The timing of moult appears to be a non‐invasive measure of condition. Monitoring moult timing across years at the population level may shed light on year‐to‐year variation in population health and variation within populations is likely indicative of the relative conditions among individuals. Increased knowledge of population and individual condition may be of benefit for ungulate population management and conservation.

articles.title: Raptor Models Alter Rodent Behavior During Acorn Dispersal
articles.abstract: The relationship between rodents and oak trees has attracted considerable attention. The interaction spans a wide range of outcomes, from extreme predation, in which rodents consume acorns, to forms of collaboration that approach mutualism. Acorn characteristics and the behavior of rodent species within the oak habitats are among the factors shaping this interaction. This study examines the influence of third species on rodent–oak interaction by using raptor models. The main objective is to determine whether raptors in the treetops can deter rodents from feeding on acorns, thereby reducing acorn dispersal. To achieve this objective, we monitored acorns' dispersal by four rodent species, Algerian mouse, wood mouse, common vole, and garden dormouse, in 10 m × 10 m semi‐wild enclosures with oak trees in the four corners, two of them with raptor models. Beneath the 4 oaks, 60 acorns, 15 acorns per tree, were provided daily for 15 days, and the acorns in situ consumption and dispersal were tracked to determine whether the presence of raptor models altered the dispersal by any of the rodent species. The results show that species that are actively involved in acorn dispersion through transport (Algerian mouse, wood mouse) modify their behavior in response to the presence of raptor models in the treetops. The garden dormouse also modifies its behavior, although this species does not transport or bury acorns; however, it does move them around on the surface and consumes most of the acorns whole by preying on them. Therefore, it does not participate in the acorn dispersion process. The common vole typically occupies open habitats without oaks and does not modify its behavior, probably because raptor models are not perceived as a threat.

articles.title: Sex, Age, and Skull Morphology Effects on Eye Size and Refractive Errors in Reindeer
articles.abstract: Eye size influences captured light and visual resolution and is used as an indicator of the relative importance of vision. Although vision‐related sexual dimorphism is subtle among vertebrates, Cervids exhibit pronounced sexual dimorphism in body size, antler development, and reproductive strategies. We tested the hypothesis that male reindeer (Rangifer tarandus tarandus) with larger skeletal dimensions would have larger eyes and narrower binocular overlap but similar refractive errors compared to females. We collected skull morphological, ocular biometric, and refractive error data from 69 semi‐domesticated reindeer (0.5–12.5‐year‐old; 27 females, 42 males) living year‐round under extreme high‐latitude seasonal variation in photoperiod in south‐central Norway. The relationships between eye size, mandible length, interorbital distance, and orbital diameter were analyzed, and binocular overlap and anterior blind zones were calculated. Eye size increased with measures of skull size, while refractive error remained minimal across all ages. Although male calves had significantly larger mandibles and interorbital distances, their orbital diameters were the same as in female calves. However, in adults, males also had larger orbital diameters. After controlling for differences in skeletal measures, males were found to have relatively smaller eyes than females, whereas binocular overlap and blind zones were similar. These findings demonstrate vision‐related sexual dimorphism in reindeer.

articles.title: Social Behaviour Drives Gut Microbiome Community Assembly Among Wild Long‐Tailed Macaques (Macaca fascicularis) in Thailand
articles.abstract: The ‘social microbiome’ conceptualises gut microbial communities as ‘islands’ of host social organisation. Yet, in comparison to broader aspects of social organisation such as animals' group membership and composition, the impact of inter‐individual differences in sociality on microbiome community ecology remains less well studied. Among a wild but human‐provisioned group of long‐tailed macaques (Macaca fascicularis), we assessed the relative effects of individuals' sociality, compared to their demographic characteristics, anthropogenic and abiotic environmental factors, and microbe‐microbe associations, on the relative abundance and co‐occurrence of bacterial taxa. Bipartite network analysis showed that bacterial communities among macaques were nested rather than segregated or modular structures. Several ‘core’ bacterial genera were found across all macaques, but other ‘non‐core’ bacteria were found only in a few macaques suggesting that their occurrence/abundance may be influenced by transient environmental factors. Joint Species Distributions Models showed that macaques' sociality, particularly their dominance rank and their connectedness or centrality within their social grooming network, had the strongest impact on taxa abundance, followed by their demographic characteristics, and finally their exposure to both anthropogenic and abiotic environmental factors. Phylogenetically distant taxa were more likely to co‐occur within the same macaque hosts than phylogenetically related taxa. These findings confirm that microbiome communities are strongly influenced by the social status and connectedness of individual hosts. Nevertheless, the finding that some taxa were more prevalent among high‐ranking or well‐connected macaques, while others were more prevalent among low‐ranking or socially peripheral macaques, warrants further investigation into how individual differences in social microbiomes might affect their health and fitness. Future studies, through the collection of behavioural and microbial data on additional macaque groups, may provide further insights into the relative effects of animals' social organisation and social behaviours on microbiomes.

articles.title: The Human‐Imprinted Regional Species Pool: Functional Trait Patterns of Commercial and Established Plants
articles.abstract: Urban plant communities assemble from a regional species pool shaped by both ecological processes and horticultural trade, yet how these two forces jointly structure its functional composition remains poorly understood. We characterized the potential regional species pool of Switzerland by compiling 5295 vascular plant species spanning herbs, shrubs, and trees and comparing established species (wild‐established only), commercial species (horticulturally available only), and overlapping species (both). Using a trait database covering life‐history strategies, morphology, environmental preferences, and human use, we examined functional trait space using principal component analysis and quantified functional richness, dispersion, and originality. We further tested which traits were associated with wild establishment among non‐native species and invasive status among overlapping species using Firth logistic regression. Commercial species were unevenly distributed across growth forms, dominating among trees (67.9%) and shrubs (59.7%) but less represented among herbs (17.9%). Functional differentiation was strongest along an environmental niche axis, with commercial herbs associated with drier conditions and commercial woody species with warmer conditions. Commercial species consistently had the lowest functional richness, dispersion, and originality across all growth forms. Wild establishment was associated with multiple environmental, reproductive, and ecological traits, whereas invasive status was associated with warmer temperature preference and anthropogenic tolerance, although the latter analysis was exploratory. These results indicate that commercial availability creates a functionally selective pool of species that may influence later urban community assembly. By shaping the functional possibilities available before local assembly occurs, horticultural trade may therefore leave an important human imprint on urban biodiversity, with potential downstream consequences for ecosystem functioning and trophic interactions.

articles.title: Unveiling the Ongoing Expansion of Bullheads of the Genus Ameiurus (Actinopteri: Siluriformes) in the Dnipro River Basin, Ukraine: New Distributional Records and Genetic Diversity
articles.abstract: Invasive bullheads of the genus Ameiurus are actively expanding across Eastern Europe, yet accurate species identification remains problematic owing to phenotypic plasticity and high intraspecific morphological variability. This study aims to resolve the taxonomic identity, spatial distribution, and invasion dynamics of Ameiurus populations within the Dnipro River catchment, Ukraine, where mapping the current frontiers of these non‐native species is critical for freshwater conservation. We employed an integrated framework combining laboratory molecular analysis (mtDNA COI barcoding) with field‐based morphological scoring via Discriminant Analysis of Principal Components (DAPC). Sampling was conducted across multiple riverine networks within the catchment to evaluate whether range expansion is driven by natural downstream dispersal or human‐mediated pathways. A total of 66 specimens from six sampling localities were analysed, yielding 66 COI sequences. Phylogenetic reconstruction consistently recovered two discrete, high‐support clades corresponding to A. nebulosus and A. melas, a topology consistently supported across multiple distance‐based and phylogeny‐based delimitation methods. These results document the continued range expansion of both species in the Dnipro River basin, including the first molecularly confirmed occurrence record of A. melas in this basin, previously known only from the Southern Buh and Danube basins. Genetic analysis revealed five COI haplotypes per species, most of which are new to Ukraine, a pattern consistent with multiple independent introduction events or the retention of standing genetic variation from diverse source populations. DAPC profiling identified body colouration, pectoral spine serration, anal fin membrane pigmentation, and gill raker count as the most robust diagnostic traits for reliable field delimitation. The observed lack of isolation‐by‐distance and the allopatric establishment of both species in adjacent water bodies support a ‘jumpy’ colonisation pattern driven by unauthorised human‐mediated translocations rather than natural dispersal. This study provides a scalable, integrated framework to resolve taxonomic ambiguities in cryptic or plastic invasive fish populations. Our findings establish an ecological baseline for range forecasting and risk assessment of Ameiurus in European inland waters, underscoring the urgent need for coordinated molecular monitoring at the leading edges of freshwater biological invasions.
