Our findings reveal CHI3L2 as an important regulator of keratinocyte-driven lipid remodeling and inflammation in psoriasis, highlighting potential as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: MIF-CD74 orchestrates synovial macrophage metabolic-inflammatory reprogramming by ENO2 interaction to drive osteoarthritis pathogenesis
articles.abstract: Synovitis is a central driver of osteoarthritis (OA) progression, yet the cellular and molecular mechanisms sustaining inflammatory circuits in the synovium remain incompletely understood. Through integrative analysis of time-resolved single-cell RNA sequencing in murine synovium and spatial transcriptomics of human OA tissues, we identified a pathogenic CD74 + macrophage subset that expands in OA and localizes at the synovial-cartilage interface. This subset exhibits a proinflammatory, nonclassical polarization and displays a metabolic dependency on glycolysis. Multiomics and mechanistic studies revealed that CD74 interacts with the glycolytic enzyme enolase 2 (ENO2). This interaction orchestrates a feed-forward signaling axis wherein CD74/ENO2 facilitates the nuclear translocation of hypoxia-inducible factor 1-α (HIF-1α)/β-catenin dimers, which coactivate glycolytic and inflammatory gene programs, thereby sustaining a metabolically driven inflammatory state. Genetic ablation of CD74 in myeloid cells or its pharmacological blockade mitigated synovitis and cartilage degradation in murine OA models. To translate this axis therapeutically, we developed synovium-targeted cationic lipid nanoparticles decorated with MIF-mimetic peptides (PcLNPs) for the delivery of CD74 siRNA. Intra-articular administration of PcLNPs efficiently targeted CD74 + macrophages, attenuated their inflammatory and glycolytic phenotypes, and ameliorated murine OA progression in vivo. Our findings establish the CD74/ENO2/HIF-1α/β-catenin axis as a critical integrator of metabolic reprogramming and inflammation in OA synovitis and present a potential targeted nanotherapeutic strategy for disease modification.

articles.title: T cell–mediated depletion of intratumoral regulatory T cells using a CCR8xCD3 T cell–engaging bispecific antibody (TCB) promotes antitumor immunity in preclinical mouse models
articles.abstract: T cell–engaging bispecific antibodies (TCBs) have seen notable successes in hematologic malignancies, and emerging data demonstrate their potential for the treatment of solid tumors. Most oncology applications of TCBs have focused on targeting tumor cells via tumor-specific antigens; however, TCBs have been underutilized for strategic depletion of immunosuppressive cells in the TME. Regulatory T cells (T reg cells) play a crucial role in suppressing antitumor immune responses, making them an attractive target for immune-based therapies. T reg cells express several surface markers that can serve as potential targets for antibody-mediated depletion, including C-C chemokine receptor type 8 (CCR8), which is highly enriched on tumor-infiltrating T reg cells. Monoclonal antibody (mAb)–mediated T reg cell depletion relies on natural killer (NK) cells, which can be scarce in some solid tumors, whereas TCBs can broadly engage the T cell compartment by overwriting antigen specificity and redirecting potent T cell cytotoxicity against target cells. Here, we have developed a CCR8xCD3 TCB and show that it effectively depletes CCR8-expressing T reg cells in a T cell–mediated manner. CCR8xCD3 TCB led to the selective depletion of intratumoral T reg cells from human solid tumor samples in vitro and mediated inhibition of tumor growth in multiple syngeneic tumor models with variable levels of T cell infiltration alone or in combination with anti–PD-L1. In cynomolgus monkeys, CCR8xCD3 TCB was well tolerated without evidence of acute phase inflammation or cytokine release syndrome and led to effective and durable depletion of the CCR8-expressing subset of T reg cells.

articles.title: Cryo-EM structure of the Arabidopsis thaliana V-type ATPase
articles.abstract: Khamina, Wunsch et al. use a bacterial effector protein to isolate and determine the structure of V-ATPase from an important model plant. The structure reveals posttranslational modifications that are specific to the plant enzyme, and interactions with an activity-modulating protein similar to interactions described previously for mammalian and fungal V-ATPases.

articles.title: AI bots swamped UK government consultation on vape restrictions, analysis suggests
articles.abstract: An overwhelming proportion of responses to the UK government’s consultation on creating a smoke-free generation and restricting disposable vape sales were generated by AI bots, an analysis suggests.1The AI generated responses were mainly targeted at opposing restrictions on disposable vape sales.Researchers from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine and the University of Bath said that the number of AI responses—and the consistency of their opposition to government restrictions—“suggest a coordinated campaign” to swamp the consultation.The government consultation, which took place in 2023, sought public feedback on a range of proposals, including making it illegal to sell tobacco products to anyone born from 1 January 2009 and placing restrictions on vape packaging, presentation, and flavours.2The new analysis, published in the journal Tobacco Control,1 examined publicly available data and freedom of information requests.Its researchers noted several limitations to their findings, including their inability to independently verify the bot detection methods...

articles.title: AI recommends vastly more expensive treatment than physicians, analysis suggests
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems suggest medical tests and treatment plans that are more than three times as expensive as those recommended by doctors, a study has found.1A small head-to-head evaluation by Israeli and US researchers analysed how 24 AI systems responded to 200 real outpatient and emergency department clinical notes.These notes were sourced from MTSamples, a public collection of deidentified US format clinical notes contributed by practising clinicians.Each AI system received the notes as they were recorded by the treating physician. The AI then produced its own assessment and plan, which was compared with the physician’s plan documented in the original notes.Orders from both plans were priced at 2026 Medicare rates. New medicines were counted rather than priced.Publishing their findings in the New England Journal of Medicine,1 the researchers found that the primary reason AI treatment plans were more expensive was because the algorithms suggested more diagnostic tests, medications, and...

articles.title: Jackdaw: The false promises of another gas field
articles.abstract: Global temperatures will increase 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.1 What once seemed unthinkable is now undeniable. But how much global temperatures increase beyond 1.5°C is still up to us. With current policies, global warming is heading towards a 2.8°C increase within this century.1 The 2026 Planetary Health Check finds that seven of the nine planetary boundaries, our life support systems, have been breached.2This is the backdrop against which the UK government approved the Jackdaw gas field. While alarm bells are going off around the world, it gave the green light to more drilling for more fossil fuels—to more emissions, more harm, and more injustice.The government is selling this decision as an act of pragmatism: protecting jobs, supporting people through the cost of living crisis, and ensuring that homes are kept warm through the winter using locally sourced fossil fuels. But Jackdaw will have no meaningful effect on any of this. An...

articles.title: Management of chronic pain secondary to temporomandibular disorders: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised trials
articles.abstract: In this article by Liang Yao and colleagues (BMJ 2023;383:e076226, doi:10.1136/bmj-2023-076226, published 15 December 2023), errors in fig 3 and the data supplement have been corrected.In fig 3, an editorial error had led to minus signs being omitted from the upper 95% CI values for the mean differences in pain relief. In the data supplement, there had been errors in the 95% confidence intervals for the indirect evidence estimates for pain relief.These were reporting errors rather than errors in the underlying NMA models or estimates, and so these corrections do not change the NMA effect estimates, the GRADE certainty ratings, or the Guideline Panel’s recommendations arising from the review.

articles.title: Should doctors be on social media?
articles.abstract: Consultant geriatrician Elena Mucci had no idea what Instagram was before creating an account, on the advice of her trainees, at age 45. Five years later, she is still making short videos in which she shares the medical knowledge she has amassed over 25 years of clinical practice.Her magnetic social media presence has attracted 290 000 followers and even a couple of visits from presidents of African countries, who have flown to see her in her private clinic in Hastings.Speaking at a Royal Society of Medicine debate on whether being on social media is an advantage to doctors, Mucci said, “If you’re a doctor with all that knowledge, you need to share it. That knowledge is now consumed via social media.”Nearly one in four people in the UK reported turning to social media and artificial intelligence chatbots for health guidance, in a survey of 2000 people conducted by the health...

articles.title: Surgeon who put brandy in his coffee after botching operation is suspended for 12 months
articles.abstract: A consultant surgeon who abandoned an operation, carried on with another procedure when he should have stopped, and drank alcohol while on duty has been suspended from the medical register for 12 months.1Aleksandras Uzkalnis, who qualified in Lithuania in 1990, was a consultant in general surgery at University Hospital Lewisham in London when the events took place on 9 February 2024.A medical practitioners tribunal heard that patient C was undergoing a laparoscopic cholecystectomy performed by a surgical registrar, D, assisted by Uzkalnis. But the consultant decided to abandon the operation when only the camera port, one of the usual four ports required for the operation, had been inserted.He later told an investigation by Lewisham and Greenwich NHS Trust that he was unhappy with what he found in the abdominal cavity and believed that it would not be safe to continue the procedure.However, an expert witness, K, told the tribunal that...

articles.title: [Countdown] The 2026 report of the Lancet Countdown on health and climate change: a decade of escalating health harms and a decisive moment for all
articles.abstract: For the French, Arabic, Spanish, Brazilian-Portuguese and Mandarin translations of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

articles.title: Pazopanib alternating with bevacizumab in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to treatment: a multicentre, single-arm, phase 1/2 trial
articles.abstract: BackgroundVEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are considered the backbone for the treatment of metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. We hypothesise that the administration of bevacizumab during scheduled breaks in pazopanib (TKI) treatment can improve tolerability and prolong progression-free survival compared with historical controls.MethodsIn this single-arm, phase 1/2 trial in five US academic cancer centres, patients (aged ≥18 years) with histologically confirmed metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and adequate organ functions were included. The phase 1 portion included patients with up to one previous therapy with high-dose IL-2 or an anti-PD-1 compound alone or in combination with a CTLA-4 inhibitor. The phase 2 portion enrolled only patients with treatment-naive metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. The primary endpoint of phase 1 was to find the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). We tested a novel regimen using four dose levels: oral pazopanib (600 or 800 mg daily on days 1-28, followed by a 7 day break) alternating with intravenous bevacizumab (5, 7·5, or 10 mg/kg, one on day 36 and one on day 50) on a 10-week cycle in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to TKI treatment. The primary endpoint of phase 2 was median progression-free survival, assessed by a masked central statistician review. Dose selection (in patients who had completed 15 weeks) and activity (in patients who had completed one full 10-week cycle of the novel regimen) were analysed in the per-protocol population. Safety analyses included all patients who received any treatment. This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01684397) and is ongoing but closed to new participants.FindingsBetween Nov 21, 2012, and June 11, 2018, phase 1 enrolled 25 patients, with 18 patients evaluable for dose-limiting toxicity during the extended 15-week safety assessment period. The RP2D was established as pazopanib 800 mg daily (days 1-28) and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg on days 36 and 50 of a 10-week cycle. Between Jan 23, 2019, and Oct 19, 2023, phase 2 enrolled 53 patients, of whom 51 (including six from phase 1) were evaluable for activity and 59 were evaluable for safety. 36 (71%) patients were male and 15 (29%) were female, and 48 (94%) patients were White. 33 (65%) patients in phase 2 had favourable risk per the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium categories. After a median follow-up of 63·7 months (IQR 16·2-73·5), median progression-free survival was 24·8 months (95% CI 17·2-34·3). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were hypertension (20 [34%] of 59) and elevated aspartate aminotransferase (seven [12%]) and alanine aminotransferase (ten [17%]). Five (8%) patients discontinued the study for drug-related serious adverse events. No treatment-related deaths occurred.InterpretationThe phase 1 portion identified the safe RP2D. The phase 2 portion showed that this novel regimen has promising antitumour activity in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma in the predominantly favourable risk group who are naive to treatment. Phase 3 randomised controlled trial data are needed to confirm these findings.FundingThe Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center (RPCCC), US National Cancer Institute (NCI), Novartis.

articles.title: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus placebo plus enzalutamide in metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant (castration-resistant) prostate cancer (TALAPRO-2): a biomarker analysis of circulating tumour DNA and cells for prognosis and molecular profiling
articles.abstract: The TALAPRO-2 trial showed improved radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival with first-line talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus placebo plus enzalutamide in patients with metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer (APMR; also referred to as castration-resistant prostate cancer) unselected for homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene alterations treated. We aimed to assess HRR gene alteration status agreement between prospective solid tumour tissue and circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) testing, the potential complementary value of prospective and retrospective ctDNA testing, and the prognostic utility of baseline ctDNA burden, changes in ctDNA burden, and circulating tumour cell (CTC) reductions. In TALAPRO-2, a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, men aged 18 years or older (≥20 years in Japan) with asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic metastatic APMR prostate cancer and no previous life-prolonging systemic therapy for APMR disease were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive once daily, oral talazoparib 0·5 mg plus enzalutamide 160 mg or placebo plus enzalutamide and stratified by HRR gene alteration status and previous treatment for androgen pathway modulator-naive/sensitive disease. The sponsor, patients, and investigators were masked to allocation of talazoparib or placebo; enzalutamide was open label. In this exploratory analysis, HRR gene alteration status agreement was evaluated in the unselected intention-to-treat cohort between solid tumour tissue prospectively tested using a clinical trial assay based on FoundationOne CDx and retrospectively tested ctDNA samples, collected at screening and assessed using an assay based on FoundationOne Liquid CDx. Tumour burden was categorised as positive or negative (ctDNA tumour fraction detectable or not detectable). Reductions in CTCs, enumerated using CELLSEARCH, were defined as conversion (from five or more cells per 7·5 mL of blood to four or fewer cells per 7·5 mL of blood) or CTC0 (from one or more cells per 7·5 mL of blood to zero). Radiographic progression-free survival was assessed for patients with baseline ctDNA positivity (positive vs negative) and for patients with ctDNA conversion and CTC conversion and CTC0 at week 9 (and week 17 for CTC conversion and CTC0) by treatment group. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrial.gov, NCT03395197 and is active, not recruiting. Between Jan 7, 2019, and Sept 17, 2020, 805 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned (402 to talazoparib plus enzalutamide; 403 to placebo plus enzalutamide); median follow-up for radiographic progression-free survival was 24·9 months (IQR 21·9-30·2) for the talazoparib group and 24·6 months (14·4-30·2) for the placebo group. A high concordance in HRR gene alteration status was observed between results from prospectively tested solid tumour tissue samples and retrospectively tested screening ctDNA samples (reported for 739 [92%] of 805 enrolled patients), with 84% (421 of 501) agreement in patients evaluable as either HRR-deficient or HRR-non-deficient by both tests. Median radiographic progression-free survival for positive versus negative ctDNA burden was 21·0 months (95% CI 16·5-not reached [NR]) versus NR (NR-NR), respectively (hazard ratio [HR] 2·46; 95% CI 1·68-3·60; p<0·0001) with talazoparib plus enzalutamide, and 11·0 months (8·4-13·8) versus 33·2 months (30·3-NR), respectively (HR 4·03; 2·85-5·72; p<0·0001) with placebo plus enzalutamide. In both groups, week 9 conversion from positive to negative ctDNA was prognostic of improved radiographic progression-free survival versus remaining ctDNA positive. Patients remaining ctDNA negative had more favourable radiographic progression-free survival versus conversion from positive to negative ctDNA. CTC conversion and CTC0 at week 9 were prognostic for radiographic progression-free survival benefit in both groups.…

articles.title: From light perception to energy signaling: integrating carbon dynamics with the Tre6P–SnRK1–TOR growth–stress axis
articles.abstract: Plants growing in fluctuating environments require dynamic coordination between carbon availability and growth–stress decisions. Trehalose-6-phosphate (Tre6P), a sugar signal linked to sucrose status, helps coordinate these decisions by regulating SUCROSE NON-FERMENTING 1-RELATED KINASE 1 (SnRK1)- and TARGET OF RAPAMYCIN (TOR)-dependent growth programs. Here, we synthesize recent advances in photosynthetic carbon dynamics, carbon sensing, and Tre6P–SnRK1–TOR signaling, highlighting emerging regulatory layers including Class II TREHALOSE PHOSPHATE SYNTHASE proteins, SnRK1 compartmentalization, and stress-associated TOR regulation. We further discuss how different photosynthetic strategies of carbon fixation, including C3, C4, and crassulacean acid metabolism, as well as UV-B signaling through UV RESISTANCE LOCUS 8, influence carbon–energy signaling. Finally, we outline unresolved questions relevant to crop resilience under fluctuating environments.

articles.title: Exercise against cancer: recent advances and open questions
articles.abstract: More than a century after observations linking muscular activity to reduced cancer risk, exercise oncology has progressed from epidemiological association to interventional evidence. Large cohort studies associate physical activity with reduced cancer incidence and mortality, and a Phase 3 randomized trial now demonstrates cancer-specific survival benefits of structured exercise. In parallel, preclinical and emerging human studies provide mechanistic insight into how exercise may modulate tumor biology, including effects on immune surveillance, vascular function, metabolism, and systemic signaling. Despite these advances, gaps remain—notably, the limited integration of exercise variables into oncology trials and sparse mechanistic data from patients, particularly in pediatric cancers. This opinion article synthesizes recent clinical and mechanistic advances and outlines priorities for biologically informed integration of exercise into cancer research and the standard of care.

articles.title: Emerging roles of microtubules in directional cardiomyocyte remodeling
articles.abstract: Past research has long hinted at a connection between microtubules and the growth of the heart. Here, we highlight a new role for microtubules in directing cardiomyocyte hypertrophy by altering protein translation and intercellular adhesion and discuss how these findings illuminate open questions in cardiac remodeling.

articles.title: Mate preferences and the compatibility puzzle
articles.abstract: Researchers and laypeople commonly assume that romantic attraction depends, at least in part, on whether potential partners possess the traits that a person says they want. Yet recent studies suggest that such preference-matching effects (Preference × Trait statistical interactions) are often surprisingly small or even absent. Possible psychological explanations include (i) mate choice is multivariate, and so the matching effect for any given trait is heavily constrained, and (ii) traits permit flexible interpretations, in that the same trait can be interpreted differently depending on the partner to whom the trait belongs. Compatibility may derive not mainly from the matching of preferences and traits but rather from the way that two people recurrently extend and build upon shared positive experiences over time.

articles.title: What can machine learning discover about the nature of emotion?
articles.abstract: The science of emotion increasingly relies on machine learning (ML) in the hope of making objective discoveries that resolve century-long debates. We examine research strategies in two main research traditions and show how confirmation bias can arise when theory-based hypotheses are evaluated using theory-laden sampling strategies, model specifications, and inferences. Each tradition manifests its theoretical differences in its ML methods, and, therefore, ML methods cannot settle those differences. The reciprocal relationships between starting assumptions, findings, and conclusions illustrate that ML investigations of emotion, like all scientific investigations, are never free from human experience and beliefs; however, they can be made less biased through a theory-aware research strategy to generate more justified knowledge about emotion.

articles.title: Cell cycle-coupled CK1δ turnover, autoinhibition, and activity
articles.abstract: Casein kinase 1δ (CK1δ) is a ubiquitously expressed kinase involved in diverse cellular processes, including cell-cycle regulation. CK1δ activity is attenuated by (auto)phosphorylation. However, inhibitory phosphorylation is efficiently opposed by cellular phosphatases as CK1δ accumulates in its hypophosphorylated, active state. CK1δ is a target of the nuclear ubiquitin ligase APC/C-CDH1, yet the kinase is apparently stable. Thus, the physiological relevance of CK1δ (auto)phosphorylation, autoinhibition, and regulated turnover has remained unclear. Previously, we showed that CK1δ is dynamically regulated in a manner that is dependent on kinase activity, subcellular localization, and interaction with its binding partners, such as PER2 (Serrano et al., 2026). Here, we show that CK1δ activity and abundance are additionally coordinated in a cell cycle-dependent manner. During G1, assembled CK1δ kinase is stable while free active kinase is degraded. In S phase, unassembled CK1δ seems to be no longer degraded, likely to support functions in DNA damage signaling. Upon mitotic entry, the downregulation of phosphatases promotes CK1δ (auto)phosphorylation and consequent autoinhibition, thereby preserving a pool of kinase to rapidly re-establish the post-mitotic steady state.

articles.title: Loose coupling between Ca2+ channels and release sensors as a synaptic correlate of higher-order brain function
articles.abstract: In the mature neocortex, functionally distinct areas are built by the same archetypes of neurons, but depending on the area, these neurons and their synapses are engaged in very different functions, ranging from lower-order processing of sensory information to higher-order associations and cognitive functions. We found significant differences in the functional presynaptic nanoarchitectures of the same types of pyramidal neuron synapses, depending on whether they are located in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) or in the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) of mice. Mature synapses in PFC operated with loose microdomain coupling, as opposed to tight nanodomain coupling in S1. These differences were associated with significant differences in synaptic timing, efficacy, and plasticity between areas. Our data suggest that the mature neocortex uses tuning of synaptic topographies to specialize seemingly identical types of neurons for their required function. They suggest that microdomain coupling in pyramidal neuron synapses could be a presynaptic structure-function correlate of higher-order neocortical functions.

articles.title: Out-of-balance growth enables cost-free synthesis of the flagellum and other proteins in a single bacterium
articles.abstract: The cost of expressing unnecessary genes on growth has been explained at the population level through balanced growth assumptions. However, due to the high degree of stochasticity in growth and gene regulation, it remains unclear how classical growth laws derived from bulk measurements manifest at the level of individual cells. For example, flagellar gene expression, one of the most energy-intensive processes in Escherichia coli, is typically associated with reduced growth rates in bulk measurements. By contrast, we find at the single-cell level that a strikingly opposite behavior coexists: flagellar gene activity is associated with an increase in growth rate. We show that this apparent contradiction, reminiscent of Simpson’s paradox, results from examining in each cell instantaneous growth and gene expression without indiscriminately aggregating the single-cell data like in bulk measurements. We attribute this unrecognized behavior to out-of-balance growth boosts that temporarily offset the burden of flagellum production, likely driven by a surplus of growth factors inherited across cell division. Furthermore, we show that this non-intuitive relationship between growth and gene expression at the single-cell level is general, as we observe similar effects with synthetic systems driving the expression of fluorescent proteins downstream of constitutive promoters. Finally, we use a computational model to show that the inheritance of parental growth factors can explain the apparent contradiction and constitutes a general mechanism for mitigating the short-term cost of nonessential and biosynthetically demanding genes in the single cell.

articles.title: Plasticity associated with adoption of social roles in clown anemonefish
articles.abstract: Central questions of animal behavior are how individual phenotypes shape and how individual phenotypes are shaped by dominance hierarchies. Using clownfish (Amphiprion percula) as a model system, we investigated how individuals strategically modify their phenotype during hierarchy formation. We tested the overarching hypothesis that interactions among size- and age-matched rivals will lead to the emergence of social roles (dominant, subordinate, solitary), accompanied by divergence in four aspects of individual phenotypes: growth, feeding behavior, agonistic behaviors (aggression, submission), and gene expression. To test this, we created 30 replicates of juvenile clownfish, each comprising a size-matched pair housed together, and a solitary size-matched individual housed separately. Our results show that an individual’s social context shapes its growth trajectory through coordinated changes in feeding behavior, agonistic behaviors, and gene expression. Individuals emerging as dominant within pairs grew twice as much compared to those emerging as subordinates, while subordinate and solitary individuals showed comparable growth. Initially, paired individuals consumed more food per capita than solitary individuals, but this difference declined as size hierarchies became established. Agonistic behaviors also decreased over time among paired individuals as size differences emerged. Transcriptomic analyses revealed upregulation of conserved vertebrate growth pathways and ossification-related genes, and downregulation of satiety-associated genes, in dominant individuals compared to subordinates and solitaries. Here, we identify associations between changes in gene expression, growth, and feeding behavior regulation that reinforce social role differentiation during dominance hierarchy formation in clownfish. Our findings lay the foundation for a broader framework to explore the mechanisms underpinning strategic growth in social vertebrates.

articles.title: Structural insights into peptidoglycan hydrolysis by the FtsEX system in Escherichia coli during cell division
articles.abstract: Bacterial cell division relies on precise peptidoglycan (PG) remodeling, a process orchestrated by the FtsEX complex. Comprised of FtsE and FtsX, this complex collaborates with EnvC, a periplasmic lytic enzyme activator, to regulate septal PG hydrolysis by amidases like AmiB. While recent structural investigations, particularly of Pseudomonas aeruginosa FtsEX (PaeFtsEX), have shed light on complex interactions and proposed activation mechanisms, the structural intricacies governing PG degradation by the FtsEX complex and EnvC in Escherichia coli cytokinesis remain unexplored. In this study, we present a comprehensive biochemical and structural analysis of E. coli FtsEX complexes, unveiling a key role for ATP in complex stabilization that extends across bacterial species. Upon EnvC binding, ATPase activity markedly increases. High-resolution structures of EcoFtsEX, both in the presence and absence of EnvC, reveal a symmetrical conformation of EcoFtsEX capable of accommodating the inherent asymmetry of EnvC, mediated by flexible loops within the periplasmic domain. Our negative-staining imaging showcases an elongated EcoFtsEX/EnvC/AmiB complex reminiscent of the PaeFtsEX system. These findings collectively provide intricate insights into the regulation of PG cleavage by FtsEX in E. coli—a pivotal model system used in pilot genetic studies, suggesting a conserved mechanism for precise hydrolase activation in bacteria.

articles.title: Ultrasound neuromodulation hypotheses on the directionality of effects and community resource
articles.abstract: Low-intensity transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS) is a promising non-invasive technique for brain stimulation and focal neuromodulation. Research with humans and animal models has raised the possibility that TUS can be biased towards enhancing or suppressing neural function. Here, we first collate a set of hypotheses on the directionality of TUS effects and conduct an initial meta-analysis on available healthy human participant TUS studies reporting stimulation parameters and outcomes (n=47 studies, 52 experiments). In initial exploratory analyses with univariate tests, we find that parameters, such as the intensity and continuity of stimulation (duty cycle, DC) show statistical trends towards likely TUS neural enhancement or suppression of function. Machine-learning analyses were limited by the currently small sample size. Given that human TUS sample sizes are expected to increase, predictability on the directionality of TUS effects could improve if a database is available. Therefore, we establish an inTUS database and resource for the systematic reporting of TUS parameters and outcomes to assist in greater precision in TUS use for brain stimulation and neuromodulation. The paper concludes with a selective review of human clinical TUS studies illustrating how hypotheses on the directionality of TUS effects could be developed for empirical testing in the intended clinical application, not limited to the examples provided.

articles.title: A Two-Water-Assisted Deacylation Pathway in Class C β-Lactamase ACC-1 Revealed by High-Resolution Crystallography and QM/MM Calculations
articles.abstract: β-Lactam antibiotics are among the most widely prescribed antibacterial agents, yet their clinical efficacy is increasingly compromised by β-lactamase-mediated resistance. Class C β-lactamase ACC-1 hydrolyzes third-generation cephalosporins such as cefotaxime through a covalent acyl-enzyme intermediate, but the molecular basis of deacylation remains unresolved. Here, we report high-resolution synchrotron and room-temperature X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) crystal structures of the cefotaxime-acylated ACC-1. These structures reveal a previously unrecognized two-water configuration near the acyl center, comprising the previously proposed deacylating water, Wat1, and an additional ordered water molecule, Wat2, positioned at a Bürgi–Dunitz angle suitable for nucleophilic attack. Quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations identify a previously unrecognized two-water-assisted deacylation pathway in which the substrate C4-carboxylate and Wat1 cooperatively activate Wat2 as the nucleophilic deacylating water. This pathway exhibits a substantially lower activation free-energy barrier than the alternative substrate-assisted and Tyr150–Lys67 general-base pathways examined. Together, these findings revise the deacylation mechanism of class C ACC-1 β-lactamase by revealing how an ordered water network and the substrate C4 carboxylate can cooperate to promote acyl-enzyme hydrolysis. This atomic-level mechanism provides a foundation for rational design strategies aimed at developing β-lactam antibiotics and β-lactamase inhibitors that resist or disrupt enzymatic hydrolysis.

articles.title: Decoupled Water Electrolysis with an Air-Stable Zwitterionic Azo Mediator
articles.abstract: Decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) separates H2 and O2 evolution, improving safety and flexibility under intermittent renewable electricity, but requires durable, oxygen-tolerant redox mediators. Here we evaluate 4,4′-azo-bis(1-pyridinium-3-propane-sulfonate) (ABPS), a zwitterionic azo molecule, as an electron-coupled proton buffer for acidic DWE. Its azo/hydrazo core supports reversible two-electron/two-proton chemistry at 0.81 V vs RHE, while zwitterionic substituents provide high aqueous solubility and suppress crossover through low-cost sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) membranes. Reduced H2ABPS shows no detectable oxidation after 90 days in air or during >5 h of continuous pure-O2 bubbling. Symmetric flow-cell cycling over 1000 h yields a capacity-fade rate below 1% year–1. With commercial catalysts at room temperature, decoupled flow cells reach 1.2 A cm–2 and operate for >200 h at 500 mA cm–2 with near-quantitative Faradaic efficiencies while producing high-purity H2 and O2. These results establish zwitterionic azo chemistry as an oxygen-tolerant, durable platform for high-rate decoupled hydrogen production.

articles.title: Microphase-Engineered Homologous Ion-Exchange Layers for High-Current-Density Bipolar Membrane Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Bipolar membranes (BPMs) maintain separated acidic and alkaline environments via water dissociation at the junction, but high-current-density operation remains challenging because rapid hydrated H+/OH– migration away from the junction must be coupled with sufficient water replenishment toward it. A transport imbalance between these opposing processes causes interfacial dehydration and limits long-term operation. Here, we develop microphase-engineered homologous ion-exchange layers to balance this coupled transport. These layers are fabricated from homologous multiblock poly(biphenyl alkylene) ionomers sharing a common backbone and block architecture, promoting interlayer compatibility and interconnected ionic domains. The hydrated pathways accelerate water replenishment and ion transport, thereby maintaining a stably hydrated junction. The resulting BPM enables pure-water electrolysis at 2.11 V at 1000 mA cm–2 and sustains high-purity hydrogen production for over 1100 h at 500 mA cm–2. This work establishes molecularly engineered ion-exchange layers as an effective approach for improving mass transport in high-current-density BPM systems.

Impact of Unrestricted Artificial Intelligence Scribe Deployment in a Single Health System on Clinician Workload and Productivity
articles.abstract: BackgroundAmbient artificial intelligence (AI) medical scribes may reduce documentation burden and clinician burnout. Whether use intensity drives benefits remains uncertain.ObjectiveTo evaluate the association between AI scribe (Heidi) enrollment and documentation burden and whether changes differ by use intensity.DesignRetrospective quality improvement study using an interrupted time series (ITS) indexed on each clinician's enrollment month adjusted for patient demographics and visit complexity. A secondary 3-group ITS compared enrolled nonusers, low users, and high users.Setting14-hospital health system in Boston, Massachusetts.Participants902 outpatient clinicians enrolled in Heidi; 605 users and 297 enrolled nonusers.InterventionHeidi enrollment after system-wide implementation beginning January 2025.MeasurementsThe primary outcome was note-active time. Secondary outcomes included same-day and after-hours note closures, note length, and work relative value units (wRVUs).Results1 637 227 encounters had notes authored by enrolled clinicians between 1 July 2024 and 31 January 2026. Enrollment was associated with an immediate reduction in note-active time (-1.21 minutes [95% CI, -1.74 to -0.68 minutes]), with larger reductions among high users (-2.50 minutes [CI, -3.55 to -1.45 minutes]) than nonusers (difference, -2.20 minutes [CI, -3.46 to -0.95 minutes]) and low users (difference, -1.72 minutes [CI, -3.03 to -0.40 minutes]). High users had greater increases in note length than nonusers (difference, +170.90 characters [CI, 21.07 to 320.70 characters]) and low users (difference, +270.70 characters [CI, 131.04 to 410.36 characters]). No differences were observed in same-day closure, after-hours closure, or wRVUs.LimitationObservational design with potential unmeasured confounding; inability to distinguish AI-scribed from clinician-authored notes postenrollment.ConclusionHeidi enrollment was associated with reductions in documentation time and increases in note length, concentrated among high users. Enrollment was not associated with improvements in same-day, after-hours note closures, or wRVUs.Primary funding sourceNone.

articles.title: Laparoscopic Versus Open Liver Resection for Colorectal Liver Metastases
articles.abstract: BackgroundRandomized clinical trials (RCTs) have compared laparoscopic liver resection (LLR) and open liver resection (OLR) for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM); however, long-term outcomes and subgroup effects have not been comprehensively evaluated.PurposeTo compare postoperative and long-term oncologic outcomes after LLR versus OLR for CRLM using individual participant data from RCTs.Data sourcesPubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from database inception through March 2025 for RCTs comparing LLR and OLR for CRLM.Study selectionEligible studies were RCTs comparing LLR and OLR for CRLM.Data extractionIndividual participant data, including unpublished data, were obtained from trial investigators of all 4 published RCTs.Data synthesisAnalyses used a modified intention-to-treat approach and 1-stage individual participant data meta-analysis (IPDMA) with trial-adjusted regression models and g-computation to estimate standardized treatment effects across outcomes, with 95% CIs obtained by nonparametric bootstrap resampling. Prespecified subgroup analyses assessed heterogeneity of treatment effect for the primary outcome. A total of 761 patients were included (laparoscopic, n = 384; open, n = 377). Postoperative morbidity was lower in patients assigned to laparoscopic surgery compared with open surgery (19% vs. 27%). Among patients who received preoperative systemic therapy, morbidity did not differ between groups (25% vs. 24%). Ninety-day mortality was 1.8% after LLR and 0.8% after OLR. After a median follow-up of 93 months, overall survival and disease-free survival did not differ between groups.LimitationAnalyses were limited to variables available across all studies.ConclusionIn this IPDMA of all published RCTs in the field, LLR for CRLM was associated with lower postoperative morbidity than OLR, with similar long-term oncologic outcomes.Primary funding sourceNone. (PROSPERO: CRD42024502655).

articles.title: Obesity and Cancer Risk in Young Adults in Korea
articles.abstract: BackgroundObesity and early-onset cancer are both increasing among young adults, yet evidence remains limited.ObjectiveTo assess associations between obesity and early-onset cancer risk in young adults.DesignNationwide population-based cohort study.SettingKorean National Health Insurance Service database, 2009 to 2021.Patients6 313 338 adults aged 20 to 39 years without prior cancer, from a national health screening program.MeasurementsBody mass index (BMI) was categorized into 5 groups (underweight to class II obesity) according to Asian-specific criteria. The outcome was incident cancer.ResultsDuring a mean follow-up of 11.2 years, 151 893 cancer cases occurred. Ten-year cumulative incidence ranged from 1.84% (95% CI, 1.83% to 1.86%) in the normal-weight group to 2.24% (CI, 2.22% to 2.27%) in class I obesity and 2.62% (CI, 2.56% to 2.68%) in class II obesity, with absolute risk differences of 0.40% (CI, 0.39% to 0.41%) and 0.78% (CI, 0.73% to 0.82%). The relative association was more pronounced in men, and absolute risk differences were greater in women. In combined BMI-waist circumference analyses, people with class I obesity based on BMI and with abdominal obesity had higher 10-year cumulative incidence (2.45% [CI, 2.41% to 2.50%]) than those without abdominal obesity (2.13% [CI, 2.10% to 2.16%]), exceeding that of those with class II obesity without abdominal obesity (2.20% [CI, 2.03% to 2.36%]). The highest cumulative incidence was observed for thyroid, endometrial, and ovarian cancer. Obesity was not associated with higher risk for breast cancer diagnosed by age 50 years.LimitationsObservational design; nonrepresentative sample limited to screening participants; and unmeasured confounding, including smoking burden.ConclusionObesity in young Korean adults, measured by BMI and waist circumference, is associated with higher early-onset cancer risk persisting into midlife, with patterns varying by cancer type. Early weight management may be important for prevention.Primary funding sourceNone.

articles.abstract: Adeluwa et al. developed TFXcan, a framework that predicts personalized transcription factor binding from genotype data across ∼700 transcription-factor-tissue pairs. Applied to PrCa risk, TFXcan identified specific transcription factors and coordinated programs of transcription factors that drive the disease at risk loci.

articles.title: An in vivo T cell engager platform induces deep plasma cell depletion in autoimmune dry eye
articles.abstract: Ling et al. develop T-IDLESTCE, a T cell-targeted integration-deficient lentiviral vector that programs endogenous T cells to secrete TCEs in situ. TCE-secreting T cells infiltrate disease-relevant tissues, drive deep plasma cell depletion, and promote sustained ocular improvement in an autoimmune dry eye model.

articles.title: Escape from flatland: Strained-ring linchpins for 3D heterocyclic scaffolds in drug discovery
articles.abstract: Strained rings offer an escape from flat chemical space, enabling access to three-dimensional bridged heterocycles. This perspective examines two complementary strategies—introducing heteroatoms through reaction partners or embedding them within strained precursors—and links precursor design and activation mode to topology, stereochemistry, and substituent orientation. It highlights how heteroatom identity and placement tune molecular properties and outlines advances in stereocontrol, precursor accessibility, and medicinal-chemistry validation needed to make strain-release synthesis a practical tool for drug discovery.

articles.title: Photoinduced Charge Separation via Symmetry-Breaking
articles.abstract: Photoinduced symmetry-breaking charge separation (SB-CS) is a fundamental process in molecular photophysics that underpins energy and charge transport in reaction centers and organic, supramolecular, and hybrid materials. Despite extensive investigations across diverse systems, SB-CS is often described in system-specific terms, obscuring the underlying unifying principles. In this Review, we establish a coherent framework demonstrating that SB-CS can be understood within a multidimensional parameter space defined by electronic coupling, energetic driving force, and nuclear reorganization. We critically analyze how the interplay between locally excited and charge-transfer states governs charge separation and recombination dynamics, highlighting the existence of an optimal intermediate coupling regime that enables efficient symmetry-breaking while suppressing nonproductive decay pathways. By integrating insights from solution, solid-state, and single-molecule measurements, we show that environmental fluctuations and structural heterogeneity play a central role in driving charge localization rather than merely acting as spectators or perturbations. Importantly, we distinguish universal physical principles from system-specific manifestations, allowing the formulation of transferable design rules for achieving efficient and long-lived charge-separated states. Finally, we outline emerging directions toward predictive, data-driven models that link molecular structure to SB-CS dynamics, providing a foundation for the rational design of next-generation optoelectronic and energy-conversion materials.

articles.title: Ultrafast Nonlinear Vibrational Spectroscopy of Aqueous Solutions at Surfaces and in Heterogeneous Environments
articles.abstract: Water and aqueous electrolytes at surfaces, interfaces, and in confinement behave differently from the bulk, yet linear spectroscopy rarely combines the chemical specificity, surface selectivity, and temporal resolution needed to resolve electric double-layer formation, specific-ion adsorption, and hydration at interfaces and under nanoconfinement. This review assesses how ultrafast nonlinear vibrational spectroscopy, comprising two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy, vibrational sum-frequency generation (SFG), and time-resolved SFG, probes the hydrogen-bond network and the dynamics of interfacial water and electrolytes on femtosecond-to-picosecond timescales. We first establish vibrational benchmarks for bulk water and simple electrolytes, then treat soft aqueous boundaries, including air–water, hydrophobic and hydrophilic, lipid, surfactant, and nucleic acid interfaces. We next examine solid–liquid and electrochemical systems, spanning metal oxides, minerals, and field-induced effects, before turning to water and proton dynamics in nanoconfined geometries and complex architectures. Throughout, experimental results are set against theoretical and computational frameworks, from polarizable force fields to machine-learning potentials. Our aim is to identify which molecular-level features of interfacial water are now firmly established, where the prevailing mean-field description of the electric double layer breaks down, and which experiments would resolve the outstanding discrepancies.

articles.title: Bifunctional Electrocatalysts
Cation Radius Engineering of d10 Metal Hybrid Halides toward Coordination Modulation for Giant Optical Anisotropy
articles.abstract: Birefringent crystals are core materials for polarization modulation in optical devices, yet commercial crystals generally suffer from low birefringence values. In this work, three hybrid halide crystals, (C5H5NS)2ZnCl2, (C5H5NS)2CdCl2, and (C5H5NS)HgCl2, were successfully prepared by combining 4-mercaptopyridine unit with d10 metal chlorides to further modulate the metal coordination environments. For (C5H5NS)2ZnCl2 and (C5H5NS)2CdCl2, two π-conjugated units directly coordinate to one metal-centered tetrahedron, which further assembles into a one-dimensional structure via hydrogen-bond interactions. For (C5H5NS)HgCl2, two π-conjugated units coordinate to two metal-centered tetrahedra, forming the isolated (C5H5NS)2Hg2Cl4 dimer, and the complete crystal framework is stacked by intermolecular forces. The birefringence of the three compounds exhibits diversity with the variation of d10 metal ions. Notably, (C5H5NS)2CdCl2 sets records among cadmium-based hybrid halides with metal−halogen−organic functional groups. Structural analyses and theoretical calculations demonstrate that the birefringence of the three crystals is jointly contributed by the organic part and inorganic composition. This study verifies that modifying the coordination environment by tuning the ionic radii of metal center ions is an effective strategy for birefringence modulation and advances the research on hybrid halides for birefringent crystal applications.

articles.title: Dynamic Poly(disulfide) Interphase Enhances Ductility and Toughness of Covalent Adaptable Network Composite without Loss of Stiffness
articles.abstract: Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) offer recyclability and reprocessability, yet bond-exchange dynamics can reduce mechanical strength and toughness. Although the composite formation of CAN provides benefits in both aspectsstrengthening the CAN and adding recyclability to the compositeit still faces a stiffness−ductility trade-off that limits material usefulness. Here, we demonstrate a CAN composite design in which silica nanoparticle incorporation, combined with interfacial chemical structure, enhances ductility and toughness in a highly crosslinked matrix without compromising the high elastic modulus. Introducing poly(disulfide) dynamic covalent bonding chains into the network and at the filler interface significantly increases ductility, toughness, and stress at break. Together with a comparison to composites with permanent interfacial bonding, these results underscore the important role of interfacial chemistry. Based on these comparative experiments, the observed toughness enhancement is proposed to arise from energy dissipation via reorganization at the interphase through stress-activated disulfide exchange and network topological rearrangement. The resulting stress-responsive viscoelasticity enables stable deformation and allows CAN-based composites to overcome the stiffness−ductility trade-off.

articles.title: Heteroanionic Tuning of Cooperative Ta Off-Centering in Quasi-One-Dimensional CsTaS3− x Cl x Semiconductors
articles.abstract: The structural behavior of CsTaS3 was investigated alongside that of the new heteroanionic compound CsTaS2.16Cl0.84, synthesized via the reaction of Ta and S in a CsCl flux. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that both compounds are isostructural, crystallizing in the centrosymmetric hexagonal space group P63/mmc with split Ta positions along the face-sharing octahedral chain direction. Pair distribution function analysis of both compounds, supported by STEM imaging of CsTaS3, identifies the local intrachain displacement motif as cooperative Ta sliding rather than alternating Ta−Ta dimerization. While X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy (XANES) confirms the decrease of the average oxidation state in CsTaS2.16Cl0.84, the same structural distortion persists, albeit now with a reduced magnitude. Both materials are semiconducting, and Cl incorporation increases the band gap from ∼1.00 eV in CsTaS3 to ∼1.12 eV in the heteroanionic phase. Single-crystal detectors fabricated from CsTaS2.16Cl0.84 exhibit high resistivity, which effectively suppresses dark current and enhances signal-to-noise performance. These devices deliver an X-ray sensitivity of 7470 μC Gyair−1 cm−2, demonstrating efficient charge generation and collection under irradiation.

articles.title: Interplay of Synthesis, Structure and Thermoelectric Properties in Two Families of Silicide Zintl Phases Grown in Magnesium-Rich Flux
articles.abstract: Large crystals of metal silicide Zintl phases with general formula (Ca/Eu/Mg)2Si were grown from reactions of silicon with varying amounts of europium and calcium in magnesium/zinc flux. The Eu/Ca reactant ratio determined the structure type of the products. Calcium-rich reactions yielded Ca1−xEuxMgSi (0 < x < 0.7) compounds adopting the orthorhombic TiNiSi structure type in space group Pnma. Increasing europium content led to the prevalence of Eu8−yCayMg16Si12 (0 < y < 3.4) products with the hexagonal Ho5Ni19P12 structure type in space group P6̅2m. Single crystal X-ray diffraction studies indicate mixing of Zn on one Mg site in the hexagonal structures; thus, the formula can be expressed as Eu8−yCayMg16−αZnαSi12. Magnetic susceptibility data indicate europium is divalent in all of the compounds, with low-temperature magnetic ordering transitions. Density of states calculations show a pseudogap at the Fermi level for both structures, indicating semimetallic character; transport measurements indicate p-type behavior. Ca/Eu mixing and higher ratios of Eu2+ suppress lattice thermal conductivity in both structure types. In Ca1−xEuxMgSi, Eu-substitution lowers resistivity but yields minimal Seebeck enhancement; in Eu8−yCayMg16Si12 (Eu8−yCayMg16−αZnαSi12), Ca-substitution increases resistivity and markedly improves the Seebeck coefficient, with Eu7.59Ca0.41Mg15.62Zn0.36Si12 reaching S ≈ 150 μV K−1 at 300 K.

articles.title: Nonclassical Dihydrogen Bond-Directed Assembly of o -Carborane-Based Molecules into Macroscopic Architectures with Circularly Polarized Luminescence
articles.abstract: Hierarchical architectures are ubiquitous in nature; however, the bottom-up construction of multilevel chiral macroscopic assemblies from small organic molecules remains highly challenging. Herein, we report an unprecedented assembly strategy for constructing hierarchically organized particles (HOPs) through the co-assembly of achiral o-carborane-based molecules (C-1 and C-2) with chiral (R/S)-limonene. Intriguingly, C-1-(S)-limonene forms microscale cocoon-like superstructures, whereas C-1-(R)-limonene undergoes self-assembly into fibrous architectures that ultimately evolve into random aggregates at the micrometer scale. In contrast, C-2-(R/S)-limonene assembles into bowtie-shaped microarchitectures. Graph Theory (GT) analysis reveals structural complexity indices (CIs) of 5.5 and 54 for the C-1-(S)-limonene- and C-2-(S)-limonene-based HOPs, respectively, indicating significantly higher architectural complexity for the latter. These assemblies exhibit distinct circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) properties: C-1-(S)-limonene displays intense CPL emission at 504 nm with a high luminescence dissymmetry factor (glum) of +0.006, whereas C-2-(S)-limonene exhibits CPL emission at 560 nm with a glum value of +0.002. These results demonstrate that chirality signals are transferred across multiple length scales from the molecular level to macroscopic architectures. The observed structural divergence originates from the synergistic effects of nonclassical dihydrogen bonding (Bδ+−Hδ−···Hδ+−Cδ−) between achiral o-carborane derivatives and chiral limonene, together with molecular polarity and elasticity effects. This study establishes a paradigm for fabricating chiral o-carborane-based hierarchical aggregates with programmable architectures and tailored chiroptical properties.

articles.title: Progressive Fluorination-Controlled Steric Effects in Low-Dimensional Bismuth Bromides
articles.abstract: Although fluorination introduces tunable lattice rigidity and steric matching that influence molecular dynamics, the use of progressive fluorination as an effective method for structure−property tuning remains limited. Here, we report structural, thermal, dielectric, vibrational, and optical investigations of two members of zero-dimensional (0D) hybrid bismuth bromides with the general formula A3BiBr6, where A denotes 2,2-difluoroethylammonium and 2,2,2-trifluoroethylammonium cations. Differential scanning calorimetry reveals that the difluorinated compound undergoes a first-order phase transition at 184.3/177.5 K (heating/cooling), similar to the monofluorinated analogue, whereas its trifluorinated counterpart exhibits no structural phase transitions within the studied temperature range. A single-crystal X-ray diffraction study shows that the trifluorinated compound adopts trigonal symmetry (space group P3̅). In contrast, the difluorinated analogue crystallizes in the orthorhombic space group Pnnm at room temperature and transforms upon cooling into a monoclinic phase described by the P21/n space group. Temperature-dependent infrared and Raman spectroscopies indicate that the phase transition mechanism is governed by order−disorder processes. The noncovalent interaction calculations support that the F···F intermolecular interactions originate from sterically constrained packing rather than attractive interactions, contributing to dense crystal arrangement. Optical studies reveal that band gap energies correlate with octahedral deformation and level of fluorination. The difluorinated compound exhibits orange luminescence of excitonic origin, which is still observable at room temperature. The presented data demonstrate that degree of fluorination is a versatile design strategy for tuning dipolar degrees of freedom, intermolecular interactions, the strength of organic−inorganic coupling, and optical properties in hybrid halides.

articles.title: Reductive Electrodeposition of Cationic Polymer Networks for Conformal Permselective Interphases
articles.abstract: The integration of ultrathin and conformal interphases onto electrodes can lead to advanced electrochemical systems with control over the near-surface nanoenvironment impacting the double layer, electrode stability, reagent access, and solvation. However, the precise fabrication of nanometric interphases with tailored thickness and composition without blocking active surface sites is challenging, especially on porous application-relevant electrodes. Here, we report the reductive and self-limiting electrodeposition of polymer networks (EPoN) as a versatile and tunable method to uniformly coat non-planar and porous electrodes with physically adhered ultrathin functional polymer networks. The deposition chemistry is based on cathodically mediated methylpyridinium crosslinking and achieves the fabrication of polymer thin films on oxidation-sensitive catalytic metals. Our reductive EPoN process follows a self-limiting growth mechanism, yielding uniform and defect-correcting coatings with tunable nanometric thickness and charge density. The polymer network interphase is permselective, retaining molecular access to the functional surface, but modulates its permeation and activity based on charge and size, as demonstrated with a positively charged nanometric interphase as a functional barrier for regulating the hydrogen evolution reaction on copper. Our reductive EPoN strategy establishes a robust platform to tailor catalytic interphases for precise control over the electrochemical nanoenvironment.

articles.title: Structure-Directing Agents of Chaordic Materials Using High-Entropy Alloying
articles.abstract: For nearly a century, alloy design has been guided by the Hume-Rothery rules, which describe the conditions required for solid solution formation and have traditionally constrained the compositional space available to materials scientists. The emergence of high-entropy alloys fundamentally altered this paradigm by demonstrating that configurational entropy can stabilize compositions that would otherwise be thermodynamically unfavorable. Since their discovery, high-entropy concepts have expanded beyond metallic systems into ceramics, including oxides, carbides, silicides, nitrides, and borides, creating new opportunities to access unconventional chemistries and local atomic environments. This review examines how high-entropy alloying can be used to transcend classical alloying limitations and stabilize elements in coordination environments that are inaccessible in conventional materials. Particular emphasis is placed on high-entropy borides, where ordered boron frameworks provide a structural scaffold that accommodates chemically disparate elements while preserving phase stability. Recent examples, including Pt- and Si-containing high-entropy diborides, demonstrate how entropy stabilization enables the incorporation of elements that do not form stable binary diborides (MB2), resulting in unique electronic structures, bonding environments, and functional properties. More broadly, these systems illustrate how the interplay between disorder and local order can be leveraged to design next-generation materials beyond the boundaries imposed by traditional alloying rules.

articles.title: Symmetry-Broken Co3O4 via Site-Selective Pd Substitution for Bifunctional Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Spinel oxides generally show subpar activity for electrochemical water splitting because of low electronic conductivity, suboptimal adsorption energies, and poor operational stability. To overcome these limitations, Pd2+ is introduced to induce lattice strain in a metastable Co3O4 phase featuring off-centered cobalt and oxygen atoms. While pristine Co3O4 typically crystallizes in the centrosymmetric Fd3̅m space group, 1.2 at % Pd transforms it to the dominant non-centrosymmetric F4̅3m space group. This unconventional lattice contains two non-equivalent tetrahedral sites and one octahedral site. Pd2+ preferentially substitutes the Co1 atom at the (0, 0, 0) 4a tetrahedral position, with a relative stabilization of −1.02 eV. Pd2+-induced enhancement of the density of states near the Fermi level tunes the d-band center, while Co-to-Pd charge redistribution activates the otherwise less active tetrahedral site alongside the intrinsically active octahedral site, thereby enhancing alkaline water electrolysis. For oxygen and hydrogen evolution, this bifunctional catalyst delivers mass activities of 60.6 and 31.0 A/g and turnover frequencies of 0.32 and 0.28 H2 s−1 at 300 and 250 mV overpotentials, respectively. In a two-electrode configuration, it reaches 50 mA/cm2 at an iR-uncorrected cell voltage of 1.85 V, while at 200 mA/cm2, it produces 25.4 mL/h H2 at a cell voltage of 2.31 V.

articles.title: The AtomicLimits Database: Towards Artificial Intelligence as a Research Assistant for Atomic Layer Deposition and Etching
articles.abstract: The AtomicLimits ALD/ALE database is a community resource that catalogues atomic layer deposition (ALD) and atomic layer etching (ALE) processes reported in the literature. While widely used, it currently captures only a small fraction of the available information, with limited process information per entry, and relies on manual curation. As ALD/ALE process development grows in demand and complexity, with many interdependent parameters and increasingly sophisticated chemistries such as for multicomponent films, decades of experimental and simulation knowledge remain locked across publications, supplementary files, and lab notebooks. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and large language models (LLMs), offer a path to unlock this knowledge for data-driven analysis and process design, but realizing this potential depends on structured, machine-readable data. In this perspective, we propose a framework to evolve AtomicLimits into an AI-ready knowledge infrastructure that integrates literature-extracted, experimental, and simulation data through a community-defined schema, a structured template that specifies which data fields to capture and how to organize them. We outline the AI capabilities this enables, from structured querying to autonomous experimentation, and discuss the coordinated community effort required to realize this vision for the atomic-scale processing field.

articles.title: Unraveling the Correlation between Crystallite Orientation in Conjugated Polymer Thin Film and Charge Transport Properties
articles.abstract: Despite great progress in tailoring the molecular structures of donor−acceptor (D−A) copolymers, the ability to precisely tailor their solid-state chain packing and establish a comprehensive structure−property relationship remains a grand challenge. Here, three diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP)-based copolymers adjusting alkyl side chains with various lengths are developed to control their aggregation behavior in different solvents and the corresponding crystallite orientation in thin films, establishing the structure−charge -transport −property relationship and elucidating the underlying mechanism. Specifically, DPPs with longer side chains exhibit weaker solution aggregation, favoring the formation of a face-on orientation in as-cast films, where the face-on to edge-on orientation can be further achieved by strengthening their solution aggregation via changing the solvent from chloroform to chlorobenzene and xylene. Remarkably, by using a floating-film transfer method, the initially face-on crystallites in as-cast DPP films can be transformed into narrower distributed edge-on crystallites, resulting in the charge mobility being nearly tenfold higher than that of the corresponding as-cast sample. This study highlights how molecular engineering and processing strategies collaboratively guide the aggregation and packing of DPPs in the solution and solid state, offering key insights into the structure−processing−property relationship of D−A copolymers for high-performance optoelectronic devices.

articles.title: Unravelling the Role of Stacking Disorder on the Optoelectronic Properties of Zn3P2
articles.abstract: Zinc phosphide (Zn3P2) is a promising photovoltaic absorber for thin-film and flexible solar cells due to its earth-abundant composition and favourable optoelectronic properties. Recent advances in epitaxy have enabled the growth of high-quality Zn3P2 thin films despite the challenges posed by its incompatible lattice parameter and thermal expansion coefficient. However, Zn3P2 remains prone to intrinsic extended defects, such as rotated domains, that can limit device performance. Here, using (scanning) transmission electron microscopy, we identify a class of extended defects that appear as planar faults described by displacement vectors lying in the (001) plane. Within a pseudo-cubic description of Zn3P2, we establish a direct correspondence between planar faults and rotated domains, showing that both arise from the flexible ordering of vacant sites in the Zn sublattice. First-principles calculations reveal an extremely low planar-defect formation energy of 2.5 mJ m−2, demonstrating that these defects form at essentially negligible energetic cost, in excellent agreement with their high experimentally observed occurrence. Additional density functional theory calculations show that the studied intrinsic planar defects neither introduce mid-gap electronic states nor significantly perturb the local electrostatic potential, indicating that they are electronically benign. Our results suggest that any connection between the observed planar defects and a reduction in device performance must therefore involve indirect mechanisms, such as strain effects or interactions with other defects.
