Non-equilibrium fluctuations in the corrosion process
articles.abstract: Why does corrosion attack specific sites under some conditions but spread uniformly under others? Liang et al. combine real-time nanoscale imaging with atomistic simulations to show that corrosion reflects a competition between local structural heterogeneity and thermodynamic driving force. Near equilibrium, strained regions preferentially corrode and promote localized pitting; far from equilibrium, stronger driving forces overwhelm these local differences and produce rapid, uniform corrosion. The findings provide a framework for understanding and controlling localized material degradation.

articles.title: Polymer coordination enables alloying-free synthesis of stable α-FAPbI3 thick films for real-time X-ray imaging
articles.abstract: Stable α-FAPbI3 is promising for high-performance X-ray imaging but is difficult to produce without alloying. Here, polymer coordination with PVP enables stable, alloying-free α-FAPbI3 thick films by controlling crystallization and lattice strain. The resulting detectors combine high sensitivity, low-dose operation, and fast response, enabling high-resolution, real-time X-ray imaging.

articles.title: An AI‐based and coding‐free integration for forest Leaf Area Index calculation
articles.abstract: Seasonal and spatial variations in Leaf Area Index (LAI, or plant area index, PAI) are challenging to delineate in tropical forests because the changes are often too subtle to be reliably detected. Many existing DHP software tools offer one‐click processing of all images using auto‐threshold segmentation (e.g. HemispheR, HemiPy and Hemisfer), but they produce results with large discrepancies. Some software (e.g. CAN‐EYE) requires manual tuning of each image, making large‐scale analysis impractical. We analysed 19,044 images from four tropical forest subtypes and found that using coding‐free AI software to process hemispherical images can significantly improve the consistency of canopy‐sky segmentation, thereby improving the detection of temporal and spatial variation of PAI. The results show that replacing the auto‐threshold segmentation with AI substantially reduced inter‐software disagreement, with the mean inter‐software range for PAI decreasing from 4.31 to 1.19, and delineating correct seasonal and spatial patterns. CAN‐EYE could identify the correct seasonal patterns but produced less accurate results than the CAN‐EYE‐AI integrated approach due to subjective bias. The high consistency achieved after AI integration enables reliable cross‐site and temporal comparisons. As users can combine the AI segmentation with other DHP software, our integrated, affordable and coding‐free method offers wide applicability and high consistency of PAI measurements, facilitating the advancement of tropical forest monitoring and research.

articles.title: Every scientist a modeller? The promise and peril of AI‐assisted mechanistic models
articles.abstract: Mechanistic models, expressed as simulations that can be run and visualised, are a powerful way to understand biological and other systems. Building them, however, requires formulating mathematical or rule‐based descriptions and translating them into working code, skills that many ecologists and other disciplinary researchers do not have. Generative AI can now perform much of this translation, making mechanistic modelling accessible to researchers, educators and students previously excluded by its technical demands. But delegating this translation to AI also carries real risks: modelling assumptions can become hidden, plausible but incorrect code can pass unnoticed, and the skills and critical habits that model building once developed may never form. We examine the benefits and risks of using generative AI as a modelling companion at each stage of model development (conceptual specification, formalisation, implementation and exploration), drawing on recent experimental evidence on AI‐assisted learning and on a worked predator–prey example built with AI, with a rule‐based epidemic model as a parallel case. At each stage we identify where consequential decisions are silently delegated to the AI and set out practical mitigations that keep human judgement engaged without requiring the technical skills AI has made optional: specifying the conceptual model explicitly before engaging AI, having the AI translate its formalisation back into plain language, testing the implementation against outcomes known from domain knowledge and designing the interface to support interrogation. This new opportunity is substantial: researchers, educators and students who understand their systems but have never been able to build models of them are now able to explore these systems mechanistically, testing how components interact and how the system responds to conditions it has not yet experienced, questions that correlative approaches alone cannot answer. Used carelessly, AI risks eroding modelling skill for little lasting benefit, but used deliberately, in the ways set out here, it opens a new pathway to mechanistic understanding without removing the critical thinking the old technical barrier once enforced.

articles.title: Amyloid-mediated RNA uptake by sperm for embryonic delivery
articles.abstract: Semen carries extracellular RNA that shapes early embryonic development, but how it reaches sperm is unclear. Mallen et al. show that amyloid fibrils in seminal fluid bind RNA, enter sperm, and deliver their cargo to the zygote at fertilization, where chaperones release it for translation.

articles.title: Small genomes, big lessons: What viruses teach us about structure-based riboregulation
articles.abstract: Viral RNA genomes fold into networks of compact structures, so their RNA sequences do more than carry genetic code. Hann et al. review how viral RNA structures control viral gene expression, replication, and immune evasion, revealing viruses as simple model systems for regulatory principles that also shape human gene expression.

articles.title: The 9-1-1 complex protects ssDNA gaps in BRCA2-deficient cancer
articles.abstract: Grimsley et al. demonstrate that the 9-1-1 complex safeguards BRCA2-deficient cells from lethal ssDNA gap accumulation by suppressing PRIMPOL-dependent gap formation, restraining EXO1 degradation, and promoting POLζ-mediated filling. This identifies an ATR-independent 9-1-1 role in post-replicative repair and establishes gap length as a key determinant of repair pathway choice.

articles.title: A double debris disc around a white dwarf sculpted by two planetary bodies
articles.abstract: Many planetary systems survive the metamorphosis of their host stars into white dwarfs, as demonstrated by the detection of dusty circumstellar discs around these stellar remnants and chemical signatures of planetary debris in atmospheres of these stars. A small fraction of these circumstellar discs also contain gas, detected in the form of emission lines from various ionic transitions (most commonly the near-infrared Ca II triplet). All of the 21 known gas discs exhibit double-peaked line profiles characteristic of a rotating flat disc. The mechanism behind the generation of gas is still debated, but for at least one system it has been linked with the presence of a surviving planetesimal embedded within the dust disc. Here we report the discovery of WD J132800.85–145019.95, a new gas-disc system that exhibits quadruple-peaked instead of double-peaked line profiles. These emission lines originate from two separate gaseous rings extending from 0.14 R ⊙ to 0.34 R ⊙ and from 0.54 R ⊙ to 1.93 R ⊙ . We propose that this structure results from the presence of two distinct planetary bodies within these discs, ranging in size from a few kilometres to the size of Pluto. The detection this stable double-disc presents a new challenge for the current models of debris disc formation and evolution.

articles.title: Retention of primordial atmospheres through giant impacts
articles.abstract: Giant impacts help rocky planets retain hydrogen-rich atmospheres because accreted mass increases atmospheric gravitational binding more than collisional heating drives atmospheric loss. This may explain the bimodal radius distribution of exoplanets.

Enzymatic oxidative esterification with an unconventional regioselective control
articles.abstract: Regioselective esterification remains challenging, particularly when multiple alcohol groups with similar reactivity are present. Now it has been shown that aldehyde dehydrogenases can be engineered into oxidative ester synthases with programmable alcohol selectivity, enabling controlled ester bond formation through active-site remodelling.

articles.title: A CD4-lineage erythro–myeloid progenitor within the adult bone marrow defines an alternative pathway for macrophage generation
articles.abstract: Tissue-resident macrophages originate from distinct developmental sources, but their adult replenishment is thought to depend exclusively on circulating monocytes. Here we identify a previously unrecognized CD4-lineage erythro–myeloid progenitor (EMPROR) in the adult bone marrow that provides an alternative pathway for macrophage generation. EMPROR cells are phenotypically and transcriptionally distinct from hematopoietic stem cells, common myeloid progenitors and monocyte precursors, lacking Csf1r and Ccr2 while expressing Cd4 and Kit . Single-cell RNA sequencing, RNA velocity analysis and lineage assays reveal macrophage, neutrophil, megakaryocytic and erythroid potential. EMPROR cells generate perivascular and tumor-associated macrophages independently of CCR2-mediated monocyte recruitment and contribute to erythroid and granulocytic lineages under inflammatory and neoplastic conditions. Transcriptomic comparisons position EMPROR cells closest to embryonic erythro–myeloid progenitors, indicating the persistence of an embryonic-like program in adult bone marrow. These findings reveal an alternative pathway of adult myelopoiesis that sustains macrophage diversity beyond the classical monocyte lineage.

articles.title: The EMPROR’s new groove
articles.abstract: Two studies shed new light on macrophage origins. Perivascular macrophages derive from extraembryonic erythromyeloid progenitors arising at a newly discovered hematopoietic site at the maternal–fetal interface and a related population of adult bone marrow progenitors.

articles.title: The maternal–fetal interface is an early hematopoietic niche enriched in distinct erythro-myeloid progenitors
articles.abstract: Embryonic hematopoiesis is thought to occur exclusively in the extraembryonic yolk sac before hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) arise in the aorta–gonad–mesonephros region. Here we identify a previously unrecognized hematopoietic site at the maternal–fetal interface in mice, termed MIXER (Maternally Interfaced eXtraEmbRyonic) tissue, which develops contemporaneously with the yolk sac and exhibits robust hematopoietic activity. MIXER contains abundant hematopoietic precursors, including classical CSF1R + erythro-myeloid progenitors and a unique embryonic CD4 + CSF1R − Erythro-Myeloid PRogenitOR (eEMPROR) population. Lineage-tracing experiments demonstrate that eEMPROR cells contribute to select macrophage subpopulations during fetal development, primarily in the perivascular space. Notably, early human placental villi, before HSC emergence, also harbor CD4 + nucleated erythrocytes, indicating a conserved hematopoietic role for the maternal–fetal interface. These findings establish MIXER as an anatomically distinct niche for embryonic hematopoiesis and expand the developmental map of blood cell emergence in mammals.

articles.title: Chronic progressive demyelination induces a microglial state with lysosomal dysfunction
articles.abstract: Dysfunctional immune responses impair remyelination and contribute to neurodegeneration. While immune and metabolic responses to acute myelin injury are well characterized, myeloid cell adaptations to chronic myelin damage remain poorly understood. Here we performed a comparative analysis of genetic and toxic mouse models of acute and chronic demyelination, which identified a distinct microglial state associated with chronic demyelination, characterized by sustained pro-inflammatory activation, lysosomal lipid sequestration and reduced lipid droplet formation. Transcriptomics profiling further revealed a metabolic program marked by upregulated cholesterol synthesis and diminished sterol efflux. Treatment with a desmosterol mimetic possessing 24-dehydrocholesterol reductase inhibitor activity reversed this microglial state, attenuated pro-inflammatory signaling (including C-C Motif Chemokine Ligand 4 expression), reduced myelin damage and improved motor performance in a mouse model of leukodystrophy. Our findings uncover a pro-inflammatory microglial state characterized by lysosomal dysfunction and increased myelin reactivity, highlighting a novel therapeutic target for chronic demyelinating disorders.

articles.title: Microglial NUS1 deficiency drives dopaminergic neurodegeneration through intercellular iron dysregulation in Parkinson’s disease models
articles.abstract: Using cellular and mouse models, this study reports that deficiency of the Parkinson’s disease risk gene NUS1 in microglia disrupts intercellular iron homeostasis, leading to neuronal iron overload and dopaminergic neurodegeneration.

articles.title: A simple twist to altermagnetism
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional altermagnets hold promise for next-generation spintronics but remain difficult to synthesize. Now, altermagnetism has been observed in an orthogonally twisted van der Waals homostructure, opening possibilities for ultrathin devices.

articles.title: Curvature and cell mechanics control tissue organization
articles.abstract: Tissue geometry mechanically regulates cell behaviour across scales. Now, it can be predicted when cells switch from full adhesion to rapid partial detachment on curved surfaces.

articles.title: Three-dimensional cell morphology is mediated by curvature sensing and interfacial stress
articles.abstract: Cells adhering to micro-curved surfaces can exhibit either complete adhesion or partial interior detachment. This is now found to be determined by the balance between the cell contractile stress and the cell–substrate adhesion stress.

articles.title: Single-cell tumour phylogenetics
articles.abstract: Single-cell sequencing has transformed the study of tumour evolution by enabling high-resolution reconstruction of cancer phylogenies. This Review discusses the models, assumptions and computational approaches underlying single-cell tumour phylogeny inference, and it highlights emerging applications in cancer biology, patient stratification and evolutionary forecasting.

Viscosity variation in fluid flows across scales
articles.abstract: Although most treatments of fluid mechanics consider the fluid viscosity to be constant or uniform, many systems have a viscosity that varies in time or space. Examples arise in microbial habitats, in the ocean, and in Earth’s mantle. In this review, the authors explain how viscosity gradients occur in real systems, examine how these gradients lead to new phenomena at both low and high Reynolds number, and highlight open research questions.

articles.title: Advances in the management of renal cell carcinoma
articles.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is the most common form of kidney cancer, with 435 000 patients newly diagnosed worldwide each year. In addition to morphology and histology, molecular subtyping has advanced the diagnostic classification of RCC. Contemporary diagnosis relies on cross sectional imaging in the form of computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging and selective biopsy. For localised disease, nephrectomy remains the standard of care, with partial nephrectomy being an option for smaller tumours. Ablation or stereotactic radiation is appropriate for selected patients. Adjuvant pembrolizumab provides improved disease-free and overall survival in high risk clear cell RCC. In metastatic disease, the introduction of immune checkpoint inhibitor based combinations has extended overall survival, providing a durable response in some patients. Despite these advances, primary and secondary resistance, along with the lack of predictive and prognostic biomarkers, remain a challenge.

articles.title: Children bear brunt of NHS waiting times in England, report finds
articles.abstract: Tens of thousands of young people in England have been waiting more than a year for an NHS appointment, a report warns.1While waiting times for most adult services are improving overall, the opposite is happening in children’s services, the Care Quality Commission’s (CQC) annual state of care report showed. This contrast was sharpest in waiting times for community health services.While the report found that the number of adults waiting more than a year for an appointment had reduced, the number of young people waiting more than a year increased by 129% in the two years to March 2026.Most of those waits were for community paediatric services, including diagnosis of neurodevelopmental conditions such as autism and ADHD. Just a few weeks ago a major government backed review found that the process for diagnosing ADHD and autism in England needed a “fundamental shift” to ensure that children receive timely support.2The CQC said...

articles.title: [Articles] First-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in participants with mismatch repair-deficient advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer (KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15): interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial
articles.abstract: First-line pembrolizumab showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival, with lower frequency of overall and grade 3 or above treatment-related adverse events. The study did not compare pembrolizumab monotherapy with the current standard of care (immunotherapy plus chemotherapy).

articles.title: [Articles] Izalontamab brengitecan for HR+/HER2– breast cancer in China (PANKU-Breast01): a randomised, phase 3 trial
articles.abstract: Iza-bren showed a significant improvement in progression-free survival versus chemotherapy in patients with HR+/HER2– breast cancer previously treated with endocrine therapy, CDK4/6 inhibitors, and one or two lines of chemotherapy (including taxanes). The overall survival data were immature, and an overall survival benefit has not been established. These results suggest that iza-bren could be a new treatment option for this population in China; however, further evaluation of iza-bren in global populations and in earlier lines of therapy for HER2-negative breast cancer is warranted.

articles.title: [Articles] Izalontamab brengitecan versus platinum-based chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancer after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PANKU-Lung01): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China
articles.abstract: In participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR TKIs, iza-bren significantly prolonged progression-free survival, although treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were more frequent than with chemotherapy. To our knowledge, these findings provide the first phase 3 evidence for a bispecific antibody–drug conjugate and support iza-bren as a potential treatment option in this population.

articles.title: [Articles] Ruzaltatug rezetecan versus chemotherapy for EGFR-mutated advanced non-small-cell lung cancer progressing after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy (HERON-Lung01): interim analysis of a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China
articles.abstract: Ruzaltatug rezetecan significantly prolonged PFS compared with chemotherapy, with a manageable safety profile, in EGFR-TKI-resistant, EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC. These data support ruzaltatug rezetecan as a potential treatment option in this setting.

articles.title: [Articles] Sacituzumab tirumotecan versus treatment of physician's choice in previously treated endometrial cancer (TroFuse-005/ENGOT-en23/GOG-3095): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial
articles.abstract: Sac-TMT significantly improved progression-free survival and overall survival versus TPC in patients with advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. These findings support sac-TMT as a new standard of care for patients with endometrial cancer who have received chemotherapy and immunotherapy and have few effective treatment options.

articles.title: [Comment] Multiple standards of care in non-small-cell lung cancer after EGFR-TKI therapy: progress, fragmentation, or inevitability?
articles.abstract: The treatment landscape of EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer harbouring exon 19 deletion or L858R mutations has advanced remarkably over the past two decades. Although acquired resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) is inevitable in most patients, novel compounds such as bispecific antibodies and antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) have expanded the armamentarium of options after EGFR-TKI therapy. Following the global MARIPOSA-2 trial that showed superior progression-free survival (PFS) of amivantamab plus platinum–pemetrexed chemotherapy over platinum–pemetrexed chemotherapy alone in patients who have progressed on osimertinib,1 this is the second-line option preferred by major guidelines including the National Comprehensive Cancer Network and the European Society for Medical Oncology.

articles.title: Alison Berner: Connecting oncology and gender medicine
Assessment of comprehensiveness of national cancer control plans using a multiagent artificial intelligence model: a global analysis
articles.abstract: BackgroundNational cancer control plans (NCCPs) vary in scope and comprehensiveness, yet expert-led review is resource intensive and limits cross-country comparability. We aimed to assess NCCP comprehensiveness across 50 countries using the policy reasoning integrated sequential model (PRISM), a validated multiagent artificial intelligence (AI) system.MethodsWe identified the most recent national NCCP for each country from the International Cancer Control Partnership repository, the WHO Noncommunicable Disease Document Repository, and government websites; sub-national plans, broader non-communicable disease or health-sector strategies, drafts, and superseded versions were excluded. We developed an analytical framework of 12 elements and 76 sub-elements, aligned with WHO, International Cancer Control Partnership, and Union for International Cancer Control guidance and validated it through a modified two-stage Delphi process (online survey of 67 experts; triangulation workshop with 31 participants). PRISM comprised document ingestion (Qwen2.5-VL-72B), policy analysis with retrieval-augmented generation (Llama 4 Scout, 109B), and semantic quality assurance. PRISM was validated against masked dual-expert ratings for six purposely selected NCCPs, then applied to all NCCPs. Scores were normalised to 0-5 and medians compared across World Bank income group and WHO region.FindingsWe identified 50 NCCPs that met the inclusion criteria. Median overall comprehensiveness was 2·78 (IQR 2·25-3·09), with high comprehensiveness classified as 4·0-5·0, moderate as 2·0-3·9, and low as 0-1·9. Europe (2·96; 2·78-3·35) and lower-middle-income countries (2·97; 2·48-3·15) had the highest medians; the western Pacific (2·21; 1·78-2·87) and low-income countries (2·05; 1·94-2·22) had the lowest. Element-level medians were highest for implementation (4·17; 3·54-4·38), health services (3·89; 2·63-4·19), and governance and organisation (3·67; 3·35-3·98), and lowest for financing (1·88; 1·00-2·69), outcomes (1·83; 1·33-2·33), and threats (2·19; 1·72-2·34). Financing showed the largest gaps-only five of eleven financing sub-elements had median scores of 1·0 or less.InterpretationOur analysis suggests that NCCP comprehensiveness varies substantially between countries with consistent weaknesses in financing, outcome measurement, and contextual analysis. A shared health systems framework and scalable AI appraisal tools, such as PRISM, could support more complete, comparable, and actionable plans to strengthen cancer control globally by providing the possibility for rapid analysis of comprehensiveness of NCCPs and generation of timely, achievable, and evidence-informed, context-specific plans that use the latest data.FundingHarvard University.

Curative-intent management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma: an evidence-based consensus guideline from the International Collaborating Oncology Organisations
articles.abstract: Patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma were historically deemed incurable and treated with palliative intent. Emergence of potent systemic therapy in combination with local treatment for both locoregional and metastatic diseases has enabled long-term survival in some patients. This international guideline was developed through consensus-building by 54 experts from 46 centres across 18 countries or regions and endorsed by 17 oncology organisations. 32 recommendations across seven clinical domains were formulated, including 29 strong (≥80% agreement [consensus] or high quality of evidence) and three conditional recommendations (67-79% agreement). We recommend that curative-intent treatment should be offered to medically fit patients with no more than three metastatic lesions in two or fewer organs at baseline or following response to systemic therapy; multimodality treatment (comprising immunochemotherapy, locoregional radiotherapy, metastasis-directed therapy, and maintenance therapy) is recommended. This guideline provides a practical framework for standardisation of clinical management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma and identification of key evidence gaps for future research.

articles.title: Development of the Children's Oncology Group long-term follow-up guideline for cancer genetics evaluation in childhood cancer survivors
articles.abstract: Up to 12% of childhood cancer survivors have an underlying cancer predisposition syndrome (CPS). As a result, these childhood cancer survivors are at increased risk for developing and succumbing to subsequent malignant neoplasms. Identifying childhood cancer survivors with CPS is essential to improving overall outcomes by informing tailored approaches to cancer screening, treatment, and, for some, risk-reducing interventions. Despite these potential benefits, it is often unclear which childhood cancer survivors warrant referral for genetic counselling and germline genetic testing. Using an evidence-based approach, a standardised guideline for referral for cancer genetics evaluation of childhood cancer survivors at high risk of having a CPS was developed and incorporated into the Children's Oncology Group Long-Term Follow-Up Guidelines for Survivors of Childhood, Adolescent, and Young Adult Cancers. This Policy Review details the importance, development, and anticipated impact of this new guideline. Raising awareness of this guideline is crucial to enhancing the integration of genetics into survivorship care and improving health outcomes for childhood cancer survivors with CPS.

Zamtocabtagene autoleucel, a tandem CD20–CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy, for second line treatment of large B-cell lymphoma in patients ineligible for transplantation (DALY 2-EU): primary analysis of an open-label, multicentre, randomised phase 2 study
articles.abstract: BackgroundAnti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy is the standard second-line treatment for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. However, there is no evidence from randomised controlled trials in patients ineligible for transplantation. To address this gap, we compared zamtocabtagene autoleucel (zamto-cel), a CAR T-cell therapy directed at CD20 and CD19, with rituximab-gemcitabine-oxaliplatin (R-GemOx) chemoimmunotherapy in patients ineligible for transplantation with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma.MethodsDALY 2-EU is an open-label, multicentre, randomised, phase 2 trial conducted at 45 centres across 12 countries in Europe. Eligible patients were adults (aged ≥18 years) with second-line relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma confirmed histologically who were ineligible for transplantation and had received first-line chemoimmunotherapy containing a combination of an anthracycline-based regimen and an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, with Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status score of 2 or less. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to zamto-cel (single intravenous infusion of 2·5 × 106 fresh (ie, non-cryopreserved) CAR T-cells per kg, capped at 100 kg, produced in a closed automated system) or R-GemOx (rituximab [375 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1], gemcitabine [1000 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 or 2], and oxaliplatin [100 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 or 2] administered for up to eight 14-day cycles). Randomisation was done with an interactive web response system and stratified by age, gender, lactate dehydrogenase, International Prognostic Index, histology, time to relapse after the start of first-line therapy, and country. The primary endpoint was event-free survival assessed by a masked independent review committee and compared all patients randomly assigned to the zamto-cel and R-GemOx groups using a one-sided log-rank test. Safety was assessed in all patients who received study treatment. This ongoing trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04844866).FindingsBetween Oct 14, 2021, and Jul 16, 2024, 219 patients were screened and 160 were randomly assigned to zamto-cel (n=82) and R-GemOx (n=78). The median age was 74·0 years (IQR 70·5-77·0). Patients were predominantly male (100 [63%] of 160 were men and 60 [38%] women) and White (91 [57%]), with race not reported for 64 (40%). Median vein-to-vein time for zamto-cel was 15 days (IQR 15-16). With a median follow-up of 17·0 months (IQR 9·0-22·8), event-free survival was longer in the zamto-cel group than in the R-GemOx group (6·21 months [95% CI 3·84-13·77] vs 2·53 months [1·97-3·35]; HR 0·39 [95% CI 0·27-0·58]; pInterpretationThe risk-benefit ratio observed in the DALY 2-EU study supports consideration of zamto-cel as a second-line standard treatment option for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma who are ineligible for transplantation.FundingMiltenyi Biomedicine.

Genetic canalization of nutrient resorption in the widespread grass Phragmites australis under salt stress
articles.abstract: Nutrient resorption is a key plant strategy for nutrient conservation, yet whether it responds plastically to non-nutrient stressors such as salinity remains unresolved. Using a common garden experiment with 110 genotypes of the cosmopolitan grass Phragmites australis, we first established that the imposed salinity treatment induced strong multilevel stress responses: above-ground biomass declined by >60%, sodium accumulated three- to fivefold across all leaf stages, and 484 metabolites showed significant differential accumulation, including canonical markers of osmotic and oxidative stress. Against this backdrop of confirmed stress, we found that nutrient resorption efficiency (NuRE) remained largely unaffected by salinity. Instead, NuRE was strongly correlated with phylogeographic lineage, ecotype, and latitude of origin, demonstrating evolutionary canalization rather than short-term acclimation. Element-specific regulatory patterns were also evident: while phosphorus resorption followed concentration-dependent control regardless of stress, nitrogen control was disrupted under salinity, and potassium resorption showed no such dependence. Our findings reveal that intraspecific variation in nutrient resorption is predominantly shaped by historical adaptation and geographic context, not by plasticity to salinity. This genetic canalization of a key functional trait implies that predictions of nutrient cycling under global change must account for the phylogeographic composition of plant populations.

articles.title: Heterogeneous responses to embryonic critical period perturbations within the Drosophila larval locomotor circuit
articles.abstract: As developing neural circuits become functional, they undergo a phase of heightened plasticity that facilitates network tuning in response to intrinsic and/or extrinsic stimuli. These developmental windows are termed critical periods (CPs) because perturbations during but not outside the CP can lead to lasting changes, such as the formation of sub-optimal or unstable networks. How separate but connected elements within a network might respond differently to a CP perturbation is not well understood. To study this, we used the locomotor network of the Drosophila larva as a model and heat stress as a CP stimulus that has ecological relevance. When embryos experienced heat stress, the subsequent development of their locomotor network was changed, creating larvae with reduced crawling speed and decreased network stability. Developing body wall muscles and central neurons are sensitive to heat stress perturbations during distinct, consecutive phases of embryogenesis. Within the CNS, transient embryonic CP perturbation leads to increased synaptic drive from premotor interneurons to motoneurons, which in turn adopt reduced excitability. In contrast, the peripheral neuromuscular junction maintains normal synaptic transmission, despite significant structural changes. Thus, connected elements respond differentially to a CP perturbation, suggesting a sequence, or hierarchy of network adjustment during the CP.

articles.title: Alicyclic Lewis Bases Enable 100 °C-Processed α-FAPbI3 Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Formamidinium lead iodide (α-FAPbI3) perovskite, despite its ideal bandgap, requires high-temperature (≥150 °C) annealing for the δ-to-α phase transformation, hindering its application in low-temperature processed inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), particularly on flexible substrates. Herein, we demonstrate that the alicyclic Lewis base caprolactam (CPL) effectively drives the complete δ-to-α phase transformation of FAPbI3 at a reduced temperature of 100 °C. Experiments and theoretical calculations reveal that CPL lowers the phase transition energy barrier and retards crystallization kinetics via strong Pb2+ coordination and controlled desorption. This strategy yields highly crystalline, fully phase-converted α-FAPbI3 films with improved morphology, reduced defect densities, and enhanced optoelectronic properties. Consequently, CPL-modified inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.64% with good operational stability. The low-temperature processability also enables high-performance flexible PSCs with a PCE of 23.73%. This work presents an additive engineering approach for realizing efficient and stable α-FAPbI3 PSCs through low-temperature manufacturing.

articles.title: Dual Functions of Halogen-Bonding Molecules for Stabilizing Ultra-wide Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) metal halide perovskite solar cells are essential for multi-junction solar cells with higher power conversion efficiency (PCE) potentials. In this work, we report the dual functions of 5-iodoisophthalic acid (I-BDC) to suppress phase segregation and uncoordinated Pb2+ related defects to enhance UWBG perovskite cell performance and stability. An I-BDC incorporated 1.95 eV perovskite film exhibited stable photoluminescence after 120 min of illumination. The best I-BDC cell achieved a certified reverse scan PCE of 16.5%, the highest for 1.95 eV perovskite cells to date. These UWBG perovskite solar cells are the most stable reported to date, with one encapsulated device retaining 90% of its initial PCE after 500 h of maximum power point tracking at ∼40 °C and another retaining 95% of its initial PCE after 206 thermal cycles (–40 ↔ 85 °C), passing the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 61215 testing protocols at the cell level.

articles.title: Making 1000 Wh/kg LiNiO2 Cathode Nearly Strain-Free by Complex-Concentrated Doping
articles.abstract: High-energy batteries require cathodes with greater capacity and specific energy. Ni-rich-layered oxides approach the performance limit of LiNiO2 (LNO), yet its practical use is hindered by severe chemomechanical degradation. Near 4.2 V, the H2-H3/H4 transition drives substantial c-axis contraction, volume shrinkage, O1 formation, oxygen loss, and rapid capacity decay. Here, we show that only 5% cobalt-free complex concentrated doping stabilizes LNO without sacrificing energy density. The modified LNO reduces c-axis strain from 7.4 to 2.1%, exhibits near-zero-strain behavior, and delivers 258 mAh•g–1 and 973 Wh•kg–1. In pouch cells, it retains 80% capacity after 1800 cycles and shows markedly improved thermal stability. These results demonstrate that complex-concentrated doping at low dopant loading can suppress strain and phase transformations at the full-Ni limit, providing a broadly applicable strategy for stabilizing high-energy intercalation electrodes while preserving their intrinsic capacity and specific energy during prolonged electrochemical cycling.

articles.title: rGO-MXene 2D Interfacial Engineering for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability of Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules
articles.abstract: In this work, we report an innovative interface engineering strategy combining bidirectional chemical anchoring and electronic bridging via a 2D reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and MXene conductive network. This hierarchical 2D structure suppresses the aggregation and stacking of single-layer MXene nanosheets while mutually compensating for individual charge transport limitations. Specifically, the abundant functional groups passivate interfacial defects (Pb2+ and I–) and bond with the PCBM layer via coordination, hydrogen bonding and π–π interactions. This synergistic architecture lowers the electron energy offset. Consequently, PSCs incorporating the rGO-MXene interlayer achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.96% (certified 25.05%) and retain 96.43% of initial efficiency after 1000 h in ambient air. Furthermore, 10 × 10 cm2 large-area PSM yields a high PCE of 20.25%, maintaining 96.05% of initial efficiency under maximum power point tracking for 963 h.

articles.title: Multi-element co-addition achieves ultrahigh strength in a ductile Ti2AlNb alloy from room temperature to 750 °C
A systematic review of deforestation outcomes in potential other effective area‐based conservation measures across Latin America
articles.abstract: Recognizing conservation contributions from areas outside protected areas (PAs), including other effective area‐based conservation measures (OECMs), is increasingly central to meeting global biodiversity targets. However, little is known about which areas could qualify as OECMs and whether they support forest conservation. Focusing on Latin America, we conducted a systematic literature review following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta‐Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines synthesizing 93 peer‐reviewed studies published through 2024 that assess the effectiveness of OECMs outside formal PA systems in reducing deforestation. First, we identified and classified area‐based measures that may qualify as potential OECMs into six types based on their conservation objectives and characteristics: strict biodiversity conservation areas, set‐aside areas for ecosystem services, Indigenous peoples’ territories, local communities’ territories, other managed sustainable‐use areas, and ancillary conservation areas. Second, we synthesized the available evidence on their effectiveness in reducing deforestation. Indigenous people's territories were the most frequently evaluated, whereas strict biodiversity conservation areas have received relatively little attention. Methodologically, most evidence relied on nonexperimental comparisons of forest‐cover trends; quasi‐experimental designs were less common but provide stronger causal inference of conservation effectiveness. Disaggregating outcomes by comparator type revealed important patterns: Indigenous territories most consistently showed reduced deforestation relative to both PAs and non‐PAs, whereas local communities’ territories showed more favorable outcomes relative to non‐PAs than to PAs. Set‐aside areas for ecosystem services showed predominantly negative outcomes, largely reflecting weak enforcement. Despite this evidence base, very few of these areas have been formally recognized as OECMs, highlighting a disconnect between available research and reporting under the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. Bridging this gap will require stronger causal evidence, broader geographic coverage, and inclusive recognition processes that account for the governance rights of those who manage these territories. Una revisión sistemática de los resultados de deforestación en otras medidas potenciales de la conservación basada en el área en América Latina Resumen Reconocer las contribuciones a la conservación procedentes de zonas ajenas a las áreas protegidas (AP), incluidas otras medidas de conservación basadas en el territorio (OECM), es cada vez más fundamental para alcanzar los objetivos mundiales en materia de biodiversidad. Sin embargo, se sabe poco sobre qué zonas podrían considerarse OECM y si contribuyen a la conservación de los bosques. Nos enfocamos en América Latina para llevar a cabo una revisión bibliográfica sistemática según las directrices de los Elementos Preferidos para la Elaboración de Informes de Revisiones Sistemáticas y Metaanálisis (PRISMA), en la que se sintetizan 93 estudios revisados por pares publicados hasta 2024 que evalúan la eficacia de las OECM fuera de los sistemas formales de áreas protegidas para reducir la deforestación. En primer lugar, identificamos y clasificamos las medidas basadas en áreas que podrían considerarse OECM potenciales en seis tipos, según sus objetivos y características de conservación: áreas de conservación estricta de la biodiversidad, áreas reservadas para servicios ambientales, territorios de pueblos indígenas, territorios de comunidades locales, otras áreas gestionadas para el uso sostenible y áreas de conservación auxiliares. En segundo lugar, sintetizamos la evidencia disponible sobre su eficacia para reducir la deforestación.…

articles.title: Fifteen years of change in biodiversity conservation across Latin America and the Caribbean
articles.abstract: Latin America and the Caribbean (LACA) is one of the most biodiverse regions globally, yet it continues to experience accelerated biodiversity loss driven by persistent and emerging anthropogenic pressures. In 2009, the Society for Conservation Biology conducted a regional assessment of conservation challenges; however, the evolution of these dynamics over the following 15 years had not been systematically reassessed. We conducted an updated regional synthesis of biodiversity conservation priorities, perceived threats, and implementation barriers across 25 countries, based on a 2024 survey of conservation professionals (n = 244). Respondents were predominantly experienced practitioners affiliated with academic institutions, nongovernmental organizations, and government agencies. Our findings were consistent with the patterns reported in 2009, with deforestation, habitat fragmentation, industrial agriculture, climate change, and pollution persisting as the most severe threats. However, these traditional drivers are now compounded by the intensification of landscape‐scale pressures and a marked shift toward the security–conservation nexus. Respondents explicitly identified organized crime and drug trafficking as primary constraints that compromise both ecosystem integrity and the safety of practitioners. Although conservation tools, such as protected areas and environmental policies, have diversified and improved in many ways, their effectiveness remains limited by a diversification without consolidation trend, characterized by chronic underfunding, corruption, and weak intersectoral coordination. Furthermore, engagement with local communities and citizen science remains predominantly low to moderate, highlighting an enduring gap between policy design and on‐the‐ground implementation. This study underscores that addressing biodiversity loss in LACA has moved beyond the need for technical solutions; it now requires a fundamental transformation in governance quality, institutional integrity, and state capacity to protect the region's natural heritage and the communities that depend on it. Quince años de cambios en la conservación de la biodiversidad en América Latina y el Caribe Resumen América Latina y el Caribe (ALC) es una de las regiones con mayor biodiversidad del mundo; sin embargo, todavía experimenta una pérdida acelerada de biodiversidad impulsada por presiones antropogénicas persistentes y emergentes. En 2009, la Sociedad para la Biología de la Conservación (Society for Conservation Biology) llevó a cabo una evaluación regional de los desafíos de conservación; no obstante, la evolución de estas dinámicas durante los 15 años posteriores no ha sido reevaluada de manera sistemática. Realizamos una síntesis regional actualizada sobre las prioridades de conservación de la biodiversidad, las amenazas percibidas y las barreras para la implementación en 25 países, con base en una encuesta a profesionales de la conservación (n = 244) en 2024. Los encuestados eran mayormente profesionales experimentados afiliados a instituciones académicas, organizaciones no gubernamentales y organismos gubernamentales. Nuestros resultados coincidieron con los patrones reportados en 2009, con la deforestación, la fragmentación del hábitat, la agricultura industrial, el cambio climático y la contaminación como las amenazas más graves. Sin embargo, a estos factores tradicionales se suman ahora la intensificación de presiones a escala de paisaje y un cambio marcado hacia el nexo entre seguridad y conservación. Los encuestados señalaron explícitamente al crimen organizado y al narcotráfico como los principales factores que comprometen tanto la integridad de los ecosistemas como la seguridad de quienes trabajan en el campo.…

articles.title: Systematic mapping of monitoring and evaluation in rewilding
articles.abstract: Rewilding is a landscape recovery approach that seeks to enhance the functioning of degraded ecosystems by reinstating natural processes, and it is increasingly being adopted by organizations and landowners. Despite its popularity, there is no accepted way to assess rewilding's impacts, which is due in part to inconsistent monitoring and evaluation. To address this gap, we developed a systematic map of a unique dataset combining academic and gray literature on monitoring and evaluation in rewilding case studies. We mapped definitions of success, study systems, methods of monitoring, and evaluation metrics for rewilding case studies to compare where the different strands of literature overlap and contrast in focus. We found that researchers and practitioners have been focused on different aspects of rewilding and that the limited recording of case study details and lack of robust experimental design make it difficult to pool and compare data. Researchers and rewilding practitioners face challenges in building a robust evidence base from which to evaluate rewilding outcomes. These challenges include resources as well as spatial and time constraints, which all limit the consistency of data gathering among projects. More comparisons across rewilding projects, better standardization of data collection and data recording methods, and increased collaboration between researchers and practitioners could help remedy these limitations. We developed recommendations for how to monitor and evaluate rewilded landscapes to improve data quality and availability. These include the broad adoption of low‐cost and scalable survey designs with greater focus on comparisons across sites and continued effort toward open‐source data storage. Mapeo sistemático del monitoreo y la evaluación en la renaturalización Resumen La renaturalización es un enfoque de recuperación del paisaje que busca mejorar el funcionamiento de los ecosistemas degradados mediante el restablecimiento de los procesos naturales. Cada vez son más las organizaciones y propietarios de terrenos quienes lo adoptan. A pesar de su popularidad, no existe una forma consensuada de sus impactos, lo que se debe, en parte, a la falta de coherencia en el seguimiento y la evaluación. Para subsanar esta carencia, elaboramos un mapa sistemático a partir de un conjunto único de datos que combina literatura académica y «literatura gris» sobre el seguimiento y la evaluación en casos prácticos de renaturalización. Recopilamos las definiciones de éxito, los sistemas de estudio, los métodos de seguimiento y los indicadores de evaluación de los casos prácticos de renaturalización para comparar en qué aspectos coinciden y en cuáles difieren las distintas corrientes de la literatura. Verificamos que los investigadores y los profesionales se centraran en diferentes aspectos de la renaturalización y que el registro limitado de los detalles de los casos prácticos, junto con la falta de un diseño experimental sólido, dificulta la recopilación y la comparación de datos. Los investigadores y los profesionales de la renaturalización enfrentan retos a la hora de crear una base empírica sólida a partir de la cual evaluar los resultados de la renaturalización. Entre estos retos se encuentran la falta de recursos, así como las limitaciones espaciales y temporales, que restringen la coherencia en la recopilación de datos entre los distintos proyectos. Un mayor número de comparaciones entre proyectos de renaturalización, una mejor estandarización de los métodos de recopilación y registro de datos, y una mayor colaboración entre investigadores y profesionales podrían ayudar a subsanar estas limitaciones. Proponemos una serie de recomendaciones sobre cómo supervisar y evaluar los paisajes sometidos a renaturalización para mejorar la calidad y la disponibilidad de los datos.…

Elevated nitrogen deposition protects an invasive plant from herbivory through altering leaf volatile‐mediated tritrophic interactions
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Atmospheric nitrogen deposition disrupts plant–herbivore interactions, but its impact on leaf volatile organic compounds (VOCs)‐mediated multi‐trophic herbivore resistance remains unclear within the context of plant invasion. In this study, we initially investigated the differences in leaf feeding damage and number of eggs laid by herbivores between the invasive weed Alternanthera philoxeroides and its native congener, Alternanthera sessilis, in different terrestrial habitats that experienced various levels of atmospheric nitrogen deposition. Furthermore, we compared the quantity and composition of leaf constitutive plant volatiles (CPVs) and herbivore‐induced plant volatiles (HIPVs) between the two plant species under simulated nitrogen deposition and tested olfactory and oviposition responses of herbivores and natural enemies at multi‐trophic levels. Field surveys showed less consumed leaf area and fewer herbivore eggs laid on A. philoxeroides than on A. sessilis in terrestrial habitats experiencing high levels of atmospheric nitrogen deposition. Laboratory bioassays revealed that simulated nitrogen deposition increased the emission and altered the composition of both CPVs and HIPVs in A. philoxeroides compared with A. sessilis. These changes reduced its attractiveness to specialist and generalist herbivores while enhancing its appeal to predatory beetles. Methyl salicylate was identified as the key compound driving these changes in insect behaviours, highlighting its critical role in mediating plant–insect interactions in A. philoxeroides under elevated nitrogen deposition. Synthesis. These findings suggest that leaf VOC‐mediated multi‐trophic interactions may facilitate A. philoxeroides invasion success under elevated atmospheric nitrogen deposition in this specific study system, providing a mechanistic basis for understanding how nitrogen enrichment could influence plant–herbivore–predator interactions. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. 摘要 大气氮沉降会干扰植物–植食性昆虫的相互作用，但其在植物入侵背景下对叶片挥发性有机化合物介导的多营养级抗虫性的影响仍不清楚。 本研究首先调查了在不同大气氮沉降水平的陆生生境中，入侵杂草空心莲子草与其本土同属种莲子草在叶片取食损伤程度和植食性昆虫产卵数量上的差异。随后，我们比较了模拟氮沉降条件下两种植物的叶片组成型植物挥发物和虫害诱导型植物挥发物的数量与组成，并测试了多营养级水平上植食性昆虫和天敌的嗅觉与产卵反应。 野外调查表明，在大气氮沉降水平较高的陆生生境中，与莲子草相比，空心莲子草被取食的叶面积更小、植食性昆虫在其上产卵数量更少。室内生物测定显示，与莲子草相比，模拟氮沉降增加了空心莲子草叶片组成型和虫害诱导型挥发物的释放量并改变了其组成。这些变化降低了其对专食性和广食性植食性昆虫的吸引力，同时增强了其对捕食性甲虫的吸引力。水杨酸甲酯被鉴定为驱动这些昆虫行为变化的关键化合物，凸显了其在模拟氮沉降条件下空心莲子草–昆虫相互作用中的关键介导作用。 综合而言，这些发现表明，在该特定研究系统中，叶片挥发物介导的多营养级相互作用可能促进了高氮沉降条件下空心莲子草的入侵成功，为理解氮富集如何影响植物–植食性昆虫–捕食者相互作用提供了机制基础。

Seed‐derived microbiota in the Medicago holobiont: Associations with host phylogeny and breeding‐associated traits
articles.abstract: Seed‐derived bacterial communities tracked host phylogeny across wild Medicago, revealing a phylosymbiotic pattern, whereas fungal communities did not. In cultivated alfalfa, bacterial composition differed between cultivars with high‐yielding and stress‐resistant traits. Trait‐associated bacterial SynComs improved plant growth under non‐stress or combined drought–salinity conditions, respectively, demonstrating the functional relevance of breeding‐associated microbiota. Abstract Seed microbiota occupy unique ecological niches within plants and can form intimate associations with their hosts. However, how seed‐derived microbial communities are related to host phylogeny and breeding‐associated traits across natural and agricultural contexts, and whether trait‐associated microorganisms influence plant performance, remain poorly understood. Here, we characterized endophytic communities in sterile‐grown seedlings from surface‐sterilized seeds of 10 wild Medicago genotypes representing 8 species and 20 domesticated alfalfa cultivars spanning multiple breeding decades. We assessed phylosymbiosis in wild hosts, examined associations between microbial community composition and breeding‐related cultivar characteristics in domesticated alfalfa, and constructed trait‐associated bacterial synthetic communities (SynComs) for functional evaluation. In wild Medicago, bacterial, but not fungal, community composition exhibited significant congruence with host phylogeny, consistent with phylosymbiosis. In domesticated alfalfa, bacterial community composition was associated with cultivar trait category (high‐yielding vs. stress‐resistant), whereas fungal communities were not. Six cultivable candidate bacterial strains associated with the two trait categories were assembled into two SynComs, SynComY (high‐yielding associated) and SynComR (stress‐resistance‐associated). In vitro assays revealed multiple plant growth‐promoting and stress‐tolerance capacities among the constituent strains, while greenhouse experiments showed that SynComY promoted plant growth and SynComR enhanced plant performance under combined drought–salinity stress. Synthesis. Together, these findings show that seed‐derived bacterial community structure is associated with host phylogeny in wild Medicago and breeding‐related trait differentiation in cultivated alfalfa, and further establish that selected bacteria associated with the latter can influence plant performance. Viewed within a holobiont framework, this combined evidence broadens our understanding of seed‐derived microbiota across natural and agricultural contexts and highlights their potential value for microbiome‐informed crop improvement.

articles.title: How the TREX-2 complex associates with the nuclear pore
articles.abstract: Obarska-Kosinska et al. combine cryo-electron tomography, AI-assisted modeling, and crosslinking mass spectrometry to build an extended model of the human nuclear pore. They identify five additional nucleoporins and show how the nuclear basket and TREX-2 complex are attached to the nuclear ring, revealing the spatial organization of mRNP export.

articles.title: Genomic Signatures of Endemic Pathogen Exposure in a Declining Amphibian
articles.abstract: Endemic wildlife diseases can impose strong selection on threatened populations, yet whether persistence is associated with adaptive genomic responses remains poorly understood. We tested whether long‐term exposure to Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd) following population declines has left detectable selection signatures in the genome of the alpine tree frog, Litoria verreauxii alpina. Because prior work suggests limited immunity to Bd within the species, we did not expect persistence to be explained primarily by repeated shifts at canonical immune genes. Instead, we expected pathogen‐associated differentiation, if present, to be diffuse and weakly shared across contrasts, potentially involving regulatory, signalling or reproduction pathways consistent with tolerance, compensatory recruitment or demographic turnover. Using genome‐wide SNP data, we compared Bd‐naïve and Bd‐endemic populations and two 11‐year temporal resampling contrasts. Candidate SNPs were annotated to identify genomic context, nearby genes, putative functions and overlap with previously reported Bd‐associated transcriptomic responses. Using an empirical 99th‐percentile XtX threshold, scans identified high‐differentiation candidate SNPs in all contrasts. Most occurred in noncoding and putatively regulatory regions, with relatively few canonical immune genes. Candidate‐associated genes were more often linked to signalling, transcriptional regulation and cell‐cycle processes. A descriptive comparison with previous work in the species identified 64 candidate‐associated genes matching Bd‐associated transcriptomic annotations, supporting several immune‐adjacent, regulatory, cellular and reproduction candidates. Persistence under endemic Bd might reflect pathogen‐associated selection, compensatory recruitment and demographic change following recurrent adult mortality rather than uniform adaptive rescue through immune resistance.

articles.title: Divarasib as Compared with Sotorasib or Adagrasib in KRAS G12C–Mutated NSCLC
articles.abstract: BackgroundDivarasib, a next-generation, oral KRAS G12C inhibitor, is more potent and selective in vitro than the first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib.MethodsIn this phase 3, international, open-label trial, patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomly assigned to receive divarasib orally at a dose of 400 mg once daily or control treatment (sotorasib orally at a dose of 960 mg once daily or adagrasib orally at a dose of 600 mg twice daily) until the occurrence of disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, loss of clinical benefit, withdrawal of consent, death, or trial termination. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival, confirmed overall response, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, and safety.ResultsA total of 338 patients received divarasib (167 patients) or control treatment (171 patients; 156 received sotorasib and 15 received adagrasib). The median follow-up was 14.3 months. The median progression-free survival was 9.8 months with divarasib and 5.7 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.44 to 0.76; PConclusionsAmong patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic NSCLC, divarasib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than control treatment. (Supported by F. Hoffmann-La Roche; Krascendo 1 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06497556.).

articles.title: Osimertinib–Savolitinib in Advanced NSCLC after Progression during EGFR-TKI Therapy
articles.abstract: BackgroundSavolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Combination therapy with savolitinib and osimertinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-TKI, has shown activity in patients with EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both, after progression during EGFR-TKI therapy.MethodsIn this international, phase 3, open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression (staining intensity of 3+ for MET in ≥90% of tumor cells on immunohistochemical analysis), MET amplification (≥10 gene copies on fluorescence in situ hybridization), or both whose disease had progressed during osimertinib therapy to receive osimertinib (at a dose of 80 mg once daily) plus savolitinib (300 mg twice daily) or intravenous platinum-pemetrexed. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival and safety.ResultsOf the 1746 patients screened, 338 were randomly assigned to receive osimertinib-savolitinib (171 patients) or platinum-pemetrexed (167 patients). Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free survival than platinum-pemetrexed (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.72; PConclusionsOsimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than platinum-pemetrexed among patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both that had progressed during osimertinib therapy (Funded by AstraZeneca; SAFFRON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05261399.).

articles.title: Sacituzumab Tirumotecan plus Pembrolizumab in PD-L1–Negative Advanced NSCLC
articles.abstract: BackgroundPembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal.MethodsIn this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, we evaluated sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab in patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of less than 1%. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Overall survival was a secondary end point. This report presents the results of the prespecified interim analysis.ResultsA total of 455 patients were randomly assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab (229 patients) or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (226 patients). After a median follow-up of 9.7 months, the median progression-free survival was significantly longer with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab than with chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (15.0 months vs. 5.7 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.49; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.36 to 0.65; PConclusionsAmong patients with PD-L1-negative advanced nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations, first-line treatment with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab led to significantly longer progression-free survival than chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. (Funded by Sichuan Kelun-Biotech Biopharmaceutical; OptiTROP-Lung06 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06711900.).

articles.title: Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and chemotherapy versus standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer (UNION): a prespecified interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial
articles.abstract: BackgroundTo our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival.MethodsThis open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years with untreated cT3-4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma (≤10 cm distance from the anal verge) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; stratified by clinical T stage and N stage), using permuted blocks, to receive neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) followed by two cycles of intravenous camrelizumab (200 mg on day 1) plus CAPOX (oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 and intravenous oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1; experimental group) or long-course chemoradiotherapy (50·4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent oral capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily) followed by two cycles of CAPOX (standard-of-care group). After surgery, both groups received six cycles of adjuvant CAPOX, and the experimental group additionally received adjuvant camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles. The primary endpoint was BIRC-assessed pathological complete response rate in the intention-to-treat population, which has been previously reported. Here, we performed a prespecified interim analysis of investigator-assessed event-free survival (one of the key secondary endpoints, defined as time from randomisation to radiographic progression precluding surgery, local recurrence or distant metastasis, or death) in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients) with a boundary of a two-sided p values less than 0·0102. Safety was evaluated in all patients who received at least one dose of the study treatment according to the assigned regimen. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04928807, and is active, but no longer recruiting.FindingsBetween July 23, 2021, and March 1, 2023, 231 patients (153 [66%] males and 78 [34%] females; 227 [98%] were Han Chinese, and four [2%] were other ethnicity Chinese) were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=113) and standard-of-care group (n=118). As of Oct 1, 2025, the median follow-up duration was 36·7 months (IQR 32·6-39·9) in the experimental group and 34·7 months (31·1-39·1) in the standard-of-care group. The 3-year investigator-assessed event-free survival rate was 91·3% (95% CI 83·9-95·4) in the experimental group versus 77·4% (67·9-84·4) in the standard-of-care group (stratified hazard ratio 0·33 [0·15-0·71]; two-sided log-rank p=0·0029). During the entire treatment period, the most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were decreased lymphocyte count (23 [20%] of 115 in the experimental group vs 31 [28%] of 112 in the standard-of-care group), decreased white blood cell count (13 [11%] vs 16 [14%]), decreased neutrophil count (13 [11%] vs 13 [12%]), and decreased platelet count (seven [6%] vs 15 [13%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 22 (19%) versus 15 (13%) patients, with the most common being decreased platelet count (one [1%] vs six [5%]), and radiation gastroenteritis (two [2%] vs four [4%]). Treatment-related deaths occurred in one patient in the experimental group (septic shock related to chemotherapy, but unrelated to camrelizumab) and none in the standard-of-care group.InterpretationIn this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX.…

articles.title: Robust Full-Spectrum-Responsive Multi-junction Tandem Solar Cells via Enhanced Near-Infrared Photon Harvesting
articles.abstract: Developing robust multi-junction tandem photovoltaics remains constrained by the instability of mixed-halide perovskite subcells, given their dominating contribution to overall power output. Integrating near-infrared (NIR) PbS quantum dots (QDs) with FAPbBr3 and crystalline silicon (c-Si) broadens spectrum utilization while improving overall operational stability by reducing the perovskite power contribution. However, enlarged (100) facets and the trade-off between film thickness and quality limit efficient NIR photon harvesting. Herein, a Lewis-basic dihydrazide molecule achieves universal passivation across diverse PbS QD facets via synergistic lead chelation and hydrogen-bonding interactions. Consequently, 0.8 eV PbS QD solar cells with a 685 nm-thick active layer achieve a short-circuit current density of 41.31 mA cm–2 and a 1100-nm-filtered efficiency of 1.80%. The resulting FAPbBr3/c-Si/PbS triple-junction tandems achieve a promising efficiency of 31.04%, with the perovskite subcell contributing 30.4% of the total power output, demonstrating a well-matched operational lifetime. This work offers a strategic framework for efficient multi-junction tandem photovoltaics.

HOST MATTER: Parasite infection drives chemical reconfiguration of decomposing host and shapes insect behavioural responses
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Host–parasite interactions shape ecosystems by driving species dynamics, yet their influence is typically considered in terms of host mortality rather than the chemical environments generated during infection and decomposition. Here, we show that parasitic infection actively reconfigures the chemical phenotype of decomposing hosts, reshaping ecological interactions through volatile‐mediated signalling. Using soil‐dwelling parasites‐entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs) and their symbiotic bacteria‐as a model system, we integrate behavioural assays, comprehensive volatolomic characterization and CO2 quantification across three insect orders and two EPN species over four post‐mortem intervals. We demonstrate that EPN‐infection generates a distinct and conserved volatile signature dominated by carboxylic acids, sulphur‐containing compounds and unsaturated hydrocarbons, accompanied by elevated CO2 emissions. These infection‐derived blends elicit contrasting behavioural responses: they repel non‐natural hosts while consistently attracting natural hosts, indicating that infected cadavers function as chemically structured information hubs. In contrast, frozen‐killed insects exhibit fermentation‐type profiles, and bacteria‐only infection produce simplified alkane‐dominated blends, demonstrating that the full chemical phenotype emerges from the nematode–bacteria complex. Our findings reveal parasitic infection as a process that reorganizes decomposition chemistry with measurable behavioural consequences, uncovering a previously underappreciated mechanism by which parasites structure soil food webs and influence multitrophic interactions. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Local adaptation to host plants in herbivorous insects: A meta‐analysis
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Local adaptation, wherein populations are well‐adapted to local biotic and abiotic conditions, is a common outcome of natural selection and a driver of diversification. Previous theory identified two criteria to detect local adaptation: (a) the home‐away criterion compares the fitness of a population in its home environment to its fitness in a different environment and (b) the local‐foreign criterion examines differences in fitness between a local and a foreign population when experiencing the local environment. We conducted a meta‐analysis synthesizing empirical evidence of insect herbivores' local adaptation to their host plants using both criteria to assess how diet breadth, geographic distance among populations, herbivore taxonomic affiliation, herbivore clonality, the herbivore response variable measured, taxonomic distance among host plants and features of the study design impact the likelihood of detecting local adaptation. Overall, we found patterns consistent with herbivore local adaptation using both the home‐away and local‐foreign criteria. Herbivore diet breadth, taxonomic affiliation and geographic distance between herbivore populations did not affect the likelihood of finding local adaptation. In contrast, the detection of local adaptation varied with herbivore clonality, the specific response variables measured, taxonomic distance among host plants and elements of the experimental design. These findings clarify the conditions under which local adaptation emerges in the world's most diverse group of multicellular organisms. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Resumen La adaptación local consiste en el desarrollo de características que permiten un mejor desempeño de las poblaciones en las condiciones bióticas y abióticas de su entorno. Este fenómeno es una consecuencia común de la selección natural y uno de los mecanismos de diversificación biológica. Se han identificado dos criterios para detectar adaptación local: (a) el criterio ‘en casa‐fuera de casa’ que compara la adecuación de una población en su propio ambiente contra la adecuación de esa misma población en un ambiente foráneo; y (b) el criterio ‘local‐forastero’, que compara la adecuación de dos poblaciones, una local y otra foránea, cuando habitan el ambiente natal de cada una de ellas. Utilizamos un meta‐análisis para sintetizar evidencia empírica de la adaptación local de insectos herbívoros a sus plantas hospederas de acuerdo con cada uno de los criterios anteriores. Este análisis nos permitió evaluar el efecto de la amplitud de la dieta, distancia geográfica, afiliación taxonómica del herbívoro, clonalidad, variable de respuesta, distancia taxonómica entre la planta local y la foránea, y características del diseño experimental, en la probabilidad de detectar adaptación local. Encontramos patrones consistentes con la noción de que los insectos herbívoros exhiben adaptación local a sus plantas hospederas de acuerdo con ambos criterios. Adicionalmente, encontramos que la amplitud de la dieta, afiliación taxonómica y la distancia geográfica entre las poblaciones de herbívoros no afectaron la probabilidad de detectar adaptación local. Por el contrario, variables que sí afectaron la probabilidad de detectar adaptación local incluyen la clonalidad del herbívoro, la variable de respuesta que se utilizó para evaluar el desempeño del herbívoro, la distancia taxonómica entre las plantas local y foránea, y algunos elementos del diseño experimental. Nuestros resultados contribuyen al esclarecimiento de las condiciones que determinan la ocurrencia de adaptación local en el grupo más diverso de organismos multicelulares.

articles.title: Biodegradable and Non‐Biodegradable Microplastics Drive Divergent Microbial Carbon and Nitrogen Metabolism Regimes in Soil–Plant Systems
articles.abstract: The accumulation of microplastics (MPs) in soils worldwide has raised concerns about their potential impacts on microbially mediated carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) cycling. However, whether biodegradable and non‐biodegradable MPs differently affect microbial C and N metabolism and coupling, and whether these responses are modulated by co‐occurring plant identity remain uncertain. We combined a meta‐analysis with a controlled pot experiment comparing soil responses under two congeneric plant species exposed to two biodegradable and two non‐biodegradable MPs at doses ranging from 0% to 2% (w/w). In the meta‐analysis, MPs generally increased CO2 emission and microbial biomass N (MBN), but had no significant overall effect on microbial biomass C (MBC). In the pot experiment, MPs likewise increased CO2 emission, whereas overall effect sizes of MBC and MBN were nonsignificant. Nevertheless, these overall responses did not capture the distinct patterns of microbial C–N metabolic coordination between MP types. Under biodegradable MPs, tighter MBC–MBN coupling with a dose‐dependent shift toward greater respiratory C loss relative to MBC collectively indicated a maintenance‐associated metabolic pattern. In contrast, MBC–MBN decoupling and stronger MBC–CO2 coupling under non‐biodegradable MPs indicated a biomass‐linked metabolic pattern. In addition, plant identity modulated these microbial metabolisms in an MP‐type manner, particularly in N‐related processes. These metabolic responses were accompanied with changes in soil property conditions and substrate availability, weakened DOC–DON coupling, and shifts in microbial community structure and life history strategy. RDA‐based hierarchical and variation partitioning and SEM further indicated that modeled soil property pathways were more prominent under non‐biodegradable MPs, while substrate‐related pathways were prominent under biodegradable MPs. Together, the meta‐analysis reveals the general microbial metabolic patterns under MP type, and the pot experiment further reveals how MP type and plant identity jointly influence microbial C–N metabolism through contrasting associations with soil substrates and property conditions.

articles.title: Conservative Spruce Outperforms Acquisitive Larch Under Warming and CO2
articles.abstract: Predicting boreal forest growth is hindered by limited experimental tests on the compounding effects of climate change and atmospheric CO2. We integrated regional tree‐ring data with a peatland warming and CO2 manipulation experiment, including 45 trait measurements, to assess growth responses of two widespread boreal conifers, Larix laricina and Picea mariana, to temperature, vapor pressure deficit (VPD), soil moisture, and elevated CO2. L. laricina growth was consistently more climate‐sensitive than P. mariana, increasing strongly with soil moisture and declining slightly with VPD at the regional scale, but responding positively to VPD and temperature—not soil moisture or CO2—at the experimental peatland. L. laricina's acquisitive strategy enhanced water and nutrient uptake, sustaining growth but reducing hydraulic safety. By contrast, P. mariana's conservative strategy maintained water‐use efficiency and hydraulic resilience without compromising growth. Our results challenge projections of widespread CO2 fertilization in boreal forests and highlight conservative conifers as potential winners under warming and drying, sustaining growth while maintaining low mortality risk. This dynamic could reshape projections of the boreal carbon sink and its role in global climate feedback.
